author: andrewb-eng
body:
… activity

Two locally captured entries can share a millisecond AND a source -- sessions backfilled from a single clock read do exactly this -- so two payload rows collided on memory_entries' on_conflict key (project_id, author_id, ts, source). Postgres aborts that whole upsert with SQLSTATE 21000; `Prefer: resolution=ignore-duplicates` cannot help, since it governs conflicts with rows already in the table, not duplicates inside the statement.

It could never self-heal: the throw happens before row signatures are recorded, so every entry stayed in the drift-resend path and the identical wedged batch retried every 60s forever. One real install had been failing since 2026-07-23, with no genuine pull since 2026-07-21.

dedupeOnConflictKey() collapses colliding rows at the one boundary both push paths (fresh and drift-resend) funnel through, so no caller can hand the backend a self-conflicting statement. Last row wins -- entries arrive in ascending ts order, so the later copy is the more current one.

Worse than the push failing was what it took down with it: pushProject threw past pullProject, so one unpushable local entry cost the user ALL teammate activity -- the entire point of team sync. Push now has its own try/catch, the same best-effort treatment the archive backfill below it already had, and the error is still recorded in `errors` so status and the dashboard surface it. Reading the team must never depend on publishing to it. The RLS hint moves into rlsHint() so a membership refusal on the push path keeps its friendly message.

The mock was why 1283 checks missed this: it looped row-by-row and silently accepted duplicate keys within one batch. It now enforces the real constraint and returns the real Postgres 21000 payload.

author: movm
body:
PR 2 des Plans, den 27k-Klassifikator durch kleine, eng gefasste Auflöser zu ersetzen (PR 1 = #2233).

## Was

Fünf Aufrufstellen erzwingen `intent: 'search'`, weil etwas angehängt wurde, das durchsucht werden muss — DocumentChat, Document, Wolke, Connect, Notebook. Der Intent steht dort **schon fest**; offen ist nur, *wonach* gesucht wird.

Diese Frage ging bisher durch `CLASSIFIER_PROMPT` — 27.198 Zeichen Werkzeug-Taxonomie, Sekundär-Intent-Regeln und JSON-Schema. Das Intent-Verdikt, das dabei herauskam, warf der Aufrufer anschließend mit hartkodiertem `intent: 'search'` weg.

Neu: `queryRefineResolver.ts`, **709 Zeichen**, nach dem Muster von `docsIntentTiebreak.ts` — harter Timeout, `null` bei jedem Fehler, `INTERMEDIATE_MODEL`, bestehender Task-Typ `chat_intent_classification` (kein neuer Task-Typ, keine Worker-Pool-Änderung). Fallback bleibt `extractSearchTopic`, derselbe, den der bisherige Fehlerzweig schon benutzte.

## Die sechs Felder, die der alte Aufruf behielt

| Feld | auf diesem Pfad | wird jetzt |
|---|---|---|
| `searchQuery` | tragend | vom Auflöser |
| `subQueries` | tragend (`searchNode` `baseQueries`) | vom Auflöser |
| `detectedFilters` | tragend | von `heuristicExtractFilters` (deterministisch) |
| `documentSubtype` | nur Dokument-**Erstellung** | entfällt |
| `targetGroupName` | kein Konsument | entfällt |
| `secondaryIntent` | Loop-Kill-Switch | **immer null** — siehe unten |

**Verhaltensänderung:** `secondaryIntent` ist hier jetzt immer `null`. Diese Turns werden damit nicht mehr vom Kill-Switch in `decideRunAgentic` aus dem Loop geworfen — ein Dokument- oder Notebook-Turn erreicht den Loop, wo das Modell die Retrieval-Werkzeuge tatsächlich aufrufen kann.

## Gemessen

15 Fälle, echtes Modell, handgeschriebener Eingabesatz (der Eval-Korpus hat für Notebooks und eingefügtes Material zusammen elf Zeilen und keinen der unbequemen Fälle):

```
Prompt:  27.198 → 709 Zeichen   (38×)
Latenz:    2,2 s → 0,7 s        pro Aufruf
```

**In 8 von 15 Fällen lieferte der alte Prompt gar keine Anfrage** — er war mit der Frage „welches von 32 Werkzeugen" beschäftigt. Dann greift `classification.searchQuery || extractSearchTopic(userContent)`, und der **Rohsatz** wird zur Suchanfrage:

```
ALT sucht:  "Bitte lies das durch und schreib mir daraus eine Pressemitteilung von
             maximal 1500 Zeichen, in der es vor allem um die Beschlusslage zur
             Ganztagsbetreuung geht, mit einem Zitat am Ende."
NEU sucht:  "Beschlusslage zur Ganztagsbetreuung"
```

Nebenbefund: bei „Was sagt **Habek** dazu?" korrigierte der alte Prompt den Eigennamen zu „Habeck" — obwohl er das selbst in Großbuchstaben verbietet.

## Was NICHT belegt ist

Eine Messung gegen das echte Qdrant (8 Fälle, 3 Sammlungen, `limit 3` wie in `executeDocumentSearchParallel`) ergab **mittlere Jaccard-Überlappung 0,52**. Die Treffermenge ändert sich also real — aber welche Seite relevanter ist, sagt diese Zahl nicht. Beim Durchsehen der abweichenden Treffer ist das Bild gemischt.

Zwei Einschränkungen: die alte Seite ist zwischen Läufen instabil (mal liefert sie eine Anfrage, mal nicht), und bei ~6 Treffern je Seite ist Jaccard verrauscht.

Struktureller Nebenbefund: bei vorhandenen `subQueries` benutzt `executeDocumentSearchParallel` die Hauptanfrage **gar nicht** (`subQueries?.length ? subQueries : [query]`). Bei mehrthemigen Anfragen entscheidet allein die Zerlegung — dort waren alt und neu identisch (Jaccard 1,00).

## Verifikation

- `classifierNode.vitest.ts`: 221/221 grün
- `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.integration.json`: sauber
- ESLint + Prettier: sauber

author: kevinkim-ogp
body:
## TL;DR

Three small GitHub Actions cost/hygiene improvements: cancel superseded CI runs on push, shorten Inspector scan artifact retention, and add per-job timeouts sized from real run history.

## What changed?

- `test-and-build.yml`: added `concurrency: { group: "${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}", cancel-in-progress: true }` so pushing again to a branch cancels the in-flight run for that same branch instead of letting it run to completion.
- `deploy.yml`: added `retention-days: 7` to the Inspector vulnerability scan / SBOM artifact upload (previously unset, defaulting to the org/repo default of 90 days).
- Added `timeout-minutes` to every job in both workflows (previously none had one, so a hang would run for GitHub's 360-minute default cap). Each timeout is set to roughly 2x the max duration observed in recent run history, floored at 5 minutes for short jobs so a single slow cache-miss run doesn't cause false-positive timeouts.

The three `deploy-*.yml` workflows (staging/uat/production) already had concurrency cancellation on their protected-branch push events, so no change was needed there.

### Timeout benchmarks

Sampled from `gh api repos/opengovsg/plumber/actions/runs/<id>/jobs` across 11 recent `test-and-build` runs and 8 recent `deploy.yml` runs (staging/uat/prod):

| Workflow | Job | Observed range | Typical | Max seen | New timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| test-and-build.yml | `setup` | 12s – 1m36s | ~15-90s | 1.6min | 5 min |
| test-and-build.yml | `lint-and-build` | 1m53s – 2m37s | ~2.2min | 2.6min | 5 min |
| test-and-build.yml | `test` | 6m37s – 11m57s | ~7.3min | 12min | 24 min |
| deploy.yml | `build` (docker build + ECR push + Inspector scan) | 2m16s – 7m16s | ~4.5min | 7.3min | 15 min |
| deploy.yml | `deploy` (ECS task def render + CodeDeploy trigger) | 14s – 3m50s | ~20s | 3.8min | 8 min |

## Tests

- [ ] Push twice in quick succession to a branch and confirm the first `Test and build` run gets cancelled.
- [ ] Confirm a deploy still runs cleanly and the scan-results artifact is downloadable, with a 7-day expiry shown in the Actions UI.
- [ ] Confirm none of the new timeouts trip on a normal run (all comfortably above observed max durations).

## Deploy notes

None — workflow-only change, no app code touched.

author: behindthedash
body:
## Outcome
`_forbidden_paths_touched` now logs a compile-accuracy signal (files a PR group touched but never declared) automatically on every real run, instead of that signal only being available via a manual `worktrail-plan-audit` invocation after the fact.

## Business or User Value
The compile-prompt tuning signal PR #62 introduced (`plan_audit.audit_plan`'s `undeclared` set) previously required someone to remember to run it by hand before task branches were torn down. Wiring it into the always-run verify path means the signal is captured for every run with zero extra effort, enabling future measurement of whether prompt changes actually reduce under-reporting.

## Route Selected
I — Investigation. The brief's own recommended-route and the classifier both landed on I at medium confidence; the change is exactly what Route I permits without further authorization: minimal diagnostics (a `self.log()` call), no behavior change to the pass/fail decision.

## Epic / Feature / Specification
none — unspecced internal tooling change to `src/worktrail/orchestrator/verify.py`. Investigation note at `docs/specs/research/wire-plan-audit-into-verify.md`.

## Behavior Before
`_forbidden_paths_touched` computed `touched` and `declared` per PR group to build the deny-list, then discarded that data. The `touched - declared` mismatch (the same signal `plan_audit.audit_plan` computes standalone) was invisible unless someone ran `worktrail-plan-audit` by hand before the task branch was torn down.

## Behavior After
When a group has declared files, `_forbidden_paths_touched` now also logs (`self.log`) any file that was touched but not declared, prefixed `compile-accuracy:`. The deny-list return value is byte-for-byte unchanged — verified by dedicated tests.

## Scope
`src/worktrail/orchestrator/verify.py` (11 lines), `tests/orchestrator/test_verify.py` (3 new tests), `docs/specs/research/wire-plan-audit-into-verify.md` (investigation note).

## Non-Goals
Aggregating the logged signal across runs to measure whether compile.py's new PROMPT wording reduces under-reporting is explicitly out of scope — the brief names it as a distinct future follow-up that needs this signal to exist in production logs first.

## Implementation Summary
Reused the already-computed `touched` (git diff) and `declared` (`self.declared_files[group_name]`) values inside `_forbidden_paths_touched`. Added a guarded, non-blocking log: only fires when `declared` is non-empty (nothing to compare against otherwise, mirroring `plan_audit.audit_plan`'s own `if not tp.files: continue` guard) and only when the undeclared set is non-empty.

## Security and Authorization Impact
None. Log-only diagnostic; no new inputs, no new external calls, no change to what is allowed or denied.

## Data or Migration Impact
None.

## UI Validation
n/a — no UI surface.

## Tests and Evidence
- `test_touched_not_declared_is_logged_but_does_not_change_result` — log fires with the mismatched file, deny-list result unchanged.
- `test_no_undeclared_files_logs_nothing` — no mismatch, no log.
- `test_no_declared_files_at_all_skips_the_compile_accuracy_check` — nothing declared, no log (matches plan_audit's own skip behavior).
- Full suite: `PYTHONPATH=src pytest -q` → 2275 passed, 98 subtests passed.
- `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m worktrail.orchestrator.orchestrate check` → GOLDEN OK (orchestrator output unchanged).

## Scope Completeness
Run record scope review recorded as `complete` for the single in-scope item (wire the log call). No deferred work identified — the aggregation follow-up is explicitly out of this change's scope per the brief itself.

## Pre-PR Test Gate
`worktrail-pre-pr-gate --repo . --risk low --run <run-record>` → PASS (`PYTHONPATH=src pytest -q && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m worktrail.orchestrator.orchestrate check`).

## Performance Impact
Negligible — one extra set difference and, only on mismatch, one log call per PR group verify pass. No new git/subprocess calls.

## Deferred Work and Handoffs
none

## Risk Assessment
low — log-only change, deny-list return value provably unchanged by tests, full suite green.

## Rollback Plan
Revert the single commit; `_forbidden_paths_touched` returns to its prior behavior with no data loss (the log line is print-only observability, not persisted state).

## Auto-Merge Eligibility
eligible — `go:risk-low` label applied per `worktrail-pre-pr-gate` output (required checks present: Lint, Test & Build; allow_auto_merge enabled). This repo's own CI automation (`CI: Auto-merge on open`) will merge it once green.

## Summary
Adds a new "Titulares" (Headlines) section to the dashboard that aggregates high-impact financial news from multiple sources and allows manual entry. Headlines are filtered to only include those affecting G10 currencies, CNY, bonds, or major equities.

## Key Changes

- **New Headlines Page** (`src/pages/Titulares.tsx`): Main UI for viewing, filtering, and managing headlines with:
  - Sync button to fetch from external sources
  - Manual headline entry form with impact level and relevance tag selection
  - Filter by impact level (alto/medio/bajo)
  - Pin/unpin headlines to appear in dashboard carousel
  - Delete functionality

- **Headlines Sync API** (`api/headlines-sync.ts`): Serverless function that:
  - Fetches economic calendar events from Forex Factory (no auth required)
  - Fetches forex news from Finnhub API (requires `FINNHUB_API_KEY`)
  - Classifies headlines by impact level using keyword matching
  - Filters to only G10 + CNY currencies, bonds, and major equities
  - Upserts to database using deterministic IDs to prevent duplicates

- **Data Layer Updates** (`src/data/MacroDataContext.tsx`):
  - Added headlines state management with localStorage fallback
  - New methods: `addManualHeadline`, `toggleHeadlinePin`, `updateHeadlineImpact`, `deleteHeadline`
  - Loads headlines from Supabase on initialization (limit 300, sorted by date)

- **UI Components**:
  - `HeadlineCard.tsx`: Reusable card component displaying headline with impact badge, source, tags, and action buttons
  - `Layout.tsx`: Added navigation link to Titulares page

- **Database Schema** (`supabase/schema.sql`):
  - New `headlines` table with columns for title, source, URL, publish date, impact level, tags, manual flag, and pin status
  - Row-level security policies for public read/write access

- **Type Definitions** (`src/types.ts`):
  - New `ImpactLevel` type ('alto' | 'medio' | 'bajo')
  - New `Headline` interface with all relevant fields

- **Utilities** (`src/lib/impact.ts`): Impact level labels and color mappings for consistent UI styling

- **Configuration** (`.env.example`): Added `FINNHUB_API_KEY` documentation

## Implementation Details

- Headlines use deterministic IDs (source + hash of title/date) from sync API to enable idempotent upserts
- Manual headlines use `crypto.randomUUID()` for unique IDs
- Keyword-based classification for Finnhub headlines since that API doesn't provide impact levels
- Forex Factory headlines already have impact classification from the provider
- "Low impact" headlines from Forex Factory are filtered out to reduce noise
- Pinned headlines can appear in a dashboard carousel (UI not yet built)
- Full offline support via localStorage when Supabase is unavailable

author: fernandobandeira
body:
Closes task `vf7a` (epic `y3ww`, proposal `3i92`).

## The gap

Two decisions had landed with **no dispatch caller**:

* **z3gi (#2837)** shipped `decide_launcher_protocol_admission(mode, declared)` — the persisted `launcher_authority_mode` singleton against an artifact's declaration — and its own doc says `UndeclaredProtocol` is "a refusal in BOTH modes … owned by `vf7a`". Nothing called it from a dispatch.
* **#2836** shipped `render_authority_protocol(declared, digest)`, which reads the artifact's declaration but never consults the persisted authority.

`ProjectRepository::resolve_dispatch_image` — the seam `djinn_k8s::runtime::prepare` already calls before it builds a Job — is where they meet.

## The decision

`djinn_db::launcher_compatibility::decide_admission` is the centralized compatibility function. It is **not** a second implementation: every artifact that declared something is routed verbatim through z3gi's verdict; only `UndeclaredProtocol` is reinterpreted. A missing protocol becomes effective `leaf-v1` only when **all** of:

* the artifact is pinned to a **canonical immutable digest** — `sha256:` + exactly 64 lowercase hex, compared **exactly**, never a tag and never an image name;
* that digest is listed in the deployment's **signed** pre-protocol inventory;
* the persisted authority mode (migration 167) is `leaf-v1`.

Every other combination refuses **before a Job is rendered**:

| shape | outcome |
|---|---|
| declaration disagrees with the authority | `Declared(ProtocolMismatch)` |
| declaration unparseable | `Declared(UnknownProtocol)` |
| authority singleton absent/unreadable | `Declared(AuthorityUnavailable)` |
| no declaration, mode `resize-v2` | `MissingDeclarationUnderMode` |
| no declaration, non-canonical digest | `MalformedDigest` |
| no declaration, digest not inventoried | `UninventoriedDigest` |
| no declaration, inventory untrusted | `InventoryUnusable` |
| no declaration, **no digest at all** | `Undeclarable` — see below |

## The inventory

An Ed25519-signed JSON document (`schema_version`, `issuer`, `issued_at`, `digests`) named by `DJINN_LEGACY_LAUNCHER_DIGEST_INVENTORY`, verified against `..._PUBLIC_KEY` / `..._SIGNATURE` over the document's **exact bytes**, read once per process so a restart re-reads it.

Every validation failure — unreadable file, absent key, absent signature, bad base64, wrong key/signature length, failed verification, unknown schema version, malformed digest entry — yields `Unusable`, which grants **no** compatibility to anything. A broken inventory is stricter than no inventory, never looser.

`ImageRepository::legacy_pre_protocol_digests()` enumerates exactly the `ready` / undeclared / digest-pinned rows, ordered by id, so an operator builds the document from the catalog rather than by hand (and so the same catalog produces byte-identical, re-signable output).

## #2831's anti-wedge guard survives

A pre-existing `status = 'ready'` row with `registry_digest IS NULL` still resolves and still yields a pull ref. It is `Undeclarable`: it carries **no** authority, and #2836's `render_authority_protocol` refuses it exactly as it does on `main` today. `a_preexisting_ready_row_with_no_digest_still_dispatches_under_leaf_v1` passes unchanged.

Making that shape a resolve **error** would break a row migration 166 deliberately keeps legal, and would turn the readiness/warm/indexer callers that share the resolver into failure paths. `get_dispatch_readiness` reads the unfenced row for the same reason. Migration 166's CHECK is untouched and still scoped to declaring rows.

## Arming

With **no inventory configured**, the *membership* test is unarmed: an undeclared, canonically digest-pinned image still maps to `leaf-v1` under `leaf-v1` mode — exactly #2836's rule. An inventory that does not exist cannot classify a digest as "unknown", and letting an absent config file retroactively strand every already-built digest-pinned image is precisely the wedge migration 166 refused to create. Configuring an inventory arms it. Every other rejection class above is unconditional.

`arming_the_inventory_is_what_narrows_an_undeclared_artifact` asserts both halves, so the one case where the fence takes something away is stated rather than discovered.

## Test matrix

`server/crates/djinn-db/tests/launcher_admission_compatibility_matrix.rs` — 10 tests. Three artifact shapes (real no-handshake legacy, explicit `leaf-v1`, explicit `resize-v2`) × both authority modes × four inventory states, driven through the **real** `ImageRepository::mark_ready` (so migration 166's CHECK and the repository's digest guard apply), the **real** `LauncherAuthorityModeRepository::set_mode` drain fence, and the **real** `resolve_dispatch_image`. No stub.

Every admitted cell asserts **exactly one** effective quota authority: admitted == mode, and (when declared) == declaration. `the_repository_seam_reports_exactly_what_the_decision_returns` sweeps all 32 combinations and asserts the DB path and the pure function agree cell for cell.

`server/crates/djinn-image-controller/tests/protocol_catalog_and_preservation.rs` — 6 tests covering AC2 (generated Dockerfiles declare the LABEL + ENV, `build_job.rs` echoes the sentinel, a newly cataloged artifact declares + pins and never consults the inventory, a declaring build with no digest is refused) and AC4.

## AC4 — no retirement

`no_containment_asset_was_retired_to_make_compatibility_work` asserts behaviour anchors, not filenames, across: the `djinn-cgroup-launcher` binary, `cgroup.kill` and `wait_empty` (launcher **and** broker **and** the worker-side process broker), `CHILD_UID = 1001` / `set_uid(CHILD_UID)`, the credential-boundary tests, the rendered credential/mount boundary, the broker mount surface (`VOLUME_LAUNCHER_IPC`, `LAUNCHER_SOCKET_PATH`, `LAUNCHER_CREDENTIAL_PATH`, `TASK_RUN_CGROUP_RUNTIME_CLASS`), the RuntimeClass manifest, and the k3s node conformance program. Nothing was deleted; no retirement is used to satisfy compatibility.

## Fixture honesty

Two fixtures used `sha256:abc` as a digest. It names no artifact, so the fence now refuses it; both are canonical 64-hex. That is the fence working — and it is why `a_protocol_less_undigested_image_creates_zero_kubernetes_objects`, which drives the **real** `KubernetesRuntime::prepare` against a recording fake apiserver, caught it. That test now also aligns the authority singleton with its declaring fixture, because a `resize-v2` image no longer dispatches while the server runs `leaf-v1`.

## Mutations (all run, real failures)

| mutation | test that fails |
|---|---|
| inventory membership always `true` | `a_missing_protocol_is_admitted_only_for_an_exact_inventoried_digest` |
| drop the `mode != LeafV1` guard | `no_missing_protocol_artifact_survives_resize_v2` |
| accept any `sha256:`-prefixed string | `a_mutable_tag_without_a_verified_digest_never_dispatches` |
| `Unusable` falls back to admitted | `an_unusable_inventory_rejects_rather_than_falling_back` |
| admit a mismatched declaration | `every_admitted_combination_has_exactly_one_effective_authority` |
| **skip the fence at the resolve seam** | **9 of 10 matrix tests** |
| drop `IS NULL` from the candidate query | `the_inventory_candidate_set_is_exactly_the_ready_undeclared_digest_pinned_rows` |
| drop `emit_launcher_protocol` | `every_generated_image_declares_its_protocol_in_build_metadata` |
| retire the RuntimeClass handler | `no_containment_asset_was_retired_to_make_compatibility_work` |

## Scope

Touched: `djinn-db/src/{launcher_compatibility.rs,lib.rs,repositories/{image.rs,project.rs}}`, two new test files, and the two fixture digests in `djinn-k8s/tests/launcher_authority_protocol_render.rs`.

Untouched: `djinn-cgroup-launcher/**`, `djinn-launcher-protocol/**`, `djinn-k8s/src/{launcher.rs,launcher_cpu.rs,job.rs,runtime.rs}`, `deploy/**`, `scripts/kind/**`. No new migration (main is at 167; none was needed — the inventory is deployment config, not schema). No `.sqlx` change (

author: trishorts
body:
Implements **Stage 2** of #2692, and only Stage 2.

## The problem

Glycosite localization is scored with c/zDot ions, so it is only meaningful against an electron-based child scan. `FindOGlycan` selected that scan by position:

```csharp
if (theScan.ChildScans.Count > 0 && GlycoPeptides.DissociationTypeContainETD(CommonParameters.MS2ChildScanDissociationType, CommonParameters.CustomIons))
{
    localizationScan = theScan.ChildScans.First();
```

`ChildScans` is populated in scan-number order, so `First()` is the lowest-numbered child **whatever its activation**. With a single child that is always the right scan, which is why this has held up for every acquisition shape the method was written for (`HCD-pd-ETD`, `HCD-pd-EThcD` — both named in the comment above it).

With two children of different types it is right only if the acquisition happens to order the electron scan first. When it does not:

- the collision-based child is selected as the localization spectrum, while the very next line generates `DissociationType.ETD` products — **c/zDot theoretical ions scored against a spectrum that cannot contain them**;
- the low-resolution tolerance branch immediately below inherits the same wrong scan, so an ion-trap ETD child sitting at index 1 also loses its wider tolerance.

Note the guard tests `CommonParameters.MS2ChildScanDissociationType` — the single, globally declared child type — rather than anything about the scan actually chosen.

## The change

Consult each child scan's own header and prefer the first child whose activation is electron-based. An absent or `Autodetect` header carries no activation information, so it is skipped rather than trusted.

When no child advertises a usable activation, fall back to the previous `First()` behavior rather than dropping localization — the declared `MS2ChildScanDissociationType` has already asserted ETD, and silently degrading identifications toward Level 3 would be worse than the status quo.

**Single-child acquisitions take the same path as before either way**, so `HCD-pd-ETD` and `HCD-pd-EThcD` data are unaffected.

## Tests

Three new tests in `GlycoSearchEngineTest`, following that file's existing reflection pattern for private instance members:

- `GetLocalizationScan_PrefersElectronBasedChild_NotTheFirstChild` — a CID child at scan 2 and an EThcD child at scan 3; the EThcD child is selected. Fails before this change.
- `GetLocalizationScan_SingleElectronBasedChild_IsUnchanged` — the regression guard for the shapes this code already supported.
- `GetLocalizationScan_NoResolvableChildActivation_FallsBackToFirstChild` — null and `Autodetect` headers.

## Verification

Built and tested against `master` at `3b9f634ec`.

- The three new tests pass.
- `--filter "FullyQualifiedName~Glyco"`: **86 passed / 5 failed** on unmodified `master`, and **89 passed / 5 failed** with this branch. Same five, so this change breaks nothing and adds three.

### Heads-up: five glyco tests are already red on master

Unrelated to this PR, but found while establishing the baseline and worth surfacing: `NandO_GlycoSearch_onlyN`, `NandO_GlycoSearch_onlyO`, `NandO_GlycoSearch_onlyO_Run2`, `NandO_GlycoSearchIndividualFileFolderOutputTest`, and `GlycoTest_WritingSummary` fail on unmodified `master` when the glyco suite is run together.

`NandO_GlycoSearch_onlyN` **passes when run in isolation**, so these look order-dependent rather than genuinely broken — the static mutable glycan state (`GlycanBox.GlobalOGlycans` / `GlobalNGlycans` / `OGlycanBoxes`, populated in the `GlycoSearchEngine` constructor) is the obvious suspect. Happy to file that separately.

## Scope

Deliberately narrow. The remaining stages of #2692 — resolving each child against its own activation for fragment generation, so a CID child contributes b/y evidence rather than being forced through one declared type, plus the parameter and UI work — are follow-ons and are better reviewed on their own.

Touches `GlycoSearchEngine` (adds one private method, changes one line in `FindOGlycan`); no existing member's behavior or signature is otherwise altered.

author: cplong90
body:
## Why

`card_vectors.extract_vectors` scans every history parquet in a sweep — measured
**680.8 s** over the 1052 files of the `population_phenotype_basal_8x16`
ensemble — so it cannot run per render. Its results had nowhere to live between
a run and a card, and the gap was being filled by a committed test fixture doing
double duty: frozen regression golden *and* live comparison input.

Those two roles pull in opposite directions. A golden should not change when the
model changes; a live sim vector must. An artifact doing both cannot say which
run it came from — and that is not hypothetical. A downstream consumer read one
of these fixtures as its live sim side while asserting a *different* ensemble in
its provenance panel, and rendered "104 cells" over values from a 20-cell bake.
Nothing in the stack could detect the drift, because the artifact had no run
identity to check against.

This adds the missing home and separates the roles.

## What

**A run-keyed cache** (`v2ecoli/library/sim_vector_cache.py`), keyed by
`(experiment_id, generation_lower_bound, extractor_version)`:

- `experiment_id` is the canonical run id from
  `docs/conventions/run-provenance.md`, so a new sweep yields a new entry
  automatically and every cached vector states which run produced it.
- `generation_lower_bound` is in the key because it changes the **ensemble**,
  not just a filter — the same sweep at gen_lb 3 vs 0 is a different set of
  cells. A key without it silently serves a stale vector after a burn-in change.
- `extractor_version` is in the key because the vector is as much a function of
  the extraction code as of the run.

Location follows the convention #418 established for S3-resident sweeps: output
goes to `out_dir`, defaulting to the sweep dir when local and **required** for an
`s3://` sweep, which is read-only. The cache is machine-local and invisible to CI
**by design** — the committed fixtures remain the run-free path CI and the report
cards grade against.

Measured: **680.8 s cold → 0.054 s warm (12,562×)**, 0.3 MB cache file.

**Two commits, not one ambiguous `sim_commit`.** `run_commit` is the code that
produced the sweep; `extracted_at_commit` is the code that ran the extraction —
different things entirely for a re-extracted older sweep, and a single field gets
read as whichever the reader assumed.

⚠️ **`run_commit` is null for every existing sweep, and that is a real finding
rather than a limitation of this change.** v2ecoli workflow sweeps record no git
identity anywhere: the `configuration` partition carries only
experiment_id/variant/lineage_seed/generation, and neither `sweep.pbg` nor
`summary.json` carries one. The cache reads a commit when the run recorded one
and stamps null otherwise, rather than substituting the extracting tree's HEAD,
which would assert something false. Making this non-null is a runner change —
see "Open question" below.

**Id-keyed omics fixtures.** The model proteome was keyed by gene symbol alone,
and symbol is not a safe join key across sources: symbol spaces differ between
databases and are not injective across them.

- `model_proteome.json` gains `by_id` (EcoCyc monomer id). This is a **re-key,
  not a re-bake** — position *i* of `monomer_counts` is both `ids[i]` and
  `symbols[i]`, so existing values are re-filed under their ids unchanged.
  4309 monomers → 4309 ids, 4309 symbols, 0 unmapped, **0 collisions**.
- New `model_transcriptome.json` keyed by EcoCyc **gene** id — 4345 genes over
  4345 mRNA cistrons, 0 unmapped, 0 collisions. Gene ids come from
  `cistron_data["gene_id"]` (which sim_data builds off `genes.tsv`) rather than
  by stripping the `_RNA` suffix; string surgery on identifiers breaks silently
  when a convention changes.

To be clear about what the collision count argues: **it is zero, and the case for
id-keying is not "collisions avoided."** The model's own symbol space is clean.
The hazard is translating *between* the model's symbol space and another
source's, which is where an id key earns its keep and where this repo cannot see
the other side.

The transcriptome is derived from the pinned reference rather than re-extracted
from whichever sweep is on disk, so the committed transcriptome and proteome
describe the **same** 20-cell ensemble. The reference's cistron-id array is
checked against `omics_labels` position-for-position first, proving the alignment
rather than assuming it. `scripts/bake_model_omics.py --from-sweep` derives it
from a sweep through the cache instead.

**No graded value changes.** Every pre-existing key in all five fixtures is
byte-identical to `origin/main`; only `by_id`/`id_key`/`keying` are added to the
proteome. The fixtures are **not** re-baked — and could not be: the 20-cell
source sweep is no longer on disk, so a re-bake would use a different ensemble
and move every value the basal card grades. That is a separate decision, and the
new `tests/fixtures/population_phenotype_basal/README.md` records it along with
the golden-vs-live distinction.

## Reviewable separately

**`fix(vs_literature)` (eb18dfc) is an independent defect fix — take it or drop
it without touching the rest.** `build()` parameterized `model_json`
(physiology) and read the other four fixtures from the module-level `FIXTURES`
constant, so a caller pointing `report_card_refs.vs_literature` at another
directory got one redirected fixture and four repo copies, silently, and graded
the wrong model side. The fixtures directory now defaults to `model_json`'s own
parent, so the existing call site redirects all five with no change and the
default path is byte-identical. The parametrized regression test fails on all
four non-physiology fixtures without it.

⚠️ `v2ecoli/library/vs_literature.py` is byte-identical in a downstream repo that
syncs from here; it will need a sync pass after this merges. Not done here.

## Open question for @eranagmon — not resolved unilaterally

The cache is the concrete form of an object the framework has no location policy
for: an artifact **derived from a run and consumed by a card**. Run identity and
a run registry already exist (`experiment_id`, `run_registry.register_run`);
what is missing is where a derived, expensive-to-recompute vector should live
between them. This PR builds a local convention rather than extending
`inputs[]` or the readout resolver, on the assumption that the framework-level
answer is yours to make. If there is a direction you'd prefer, this is small
enough to re-aim.

Relatedly: should the workflow runner register a run config the way
`run_condition_multigen_parquet` does? That single change would make
`run_commit` non-null for every future sweep and complete the identity chain
this PR can only half-populate.

## Verification

```bash
pytest -m "not sim"          # 1167 passed, 3 failed
```

The 3 failures (`test_composite_state_coverage`, `test_pack_from_state`,
`test_parquet_emitter_ported::test_expected_failures`) are **pre-existing** —
they fail identically on a clean `origin/main` checkout, verified in a throwaway
worktree. Nothing in this PR touches those areas.

New tests: `tests/test_sim_vector_cache.py` (11 — key composition, hit/miss,
S3 location policy, the two-commit provenance, honest-null behavior) and
`tests/test_model_omics_fixtures.py` (5 — value preservation under re-key, id
vocabulary, and a guard that the transcriptome and proteome keep describing the
same ensemble, since they are produced by different paths and nothing else stops
them drifting).

author: sevmorris
body:
Release preparation for 2.5.0. **Docs only — no version strings, no code.** `release.sh` rewrites version strings itself; this stays out of its way.

### Why this is a PR and not part of the release run

`release.sh` neither writes nor verifies either file:

- A missing or mislabelled **CHANGELOG** entry ships silently — nothing checks it. That is how v2.1.0 shipped with no entry at all.
- A missing **release-notes** file falls through to notes generated from commit subjects (`release.sh:342-349`, finding [#13](https://github.com/sevmorris/WaxOnWaxOff/issues/13)). For this release that fallback would have published 24 internal-sounding commit titles as the public release notes.

Both are written by hand ahead of the cut so neither failure mode can fire.

### CHANGELOG

A `[2.5.0] — 2026-07-30` entry covering the four defects closed in this release (#2, #3, #4, #11) and the #23 phase readout, plus everything else on `main` since v2.4.0 that never carried an entry — the CI toolchain fix, the release gate, the warning-free build, dead-code removal, the twelve restored tags, the dev-docs move, and the documentation corrections.

User-facing groups lead (Diagnostics, Correctness, Interface, Robustness, Documentation); Developer and Structural are separated below. All 24 commits since `v2.4.0` are accounted for.

Dated the local ship day. The UTC clock is past midnight, but every prior entry uses the local date — 2.4.0 is dated 07-23 against a tag created 07-24T03:30Z.

### Release notes

`release-notes/v2.5.0.md`, matching `v2.4.0.md`'s shape — manual link, `###` sections, macOS requirement footer.

It leads with the loudnorm fallback detection, because that closes the *"known gap, shipped deliberately"* the 2.4.0 notes themselves flagged: 2.4.0 documented that the fallback can happen and gave no way to tell whether it had. It also states the CI outage plainly rather than omitting it.

### After this merges

`main` needs one more green push run, then `./release.sh 2.5.0` — run by hand, not from here.

author: davemart-in
body:
## Proposed changes

The foundation for **Newsletter Mode** — an opt-in, focused newsletter workspace in wp-admin. This PR adds only the state and the endpoint that gate it. Nothing in it is reachable by a user; every later piece hangs off these predicates.

**What's here**

* `Mode::is_available()` — the feature gate, a documented filter defaulting to `false`.
* `Mode::is_enabled()` — availability **and** a per-site option. A plain WP option rather than the shared `jetpack/v4/settings` allowlist, deliberately: it has to be readable via `get_option()` before `admin_menu` runs, to drive menu rendering on the same page load.
* `Mode::is_active_for_request()` / `is_mode_surface()` — the request-scoping predicates every later surface gates itself on.
* A package-owned REST route, `jetpack-newsletter/v1/mode`, for reading and writing the flag. Package-owned rather than `jetpack/v4` so persisting it doesn't require registering on the shared settings allowlist.
* `modeAvailable` / `modeEnabled` on the Newsletter page's script data, so the opt-in toggle (a later PR) knows what to render.
* Bootstrap wiring in `load-jetpack.php` **and** in `jetpack-mu-wpcom` — see below.

**It ships dark.** `is_available()` returns `false` and nothing in the monorepo filters it to `true` outside tests, so on merge this changes nothing for anyone. That's what lets the rest of the series land incrementally on trunk.

### Two things worth a reviewer's attention

**1. Newsletter Mode has to be initialized twice.**

`Mode::init()` is called from `load-jetpack.php`, outside the `is_admin()` block because REST requests aren't `is_admin()`. But that file **doesn't run on WordPress.com Simple** — the newsletter classes are present there via the platform's bundled Jetpack source, while the plugin's bootstrap is not.

Without a second entry point, Simple sites would get the settings toggle while `/jetpack-newsletter/v1/mode` and every admin hook stayed unregistered. So this PR adds a `class_exists`-guarded `Mode::init()` to `jetpack-mu-wpcom`, directly beside the existing guarded `Settings::init()` — which carries a comment saying exactly why it's there. That makes this a cross-package PR with its own mu-wpcom changelog and release cadence.

**2. `init()` registers its hooks unconditionally, and should.**

It would be tempting to early-return when `is_available()` is `false`. It mustn't: `load-jetpack.php` runs while plugin files are still being included, so anything registering `jetpack_newsletter_mode_available` later — commonly on `plugins_loaded` — hasn't run yet. An early check would read the default `false`, skip every hook for that request, and make the later filter permanently ineffective. Registration stays unconditional; the gating lives in the callbacks, all of which are inert while the mode is off.

This is one of a series of PRs splitting up #50680 (a proof of concept, not for merge). It is the base the rest of the Newsletter Mode series builds on, so it's the one worth the most scrutiny.

## Related product discussion/links

*

## Does this pull request change what data or activity we track or use?

No. No Tracks events, and no data leaves the site. The PR adds one per-site option (`jetpack_newsletter_mode_enabled`, a boolean defaulting to off) and a REST route that reads and writes it, restricted to users who can `manage_options`.

## Testing instructions

Newsletter Mode is off by default and has no UI in this PR — it's verified through the REST route.

**1. Confirm it's genuinely dark**

* With no changes to your site, request `/wp-json/jetpack-newsletter/v1/mode` as an admin. It should report `available: false` and `enabled: false`.
* Confirm nothing about wp-admin has changed — no new menu items, and Jetpack → Newsletter looks exactly as before.

**2. Turn it on**

Add to an mu-plugin:

```php
add_filter( 'jetpack_newsletter_mode_available', '__return_true' );
```

* `GET /wp-json/jetpack-newsletter/v1/mode` should now report `available: true`, `enabled: false`.
* `POST` to the same route with `{ "enabled": true }`. It should persist — re-request and confirm `enabled: true`, and check the `jetpack_newsletter_mode_enabled` option.
* There should still be no visible change in wp-admin. The surfaces that react to this flag arrive in later PRs.

**3. Permissions**

* As a subscriber-level user, both the GET and the POST should be refused.

**4. WordPress.com Simple** (the reason for the mu-wpcom change)

* On a Simple sandbox, confirm `/jetpack-newsletter/v1/mode` responds at all. Before this PR it would not have — `load-jetpack.php` doesn't run there. This is the one path with no automated coverage, so it's worth doing by hand.

**5. Automated**

```
jp test php packages/newsletter        # 58 tests
jp test php packages/jetpack-mu-wpcom  # 847 tests
jp phan packages/newsletter
jp phan packages/jetpack-mu-wpcom
jp phan plugins/jetpack
```

author: ahngbeom
body:
Closes #7. **Stacked on #18 → #17 → #16.**

## The problem

The row count on the status bar came from the result buffer, and a write fills
nothing, so every `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` reported `0 rows` whatever it did.

The guard stops the user, explains what the statement will do, and makes them
type the word. Then it ran it and did not say what happened. `1 row affected`
versus `4812 rows affected` is the difference between a routine edit and an
incident — and it was the one number missing, so every write had to be
followed by a hand-written `SELECT` to check.

## The trap this avoids

`Conn.Exec` already existed and already returned the count. Using it would
have been two lines — and would have **silently cost server-side
cancellation**: `Exec` goes through `pool.ExecContext`, which takes a
connection without reading its id, so `KILL QUERY` would have had nothing to
aim at. A runaway `UPDATE` is precisely the statement a user most needs to
stop, so trading that for a number is backwards.

The exec path therefore lives inside `Stream.run`, on the connection whose id
was already read for `KILL QUERY`, after the same schema handling:

```go
if opt.Exec {
    s.done(s.exec(conn, query), false)
    return
}
```

`TestAWriteIsStillKilledOnTheServerWhenCancelled` kills a write mid-flight and
checks `information_schema.PROCESSLIST` — the same guarantee the `SELECT` path
has always had. Rerouting `exec` through the pool fails it.

## Decisions worth reviewing

- **The path is chosen from `StmtKind`, before sending.** It cannot be decided
  afterwards: a write sent as a query yields a result set with no columns and
  the count is gone. `StmtKind.ReturnsRows()` is the rule.
- **Anything not definitely a write is sent as a query.** `CALL` can return
  rows, and losing them is worse than the empty result set a count-less query
  costs. The uncertain case goes the way that cannot lose anything.
- **`Result()` is read after `Events` closes,** like `Err` and `Truncated`, for
  the reason already documented on `Event`: a terminal event can be dropped
  when a cancelled stream closes.
- **The singular is spelled out.** "1 rows affected" reads as a bug in the
  count itself, and this number is read in a hurry.
- **"affected", not "matched".** MySQL counts rows *changed*, so an `UPDATE`
  setting a column to the value it already held reports zero. That is the
  server's own answer; the wording is chosen so it cannot be taken for the
  other number. Documented in the README.

## Verification

`make lint`, `make test`, `go test -race -tags integration ./internal/...`
clean on this branch. Four new integration tests in `internal/db` and one
end-to-end on the simulation screen. Three mutations checked: routing exec
through the pool, forcing `Exec: false`, and both fail as they should.

Next: #8 reads `SHOW WARNINGS` on the same connection, which is only possible
because this change keeps holding it.

author: kadragon
body:
## Problem

`preflight.sh` reported `agy_available=false` on every Windows/Git Bash run, so Step 2-2 of `task-review` was silently skipped there — the review panel ran with Claude + Codex only, never agy. The gate was unconditional on `MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*`, so no amount of agy setup or authentication could turn it on.

The stated reason was that `agy.exe` wrote through the Windows console API (text_drip renderer) instead of stdout, making `agy ... | tee` in `agy-review.sh` capture nothing.

## Reproduction / verification

On agy 1.1.8, MINGW64 (Windows 11), the premise no longer holds:

```
$ NO_COLOR=1 TERM=dumb agy -p "Reply with exactly: PIPE_OK" > out.txt
exit=0, 8 bytes, "PIPE_OK"

$ NO_COLOR=1 TERM=dumb agy -p "Reply with exactly: TEE_OK" 2>err | tee out.txt   # agy-review.sh's own shape
pipestatus=0 0, 7 bytes, "TEE_OK"
```

After the patch, `preflight.sh --no-hub` on the same machine reports `"agy_available": true`.

## Change

Drop the platform gate. No runtime probe replaces it: a probe would cost an API round trip on every preflight, and `agy-review.sh` already fails closed — it exits 1 with the captured stderr on empty output, and again on non-zero exit with partial output, which `SKILL.md` turns into `{"agy_review":"failed"}`. A regression is caught there, at the point where it actually matters.

- `dev/skills/task-review/scripts/preflight.sh` — remove the `uname -s` case, replace the stale comment with the verified state
- `dev` plugin `4.0.20 → 4.0.21` (patch: modify), both platform manifests
- CHANGELOG entry under `## Unreleased`

author: cpunion
body:
## Summary

Merge `xgo-dev/main` through `ab2fe9c81523` into the private `llvm-coro` integration branch.

The merge preserves the stackless coroutine architecture while adapting the new upstream runtime-locality, panic/caller, standard `sync.Pool`, LLDB, and GOROOT-test changes:

- keep physical pthread `getg` bootstrap separate from logical GLS state;
- make locality classification owner-aware and retain coroutine logical-locality lowering;
- capture panic PCs in a synchronous core C leaf without dynamic funcval dispatch or retaining native frame pointers across safepoints;
- keep standard-library `sync.Pool` layout via callback-free `tls.StaticHandle`;

author: patel-om
body:
Two things: an end-to-end quality suite that found six real defects, and the persistence/email layers wired to activate on credentials. ## 1. Accessibility & E2E suite 41 Playwright checks across desktop and a **Pixel 7** profile, run against the **production build** — a dev-server audit misses minification, real hydration timing, and the actual shipped CSS. **Zero axe violations** on WCAG 2.1 A/AA. ### Six real defects it caught | # | Defect | Why it was missed | |---|---|---| | 1 | `--pillar-peach` was **4.19:1** on the peach tint it actually sits on | I verified every accent against *paper*, never against the tinted card it's used on | | 2 | `--ink-subtle` failed on two tints (**4.34** mint, **4.45** sky) while passing on paper (4.95) | Same class of mistake | | 3 | Game Corner band used `bg-ink`/`text-paper`, which **inverts in dark mode** — the dark band became light and its yellow accent dropped to **1.41:1** | Dark mode was never audited | | 4 | CTA band's yellow accent hit **1.28:1** in dark mode | Same root cause | | 5 | The `
` of impact figures nested Reveal's div inside another div and put detail text in a `

`, **breaking the dt/dd association** | Invisible on screen — the figures were simply unreadable as a definition list | | 6 | Rate limiting bucketed every unidentifiable client under one `"unknown"` key | A missing `x-forwarded-for` would have put **all anonymous visitors on a shared 5/hour limit**. Found when the sixth submission of a test run started failing | Added `--band-dark` / `--band-brand` — fixed across both themes on purpose, because a band whose whole job is to interrupt the page rhythm must not flip with the theme. ### Mobile navigation now works without JavaScript The hamburger was a React `onClick`, so with JS disabled **mobile visitors could not navigate from the header at all** — and mobile is most of our teacher and parent traffic. It's now `

`/``: opens natively with no JS, and brings correct keyboard and screen-reader semantics with it. ### What the suite actually asserts - Zero axe violations on 11 route types, light **and** dark, plus the open mega-menu and mobile sheet - Skip link is the first focusable element and is visible on focus - Focus indicator present on every element in a 25-stop tab walk - Mega-menu opens on Enter, closes on Escape, **and returns focus to its trigger** - **Journey J1 end-to-end with keyboard only** — a principal books a demo without a mouse - Validation errors are tied via `aria-describedby` and say *how to fix it* - With JavaScript disabled: content is visible, counters show real values, and **the enquiry form still submits and reports success** One harness detail worth noting: axe was sampling elements mid-reveal-transition and reading *blended* colours, producing contrast failures no user ever sees. `settlePage()` drives every reveal to its final state first — those were artefacts, and "fixing" them would have meant changing colours that were already correct. ## 2. Persistence & email Both activate on credentials with **no code change**. - **Prisma 7** schema for leads, notes, demo bookings, rate-limit buckets. Prisma 7 moved connection URLs out of `schema.prisma`, so they're in `prisma.config.ts` with the `pg` driver adapter at runtime. - Migrations prefer `DIRECT_DATABASE_URL` — running them through a pooler makes advisory locks fail intermittently and leaves a half-applied migration behind. - A school-demo lead and its booking are created in **one transaction**, so a demo lead can never exist without a booking row. - Consent is timestamped **only when actually given**. - Email is fire-and-forget and non-throwing: the enquiry is already stored, so a provider outage must never fail a completed submission. `replyTo` is the enquirer, so hitting reply in the inbox reaches them. **Deliberately not built:** the architecture doc also specifies users, resource downloads, newsletter and AI telemetry tables. Those land with the features that need them — an unused table is a migration you maintain for nothing. ## Still true after this PR **Enquiries cannot be stored in production until `DATABASE_URL` is set.** The form surfaces the phone number rather than reporting a false success. `LEAD_STORE=file` exists as an explicit opt-in for E2E and staging — deliberately opt-in, because as a *fallback* a mistyped connection string would silently write enquiries to a disk that vanishes on the next deploy. ## To activate ```bash # Postgres (Neon or Supabase) DATABASE_URL=... DIRECT_DATABASE_URL=... npx prisma migrate deploy # Email RESEND_API_KEY=... LEAD_NOTIFY_TO=... ``` `.env.example` documents every variable and what it switches on. The README now states the honest status of each capability. ## Gates TypeScript strict clean · ESLint clean · 29 unit tests · 41 E2E checks · production build clean. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: piyushdaiya
body:
Fix #8: matcher no longer defeated by zero-width space, punctuation noise, or token reordering

internal/matcherbaseline/normalize.go:
- fold() now deletes Unicode format characters (category Cf: zero-width
  space/joiner/non-joiner, byte-order mark, RTL/LTR override characters)
  instead of turning them into a token-separating space. Previously a
  single invisible U+200B character split one word into two tokens.
- fold() now also deletes period and apostrophe outright rather than
  treating them as separators, so "A.C.M.E." folds to "ACME" (one
  token) instead of "A C M E" (four), and "O'Brien"-style names fold
  correctly. Other punctuation (hyphen, comma, slash, ampersand,
  underscore, colon, semicolon) is deliberately left as a separator,
  since those more often do separate genuinely distinct words.

internal/matcherbaseline/similarity.go:
- Added bestEditSimilarity(): takes the max of the raw whole-string edit
  similarity and an edit similarity computed on token-sorted renderings
  of the same two strings. token_alignment_similarity already scores
  pure token reordering as a perfect match (each token has an exact best
  match somewhere in the other list, regardless of position) - that's
  existing, deliberate behavior. But raw edit_similarity is
  order-sensitive, so it was fighting that decision instead of agreeing
  with it. This change stops edit_similarity from re-penalizing token
  order once token_alignment_similarity has already decided it isn't
  meaningful for a name match.
- Accepted trade-off (documented in the code): this means two entities
  whose names are literally the same words in a different order aren't
  distinguishable by word order alone under this matcher. That
  trade-off already existed via token_alignment_similarity's weight;
  this change extends consistency to a second feature that was
  previously fighting it, rather than introducing a new decision.

test/fixtures/adversarial/: known_status updated to "pass" for the 3
scenarios this fixes (obfuscation-04-zero-width-space,
obfuscation-05-punctuation-noise, obfuscation-06-token-reorder),
locking them in as regression guards per the design in
internal/adversarialtest/adversarial_test.go.

Verified: all 3 targeted scenarios now score above the party_name_r1
threshold (7800bp); full 54-package test suite passes with zero
regressions. Entity-suffix-swap (GmbH -> Ltd, related but distinct -
see issue #11) was checked and confirmed still failing (scores 7346bp,
just below threshold) - NOT fixed by this change, left as-is on purpose
rather than folded in silently.

Closes #8

author: vitorpamplona
body:
## The bug

Vespa validates every `type string` field and rejects the whole document when one carries a code point outside its character set:

```
Status 400 … Could not parse field 'about' of type string:
The string field value contains illegal code point 0xB
```

Nostr has no such rule, so these arrive from the network continuously. Observed in mirrored kind-0s: `0x1, 0x3, 0xB, 0x10, 0x14, 0x16, 0x1C` — in `name`, `display_name` and `about`. Not all of it is junk: a Bluesky bridge uses `0xB` (vertical tab) as a line separator in ordinary bios.

Uncaught, it surfaces as a feed exception from the middle of a bulk write and costs **every event batched beside it**. Settled in stage A with the other no-I/O checks, it is one ordinary counted rejection — and the round trip is saved.

## Why not sanitize

The derived search fields (`name`, `about`, …) are lossy already and could be scrubbed. `content` and `tags` cannot: they are the event *verbatim*, and the signature covers them byte for byte. A stored event that fails its own signature check is worse than one not stored.

I verified against a live engine that `content` carries the same restriction, so scrubbing only the search fields would move the failure one field along rather than fix it. Storing the verbatim event in a `raw` field would lift the restriction entirely — until then, rejection is the honest outcome.

## The rule was measured, not inferred

Reasoning from "Vespa validates XML 1.0" is wrong in the direction that **silently drops storable events**. Checked against a running engine, code point by code point:

| code point | XML 1.0 | Vespa actually |
|---|---|---|
| `0x7F` DEL | illegal | **accepts** |
| `0x80`–`0x9F` C1 | illegal | **accepts** |
| `0xFDEF` | noncharacter | **accepts** |

So the real rule is: C0 except tab/LF/CR, the `U+FDD0–FDDF` block only, and `U+xFFFE`/`U+xFFFF` per plane. Mojibake'd Latin-1 lands in the C1 range constantly, so the spec-derived version would have cost real profiles. Both boundaries are pinned by test (`FDCF` and `FDE0` both store).

## Notes

- One constant rejection reason rather than one per field or code point: callers tally by reason, and a per-event reason fragments that tally into thousands of singletons instead of naming the class once.
- The check is added to both the bulk and per-event paths, since `Rejections` is documented as shared "so the two can never drift".
- 10 tests, including the real Bluesky-bridge profile and a batch case asserting one bad event does not cost the other five.

author: eightynine01
body:
## 문제

`--collector.systemd` 를 `extraFlags` 로 켜도 `/run/systemd/private` 소켓이 파드에 없어 collector 가 **매 스크레이프 실패**하고 `node_systemd_*` 9 family 가 통째로 빠지고 있었다.

```
ERROR collector failed name=systemd
err="couldn't get dbus connection: dial unix /run/systemd/private: connect: no such file or directory"
```

**조용한 손실이었다** — `/metrics` 는 200 을 계속 주고 나머지 348 family 는 멀쩡해서, 로그를 보지 않으면 "켰으니 나오겠지"로 넘어간다.

## 라이브 실측 (e21, upstream node_exporter 1.12.1 동시 기동)

| | family | series |
|---|---|---|
| upstream node_exporter 1.12.1 | 359 | **7,034** |
| nodevitals 0.8.3 | 349 | **5,441** |
| **차이** | 10 | **1,593** |

차이의 정체: `node_systemd_*` 9 family / **1,591 시리즈** + `node_exporter_build_info`(익스포터 자체 메타라 대상 아님).

## 수정

`nodeExporter.mountSystemd`(기본 `false`)로 `/run/systemd` 를 read-only 마운트.

- **hostPath type 은 `Directory`** (`DirectoryOrCreate` 아님) — systemd 없는 노드에 빈 디렉터리를 만들어 붙이면 collector 가 등록만 되고 매 스크레이프 실패하는, 이 마운트가 막으려는 바로 그 상태가 재현된다.
- **기본 false** — 호스트 init 시스템 표면을 컨테이너에 여는 일이라 `--collector.systemd` 를 실제로 켠 배포만 opt-in.
- **readOnly: true** — unix 소켓 `connect()` 는 파일 쓰기가 아니라 read-only bind mount 에서도 동작한다.

## 검증

- `helm lint` — 0 chart(s) failed
- `helm template` — `mountSystemd=true` 시 mountPath/hostPath 양쪽 렌더, 기본값에서는 출현 0
- `deploy/chart/tests/tier-runtime.sh` — PASS (마운트 렌더 + 기본값 미출현 2 케이스 추가)

author: tolanicorp
body:
## Purpose
Integrate TaskStaff into TCCG as the governed **Work Execution & Workforce Readiness Plane** for construction staffing while preserving TCCG authority for project execution, safety, quality, contracts, finance, commissioning and owner acceptance.

TaskStaff workforce capability PR #68 and synthetic Staffing Execution Canary v1 PR #69 are merged. **Canary v1.1 — Signed Staging + Construction Adapter Sandbox** is now implemented across TaskStaff PR #70 and TolaniCorp-HQ PR #74, but the live transaction remains fail-closed on missing external sandbox identities.

## Construction workforce plane
- preserves `.taskstaff/adoption.json` and PermitOps evaluation artifacts;
- maps all 14 TCCG `AG-*` prototypes to TaskStaff TAPF construction-agent IDs;
- provides assignment recommendation, credential readiness, availability matching, backup coverage and training-gap routing;
- preserves required human PM/superintendent/Safety/QC/design/financial/commissioning/owner-acceptance authority;
- defines the 12-stage staffing lifecycle and staffing KPI/readiness gates.

## Canary v1 — complete
Synthetic Canary v1 proved the full staffing control path, including PM/Safety/QC failures, actor revocation, training-gap routing, cost/capacity controls, all 14 phase activations, readiness/work evidence, Z4 preview evaluation and Tolani Labs feedback. TaskStaff PR #69 is merged.

## Canary v1.1 — implemented to the external identity gate
Target transaction:

`TaskStaff staging deploy → HQ Ed25519 signed receipt → actual HTTP/MCP request → request-digest and tenant/mission binding → replay rejection → revoked-actor API rejection → Autodesk read-only project mapping → Primavera read-only project/schedule mapping → provider write denial before network → R2 linked audit evidence → human-only / AI-assisted / hybrid-team readiness comparison`.

TaskStaff preview capability:
- capability: `taskstaff.tccg-staffing.canary.v1-1.run`
- scope: `taskstaff:tccg-staffing:canary:v1-1:run`
- path: `/v1/enterprise-preview/tccg-staffing/canary-v1-1`
- scenarios: `baseline`, `revoked-actor`
- staging only; production authority false.

## TaskStaff v1.1 evidence
TaskStaff PR #70 final validated head: `337df06563ae566d4e9a8251425f10ade4e9fcd0`.

- Dependency Review #410: **PASS**
- CI and Controlled Deploy #461: **PASS**
- staging gate repository/API validation: **PASS**
- API tests: **38/38 PASS**
- Cloudflare staging authority: **PRESENT**
- actual `taskstaff-api-staging` Worker secret inventory: **INSPECTED**
- TCCG Staffing Canary v1.1 Staging run #7: **BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_IDENTITY**
- staging deployment: **NOT PERFORMED**
- Autodesk/Primavera provider egress: **NOT PERFORMED**
- production deployment: **NOT PERFORMED**

Sanitized blocker evidence:
- workflow run ID: `32428158962`
- artifact ID: `9428152785`
- artifact SHA-256: `b82d457e9db831b734c297854307c88bc174ee0960c994211820a4c5d4c9a7e8`

The staging Worker and protected GitHub staging fallback both lack:
- `AUTODESK_CANARY_ACCESS_TOKEN`
- `AUTODESK_CANARY_HUB_ID`
- `AUTODESK_CANARY_PROJECT_ID`
- `PRIMAVERA_CANARY_BASE_URL`
- `PRIMAVERA_CANARY_ACCESS_TOKEN`
- `PRIMAVERA_CANARY_PROJECT_ID`

## HQ authority plane
TolaniCorp-HQ PR #74 registers v1.1 in the enterprise capability registry and normal Preview MCP gateway. HQ remains the Ed25519 private signer; TaskStaff remains the public-key verifier.

The HQ branch has a READY Vercel Preview deployment for the v1.1 gateway/status code. GitHub Actions `Preview` does not contain `ENTERPRISE_PREVIEW_PRIVATE_KEY_PKCS8_B64`, so the direct CI acceptance harness fails closed before issuing a receipt. The deployed Vercel Preview signer may have its own Preview environment key, but its secret-presence status could not be read through deployment protection in the current execution context; therefore it is recorded as **UNVERIFIED**, not absent.

## Adapter security boundary
- provider credentials are server/Worker-side only and never accepted through MCP input;
- Autodesk origin is fixed to APS and reads the configured project only;
- Primavera origin must be HTTPS on an approved Oracle Cloud hostname and performs project/activity GET reads only;
- provider payloads are bounded and reduced to mapping metadata and SHA-256 digests;
- mutating methods are denied before `fetch()` and evidence records `networkRequestPerformed:false`;
- raw provider payloads and credentials are not retained.

## Staffing comparison
The v1.1 benchmark is a readiness/control comparison, not a productivity or ROI claim:
- human-only: expected `NOT_READY` because required AI capability coverage is absent;
- AI-assisted without critical high-risk backups: expected `NOT_READY`;
- complete governed hybrid team: expected `READY`.

## Rerun order
1. provision the six TaskStaff staging Autodesk/Primavera sandbox bindings;
2. rerun TaskStaff PR #70 `TCCG Staffing Canary v1.1 Staging`;
3. require staging deploy, health smoke and real provider mapping PASS;
4. use the deployed HQ Preview gateway signer if its Preview signing key/scope is confirmed, otherwise restore/provision the HQ Preview Ed25519 signer paired to the TaskStaff verifier;
5. rerun HQ PR #74 signed acceptance or invoke the authenticated HQ Preview gateway;
6. require real receipt issuance, HTTP/MCP success, digest/context binding, replay rejection, revoked-actor denial, read-only mapping, write-denial, audit-root and staffing benchmark PASS;
7. record final immutable evidence IDs/audit root here;
8. keep real TCCG project activation disabled until explicit Canary v2 authorization.

## Production posture
**NO-GO for a real TCCG project.** Canary v1.1 code and CI are implemented, but no live signed Autodesk/Primavera transaction has completed. No production deployment or provider write authority is authorized.

**F-040**: a pure `agent_core.store_sync.soak_progress(records, target)` summary over the
merge-gate outcome store, plus an opt-in `stats --soak-target N` CLI flag that adds a
reserved `_soak` JSON block. Makes progress toward the ADR 0005 soak-enablement bar
observable without touching the gate itself (no TCB edit, no store mutation, no schema bump).

Only the ledger files (`CHANGELOG.md`, `NEXT_STEPS.md`, `features.yaml`, `progress.md`,
`agent-core/tests/public_surface_baseline.json`) conflicted with main — the code itself
merged clean. Conflicts resolved by hand / by regenerating the baseline.

This PR closes #43.

## What's new

- `store_sync/store.py`: `soak_progress()` — total/pending/labeled, HUMAN_AUDIT count
  (the only label source that feeds tau/health), per-domain cold-start flags (keyed on
  `AuditConfig.per_domain_floor`, config-driven), n-vs-target shortfall, merge velocity
  (records/day), days-to-target.
- `store_sync/__init__.py`: `stats --soak-target N` (opt-in; bare `stats` output stays
  byte-identical) and `--audit-floor N` (see hardening below).
- `scripts/validations/F_040.py`: offline structural validator (17 checks).
- `agent-core/tests/test_store_sync.py`: +12 tests for the soak/stats surface.

## Hardening applied during this rebase

An independent `feature-dev:code-reviewer` subagent audit (adversarial, diffed against
main) found two real defects in the original branch's code, both reproduced before fixing:

1. **Critical — `_parse_ts` reimplemented ISO-8601 parsing** instead of reusing the
   project's existing `agent_core.timeutil.parse_iso8601` (already used by
   `outcome_labeller.py` for this same `merged_at` field). A bare `datetime.fromisoformat`
   call (a) silently drops Z-suffixed timestamps on Python 3.10 — this repo's CI version —
   since Z-suffix support was added in 3.11, and (b) **crashes the entire `stats
   --soak-target` invocation** (`TypeError`, exit 1, no output) if the store contains a
   naive timestamp alongside an aware one, since `OutcomeRecord.merged_at` is an
   unvalidated free-form string end-to-end. Fixed by delegating to `parse_iso8601`;
   both failure modes are now regression-tested.
2. **Important — the soak report's cold-start floor didn't match the live operational
   floor.** `AuditConfig.per_domain_floor` defaults to 30, but the actual
   `merge-gate-audit.yml` workflow runs with a lower floor (`vars.MERGE_GATE_AUDIT_FLOOR`,
   typically 3) specifically because 30 "would select nearly every record per domain in
   the early low-volume regime." The stats CLI had no way to pass a matching value, so
   `per_domain_cold_start` would over-report cold-start by ~10x relative to what audit
   selection actually enforces. Fixed by adding `--audit-floor` (default unchanged).
3. **Minor** — a duplicate `## Session 012` heading (main had already used that number)
   and a stale "N≥20 is the soak bar" claim (the doc's own corrected framing, a few
   sections below, already established the real bar at ~380 audited records/domain) —
   both were being reintroduced by the rebase. Corrected in `progress.md`,
   `NEXT_STEPS.md`, and `features.yaml`.

## Verification

- `python scripts/validations/F_040.py` → 17/17 checks pass
- `python scripts/validate.py --tier fast` → 45/45 done-status features pass
- `agent-core/tests/test_store_sync.py`: 51 tests pass (real-git push/pull included, no mocks)
- `store.py` and `store_sync/__init__.py`: 100% branch coverage; package-wide 98.7%
  (only the pre-existing, untouched `__main__.py` shim is uncovered)
- Full `agent-core` suite: no regressions
- `ruff check` + `mypy --strict`: clean
- `agent-core/tests/test_public_surface.py`: passes (regenerated baseline correctly adds
  `soak_progress`)
- **Live smoke test** against `origin/merge-gate-data` (64 real records, 0 human_audit):
  `stats --soak-target 380 --audit-floor 3` → `shortfall=316, velocity_per_day≈2.4,
  days_to_target≈131.5`, all domains correctly still cold-start
- Bare `stats` (no flags) confirmed byte-identical against the same live store

## Notes for reviewers

- `agent-core/tests/**`, `features.yaml`, `scripts/validations/**` are protected paths —
  this PR needs the `eval-change-approved` label.
- Soak enablement itself remains time-gated per ADR 0005 (~380 near-perfect audited
  records/domain, not the old N≥20 framing) — this PR only makes progress observable.
- `AGENTS.md:71` in this worktree carries a pre-existing orphan merge-conflict marker
  inherited from `main` (unrelated to this branch — already fixed pending in #111, not
  yet merged). Out of scope here to avoid conflicting with that PR.

body:
> Reemplaza al #20, que GitHub cerró automáticamente al borrarse su rama base (`docs/rama-master-y-vercel`) tras mergear #19. Mismo contenido, rebasado sobre `master`.

## Lo que pediste

El SMTP deja de ser variable de entorno. Se configura por negocio desde una sección nueva **"Servidor de correo (SMTP)"** en Configuración del Negocio: servidor, puerto, tipo de cifrado, usuario, contraseña y nombre del remitente.

## Lo que encontré por el camino

Guardarlo en `cfg_negocio`, donde vive el resto de la configuración, habría sido un agujero:

```sql
create policy cfg_negocio_lectura_publica on comun_configuracion.cfg_negocio
  for select using (true);
```

con `grant select` a `anon`. Es información de vitrina, pública a propósito. La contraseña SMTP ahí —o en su JSONB de detalle— habría quedado legible desde internet. Por eso hay tabla aparte, `cfg_smtp`, sin lectura pública.

## Dónde acaba la contraseña

En **Supabase Vault** (ya instalado, v0.3.1). En la tabla solo queda su `uuid`.

Consecuencia deliberada: **nadie puede volver a leerla, ni el administrador que la escribió.** La pantalla solo indica si existe; el campo vacío significa "consérvala" y hay un botón aparte para eliminarla. Una credencial que la UI puede volver a mostrar es una credencial que se puede exfiltrar desde la UI.

## Por qué aparece una Edge Function

No es sobreingeniería, es la única salida:

- La contraseña solo la descifra `cfg_fn_obtener_smtp_credenciales()`, con `execute` concedido **solo** a `service_role`.
- El correo más crítico es el OTP de registro, y ese flujo es **anónimo**: el usuario aún no tiene sesión.
- Abrirla a `authenticated` la daría a cualquier usuario con cuenta; a `anon` —necesario para el registro— la daría a internet entera.
- Luego el envío tiene que ocurrir donde vive `service_role`, que por regla propia del repo es exclusivamente una Edge Function.

`enviar-correo` se autentica con el secreto compartido `CORREO_FUNCION_CLAVE`, comparado en tiempo constante, porque en el registro no hay JWT. **Riesgo residual documentado en el ADR:** quien obtenga ese secreto puede enviar HTML arbitrario desde el buzón del negocio. La mejora que lo cierra cabe después sin rehacer nada.

## Otros cambios de comportamiento

- `enviarCorreo()` exige `negocio` y devuelve resultado. Antes un fallo se perdía en silencio; ahora el registro avisa de que la cuenta se creó pero el código no salió. `solicitarRecuperacion()` sigue ignorándolo a propósito: su respuesta debe ser idéntica exista o no la cuenta.
- `smt_activo` es independiente de "está configurado", y activar exige host, usuario y contraseña — comprobado contra la fila real, no contra lo que diga el formulario.
- **Mientras un negocio no configure su SMTP, no envía correo.** No hay remitente compartido de respaldo.

## Verificación

Pipeline completo con caché desactivada, en el mismo orden que CI:

| Paso | Resultado |
| :--- | :--- |
| `lint` | 4/4 — 0 errores |
| `typecheck` | 12/12 |
| `test` | 1/1 |
| `build` | 4/4 |
| `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` | sin hallazgos |
| Sección renderizada en navegador | Puerto 465 por defecto, cifrado marcado, contraseña `type=password` con `autocomplete=new-password`, sin desborde horizontal |
| Validación "activar sin host" | `"Indica el servidor (host) antes de activar el envío."` — probado contra la Server Action real |

**No verificado, necesita despliegue:** el envío real y la Edge Function.

## Orden de despliegue

El correo no funciona entre el paso 1 y el 4:

1. Aplicar la migración `20260730000006_cfg_smtp_por_negocio.sql`.
2. Regenerar tipos con `supabase gen types` — los de este PR están escritos a mano porque la migración aún no estaba aplicada.
3. Desplegar la función con `--no-verify-jwt` y cargarle `CORREO_FUNCION_CLAVE`.
4. Cargar el mismo valor en Vercel y retirar las `SMTP_*`.
5. Configurar el SMTP de cada negocio desde su consola y activarlo.

Docs: ADR-0005 nuevo, `PLT-008` regla 6 con criterios Gherkin, política de credenciales, estándar de despliegue y README de `supabase/functions` y del paquete.
