author: chazmaniandinkle
body:
## What and why

`process: observer surprise` was firing at `error=1.0000` every consolidation cycle, permanently. The sprint triage summary described this as needing "a Jaccard empty-set guard," but that's not quite the mechanism -- see How below for what the code actually does and where the fix lands.

Fixes #428

## How

The sprint summary's framing ("`jaccardDistance` has no one-sided-empty guard") is true as a description of `jaccardDistance`, but that function's one-sided-empty behavior is intentional and documented (`observer.go:227-230`): `1 - |A∩B|/|A∪B|` for an empty vs. non-empty set is standard Jaccard distance, and it's correct in the one case where a real attendedSet legitimately diverges from an empty lastPrediction (e.g. right after a model reset). I left `jaccardDistance` itself untouched.

The actual defect is one level up, in `TrajectoryModel.Update` (`observer.go:113`): `attendedSet` is built from `readRecentAttentionSignals`, which reads `.cog/run/attention.jsonl` -- a file nothing has appended to since 2026-05-12 because the external attention-signal producer (the "Phase 3 OMZ plugin" named in `serve_attention.go:3-9`) isn't wired in this deployment. So `attendedSet` is structurally empty every cycle, not occasionally empty. From the first cycle that populates `lastPrediction` from field scores onward, `jaccardDistance(nonEmptyPrediction, emptyAttendedSet)` returns its documented `1.0` -- a real total-miss value, correctly computed, over a comparison that has no evidence behind it. That value isn't just logged: it's written into the hash-chained ledger (`observer.prediction` event, `process.go:743`), the `consolidation.complete` event, and the per-cycle CogDoc (`writeConsolidationDoc`), so fixing only the WARN-log emission in `process.go` would have left the ledger permanently poisoned with false surprise data.

Fix: guard on `len(attendedSet) > 0` at the call site in `Update()` before invoking `jaccardDistance` at all. No attention data this cycle means no measurement, not a maximal miss, so `predErr` stays `0.0` in that case. This only changes the one production-triggering branch (attendedSet empty, lastPrediction non-empty); the both-empty case already returned 0 and is unaffected, and the reverse case (lastPrediction empty, attendedSet non-empty -- a real early-model total miss) still computes the true Jaccard distance exactly as before.

## Class sweep

Per the runbook: grepped for the shape of what changed -- similarity/ratio computations that divide by or compare against a possibly-empty set.

| Site | Disposition | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/engine/observer.go` `jaccardDistance` / `TrajectoryModel.Update` | **Covered (this PR)** | The actual #428 defect |
| `internal/engine/benchmark.go:143` `matchScore` (recall/precision) | Not applicable | Already guards both `len(expected)==0` and `len(injected)==0` explicitly, returning sentinel values for each |
| `internal/engine/reconcile_daemon.go:265` `LastCoherence` (`cB = 1 - driftSum/len(types)`) | Not applicable | `types` is derived from `snapshot`, and `len(snapshot)==0` returns early (`:222`) before `types` is ever built, so the division is unreachable with an empty divisor. Per-provider `driftFraction` also already special-cases `Total()==0` (comment cites IMPL-SPEC B2, blind-review-1) |
| `internal/engine/proprioceptive.go:104` `ComputeEntry` (`delta = hits/len(predicted)`) | Not applicable | Already guarded with `if len(predicted) > 0` |
| `internal/engine/context_assembly.go:1078` `messageRelevance` | Not applicable | Already guards `len(keywords)==0` |
| `internal/engine/context_assembly.go:1150` `queryRelevance` | Not applicable | Same guard, same file |
| `internal/engine/trm_index.go:167` `cosineSim` | Not applicable | Already guards `denom==0` (zero-vector case) |
| `pkg/cogdoc_review/similarity.go:140` `cosineSimilarity` | Not applicable | Dot product of pre-normalized vectors only, no division, no empty-set ratio |
| `internal/testkernel/experiment/calibration.go:117,132` `mean`/`cv` | Not applicable | `mean` guards `len(xs)==0`; `cv` calls `mean` first and returns early on `m==0` before the `variance := sumSq/len(values)` division, so an empty slice never reaches it |

Everything else this class of bug could plausibly hide in was already guarded at the time this defect was filed. `observer.go` was the one miss.

## Acceptance

- [x] Root cause identified and confirmed against current code (not just the sprint summary)
- [x] Fix lands at the point where `predErr` first goes bad, not just at the log/emit call site, since the value is recorded into the ledger every cycle
- [x] Test pins the degenerate case (`TestTrajectoryModelNoAttentionSignalIsNotSurprise`): repeated empty-attendance cycles after a prediction is populated must yield `PredictionError=0.0` and `MeanError=0.0`, not `1.0`
- [x] `jaccardDistance`'s own documented semantics and existing test (`a empty b non-empty -> 1.0`) are unchanged
- [x] Class sweep of sibling ratio/similarity computations dividing by a possibly-empty set (table above)

## Test evidence

```
go build ./...                                   # clean
go vet ./...                                     # clean
go test ./internal/engine/... -race              # ok, 36.3s (full package, includes new test)
go test ./internal/engine/... -run 'TestJaccard|TestTrajectoryModel|TestApplyObserverActions|TestWriteConsolidationDoc' -race -v
  --- PASS: TestTrajectoryModelNoAttentionSignalIsNotSurprise (0.00s)
  --- PASS: TestJaccardDistance (+ 5 subtests, unchanged)
  --- PASS: TestTrajectoryModelFirstCycleEmptyAll
  --- PASS: TestTrajectoryModelStatsAccumulate
  ... (all existing observer tests pass unmodified)
```

author: chaowao
body:
## The leak

**#1605** changes three files, all under `examples/workers/l3/` — two READMEs and one `main.py`. What ran:

```
ut / ut-a2a3 / ut-a5          skipping    ← category axis working
st-sim-* / st-onboard-*       running     ← correct
packaging-matrix ×2           running     ← ~9 min each, cannot be affected
profiling-flags-smoke         running     ← ~11 min, cannot be affected
```

## Why those two are different from every other job

They are the only jobs that **build and install the product and then exercise it with a fixed, tiny payload**, rather than reading a test suite as a corpus:

| Job | What it actually runs |
| --- | --------------------- |
| `packaging-matrix` | `tools/verify_packaging.sh` — import surface plus one entry-point script |
| `profiling-flags-smoke` | rebuilds the runtimes under six `CXX` define permutations, runs one `vector_example` |

Nothing under `examples/` reaches either: it is absent from `wheel.packages` **and** from the sdist `include`, and neither job opens it.

So they take a fourth flag, `examples_only`, in the same shape as the arch and category axes with `NON_CODE` subtracted first. `profiling-flags-smoke` also moves off `st_affected`, which was never the right question for it — its inputs are `src/` and the build system, not the scene-test corpus.

## What deliberately stays in

**`tests/` still triggers packaging.** `verify_packaging.sh` runs

```bash
python tests/st/a2a3/.../paged_attention_unroll/test_paged_attention_unroll.py --help
```

as its entry-point smoke, and `tests/` is in the sdist `include` (`pyproject.toml:64`; only `tests/st` is excluded, and only from the wheel). Just `examples/` is provably absent from both jobs, so just `examples/` is subtracted — the narrow cut, not the convenient one.

**One consequence worth naming:** a change confined to `examples/{arch}/.../vector_example/` now skips the profiling smoke. Acceptable — `st-sim-*` and `st-onboard-*` run `vector_example` on both sim and hardware anyway, and the smoke's unique coverage is the six build-flag permutations, which no example can affect.

## Resulting gates

| Job family | Gate |
| ---------- | ---- |
| `st-sim-*`, `st-onboard-*` | `<arch>_changed && st_affected` |
| `profiling-flags-smoke` | `(a2a3_changed \|\| a5_changed) && !examples_only` |
| `ut`, `ut-a2a3`, `ut-a5` | `non_code_only != true && ut_affected` |
| `packaging-matrix` | `non_code_only != true && !examples_only` |

## Testing

Simulated the filter against nine file lists:

| Input | `examples_only` | packaging / profiling smoke |
| ----- | --------------- | --------------------------- |
| #1605's diff (2 README + `main.py` under `examples/`) | **true** | **skip** |
| `examples/a2a3/.../kernels/aiv/x.cpp` | **true** | **skip** |
| docs-only | **true** | skip |
| `tests/st/.../test_foo.py` | false | run |
| `tests/ut/py/test_x.py` | false | run |
| `src/common/log/host_log.cpp` | false | run |
| `simpler_setup/build_runtimes.py` | false | run |
| `pyproject.toml` | false | run |
| `examples/` mixed with `src/a5/` | false | run |

- [x] `yaml.safe_load` on `ci.yml`; every `if:` re-read after rewiring
- [x] The new flag is added to the fail-open guard, so an unusable file list still runs everything
- [x] `mkdocs build --strict` — exit 0; `markdownlint-cli2` clean
- [x] `docs/ci.md` and `.claude/rules/ci-change-detection.md` updated, **including the paragraph that argued `packaging-matrix` was "not worth a fourth condition"** — #1605 is the counterexample to my own call in #1590

This PR touches `ci.yml`, so all axes report affected and the full matrix fires here — the intended self-check.

author: jatin-ge
body:
## Symptom
Refreshing `crm.growthescalators.com/wizmatch/today` returns raw `{"error":"too many requests"}` instead of the app.

## Cause
`app.use(generalLimiter)` is global at **100 req/min per IP** and counted **every static asset**. The admin SPA ships **~140 lazily loaded JS chunks**, so one page load can exceed 100 requests — a single refresh exhausted the budget and then 429'd the page itself.

Confirmed in production HTTP logs, not inferred:
```
GET /assets/ErrorRetry-DGnrOkaB.js   429
GET /wizmatch/today                  429   <- the SPA shell, blocked
GET /favicon.ico                     429
GET /api/inbox/unread-count          429
```

## Fix
Static assets exempt — immutable content-hashed files served from disk, not the abuse surface. **Everything else stays limited at the same 100/min**: `/api`, SPA document routes, and scanner probes (`/.env`, `/wp-config.php.bak`) which the limiter is correctly catching today. `/auth` (10/min) and `/webhooks` (300/min) untouched.

## Tests
20, pinning both halves — an over-broad skip would silently disable API rate limiting. Mutation-verified: removing the skip → 1 red; a loose `/\.(?:js|css)/` → 4 red, including that `/api/x.js/steal` must **not** be exempt.

**141 files / 1689 tests**, 0 failed.

author: victor-w-madeira
body:
## What was wrong

`CLAUDE.md` says the fixture's two monitors are deliberately asymmetric, and that the asymmetry is what a green run is worth (#1084): an `http_error` is logged and never fails a test, a `flow_error` **fails** it. On Langflow 1.12.x the second could not fire for a playground, agent **or node** run at all — two independent reasons, both measured on 1.12.0.dev10 from a Playwright trace:

1. The URL filter covered `/events?event_delivery=`, `/build/` and `/run/`. The run is `POST /api/v2/workflows` — none of them matched.
2. Even had it matched, the body was skipped: that response is `content-type: text/event-stream`, and the detector returned early for stream-like content types.

An Anthropic 400 therefore reached the UI with **no verdict** — no `🚨 Flow Error Detected`, nothing — while the stream carried `{"type":"RUN_ERROR","message":"Error code: 400 …"}` verbatim. `page.allowFlowErrors()` was a no-op on that path for the 13 specs that call it, and `agent-empty-refusal-response.spec.ts` — which documents the monitor as its crash guard — had no guard. Zero `flow_error` verdicts appear across 27 recorded CI runs since 2026-05-11, which reads as a dead mechanism rather than a quiet quarter.

That silence is why #1059's failure had to be triaged by hypothesis: the reason the run failed was in the stream seven seconds in, and the suite reported a count assertion 120 s later.

## Why this lands in two steps

Turning on a gate that has been dead for a whole endpoint is not a no-op. **88 specs** trigger a run (node *or* playground), **75 without a hatch**, and some provoke an execution error on purpose — `core-components/validate-raise-errors-components.spec.ts` raises a `ValueError` from a custom component and asserts the error UI, is `@stable @release`, and has no hatch because it never needed one.

So, the order #1084 used for the HTTP half — fix the classification first, decide about failing second:

| | v1 endpoints (always watched) | v2 run path (new coverage) |
|---|---|---|
| **step 1 — this PR** | keeps **failing** the test (and gains three cases — see below) | verdict **logged as ADVISORY**, does not fail |
| **step 2 — follow-up** | — | flip to failing, after auditing/hatching the 75 |

Nothing loosens: no path that failed a test before stops failing. And step 1 already delivers what #1059 needed — the cause is in the output.

## Evidence

Proven end to end on 1.12.0.dev10. Before, the same run printed nothing; now:

```
🚨 Flow Error Detected in Event Stream - http://localhost:7860/api/v2/workflows (ADVISORY)
   Shape: event_type=error
   Error: Error code: 400 - {... 'Your credit balance is too low ...'}
   ADVISORY: this does NOT fail the test yet — …(#1162, step 2)
```

and on the v1 path the gate still interrupts the **running** test, measured with a throwaway probe (v1 error, then a 10 s wait):

| | elapsed | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| tracked read (the bug) | 10 249 ms | ran the full wait, failed only in teardown |
| untracked read (fixed) | **238 ms** | `Flow execution error detected during test` |

`tests/fixtures/flow-error-gate.spec.ts` runs the gate against a local `node:http` server — no container, no provider key, no LLM — pinning that the hatch still suppresses v1 and that a v2 error is logged-but-not-failing. 239 unit tests green (`npm run test:units`), `tsc --noEmit` clean, ESLint 0 errors.

## Review

Reviewed independently, and the review **rejected the first commit**. Two blockers, both mine, both measured:

- I had silently downgraded the working half: wrapping the handler in a tracked promise marked its rejection handled, so the intentional throw stopped reaching the test — and my comment called it "best-effort" instead of "inert". That reinstated the exact problem this issue exists to remove. Fixed structurally: only the v2 read is tracked, pinned by a unit assertion because it regressed once already.
- My impact claim ("no spec provokes an execution error without the hatch") was **false** — see `validate-raise-errors-components.spec.ts` above. I had grepped playground markers only, missing node runs; the real surface is roughly double what I reported, and my "17 specs call `allowFlowErrors()`" counted files that merely mention the string (13 do call it, 21 call sites).

Also applied: the raw-text traceback patterns no longer run over a structured stream (they flagged ordinary agent prose explaining a `TypeError`); the minimal v2 error payload no longer yields `[object Object]`; URL matching is anchored on the pathname (`includes("/build/")` matched `/assets/build/index.js`); the `/api/v2/workflows/pending` 5 s poll is excluded; the v1 `{"event":"error"}` envelope is matched (its payload carries `error: false`, so neither old v1 shape was the error carrier); all four give-up paths are counted and printed instead of three of them being silent; the teardown drain is 3 s instead of a measured 15 s of waste.

## Before merging

`tests/fixtures/**` is **suite-wide** by `pr-validation.yml`'s import-graph rule (#1054): the PR lane runs a bounded subset and warns to dispatch `manual.yml` for the full suite. That dispatch is worth much more now than it was on the first commit — the read race that made verdicts timing-dependent is closed, so a full run's greenness means something. I have **not** dispatched it; it needs an owner's call on spending the run.

## Second review round

Reviewed again after the commits above. Three fixes, all measured:

- **The new guard ran nowhere — including on its own PR.** `flow-error-gate.spec.ts` carried only `@regression`. This PR's own run (30597091776) reads *"237 impacted, 20 run, 217 dropped"* — a `tests/fixtures/**` change resolves to every spec, `pr-validation.yml` caps at 20 with `@stable` first, and the gate spec was in the dropped 217. It was listed as a changed file and never executed; `daily-stable.yml` (`--grep @stable`) would not have run it either, and `nightly.yml` is dormant. A guard against *"a regression shipped because nothing executed the gate"* that itself executes nowhere is that defect wearing the fix's clothes. Now `@stable` — no backend, no key, ~5 s, and outside the QA-CHECKLIST globs so no bullet is required.

- **"v1 keeps failing the test, unchanged" was not accurate.** The old detector skipped **by content type before it looked at the URL**, so a v1 `text/event-stream` or `application/x-ndjson` body was never classified, and the `{"event": "error"}` envelope matched nothing. All three fail the test now — the same dead-gate flip this PR argues against for v2, done without staging. Kept, with the bound written down instead of the claim: `/api/v1/build/{id}/flow` has been retired since 1.11, which is what every scheduled lane targets, so it is latent there and live only for a supervised `manual.yml` dispatch at ≤ 1.10. Staging v1 too would leave the suite with **no** failing flow-error gate at all.

- **The 240 s budget is now v2-only.** It follows from the drain invariant this PR already relies on: only v2 reads are tracked, so a v1 read carrying the long budget had no owner — it could resolve after `await use(page)` and either push into an already-rendered `errors` array or throw outside the test that caused it. That window did not exist before (2 s, or skipped). v1 keeps 2 s; the give-up is counted, not silent.

Also: advisories no longer inflate the `📋 Found N backend error(s)` line (the number the human gate scans) and get their own line; the budget timer is `unref`'d; a unit test pins the budget below `playwright.config.ts`'s per-test timeout with 30 s of margin, since it is hand-copied across files and a budget at or above the timeout can never fire; `isRunStreamUrl` removed (no call site outside its own test); `firstLine` → `summarize` (it joins three lines, and its docblock opened by denying its name).

240 unit tests green, `tsc --noEmit` clean, ESLint 0 errors, and the gate spec passes against a live 1.12 instance in 5.0 s.

Closes #1162.

body:
## Symptoms (reported from the wallboard)

- "Hallucination rate (max)" showing **100% in red** while the latest stored suite run (today 08:20 UTC) has 0% on all five golden entries.
- "Time since last suite run" **frozen at ~15h for hours**.

## Diagnosis (verified against live Prometheus)

Instant queries for `eval_*` returned **empty** — the current prod/qa pods expose no eval gauges at all. Both stats were rendering `lastNotNull` remnants of **dead pods' series** (I found frozen pre-calibration hallucination rates of 60/20/80/40% on GD-02→05 from a replaced prod pod). Three root causes:

1. **`restore_gauges` read the root partition.** On the cloud, both producers (nightly executor, ingest route) store `eval_results.json` into the **owner partition** — so every deploy silently dropped all eval gauges. Now enters `ENTRA_OWNER_OID`'s partition, same as `evals/work`.
2. **Restore stamped "last run" with `time.time()`.** Every restart reset the age clock, masking a stalled schedule. Ingest now records `completed_at` on the payload; restore reuses it, and legacy payloads without one set **no** timestamp gauge (absent is honest).
3. **No namespace filter on the panels.** `max(eval_hallucination_rate_pct)` aggregated qa + prod pods. All eval panels (cloud + pi dashboards) now select `namespace="jcmcp"`, and the "time since" stat collapses pod series with `max()`.

The red-at-any-nonzero threshold on the hallucination stat is intentional (truth-gate posture) and unchanged.

## Tests

Three new regression tests: restore preserves the run timestamp (not "now"), legacy payloads restore scores but no timestamp, and restore reads the owner partition. `tests/test_evals.py`: 48/48 pass.

## 배경

맥 크롬·사파리에서 지난브리핑 「최신」 배지가 '최'/'신' 두 줄로 갈라졌다. 로컬 테스트는 통과했는데 실제 화면에서만 깨진 것이 문제의 핵심이다.

**원인**: 이 저장소의 테스트 환경에는 Noto 한글 서체가 없어 대체 서체(폭이 좁음)로 렌더된다. 실제 사용자는 Noto가 로드돼 글자 폭이 넓어지고, 그만큼 담긴 상자가 눌리면서 어절 중간에서 끊긴다. 어절 중간 줄바꿈 금지를 **요소마다 손으로 발라 왔기 때문에** 새 요소에서 번번이 빠졌다.

그래서 개별 수정에 그치지 않고, 사고가 못 생기는 구조로 바꿨다.

## 변경

**1. 배지 자체 수정**
- `.arch-card.latest .an::after`에 `display:inline-block` + `white-space:nowrap` 추가 — `.edition-chip`(종합/연휴 배지)에는 원래 있던 처리가 이 배지에만 빠져 있었다
- `.an`에도 `nowrap` — 좁은 폭에서 '제8호'가 '제/8/호' 세 줄로 쪼개지던 문제까지 해결
- `.arch-head`를 `flex-wrap:wrap`으로 — 자리가 모자라면 날짜가 아랫줄로 내려가고, 호수·배지는 눌리지 않는다

**2. 전역 원칙화**
- `body`에 `word-break:keep-all` — 어절 중간 줄바꿈을 기본으로 차단 (CLAUDE.md 원칙을 요소별 적용에서 전역 기본값으로 승격)
- 안전장치로 `overflow-wrap:break-word` — 긴 URL처럼 끊을 데가 없는 문자열만 강제로 끊는다. `anywhere`는 flex/grid 항목의 최소 폭 계산까지 바꿔 칸을 무너뜨리므로 쓰지 않았다
- 한 줄 유지가 필요한 배지·태그·칩·버튼 16종(`.kind-tag` `.type-tag` `.pin-badge` `.att-badge` `.mlog-badge` `.edition-chip` `.ev-pill` `.cat-label` `.cd-label` `.auth-btn` 등)에 `nowrap` 일괄 적용

**3. 함께 발견된 기존 버그 수정**
- `nav`에 `flex-wrap:wrap` 추가. 탭 6개 + 로그인 영역의 실폭이 876px이라, 줄바꿈이 640px 이하에서만 켜져 있던 탓에 **641~876px 구간(아이패드 세로 768px, 아이패드 에어 820px 등)에서 메뉴가 화면 밖으로 넘쳐 문서 전체에 가로 스크롤**이 생기고 있었다. 이 PR의 새 테스트가 잡아냈다

## 검증

**`tests/layout.test.js` 신규** — 320~1400px 14개 폭을 훑으며 세 탭(지난브리핑·이슈브리핑·일정공유)에서 검사:
- 한 줄 유지 대상 요소가 두 줄로 갈라지는지 (높이 ÷ 줄높이로 판정)
- 문서에 가로 스크롤이 생기는지
- 전역 `keep-all`·`break-word`가 살아 있고 하위로 상속되는지
- 카드 폭을 140px까지 강제로 좁힌 최악 조건에서도 호수·배지가 한 줄인지

다른 브라우저 엔진(WebKit·Firefox)은 이 환경에서 내려받을 수 없어 실행하지 못했다. 대신 **서체가 넓어진 상황을 폭을 좁혀 흉내 내는 방식**으로 실제보다 가혹하게 검사한다.

기존 테스트 4종(editor·export·calendar·workflow) 전부 통과.

## 눈에 보이는 변화

전역 `keep-all` 적용으로 **모바일 헤더 제목의 줄바꿈 위치가 달라진다.** 기존에는 "AI혁신정책연구 / **단** 지식 플랫폼"으로 어절 중간이 끊겼는데, 이제 "관악구 / AI혁신정책연구단 지식 / 플랫폼"으로 어절이 온전해지는 대신 한 줄 늘어난다. 내용은 그대로다.

author: awyborn2
body:
Three commits, shipped together because they're the last of the assessment workstream.

---

## 1. The seeding script was overwriting the link it was given

`author-track-dozer-tool.mjs` re-paired every theory question with the next `check_cross` in document order, then wrote that guess over `question.outcomeTarget`.

By then **publish has already resolved that link** from the printed references the model read off the page — `questionRef`, shipped in #76 for exactly this, applied through `linkOutcomeTargets` in [import-session.ts:1319](apps/web/src/lib/data/import-session.ts:1319). The script threw the better answer away and reinstated the guess `questionRef` exists to retire. Its own comment still argued for adjacency *"labels vary — 'Q1 Outcome', 'BBM Q1 Outcome'"* — which stopped being true when references replaced label matching.

The published link now wins; adjacency survives as a reported fallback; only an **inferred** link is written back.

**The all-or-nothing count check stays, and I was wrong to plan on loosening it.** The key identifies answers by section and number, and nothing on a published field carries that number — `questionRef` is consumed at publish and dropped. So entries align **by order**, and one missing pair writes question 8's answers onto question 7: marking a candidate wrong on a question they answered correctly, on a safety record. What changed is the diagnosis — it now names the questions with no outcome box.

The rule moved to `@formai/shared` beside the resolver whose output it reads, with **8 tests**. The script has none and writes answer keys onto a competency record.

## 2. The answer key can live outside the repository

`--key <path>` (or `ANSWER_KEY_PATH`) replaces the fixed in-repo path, so `docs/assessment-tools/track-dozer.answer-key.json` can be deleted. The old path stays as a fallback while that file exists, so nothing breaks mid-migration; once it's gone the error says where to put one.

Two things worth being plain about:

- **The key is in git history and removing the file does not retract it.** Treat those answers as disclosed.
- **Runtime confidentiality was never this file's problem** — #87 gated `GET /forms` and `GET /forms/:id` on `forms.view`, so a candidate can't read a key through the API. This is about not shipping one in the source tree.

## 3. The assessor's signature now reaches the page

Sign-off captured a signature and the exporter knew where to put it, but the page stayed blank — there was no image-embedding call anywhere in `apps/api/src/pdf`, so it fell through to the text path where a guard correctly refused to draw base64 across the record.

`round-trip.ts` now embeds it, **scaled to fit and centred, never stretched**. A signature is drawn on a canvas of whatever size the pad was and the box is whatever the reviewer placed; filling the box would distort a person's signature on the document that certifies them.

**Every failure draws nothing.** Only PNG is recognised (pdf-lib must be told which decoder to use, and guessing wrong throws inside the export); malformed payloads, unsupported formats and decoder errors all fall through to blank. A missing signature is a visible gap someone chases up; a broken one is a crashed export or a defaced certificate.

The panel copy flips back in the same change. It has now been rewritten **twice in opposite directions**, and both times the copy followed the renderer — promised the signature when nothing could draw one, corrected to "leave it unplaced", and now promises it again, because copy telling a reviewer to skip the box would leave the signature block empty on every certificate.

---

## Verification

- shared **181**, api **995**, web **924**. `pnpm -r typecheck` clean.
- Both embed tests fail against the unbranched renderer; the malformed-PNG and wrong-format tests pin the blank fallback.
- The runbook now passes `--key` and asks for the pairing breakdown as a check: *"31 from the published questionRef link, 0 inferred from document order"* is the healthy report.

## What still isn't wired

The Track Dozer manifest doesn't yet name `signOff.assessorSignatureFieldId`, so the block still exports blank until the authoring script declares it — the renderer is ready, the manifest isn't. That's authoring, not code.

# 🚀 PR: Implementação da Camada de Recuperação Vetorial (RAG) e Reindexação

## 📌 Título Sugerido
`feat(rag): implementa camada de recuperação vetorial, reindexação e integração com Gemini API`

---

## 🎯 O que foi feito?
Este PR implementa e consolida a **camada de recuperação (RAG)** do assistente **Turi**, configurando a persistência de documentos vetorizados no ChromaDB e integrando a geração de embeddings com a API oficial do Gemini.

---

## 🛠️ Alterações Realizadas

### 1. Geração de Embeddings e Vector Store (`src/vector_store.py`)
* **Endpoint REST:** Atualizado o envio de requisições para utilizar o modelo `gemini-embedding-001` (3072 dimensões) via chamada HTTP REST direta, contornando desvios de versão e rotas instáveis de SDKs.
* **Resiliência de Dados:** Adicionado suporte a chaves flexíveis nos dicionários dos chunks (`id` / `chunk_id` com fallback sequencial dinâmico).

### 2. Rotina de Reindexação (`reindex.py`)
* **Gestão de Caminhos:** Corrigida a resolução de diretórios com `Path(__file__)` apontando corretamente para `data/pdfs`.
* **Tratamento de Exceções:** Adicionada verificação de segurança para evitar tentativas de gravação vetorial no ChromaDB quando a lista de chunks estiver vazia.

### 3. Interface e Experiência (`app.py` / `src/generator.py`)

author: madarauchiha-314
body:
# A `produces` entry names an artifact, not a filename — reviewer briefing Closes #124. ## TL;DR the-loop has documented `bugfix.md` as a bug's phase-1 spec since long before the process graph existed. The graph's `requirements-definition` node produced `requirements.md` and nothing else, so **an agent that followed the documented process was blocked by that same process** for not having written a file it was told not to write. Per the maintainer's call on the ticket (Option 1), a `produces` entry now names an *artifact* that may accept several names, exactly one of which may be present — and a new parity test makes the disagreement impossible to reintroduce. Root-causing turned up **two more instances** of the same mismatch that the ticket had not seen. One of them is a security gate that has been reporting success without running. ## Where to focus (in this order) 1. **The fail-closed choice** — `cli/the_loop/graph/hooks/artifacts.py:77-91`. Accepting "any one of N names" is by construction easier to satisfy than "this exact name", so the one thing worth arguing about is what happens when **both** are present. It blocks as ambiguous rather than preferring the first-declared name. Rationale in [decision-045](https://github.com/MadaraUchiha-314/the-loop/blob/claude/github-issue-124-7su07m/docs/decisions/decision-045.md#decision): two artifacts filling one slot have no defined source of truth, and picking one lets a gate pass against a stale spec while the live one sits beside it. If you'd rather it picked, say so — it's a two-line change and a test. 2. **RC2, the quiet one** — `cli/the_loop/graph/hooks/artifacts.py` (`enforces_boundaries_from`) and `pdlc.yaml`'s `design` node. The same literal `requirements.md` appears as that hook's `upstream`. For a bug it resolved to nothing, the hook took its "absent" branch, and **a skip passes the chain** — so the check that every trust boundary raised in phase 1 is answered in `design.md` has never run for a `bugfix.md` work item, while reporting success. This is worse than the ticket's defect, which at least failed loudly. The hook had **zero tests**; it now has five. 3. **The parity test** — `cli/tests/test_graph_parity.py`. The ticket calls this the actual defect, and it is the half that matters after today. Three files have to agree — the shipped graph, `.the-loop/manifest.yaml`, and the bundled templates — and nothing compared them. Worth checking that P1/P2/P3 are the *right* three assertions and that the exclusions (a manifest entry with no `phase`, a `pathPattern` ending in `/`) are data-driven rather than an allow-list. 4. **The resolver** — `cli/the_loop/graph/model.py`. `ArtifactSlot` + `resolve_produces`, deliberately *not* choosing between present alternatives; that's policy and it belongs to the hook. Also collapses a byte-identical private copy that both hooks were carrying — the same defect one level down. 5. **Skim** — `pdlc.yaml`, `templates/bugfix.md`, docs. The template change (RC3) is small but load-bearing: see below. ## What changed (map) ```mermaid flowchart TD Y["pdlc.yaml
produces: requirements.md or bugfix.md"] --> C["compile_graph"] C -->|"validates each entry"| V["empty alternative = GraphConfigError"] C --> N["Node.produces
entries kept verbatim"] N --> R["resolve_produces
one ArtifactSlot per entry"] R --> A["validate-artifacts
missing / ambiguous / validate"] R --> L["lint-artifacts
lint every present file"] R --> B["enforces-boundaries-from
upstream resolved the same way"] M[".the-loop/manifest.yaml"] --> P["test_graph_parity.py"] T["skills/the-loop/templates/"] --> P Y --> P ``` ## Key decisions & why (education) - **`|` alternation over list-of-lists.** `[[requirements.md, bugfix.md]]` needs no parsing, but reads as nesting rather than choice, makes the common single-name case irregular, and changes the JSON shape of `graph show` for every existing node. The entry is kept **verbatim** in `Node.produces`, so `the-loop graph show --format json` reports what the graph declares instead of claiming two artifacts where it means one. — [decision-045](https://github.com/MadaraUchiha-314/the-loop/blob/claude/github-issue-124-7su07m/docs/decisions/decision-045.md) - **Option 2 was declined, and that shaped everything.** Retiring `bugfix.md` was cheaper to implement and is what #119's workaround already does in practice — but it changes documented plugin behaviour for consuming repos. `bugfix.md` is therefore retired from nothing; every place that blessed it still does, now stating that both names clear the same gate and only one may be present. - **RC3: the template, not a second alternation mechanism.** The node requires a `Requirements` section; `templates/bugfix.md` offered `## Acceptance criteria (EARS)`. Teaching `sections:` its own alternation would have left the-loop with two names for the same *section* as well as two for the same file. The template gained `## Requirements` with the EARS criteria nested under it — one vocabulary, one gate. Reproduction / expected-vs-actual / root-cause are untouched. - **Two self-review findings, both acted on.** (1) Resolving the downstream through *present* files alone silently turned "declared but missing" from a block into a skip in `enforces-boundaries-from` — unreachable in the shipped graph, but a weakening in the very hook this work item is about; original semantics restored and pinned. (2) P3 extracted headings with its own regex while the gate uses `frontmatter.sections`, which ignores headings inside fences — a template could have been called compliant on the strength of a heading in an example block. P3 now uses the gate's own parser. - **This PR's own spec is a `bugfix.md`, on purpose.** `the-loop-gate.yml` runs `the-loop check --recompute --fail-on block` on every spec folder a PR touches, so the gate passing on `docs/specs/issue-124/` **is** the end-to-end regression test for the headline defect. ## Evidence **The reproduction, before:** ```console $ uv run the-loop check issue-104 --recompute issue-104: UNMET (at requirements-definition) BLOCK requirements-definition · required artifact is missing (docs/specs/issue-104/requirements.md) ``` **After — a `bugfix.md` work item clears phase 1 and parks at the human gate:** ```console $ uv run the-loop check issue-124 --recompute issue-124: UNMET (at requirements-approval) WAIT requirements-approval · no authorized feedback yet ``` **Red-then-green, and the order is the finding:** P1 was red on the untouched tree (`bugfix.md … that phase's node(s) accept ['requirements.md']`). After the name fix, **P3 went red** — `node 'requirements-definition' requires a 'Requirements' section the template does not offer`. The test, not a person, discovered that fixing the filename moved the block one line down. **Checks:** `uv run pre-commit run --all-files` fully green — ruff lint + format, pyright 0 errors, markdownlint 0 errors, **868 passed / 1 skipped** (867 before; +19 tests, of which 3 are the parity assertions and 5 are the first tests `enforces-boundaries-from` has ever had). No pre-existing test was modified. **A single-name `produces` is bit-identical** — same resolution, same message text, same `path`, same aggregation; pinned by `test_a_single_name_node_reports_missing_exactly_as_before`. ## Open questions for the reviewer 1. **Ambiguity blocks — confirm?** Focus item 1. The cost is that a repo mid-migration with both files sees a block it didn't before; the message says exactly what to do. 2. **The five historical bug specs.** Left as a historical record per your call, so they keep their pre-graph `## Acceptance criteria (EARS)` headings. After this change their *name* resolves fine and they block on the *heading* instead. Nothing re-runs a closed work item — but the gate runs on folders a PR **touches**, so a future PR touching one of those five would block on it. Recorded in the execu

author: asklar
body:
Makes lvt consumable by other projects: a static `lvt_core` library plus the CLI and TAP DLLs, installed as a `find_package()`-able CMake package, with a vcpkg port and an in-repo git registry.

## Why

Everything was compiled directly into `lvt.exe`, and `lvt_unit_tests` recompiled the same 17 sources, so there was nothing for another project to link against and no `install()` rules anywhere.

## What changed

**`lvt_core` library.** The shared sources move into a static library; `lvt` is now `main.cpp` linked against it, and the unit tests link it instead of rebuilding it. Public headers install to `include/lvt/`, exported as `lvt::core`.

**TAP DLL discovery no longer assumes it is `lvt.exe`.** `get_exe_dir()` was duplicated across three providers, each calling `GetModuleFileNameW(nullptr)` — the *process image* directory. Replaced with a shared `module_util` that resolves the directory of the module containing `lvt_core` via `GetModuleHandleExW(FROM_ADDRESS)`, plus `set_tap_directory()` and `LVT_TAP_DIR` overrides. Centralising the architecture suffix also picked up the x86 case that `xaml_diag_common` was missing.

**Plugins are found in a packaged install.** `load_plugins()` only ever looked in `%USERPROFILE%\.lvt\plugins`, so a packaged install could never find the plugins it shipped. It now searches `$LVT_PLUGIN_DIR`, then `<module dir>/plugins`, then the user profile.

**Per-framework build options.** `LVT_ENABLE_{XAML,WINUI3,WPF,WINFORMS,AVALONIA,CHROMIUM}` plus `LVT_BUILD_{TOOL,MANAGED,TESTS}`. The split that matters for packaging is native vs managed, not framework by framework: WPF, WinForms and Avalonia each have a native half that hosts the CLR and a managed tree-walker assembly, and only the latter needs `dotnet`. With `-DLVT_BUILD_MANAGED=OFF` the entire native build works with no .NET SDK and no NuGet restore.

**C++/WinRT generator now comes from the `cppwinrt` port.** The projection in `src/tap/winui3` holds only the `Microsoft.*` half while `winrt/base.h` came from the Windows SDK, and generation was guarded by `if(NOT EXISTS)` — so the cached half never refreshed and upgrading the Windows SDK broke the build inside generated headers. Taking the generator from the port means both halves come from one version by construction, and since vcpkg installs only one version of a port per triplet, a consumer already depending on `cppwinrt` picks the version for both. Regeneration is now keyed on a signature hashing the generator plus the Windows App SDK inputs.

**gtest only when tests are built.** It was an unconditional manifest dependency, so the toolchain installed it during `project()` regardless of `LVT_BUILD_TESTS` — which broke cross-compiling for arm64 even though nothing would have linked it. Now behind a `tests` manifest feature.

**vcpkg port and registry.** `ports/lvt` maps frameworks onto features; `versions/` makes the repo usable as a git registry. The port always passes `LVT_BUILD_MANAGED=OFF`, since vcpkg builds have neither network access nor a .NET SDK. The Windows App SDK winmds come from a NuGet package fetched with a pinned SHA512, following the pattern the `cppwinrt` port uses.

**CI.** New `packaging` job builds the offline configuration across x64/x86/arm64, installs it, and builds `tests/package_consumer` against the result as a separate CMake project — so a regression in the install rules, the exported target name or the public headers breaks the build. New `port` job runs `format-manifest` and `x-add-version` and fails on any diff; both had already drifted by hand.

## Verification

- default all-on build: 60 unit, 18 chromium, 31 integration tests pass (1 skipped — this Notepad is WinUI 3 rather than system XAML)
- offline build completes with zero `dotnet` invocations
- **the port installs through a real vcpkg**, with source acquisition stubbed to a `git archive` export since the tag does not exist yet: all default features, post-build validation passes, and a consumer then walked 898 elements out of a live WinUI 3 Notepad
- x64 and x86: build, install and consumer smoke test all pass, including correct `lvt_tap_x86.dll` resolution
- `/showIncludes` confirms `base.h` and `Windows.*` resolve to the cppwinrt port, `Microsoft.*` to the generated projection, and no SDK cppwinrt header is pulled in

## Known gaps

- `SHA512` in the portfile is a placeholder until `v0.2.0` is tagged; `scripts/update-vcpkg-port.ps1` fills it in and refreshes the versions database afterwards. The registry is therefore not usable until that follow-up lands.
- arm64 could not be validated locally — the active Windows SDK on my machine has no ARM64 libraries — so the arm64 CI leg is running for the first time in this PR.

author: mblauberg
body:
Closes #548.

Design authority: `.agent-run/design-council-2026-07-31/SYNTHESIS.md` P5 row and proposal-2.md section 2.4. Built on the projection primitive from #567.

## What each surface gets

| Doc claim | Source of truth | Gate form |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery state-machine Mermaid body, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | `NORMAL_STATES` / `SIDE_STATES` / `TRANSITIONS` in `skills/deliver/scripts/validate_delivery.py` | marked region, `scripts/render_doc_projections.py` |
| Risk-factor table, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (new) | `config/risk-policy.json` | marked region, same renderer |
| Review-pressure table + machine-checking sentence, `HARNESS.md` | `skills/_shared/review_ladder.py`, `config/risk-policy.json` | comparison form, `scripts/check_doc_constants.py` |
| Review-pressure table, `README.md` | `config/risk-policy.json` tier order | comparison form |
| Repair-budget phrases, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (accDescr + edge label) | `REPAIR_BUDGETS` | comparison form, expected phrase generated from the constant |
| Grep-constant floor: states and tiers | validator constants + tier order | both directions: sources must be mentioned, state-diagram identifiers must exist in the validator |
| Every repo path cited in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `README.md` | the tree | `scripts/check_doc_paths.py`, tolerates `:line` suffixes and globs |

All three gates run in `scripts/check-harness`: `--check` renders in memory and diffs, CI never writes; maintainers regenerate with `--write`. `MAINTAINING.md` now declares the three documentation tiers, including the deliberately unchecked prose tier.

## Two constraints that shaped the design

- HTML comment markers are a Mermaid parse error inside a fence, so the state-machine region wraps the whole fence and the renderer preserves `accTitle`, `accDescr`, `classDef`, `class` lines, group titles and edge labels editorially (the same pattern `render_skill_catalogue.py` uses for Area rows). Only the graph structure is generated; a deleted marker fails instead of skipping.
- `HARNESS.md` sits exactly at its 60-line hard cap and `tests/test_harness_contract.py` forbids any `config/` or `scripts/` path in the ambient files, so a marker pair is impossible there. Its ladder claims are drift-checked in comparison form; the checker prints the expected source-derived text on failure. The rationale is recorded in the `check_doc_constants.py` docstring.

## Drift found

None in the current tree, verified rather than assumed: the hand-written state diagram matches the validator's 12 normal states, 3 side states and all 13 transitions byte-for-byte once rendered; the repair budgets, both review-pressure tables and the ladder sentence match their constants; all 83 cited paths exist. Detection power is proven by injected-drift tests (`tests/test_doc_projection_gates.py`): removed edges, invented transitions, stale class lines, edited budget figures, reordered tier rows, deleted markers and vanished paths each fail their gate, while rewording the hand-written accessibility text round-trips freely.

## Checks

- `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q`: 1467 passed, 178 subtests passed
- `scripts/check-harness`: exit 0, including the three new gates (`PASS: ARCHITECTURE.md state machine and risk-factor table match their sources`, `PASS: docs match review_ladder.py, validate_delivery.py and risk-policy.json (15 states, 4 tiers)`, `PASS: 83 cited paths exist across 2 documents`)

## Summary

Add `areno show <run_id>` — display model, dataset, algorithm, resolved key settings, current stage, latest metrics, and last error for a single training run. Reads from existing local artifacts with no new dependencies.

## Usage

```bash
areno show <run_id>                  # human-readable output
areno show <run_id> --format json    # structured JSON
areno show <run_id> --format table   # compact key-value table
```

Run ID can be a full ID, partial ID prefix (if unique), or PID.

## CLI Output

```
Run: train sft Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B  (id=841950e0f0ed)
Kind:     train
Status:   exited
Stage:    train_start
Step:     1027
Created:  2026-07-30T06:07:24+00:00
Updated:  2026-07-30T06:22:21+00:00
Metrics:  /tmp/areno/tfevent_sft

Key settings:
  algo                   sft
  ckpt                   Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B
  dataset_path           yahma/alpaca-cleaned
  world_size             2
  batch_size             2
  mini_bs                2
  optimizer_lr           1e-06
  lr_decay_style         cosine
  weight_decay           0.01
  ...

Latest metrics (29):
  rollout/accuracy               0.0  @step 1026
  rollout/prompt_len_mean        25.0  @step 1026
  rollout/response_len_mean      54.5  @step 1026
  train/loss                     1.4218  @step 1026
  train/grad_norm                45.300  @step 1026
  ...

Timing (80 steps recorded):
  Avg total / step:    1.16s
  Avg train / step:    1.16s

Recent logs (last 1 lines):
  registered AReno command: areno train --ckpt Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B ...
```

## What changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `areno/cli/show.py` | New: `areno show` CLI with human/table/json output |
| `areno/cli/main.py` | +1 line: register `show` command |
| `tests/test_cli_show_cpu.py` | New: 20 CPU tests |
| `docs/show-run.md` | New: user guide with usage, examples, limitations |

## Edge cases handled

| Scenario | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| Run ID not found | Clear error, exit code != 0 |
| Ambiguous partial ID | Lists matching IDs, exit code != 0 |
| Partial ID prefix | Matches if unique |
| Missing metrics | Section omitted, no error |
| Missing config | Section omitted, no error |
| Partially written artifacts | Still produces output with available fields |
| Active/running run | Shows "running" status and current stage, no exit code |
| Secrets in config | Auto-redacted (key/token/password/credential) |
| Full samples | Never printed |

## Design decisions

- **Dashboard API first, local fallback**: Tries `GET /api/jobs/{id}` first for full data, falls back to reading local artifact files when server is unavailable.
- **Sections config normalization**: Dashboard API returns config with a `sections` key for structured display. `_normalize_dashboard_config()` extracts flat key-value pairs for CLI consumption.
- **Secret redaction**: Config keys matching `key/secret/token/password/credential` patterns are automatically hidden from output.
- **Partial ID matching**: Users can type a prefix of the run ID instead of the full 12-character hex.

## Tests (20 CPU)

| Category | Count | Coverage |
|----------|-------|----------|
| Human format | 7 | Basic output, key settings, metrics, error section, timing, secrets redaction |
| JSON format | 1 | Valid JSON with expected fields |
| Table format | 1 | Key fields present in table output |
| Invalid input | 6 | Nonexistent ID, ambiguous partial, partial match, empty metrics/config, partial artifacts |
| Active runs | 2 | Running status, stage display, no exit code |
| Resolve job | 3 | Exact ID match, PID match, no match |

## Related Issue

Closes #251
```

author: mosluce
body:
Two documentation commits, deliberately separate.

## `docs(roadmap)` — in-app version display

The app shows its version nowhere (no `package_info_plus` dependency). With three TestFlight builds live at once, "which build is installed?" could only be answered from TestFlight's side — which cost a debugging round today, briefly suggesting a release-vs-debug behaviour difference that did not exist.

## `docs(openspec)` — `add-checkin-manual-label`

All 10,239 imported legacy records carry a `manual_label`; the app has never been able to produce one. The plumbing has been in place from the start — `pending_events.manualLabel`, the background-sync passthrough, `SubmitCheckinEventRequest.manual_label`, server validation at 1–120 chars — with nothing in the UI to set it. **No server change is needed.**

The design constraint worth reviewing: `app-checkin` forbids any dialog, modal or sheet between the tap and the enqueue, which is exactly what collecting a label wants to add. The proposal collects it *before* the press instead — a required field with the action buttons gated on it, the same pattern the login form uses — so that requirement is untouched rather than amended.

Decisions were driven by the imported data rather than intuition: 6 recent-label chips because the median AppUser has used 7 distinct labels ever; frequency ordering rather than recency so the dominant site keeps a stable position; cleared after every event because 83.3% of days use one label throughout, and stickiness fails *silently* on the other 16.7%.

Note the proposal states plainly that this puts a required field on the app's primary path — a worker who cannot supply a label cannot clock in — and why the chips are part of this change rather than a follow-up.

**Site names in the artifacts are synthetic placeholders.** The real values are the customer's own customers, and this repository is public. Statistics are kept because they carry the design signal without identifying anyone.

body:
> *"use the horizontal version there, unless the arranger gives us a tall frame. People are used to the original layout — the rotated version will work in a pinch but should be avoided in regular cases."*

Recorded. Upright is the default and rotated is a **fallback, not a co-equal option**.

**The corner already renders upright**, which is correct under this rule — so nothing needed changing. Both forms exist and are prop-driven (`rotated`).

## What I built, measured, and reverted

Automatic selection between them. It was wrong in **both** directions:

| available | result | should have been |
|---|---|---|
| 120px | stayed upright, **didn't fit** | rotated |
| 320px at 1.5× | stayed **stuck rotated** with ample room | upright |

**Cause:** a `ResizeObserver` on the component root doesn't fire when only `--table-scale` changes — the root is a full-width block, so its box is unchanged. The orientation goes stale on any scale-only relayout.

A correct version needs to react to scale as well as width, and needs hysteresis so it can't oscillate at the boundary.

## The circularity worth remembering

This is why the choice landed in the component at all: the **shell supplies the reserve**, which is an *input* to the allocation — so the shell cannot know the allocation at the moment it must choose. Either the component measures its own box (needs the fix above), or the shell chooses from the previous pass's ledger (a feedback loop that wants care).

Shipping a flaky orientation switch into the review corner — the exact surface this roadmap has spent the day repairing — would have been careless. The default is correct; the follow-up is honestly described.

author: lucaszaous-creator
body:
Até aqui **todas as pontes iam para a frente**. A sessão virava guia, a guia virava receita, a receita virava indicador — e nada voltava.

## O mapa, antes

O que **já** comunicava (e continua):

| Ponte | Sentido | Onde |
|---|---|---|
| Concluir a sessão → guia + pacote + insumo + caixa | Recepção → Faturamento, Financeiro | `FechamentoSessaoService` |
| Guia efetivada sem receita lançada | Faturamento → Financeiro | `GuiasSemLancamentoAsync` (Conciliação) |
| Pendência de guia no cartão de quem chega hoje | Faturamento → Recepção | `PainelRecepcaoService` |
| Preço negociado e retenção na fonte | Gerente → Financeiro | `PrecoConvenioService`, `Tributo.ConvenioCodigo` |
| Alerta que LEVA à tela dona | Gerente → todos | `PainelDirecaoService` + `ChavesSuite` |

Os apps compartilham o **banco**, não mensagens: o que um grava o outro lê, e a ligação é sempre uma chave estrangeira (`LancamentoFinanceiro.CodigoFaturamentoId`, `Agendamento.AtendimentoId`). Não há mensageria entre os `.exe` — decisão registrada, não esquecimento.

## Os três buracos que esta parcela fecha

**1 · A glosa nunca chegava ao Financeiro.** `grep -rl "Glosa" src/Clinica.Modulo.Financeiro` → nada. `GlosaService` mexia só no `CodigoFaturamento`. O convênio recusava a guia e o dinheiro **continuava no fluxo de caixa, no previsto e na rentabilidade por convênio**, como se fosse entrar.

> Receita fantasma é a pior espécie de número errado, porque tem cara de número exato. Não há linha vermelha: a direção olha a previsão do mês e decide errado sem saber que está decidindo errado.

`ReceitaGlosadaService` é a ponte, e mora fora dos dois serviços pela mesma razão de sempre — o `AtendimentoService` é compartilhado com o app congelado. Três regras:

- **A glosa não apaga o lançamento.** É fato datado, como o consumo de pacote: sai do total, não do histórico. Cancelar com motivo deixa a prova de que a receita caiu por GLOSA, e não por erro de digitação — são coisas diferentes na hora de negociar com a operadora.
- **Só o PREVISTO se cancela.** O REALIZADO é dinheiro que entrou na conta; cancelá-lo faria o caixa parar de bater com o extrato e levaria junto a conferência do dia. Se a operadora estornou, isso é uma **saída**, com a data do estorno. O serviço recusa, e a tela explica em vez de deixar o botão aceso.
- **A guia volta sozinha para a conciliação.** Cancelado o vínculo, ela deixa de ter receita ativa e reaparece em `GuiasSemLancamentoAsync` — o caminho de volta funciona sem uma linha de código para isso: recuperado o recurso, ela está lá esperando ser lançada com o valor e a data daquele momento.

**2 · A conciliação convidava a lançar receita de guia recusada.** A linha era idêntica à de uma guia paga. Agora a guia glosada **aparece marcada, nunca sumindo** (mesma regra da central de documentos — linha que desaparece sem explicação faz procurar a tarde inteira o que se viu ontem), e lançar receita dela pede confirmação em vez de ser proibido: a clínica pode estar certa de que recupera no recurso, ela só precisava saber.

**3 · O balcão não sabia de nada que os outros módulos sabiam sobre o paciente à frente dele.** A conta vencida existia desde a parcela 12 e virou tela na 23 — no Financeiro. A glosa existia desde o começo — no Faturamento. Quem podia resolver as duas em trinta segundos, com a pessoa presente, era exatamente quem não via nenhuma.

`ElegibilidadeService` alargou o contrato de propósito, com um critério explícito: **entra ali o que se resolve com o paciente presente e fica caro depois.** Como ele já é chamado no check-in da fila e no agendamento, os dois avisos nascem prontos nos dois pontos.

- O atraso só alarma a partir de **5 dias** — a conta de ontem costuma estar em trânsito, e alerta que dispara para todo mundo é alerta que ninguém lê.
- A dívida é sempre **amarela**: vermelho neste serviço significa "a guia vai ser recusada", e dívida é assunto de conversa, não impedimento de atender.
- A glosa fica **vermelha** só quando ainda dá para agir e o prazo está acabando (≤ 7 dias); passado o prazo, o aviso perde a função de pedir pressa.

## Também nesta parcela

- **Painel da direção**: alerta `ReceitaGlosada` com valor somado, gravidade **Perigo** (os outros alertas são coisas a fazer; este é um número errado em outra tela) e destino de navegação para a nova aba.
- Permissão dupla no botão novo (`IsEnabled` + `Exigir`), auditoria no cancelamento (via `FinanceiroService`, que continua sendo o único lugar que grava dinheiro) e **terceiro estado** na aba: falha de leitura não pode ser exibida como "nenhuma receita glosada".

## Verificação

- `python3 tools/verificar-suite.py` → **OK** (83 XAML, 7 projetos, 64 construtores).
- Testes novos: `ComunicacaoEntreModulosTests` (11 casos, o circuito inteiro — sessão → guia → baixa → receita → glosa → cancelamento → volta à conciliação) e 6 casos novos em `ConsentimentoElegibilidadeTests`.
- **Não foi possível rodar `dotnet build`/`dotnet test` neste ambiente**: não há SDK .NET e a política do proxy bloqueia o download. Compilação dos quatro apps e suíte de testes ficam com o CI (runner Windows).

## Banco

**Nenhuma migration.** A parcela é toda de leitura cruzada sobre o que já estava gravado — que é exatamente o ponto dela.

body:
## 摘要
新增「文件領航員 (Document Navigator)」通用互動式流程提示詞模板：使用者上傳任意文件後，LLM 產生 mermaid 流程圖，並以嚴格引用文件內容的方式逐節點導覽。同時補齊根目錄 README 的可用模板清單。

## 問題
現有模板（ML／OpenCV／PE）都是針對單一領域手工打造的流程文件，缺少一份「對任意文件都能用」的通用模板；且根目錄 README 的模板清單只列了 ML、連結還指向不存在的 `./ML/` 資料夾。
此改動「不會」解決的：提示詞在各家 LLM 上的實際遵循度（屬 runtime 行為，需實測迭代）。

## 變更內容
### `Document_Navigator/dn-interactive-process-zh-TW.md`
- 新增提示詞主文件，採 Fabric 式三段結構（角色 → 流程 → 輸出硬約束）
- 核心規則：嚴格引用（僅整理文件內容、逐點附出處、未涵蓋明說）、流程來源標示（📄 文件原生 vs 🤖 AI 歸納）、兩段式產圖（先節點清單＋出處對照表、再產 mermaid）
- 導覽協定指令表：`下一步`／`N`／`圖`／`深度 淺|深`／`測驗`／`調整流程圖`／`結束`
- mermaid 防錯規範（固定 `flowchart TD`、引號包裹、節點編號即導覽指令）與例外條款
- 全文件依「Mandatory Steps, Not Prose」規範使用強制措辭（必須／禁止），無「可／建議」類軟性指令

### `Document_Navigator/README.md`
- 新增使用指南，格式比照現有模板（上傳文件＋貼啟動提示詞）

### `README.md`
- 可用模板清單補上 Document Navigator、OpenCV、Prompt Engineering 三個條目
- 修正失效的 ML 連結（`./ML/` → `./Machine_Learning/`）

## 設計決定
- 嚴格引用而非「文件為主＋AI 補充」：防幻覺優先；文件外知識設同意閘門（先詢問、未同意禁答、回答須標示「⚠️ 非文件內容」）
- 開場五段限定單則回覆完成：兩段式產圖（先規劃後畫圖）提升圖的正確性，但不強迫使用者多一輪確認
- 節點編號同時作為導覽指令：借鑑 Mr. Ranedeer（指令協定）與 GitDiagram（圖即索引）的高星專案設計

## 測試
| 項目 | 結果 |
| --- | --- |
| mermaid 語法範例逐條驗證可渲染（引號、subgraph、菱形節點、圖表類型名） | ✅ 由 review agent 確認全部合法 |
| 根 README 連結目標存在於磁碟 | ✅ 四個資料夾連結均存在 |
| Standards／Spec 雙軸 code review | ✅ 無 must-fix；判斷級發現已修正或說明 |

**未驗證**：提示詞在實際 LLM 對話中的端到端行為（導覽循環、指令遵循度）尚未實測。

author: isaacslee
body:
Closes #157.

The skin had been paying both costs at once: the obligations of redistributing a font — the rename the OFL requires, the licence travelling in the package — and a jsDelivr request on every page load that the design still leaned on. Bundling bought none of what it was for.

### What decided it

Latin-only rested on the fallback being a fair substitute, which holds for an audience mostly on Apple hardware or Android. That was assumed. Measured on the live blog:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| desktop | **91.4%** |
| mobile | 8.6% |

In Korea a desktop overwhelmingly means Windows, which means Malgun Gothic — visibly older than the rest of the page, and what nearly every reader would have seen for nearly all of the text.

### The numbers, cut here rather than quoted

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Latin only | 51 KB |
| **Latin + Hangul, wght 300–800** | **596 KB** |
| Latin + Hangul, wght 400–700 | 1152 KB |
| source | 2009 KB |

ADR-0003 recorded 821 KB from an external figure; cut at build time it is 596. Narrowing the weight axis makes the file *larger*, because a narrower range has to interpolate new masters where the wider one keeps the ones already in the file.

Package: 338 KB → **900 KB**, or 4.4% of Tistory's 20 MB limit.

### Verified in the preview

```
fonts registered   Quiet Sans loaded
Hangul via face    364px, against 410.63px for serif  → the face covers it
requests to CDNs   none
font requests      quiet-sans.woff2  596KB
```

### Two things renamed or removed

**Quiet Latin → Quiet Sans.** A file holding 11,172 Hangul syllables is not a Latin subset and should not be named as one. The OFL rename requirement is met either way.

**The `unicode-range` is gone.** It kept a page with no Latin from asking for the file, which saves nothing once the file covers the script the blog is mostly written in — and left as it was, it would have kept the browser from using the font for Hangul at all.

### Trade made deliberately

Mobile readers, 8.6% here, pay the most for a fallback that was already good on their platform. `font-display: swap` bounds it: a first visit paints in the system stack and swaps when the file lands. 8.6% pay so that 91.4% see the page as it was drawn.

Reversible — nothing about the settings surface changes, so going back is a minor release.

author: neovand
body:
## What this adds

A speech-to-speech **voice assistant for the open document**, built on OpenAI's Realtime API (`gpt-realtime-2.1`, WebRTC). Like every premium path it is BYOK and browser-only — the user's key mints a short-lived client secret, and everything else happens peer-to-peer with OpenAI. No server, per the app's architecture.

**Interaction (Wispr-Flow-style push-to-talk):**
- **Hold the mic chip — or hold Space anywhere in the reader** — and speak; release to send. Chimes mark the microphone opening and closing. The mic is closed except while held and turns are committed manually (`turn_detection: null` + `input_audio_buffer.commit`), so the assistant can never hear its own voice through the speakers.
- **Double-tap** the chip for a hands-free conversation (`semantic_vad`, barge-in supported); a quick Space tap still toggles playback (moved from keydown to keyup, under a 250 ms hold threshold).
- **Click** the chip for options: all 10 realtime voices, model (2.1 / 2.1-mini), and thinking effort (`session.reasoning.effort`, minimal→xhigh). The same knobs live under **Settings → LLM → Voice assistant**, and both persist via the settings store.
- A caption pill above the player bar shows status and a live transcript; the reader's narration pauses while a session runs.

**How it sees and points at the document:** the whole document is serialized with `⟦n⟧` segment markers (outline included, ~90k-token budget, `read_passage` tool for anything truncated) into the session instructions — sent in the mint request body because data-channel messages cap at ~64–256 KB. The model calls `show_passage` / `clear_highlight`; the reader resolves ranges to segments, reuses the Explain flow's `.explaining` pulse (segment-precise), and scrolls with the existing `scrollNarrationIntoView`.

**Also in this PR:**
- A GPT key now advertises the assistant: provider tagline in Settings and a note in onboarding.
- **Removed the page-jump chip** from the player bar — scrolling is the reader's navigation, and the chip overflowed its fixed 132px column onto the timeline whenever a paged document was open. Margin page markers, the header page count, and the original-page peek all remain.
- Reader tour step for the chip; `llm` tour step for the settings section; `.env.example` documenting the dev key vars.

## Testing

- `npm run quality` green: lint, svelte-check (0 errors), 341/341 unit tests with coverage thresholds (new `assistant-context.ts` at 100% lines), build.
- All 36 Playwright tests pass; visual baselines regenerated for **darwin and linux** (Docker, `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble`) — only the three reader-workspace shots changed (new chip, 120px left column).
- Live-tested end to end with a real microphone: greeting names the document, highlight+scroll tracks the answers, PTT eliminates the self-interruption seen with an open mic.

## Notes & follow-ups

- Realtime pricing is per audio minute (~$0.06/min in + $0.24/min out at current rates); the doc context is cached after the first turn.
- Future: Gemini Live as a second assistant provider; showing the reader's own words in the pill (input transcription); letting the assistant start narration playback.

author: cboettig
body:
Closes #346.

## Problem

`browse_stac_catalog` reported the server-side `STAC_CATALOG_URL` verbatim. On cirrus that is an in-cluster address, so the one line telling a client where the catalog lives was the only URL in the whole session a client couldn't resolve. Still reproducible on `duckdb-mcp.carlboettiger.info` as of this PR:

```
# Available Datasets (219 collections)

STAC catalog: `http://minio-svc.minio.svc.cluster.local:9000/public-data/stac/catalog.json`
```

Meanwhile `get_collection` hands back hrefs on `https://minio.carlboettiger.info` — the exact mirror a client needs. Finding it during yesterday's Ceph outage meant reading `k8s/cirrus-*.yaml` and guessing hostnames.

## Change

1. **`stac.py`** — `public_catalog_url()` reads `STAC_PUBLIC_CATALOG_URL` at call time, defaulting to `STAC_CATALOG_URL`. Same contract as `MCP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` in `tiles/pyramid.py`. Blank/whitespace is treated as unset.
2. **`list_datasets`** — reports the public URL; when the two differ, names the internal one as a labelled aside so the client knows which to put in its config:
   ```
   STAC catalog: `https://minio.carlboettiger.info/public-data/stac/catalog.json`
   (server reads it at http://minio-svc.minio.svc.cluster.local:9000/... — use the first URL in client configs)
   ```
   Covers the `No datasets loaded` branch too — degraded start (#262) is exactly when an operator is hunting for a reachable catalog. A caller-supplied `catalog_url` is echoed unchanged.
3. **`GET /version`** — item 4 of the issue, structured rather than prose:
   ```json
   {"version": "...", "git_sha": "...",
    "stac_catalog_url": "https://minio.carlboettiger.info/public-data/stac/catalog.json",
    "public_base_url": "https://duckdb-mcp.carlboettiger.info"}
   ```
   No MCP session, no auth token, no markdown parsing — a geo-agent app can take `mcp_url` alone and derive its `catalog` at boot, which retires the class of failure behind geo-agent#287. **Public URLs only**: this route is deliberately auth-exempt, so the internal address stays inside authenticated MCP responses (asserted by a test).
4. **`k8s/cirrus-deployment.yaml`** — sets `STAC_PUBLIC_CATALOG_URL`.
5. Docs: env-var table in `deployment.md`; `mirror-failover.md` gains an "ask the head" step and its stale "#346 is a display bug" bullet is corrected.

NRP prod is unaffected — `STAC_CATALOG_URL` there is already public, the two strings are equal, and output is byte-for-byte what it was (asserted by a test).

## Verification

- `395 passed` (full unit suite), including 7 new `TestPublicCatalogUrl` cases and 3 on `/version`.
- Advertised cirrus URL is fetchable from outside the cluster — the value in the manifest is correct, not just plausible:
  ```
  $ curl -sI https://minio.carlboettiger.info/public-data/stac/catalog.json | head -1
  HTTP/2 200
  ```

### Not done here

The cirrus rollout. This k3s cluster isn't in the kubeconfig available to me (only NRP `nautilus`), so it needs to be run from a machine with cirrus access — the deployment tracks `:main`, so after merge:

```
kubectl apply -f k8s/cirrus-deployment.yaml           # picks up STAC_PUBLIC_CATALOG_URL
kubectl rollout status deployment/duckdb-mcp -n mcp
curl -s https://duckdb-mcp.carlboettiger.info/version  # expect stac_catalog_url on minio.carlboettiger.info
```

The issue's second verification step (a geo-agent client configured only from that URL boots and answers the ca-30x30 slice) needs the client-side change to consume `/version`, which lives in geo-agent — worth filing there against #287 once this is deployed.

author: maxachis
body:
Extends the shared schema-comment gate from columns to enums, in both places a comment can live.

## What changes for a consumer repo

1. **A touched enum declaration or member needs a `///` doc comment.** Diff-scoped exactly like the column rule — existing enums stay grandfathered, so this only bites work a PR actually writes.
2. **A touched enum needs a `COMMENT ON TYPE` in the same PR's migration.** Prisma Migrate emits no `COMMENT ON` from `///`, so without this the description exists only in `schema.prisma` and is invisible to psql, BI tools, and every other schema browser.

Rule 2 is skipped unless the datasource provider is `postgresql`, so MySQL/SQLite consumers are unaffected. `env("...")`-indirected providers are treated as not-Postgres: a false skip costs a missing DB comment, a false demand costs a build nobody can make green.

## Why one comment per type and not per member

Postgres has no per-label comment. Verified on PG 15:

```
COMMENT ON TYPE t_demo IS '…'          → COMMENT
COMMENT ON ENUM LABEL t_demo.ALPHA …   → ERROR: syntax error at or near "ENUM"
COMMENT ON VALUE t_demo.ALPHA …        → ERROR: syntax error at or near "VALUE"
```

So folding member descriptions into the one type-level comment isn't a loose approximation of the rule we'd want — it's the strictest rule the engine can express. The failure message says so, and shows the shape.

## Why parity is scoped to added lines

A `COMMENT ON TYPE` written when an enum had two members says nothing about the third, but sits in the migrations tree looking like compliance. Requiring the statement in *this* diff is what keeps the comment tracking the member list. There's a test pinning exactly that (`a COMMENT ON TYPE in an EARLIER migration does not satisfy parity for a new member`).

## Tests

9 new cases, 24 total, all green (`node --test tests/schema-comment-check.test.mjs`). They cover both halves, both ways parity must not be satisfiable, the `@@map`'d type name, and the fail-closed path for an unclassifiable line inside an enum. The test helper now writes nested paths so a fixture migration can live at `migrations/<ts>/migration.sql`.

Fail-closed behavior is preserved throughout — an enum line the parser can't classify exits `CANNOT VERIFY` rather than passing.

## Rollout

Reportal consumes this next, together with a backfill of all 37 of its enums and their 171 members (IMP-173). Other consumers pick it up on their next `install.sh` sync; because both rules are diff-scoped, that sync doesn't red any existing PR.

author: tajaa
body:
## What

Two follow-ons to #107 (which fixed a `**bold**`-shows-as-literal-asterisks bug by stripping the emphasis entirely):

1. **Restore the emphasis, properly this time.** Backend pills carry `**category**` again. Frontend gets a scoped renderer (`work/pages/ChannelView/systemContent.tsx`) that understands `**pairs**` — the one construct Huume's server-composed strings use — and nothing else. `renderSystemContent()` for the message body, `stripEmphasis()` for compact single-line previews (reply banner, quoted stub).
2. **Give Huume presence.** System rows (`sender_id` is null) previously rendered as a centered, unattributed chrome pill. Now:
   - ASCII avatar (`work/components/channels/HuumeAvatar.tsx`) — no asset, renders identically wherever the font stack lands.
   - Named "Huume" in accent color, same avatar/name/timestamp/body layout a human message uses.
   - Mirrored to the right side of the pane (`flex-row-reverse`), so the channel reads as two parties talking instead of one long left-aligned column with an agent's asides mixed in — the standard chat-app pattern for "the other party."

## Why scope the parser to just `**`

Content is server-composed from a closed vocabulary (`_confirmation_text` + the two "Updated" strings in `channels_ws.py`) — there's no user text in it to justify a richer parser. `**` is the only markup those call sites ever emit.

## Tests

- `systemContent.test.tsx` (6) — split behavior, plain no-op, unbalanced-marker safety (a stray `**` must not swallow the sentence tail in a compliance-facing pill), multi-line clarify-question form.
- Backend `test_carries_no_markdown` → `test_emphasizes_only_the_category`: asserts exactly 2 markers wrapping the label (not just "no markdown anywhere").
- `pytest tests/ems/ tests/channels_ws/` — 83 passed, 5 skipped.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` — clean.

## Live verification

Sent a real `@huume` message over the dev WS stack and read the stored row back:

```
SYSTEM PILL: '📋 Logged **Equipment** event (visible to HR admins in Events).'
```

Confirms the backend emits the marker and the frontend has something real to parse.

author: idlepcvr
body:
\`/\` was five folds of prose. The audience for it — a partner, a parent, someone who already cares and just can't picture the day — doesn't read to be reassured, they look. Every fold is now **one diagram and one sentence**:

| fold | the picture |
|---|---|
| what a trade is | two of them side by side, one that worked and one that didn't |
| how one gets made | the loop, with **ME** as the only lit cell — the machine never decides |
| most answers are no | every setup ever found, one dot each, most of them dark |
| it cannot press the button | the severed link: no keys, the route to the exchange goes through him |

## The swing-trading fold is cut, not translated

The prose claimed *"I hold for days or weeks, a day trader goes in and out several times a day, that isn't what I do."* Measured across all 496 hedge fills:

- median hold **2.1 hours**
- 32% close inside the hour, 95% inside a day
- **not one position ever held past 3 days** (longest: 2.8)

Survivable as a loose sentence. As a diagram it would have been the most authoritative-looking element on the page and the only untrue one. The trend underneath is real — volume fell from 137 fills in Feb to 15 in Jul, mean hold roughly tripled since May — but *moving toward* swing trading isn't *is* a swing trader, and this page can't spend its credibility on the difference. **Easy to restore if he disagrees; the docstring says to re-run the hold-time query first.**

## Two rendering faults, found by screenshotting rather than asserting

- The entrance animation faded opacity from 0 with \`fill-mode: both\`, so any render during the delay — headless, print, paused tab — shipped **the hero blank**. It moves now, it never fades. \`home_page.py\` already documents this exact rule for the /system matrix.
- The lit dots carried a glow that made a quarter read as nearly a half, arguing against the caption directly beneath them. The proportion *is* the message, so nothing may inflate it.

## Tests

\`tests/test_explain_page.py\` guards the rules the docstring states, not the markup: the dot grid matches the ledger row for row, no money figures, no jargon, no solicitation while AKA is in wind-down, and both trade outcomes shown — never just the winner. 7 new tests, all passing.

The 3 \`test_plan.py\` failures and 7 collection errors in the full suite are **pre-existing** — identical on the base commit, verified by running the same command on a stash.

Verified visually at 1100px and 390px.

author: seriouslysean
body:
## Closes

Closes #32, closes #44

## What was wrong

Five smaller defects batched in #32, plus #44's vacuous test. `add` was the only pins-file writer that never validated it, exiting 0 over unresolved conflict markers while sorting relocated them. Version verification trusted a pipeline whose exit status was `tr`'s, so a binary printing the pinned version then failing satisfied it — the old code published that binary; the panel reproduced it against the previous release. A version-mismatch die leaked the staging directory. Tool-name validation was a basic regex, so `swift.int` passed the guards and failed later with misleading messages. And `add records a hash for every platform` reported ok when `add` wrote nothing at all.

## The test that fails without this

Six tests (five watched failing, one guarded per #37's precedent):

- `add refuses to write over a pins file with unresolved conflict markers`
- `an install does not verify when the archived binary itself exits nonzero` — the archive-fixture now carries a configurable exit status; against the previous release this published the broken binary and reported ok
- `a version-mismatch install does not leave a staging directory in the cache` — staging brought under the existing EXIT trap
- `path rejects a tool name that known_tools' regex check would silently let through` — new `is_known_tool` does a literal match at all three call sites
- `check names the pins-file line when a regex-matched tool name should be an outright rejection` — add's own half is not CLI-observable (the literal case in `tool_url` dies identically), documented in the suite where it matters
- `add records a hash for every platform the tool publishes` — now guards `add`'s exit status and a non-empty pin line before reading columns, proven by a demonstrated old-body-ok/new-body-FAIL pair

The stale-lock item stays a documented manual step by decision. Two low-severity hardening gaps found by the panel are tracked in a follow-up issue.

Verified: offline 73 passed, 0 failed under sh and dash; `--network` 80 passed, 0 failed on macOS and Linux (container, non-root); reviewer confirmed every new test fails with the fix stashed; shellcheck findings unchanged.

- [x] I watched this test fail on the unfixed code and pass on the fixed code.
- [x] `test/run.sh` passes.
