body:
Raised by accounting.

## Problem

Carmen sells **services** to **Thai juristic persons** (every tenant is a hotel company on Carmen ERP), so the buyer is legally required to withhold 3% income tax at source under ท.ป.4/2528 and remit it to the Revenue Department themselves.

The proforma printed `Grand Total ฿1,059.30` as the amount to transfer. A compliant corporate buyer transfers **฿1,029.60** — so the document stated a figure nobody could legally pay, and the 3% gap landed on the admin reviewing the slip with no basis to approve it.

## Fix

Two rows below the amount-in-words line:

```text
Grand Total                                 ฿1,059.30
      (One Thousand Fifty Nine Baht and Thirty Satang)
WHT (3%) Amount                                (29.70)
Payment Amount                                1,029.60
```

Three rules this respects:

- **WHT is a deduction the buyer makes, not a charge we add.** `Subtotal`, `VAT`, `Grand Total` and `credit_orders.amount_thb` are unchanged — `amount_thb` is the invoiced debt, which was already correct.
- **The base is the ex-VAT subtotal**: `990 × 3% = 29.70`, not `1,059.30 × 3% = 31.78`.
- **A slip short by exactly the WHT is a full payment** — the 3% reaches the Revenue Department in Carmen's name. The admin "Amount due" hint now shows that figure too, so a short slip reads as expected instead of suspicious.

Display-only: **no migration, no new column, no backend change**. WHT is a pure function of `billing_documents.subtotal`, derived at render time.

Terms gained a 5th item asking for the Withholding Tax Certificate (or e-Withholding Tax via bank) — without it the withheld 3% can't be credited against corporate income tax and is simply lost. The printed body stays hardcoded English: fixed format, never translated.

## Changes

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `frontend/src/lib/money.ts` | `WHT_RATE_PCT = 3` + `whtDeduction(subtotal, ratePct)` |
| `frontend/src/components/pricing/ProformaDocument.tsx` | the two rows + terms item 5 |
| `frontend/src/styles/pages/pricing.css` | `.pf-subrow` (regular weight); no print rule needed — inherits `.pf-totals` 8.5pt |
| `frontend/src/components/admin/OrderWorkspace.tsx`, `frontend/src/i18n/dict.ts` | `orev.verify.amountHint` extended with the WHT-deducted amount (EN + TH) |
| `frontend/src/lib/money.test.ts` | 3 cases: 3%-of-net not gross, satang rounding, printed payment amount |
| `changelog/2026-07-31.md`, `docs/Billing_Purchase_Flow.md` | log + a WHT section under Pricing |

Pending release note is recorded in the changelog — batched, so no `VERSION` bump here.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run` — 348 passed (31 files)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean (proves both `en` and `th` got the new interpolation)
- [x] `npm run build` — clean
- [x] `eslint` on all changed files — no warnings
- [x] Manual: `#/pricing` → buy Growth (990) → proforma reads `WHT (3%) Amount (29.70)` / `Payment Amount 1,029.60`, amount-in-words still bound to 1,059.30
- [x] Manual: Ctrl+P — both rows land inside the A4 frame
- [x] Manual: `#/admin/credit-orders` → "Amount due" hint in EN and ไทย

## Not in scope — flagged for finance

Carmen AR will now carry a 3% open residual per invoice until the certificate arrives and finance clears it against WHT receivable. The AR posting (`credit_order_service.py:506-510`) still sends `total/net/vat` only. If that reconciliation turns out to be painful in practice, sending the WHT split to Carmen AR is the follow-up.

body:
Closes #56

Turns the mesh from milestone-level into **session-level** tracking — the core of "single source of truth for every teammate's Claude Code session."

## What it does
`ClaudeSession` now reports its own lifecycle to the injected mesh:
- `session_started` `{dev, branch, kind}` before the agent runs
- `session_heartbeat` `{alive, files_touched}` every `heartbeat_interval` while running (daemon thread) — so #57's `active_sessions()` can distinguish a live session from a dead one
- `session_ended` `{ok, duration_s, files_touched}` in a `finally`

## Design
- Lives in `sessions/` (Lane C) against the **frozen `contracts.Mesh`** — no coupling to the concrete mesh.
- **Best-effort**: SupabaseMesh already swallows errors, so tracking never breaks a run; with no mesh injected it silently no-ops.
- `build_pipeline` now builds the mesh *before* the sessions and passes `mesh` + `config.name` into both.

## Tests
- Real stand-in agent + `FakeMesh`: asserts `session_started` → `session_ended` fire with `kind`/`dev`/`duration`/`files_touched`
- No-mesh path: run still works, no crash
- `uv run pytest` — 223 passed; `ruff` clean

Pairs with **#57** (session-aware mesh reader / `active_sessions()`), which consumes these events for the live dashboard (#59).

author: philipreese
body:
Closes #832

## What

Held-work rendering and wake derivation are now shape-aware — the two halves of the same defect,
one human-facing and one machine-facing:

- **`HeldWorkReconciler.RenderStatus`** branches on `Shape` first: a `memory-proposal` item's
  existence probe is its capture FILE (the ref is the file's path, per #801), and it renders
  `"awaiting operator decision (memory proposal)"` — or an honest
  `"proposal file missing (…)"` when the capture is gone — instead of the misleading
  `"dispatch recorded; lane never started"`. Every other shape, including unknown future ones,
  keeps today's lane rendering exactly; that default is deliberate (there is no registry of
  lane shapes anywhere to positively match against), pinned by its own test, and documented at
  the branch point.
- **`RoomWakeDerivation`/`RoomWakeBridge`** (found by this branch's review): the wake pipeline
  was shape-blind — a capture-file ref can never have a `flow.jsonl`, so every pending memory
  proposal derived a spurious `DispatchOrphaned` wake on every 500ms tick. Guarded in the
  derivation (so a caller handing in a probe anyway cannot resurrect the orphan) and skipped in
  the bridge's probe loop. A proposal waiting on an operator decision is doing exactly what its
  shape does; it wakes no one from the lane machinery.

## Second reader (claude sonnet high)

- **High, fixed**: the wake-pipeline shape-blindness above — confirmed by the reviewer with the
  exact call path (`LaneTerminalProbe.ProbeAsync` on a file ref → `JournalExists` always false →
  `DispatchOrphaned` per tick).
- **Low, fixed**: the reconciler's Escalated arm for memory proposals was untested; now pinned
  (`"escalated to operator"`, the generic escalation line).
- One unverified process note: the reviewer had no shell (the known #789 instrument gap) and
  reviewed current-tree state rather than the diff.

## Verification

- Red proven twice, both against unmodified code: the implementing session's temporary probe
  confirmed today's reconciler renders the misleading lane line for a memory-proposal item
  before any change; the orchestrating session ran the new derivation test against unguarded
  `RoomWake.cs` and observed the spurious orphan wake before the guard landed.
- Seven polarity arms across the two files: lane-with-journal, lane-without-journal (both
  pinned to today's exact lines), proposal-with-capture, proposal-without-capture, escalated
  proposal, unknown-shape default, and proposal-never-wakes-even-with-a-probe-handed-in.
  21/21 green across both touched test files.
- Full `pixi run gates` green on the final tree before push; `recordonce.py` clean (two
  restated passages caught and turned into pointers before ship).

author: minyongp
body:
[back#122](https://github.com/Team-PinLog/back/issues/122)가 곁다리로 지목한 `configuration.md`의 낡음을 고친다. **문서 전용이고 `back#122` 자체를 닫지 않는다** — 그쪽의 본체는 인프라·AI 파트 몫이라 열어 둔다.

## 고친 것 셋

**① 인프라 계약 반영 여부가 거짓이었다**

> ~~`DB_PASSWORD` 외에 아래가 필요합니다. **인프라 계약에 아직 반영되지 않았으므로 배포 전에 요청해야 합니다.**~~

확인해 보니 반영돼 있다. `infra/policy/sealedsecrets/back-prod.yaml`이 허용 키 8개를 규정하고, `infra/secrets/prod/back-owner-secrets.sealedsecret.yaml`로 봉인돼 `apps/prod/back/values.yaml`의 `envFrom`으로 주입된다(S15P11A705-154).

**② `PINLOG_AI_INTERNAL_SECRET`이 표에 없었다**

운영 필수인데 — 없으면 운영 프로파일이 **기동 실패**한다(`AiProcessClient.requireSecret`) — 이 문서에 `PINLOG_AI` 문자열 자체가 **0건**이었다.

**③ `PINLOG_AI_EMBEDDING_PROFILE`은 요청 대상이 아니다**

`application.yml:130`에 리터럴 기본값이 있어 환경변수는 덮어쓰기 수단일 뿐이다([BD-39](https://github.com/Team-PinLog/back/blob/dev/docs/backend/decisions/BD-39-embedding-profile-in-application-config.md)). `PINLOG_AI_BASE_URL`도 비밀값이 아니라 평문 주소다. 둘을 비밀값으로 요청하지 않도록 명시했다.

## 딸려 나온 것 둘

**표에 행 하나를 더하니 아래 문단이 거짓이 됐다.** *"셋 중 **이것만** 기동을 막습니다"* 가 이제 둘이다. 함께 고치면서 두 값이 **같은 이유**로 묶인다는 것을 적었다 — 없어도 뜨게 두면 조용히 망가진다(서명 키는 전면 로그아웃, AI 시크릿은 임베딩이 하나도 안 생기는 것을 아무도 모름).

체크리스트의 *"비밀값은 `DB_PASSWORD`만 환경변수"* 도 같은 계열의 낡음이라 고쳤다.

## 일부러 건드리지 않은 것

**§5의 *"`Team-PinLog/infra`가 정한 주입 계약은 `DB_PASSWORD` 하나입니다"*.** 전역으로 읽으면 틀려 보이지만 `infra/docs/backend-conventions.md`를 확인하니 그 문장이 인용하는 §5의 범위가 datasource·redis라 **지금도 정확하다.** 이번 절이 다루는 `back-owner-secrets`는 별개 경로이므로, 새 절의 첫 문장에 "위 §5의 datasource 계약과 별개로"를 넣어 두 계약이 구분되게 했다.

**`PINLOG_AI_BASE_URL`이 운영에 주입돼 있지 않은 것.** 문서 문제가 아니라 인프라 쪽 미결이라 사실만 적고 back#122로 넘겼다.

author: aleonnet
body:
## O que muda

O caminho padrão do `install.sh` deixa de clonar e compilar: resolve a última release estável (ou a pinada por `--version X.Y.Z`), baixa o bundle (~10 KB) com SHA256 verificado ANTES de abrir o tar, valida o conteúdo antes de tocar o disco e sobe a stack por `docker compose pull` da imagem publicada no GHCR. git sai dos pré-requisitos do caminho padrão (vive em `--from-source` e no auto-despacho por `.git` — instância clonada nunca migra sozinha); `tar` entra.

**Sem bump de versão**: mudança de instalador não altera a versão do App (decisão de 2026-07-31); o `install.sh` chega pelo raw/main no merge.

## Destaques

- Update sem clobber: hash no manifesto (`bundle_sha`) prova "nosso e não editado"; arquivo editado ganha backup datado com aviso nomeando.
- Downgrade detectado exige confirmação interativa (`--yes` não pula).
- Uninstall/doctor ganham o mundo `repo_clone=bundle` com as MESMAS guardas do clone (install_dir + arquivo estranho via manifesto).
- Cross-branch do `af_update_clone` corrigido (achado 1 da Fase 3, refspec explícita) — provado na VM real.
- Achado do E2E corrigido: `un_compose_down` sobrevive a `.env` removido (placeholders via `--env-file`; export morre no shim de sudo).

## Prova

- Bancada 253→291 PASS (casos novos nascidos VERMELHOS antes da implementação); `check_consistency.py` verde; `make test` completo verde.
- **11 mutantes mortos**, cada um reprovando exatamente no caso-alvo.
- **E2E completo na VM lima** (medições reais): install bundle contra a release v1.0.0 pública em 1m07s (pull 17s), smoke OCR/triagem/busca/MCP verde, re-run idempotente 33s, ciclo `--keep-data` com índice sobrevivendo, `--from-source` + re-run cross-branch (1s), purge final limpo.
- Plano revisado ANTES por 3 revisores adversariais locais (3 bloqueantes derrubados); registro completo em `docs/planos_concluidos/fase4a_installsh_sem_clone_bundle_pull.plan.md`.

## Pendência antes do merge

- Smoke Windows (D9) via seam `ATLASFILE_SH_URL` apontando para o raw desta branch.

author: chris17453
body:
Root cause of the wedge B1579 flagged. It is NOT a path-lookup race and NOT cross-CPU; that framing is disproven by both CPUs' stacks at the wedge.

Mechanism: `vt_console_sink` holds VT_STATE across `vtdata::render`. A LAPIC timer interrupt lands inside that section, the IRQ tail runs softirqs, and `FbconFlush -> repaint` spins for the lock the interrupted context on the SAME CPU already holds. Self-deadlock. CPU#1 is parked in `ap_main_x86 -> halt_forever` and never joins scheduling, so no cross-CPU cycle is even possible. VFS, dcache, rename_lock, kthread_use_mm, mount locks and TLB shootdown are all eliminated — none are on the stack.

It looked like a lookup race because the `[UMH-STAGE]` markers are themselves klog calls, so the wedge lands on whichever marker the timer happens to hit.

The real precondition is spin_lock_bh discipline, not SMP: VT_STATE is shared between the FbconFlush softirq and every process-context console write/VT-switch/query, all taken with a plain lock. x86 syscall entry masks IF, so userspace-driven console traffic could never be interrupted mid-section — but a kernel thread runs with interrupts ON, and khelper is simply the first kernel thread that ever wrote to the console. Latent for every future in-kernel klog caller.

Fix:
- fbcon: process-context VT_STATE acquisitions go through `lock_vt()`/`try_lock_vt()` (`Spinlock::lock_bh`); the softirq's own acquisition stays plain since it is already bh-accounted; `repaint()` split from `flush_softirq()`.
- sched::bh: `local_bh_enable` no longer drains softirqs or takes a reschedule when called from a hard-IRQ handler — Linux's `!in_interrupt()` gate was missing. Adds `local_bh_enable_no_drain`/`BhGuardNoDrain`, used by the klog sink since it is reachable from inside any other subsystem's critical section and must not run handlers inline on the way out; nothing is lost because the sink re-raises FbconFlush.

Evidence: 5 new hosted tests in an ungated fbcon module (count 35 -> 40), one of which encodes the BUG SHAPE (drain runs the handler, handler reaches a held lock) and fails against the old code; plus a sched::bh hard-IRQ test (4 -> 5). `cargo test -p fbcon` 40, `-p sched` 790, `-p softirq` 6, 0 failed. Boot x86_64 SMP=2: all five UMH probes report (previously hung on the third), no SMP-STALL, basic.target 9.3s, graphical.target 10.4s. Boot aarch64 SMP=2: all five probes, sysinit 21.6s, basic 22.3s, multi-user 29.6s.

Flagged for a separate lane: the x86 AP parks in halt_forever and never schedules, so `-smp 2` currently buys no parallelism on x86 and the cross-CPU stall detector has no second observer.

author: iwanabethatguy
body:
## What is this PR solving?

Part of #10263 (stacked on #10532; supersedes #10533, which could not be reopened after its branch was amended).

#10532 merges an already-loaded shared dependency only when partial `import()` usage proves the extra exports unobservable. When the namespace is observed opaquely (`export const app = import('./app.js')`, `Object.keys(ns)`, rest-destructuring) or a read targets an unexported name, Rolldown still split — Rollup emits 3 chunks there via its `generateFacades` fallback (`Chunk.ts` includes `module.namespace` in the chunk, exports it, and call sites extract it with `.then(n => n.a)`).

## How

Rolldown already owns that exact machinery for eliminated facade chunks: `common_chunk_exported_facade_chunk_namespace`, the narrowed simulated namespace, the cross-chunk namespace export, and the finalizer's `rewrite_dynamic_import_for_merged_entry` (`import('./chunk.js').then(n => n.<alias>)`, all formats and wrap kinds). This PR opts the surviving dynamic entry chunk into it from the already-loaded pass: register the entry in the map, narrow its namespace statement to link-retained getters, include the namespace/wrapper symbols (`SymbolIncludeReason::SimulatedFacadeChunk`), and record the `__exportAll` demand before standalone runtime extraction so placement stays normal.

The #10532 fast path still wins when provable, so the issue's own graph keeps the leaner no-extraction output.

Extraction is refused when the simulated namespace cannot reproduce the entry's interface:
- a statically known `then` export — the chunk namespace would become thenable and `import()` would assimilate before the extraction callback runs (`already_loaded_then_export_keeps_split`);
- dynamic exports, e.g. a CJS `export *` (`already_loaded_cjs_star_keeps_split`) — the external-star case is then lifted by #10559 on top of this PR.

## Tests

- `already_loaded_opaque_namespace_extraction` — `Object.keys` observes exactly the entry's exports; 3 chunks
- `already_loaded_unexported_read_extraction` — `ns.missing` stays `undefined` through the extracted namespace; 3 chunks
- `already_loaded_then_export_keeps_split`, `already_loaded_cjs_star_keeps_split` — refusals pinned; 4 chunks with source-faithful runtime behavior
- `dynamic_dominator_with_exports_no_merge` — now inlines `sharedDynamic` into `dynamic1` (snapshot-only change; its runtime assertions are unchanged)

All `_test.mjs` files execute the emitted output. Full Rust suite passes.

body:
The "buttons from different design systems" problem, solved at the root, plus the liveliness pass.

## The diagnosis

Two design systems were living in this repo. The app's own (`.pill`, `bg-primary`, DSM-minimal) — and a complete **shadcn scaffold in `components/ui`: forty components including a rival `button.tsx`, of which the app imported seven**. Meanwhile `/profile` still spoke a third dialect: v0's square `bg-foreground text-background` blocks.

  - `.btn` + `primary/secondary/ghost` × `sm/lg/icon` — press-scale, hover lift-with-shadow on primary

author: cbb330
body:
## Summary
Problem: I have a feature which I want to ramp on the server. but I also don't want to prevent table owners from self-serve opting in. A generic function to handle that overlap doesn't exist today. 

Extend the existing `TableFeatureToggle` with self-service table overrides while preserving its server-managed targeting API.

An explicit `<featureId>.enabled=true|false` table property wins. When the property is absent, activation delegates to the server toggle. Server rules now support trailing-`*` prefix matching independently for database and table names.

## Changes

- [ ] Client-facing API Changes
- [x] Internal API Changes
- [ ] Bug Fixes
- [x] New Features
- [ ] Performance Improvements
- [ ] Code Style
- [ ] Refactoring
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests

Adds a binary-compatible default method to `TableFeatureToggle`:

```java
isFeatureActivatedWithOverride(TableDto tableDto, String featureId)
```

It is deliberately **not** an overload of `isFeatureActivated`. The two carry different safety contracts, and a distinct name makes the difference visible at the call site: authorization gates such as `enable_mor` decide whether a user may write a preserved table property, so they must keep using the server-only `isFeatureActivated(String, String, String)`. The override-honoring form reads a property the gated user can write.

An override that is neither `true` nor `false` fails closed: it is logged and the feature is treated as inactive. The gate is evaluated on the table-load path, so throwing would turn a typo like `read-bridge.enabled=flase` into a `400` and make the table unloadable.

Extends the existing toggle rule matcher while preserving exact and `*` matching:

- `tracking.events` matches exactly.
- `tracking_*.events_*` matches database and table prefixes.
- `*.*` matches every table.

## Testing Done

- [ ] Manually Tested on local docker setup. Please include commands ran, and their output.
- [x] Added new tests for the changes made.
- [ ] Updated existing tests to reflect the changes made.
- [ ] No tests added or updated. Please explain why. If unsure, please feel free to ask for help.
- [ ] Some other form of testing like staging or soak time in production. Please explain.

Ran:

```shell
JAVA_HOME=$(/usr/libexec/java_home -v 17) ./gradlew \
  :services:tables:test \
  --tests 'com.linkedin.openhouse.tables.toggle.TableFeatureToggleTest' \
  :services:housetables:test \
  --tests 'com.linkedin.openhouse.housetables.mock.WildcardTableToggleRuleMatcherTest' \
  -x CopyGitHooksTask
```

All 12 focused tests passed, covering server fallback, explicit opt-in and opt-out, fail-closed handling of unparseable overrides, exact matching, wildcard matching, and paired database/table prefix matching.

# Additional Information

- [ ] Breaking Changes
- [ ] Deprecations
- [x] Large PR broken into smaller PRs, and PR plan linked in the description.

This is an independent OSS foundation for the read-bridge stack in #645 and the corresponding `li-openhouse` implementation PRs. Feature-specific default derivation remains outside this PR.

Note for reviewers: the matcher change widens any existing `table_toggle_rule` row whose pattern ends in `*` but is not exactly `*`. Those previously matched nothing. Worth auditing HTS before merge.

author: natsuki-engr
body:
This is direction 1 in the issue: returning an array stays unsupported, and the failure says so.

The alternative, supporting the array return, is on `fix/jsx-component-returning-array`. **The two are alternatives, not a pair.** Only one should be merged, and I will close the other.

## Problem

A function component that returns an array reaches `escapeToBuffer()` in `src/utils/html.ts`, which starts with `str.search(escapeRe)`. The request responds 500 with `TypeError: str.search is not a function`, naming an internal helper rather than the code that has to change.

## Solution

`JSXFunctionNode.toStringToBuffer()` gets a branch for arrays, which throws instead:

```
A function component must not return an array. Wrap the elements in a Fragment: <>...</>
```

No type changes are needed. The type layer already rejects the code with `TS2786`, so this only makes the runtime agree with what the types already say.

`hono/jsx/dom` renders an array-returning component correctly, and this PR leaves that difference in place. Removing it is what the other direction does.

## Tests

`src/jsx/index.test.tsx` asserts the thrown message. The test needs `@ts-expect-error` on the JSX expression, which doubles as a check that the type layer still rejects it.

author: murderteeth
body:
### Summary

Adds `review-pr-workflow`, a higher-horsepower companion to `review-pr`. Instead of one agent reading the whole diff, it fans review out across parallel lenses and then puts every finding in front of a verifier prompted to refute it. This targets the main failure mode of automated review — confident, plausible, wrong findings landing in someone's PR.

`review-pr` is unchanged and remains the right tool for routine reviews. This skill costs many times more tokens.

### How to review

`skills/review-pr-workflow/SKILL.md` is the whole change; the README row is bookkeeping.

Read in this order:

1. **Phase 0 (main loop)** — everything racy stays out of the fan-out. Subagents share one working directory, so branch checkout happens once up front and no agent starts a dev server.
2. **Tier Detection** — the part most worth arguing with. Two rules govern it: sensitivity can only upgrade, size can only downgrade, and sensitivity wins. Ambiguity escalates rather than downgrades, because the failure that matters is under-reviewing a small dangerous diff. The sensitive-path list is tuned by hand and is the thing most likely to need adjustment for what we actually ship.
3. **The workflow script** — five lenses pipelined into per-finding verification. Blockers get a three-vote panel at full tier. `MAX_VERIFY_PER_LENS` bounds the agent count and logs whatever it drops.
4. **Phase 4** — Playwright runs once here, not in the fan-out, then the review renders in `review-pr`'s existing format behind its existing approval gate.

Two deliberate constraints worth checking I actually held:

- The workflow returns findings and **cannot post**. Rendering, approval, and posting all stay in the main loop.
- A finding that fails verification never reaches the author. If `codex` errors or returns nothing parseable, that counts as refuted — unverified claims don't get published.

### Test plan

- [x] Manual: run end-to-end against a real PR — confirmed working
- [x] Automated: workflow script parses (`node --check` under an async wrapper, since top-level `return` is legal in workflow scripts but not in a plain module)
- [x] Manual: exercise `verify-agent=codex` — the codex path's stdout parsing has not been run yet
- [ ] Manual: confirm tier detection picks `light` and `skip` correctly on small and docs-only PRs

### Risk / impact

Low blast radius — this adds a new skill and touches no existing one. Nothing here writes to a repo under review; every workflow agent is read-only, and the GitHub write path is unchanged from `review-pr`, including its approval gate.

Two honest caveats:

- **Agent count can exceed the usual guideline.** `MAX_VERIFY_PER_LENS = 4` bounds it, but a full-tier review with several blockers can reach 25–30 agents, since verifier count scales with findings. That's inherent to verifying each claim rather than a defect, but it's a real cost. Lower the constant for a harder ceiling.
- **Lightly exercised.** One successful end-to-end run. The codex verifier path and the `light`/`skip` tiers haven't been run. The lens prompts may need tuning once we see whether they produce findings at the right granularity.

Rollback is deleting the directory and the README row.

##### Security

Four security vulnerabilities have been identified, and fixed, in this release. Users are advised to update gh to version `v2.97.0` as soon as possible.

Several commands (including `gh gist view`, `gh api`, `gh pr diff`, `gh release download --output -`, `gh codespace logs`, `gh skills preview`, and `gh agent-task view`/`create`) printed externally controlled content without neutralizing terminal escape sequences, allowing escape sequence injection into a user's terminal.

Some request URLs were built without escaping their variable path components, so a value containing URL path metacharacters could alter the request path and cause `gh` to address a different resource than intended.

See <https://github.com/cli/cli/security/advisories/GHSA-4fjg-2h4q-fwg3> for more information.

`gh auth status` (without `--show-token`) could print a portion of the authentication token in plaintext for token types whose format contains an underscore after the prefix, such as `github_pat_*`, `ghs_*`, and `ghu_*`.

See <https://github.com/cli/cli/security/advisories/GHSA-cg6r-mpgc-h9mm> for more information.

`gh attestation verify` built the certificate matcher from `--signer-repo` and `--signer-workflow` without escaping regex metacharacters, so a lookalike repository or workflow name could satisfy a matcher intended for a trusted signer and bypass attestation verification.

## Summary

The workflow fetched it once after about thirteen seconds, received 404, and failed after immutable registry mutation. Shell-redirected curl retries could also preserve partial response bytes.

author: tmcinerney
body:
Stops the macOS keychain re-prompting for the login password on every upgrade.

## The cause

An ad-hoc signature's designated requirement **is** the code hash:

```
granola 0.5.1     designated => cdhash H"f0fb14519cab7d8e1e487ba5e6459652f3bf3d42"
a local build     designated => cdhash H"44e6ec1da4014e023a095b85b5a4533a0e81c1c6"
```

The keychain pins an "always allow" grant to that requirement, so every build is
a different application to it and the grant never matches twice. Compare a signed
app, which updates freely without re-prompting:

```
Granola.app   designated => identifier "com.granola.app" and anchor apple generic and certificate ...
```

## The fix

Sign the two darwin binaries with a fixed self-signed certificate. Verified
locally — two genuinely different binaries produce byte-identical requirements:

```
t1 (0.5.2 release)   designated => identifier "com.tmcinerney.granola" and certificate root = H"2af6bd95..."
t2 (a debug build)   designated => identifier "com.tmcinerney.granola" and certificate root = H"2af6bd95..."
```

`certificate root` rather than `leaf` because a self-signed cert is its own root.

## The verification step is not defensive padding

While prototyping, `codesign` **exited 0 while refusing to sign**:

```
$ codesign --force -s "granola-cli self-signed" ... t1
  granola-cli self-signed: no identity found
$ echo $?
  0
```

The identity was present but untrusted (`CSSMERR_TP_NOT_TRUSTED`), and the binary
kept its ad-hoc requirement. Checking exit status alone would ship unsigned
binaries whose only symptom is users' password prompts silently returning. So the
step asserts the requirement contains `certificate root` and no longer contains
`cdhash`, and fails the build otherwise. It also refuses to run at all if the
signing secrets are absent.

Trust is established in a throwaway keychain on the runner (`add-trusted-cert`,
user domain, no sudo required), which is added to the search list only for the
duration of the signing step and removed afterwards.

## Deliberately not Developer ID

These are not notarized and Gatekeeper rejects them. Verified that this doesn't
matter for the distribution path:

```
Homebrew binary   attrs: com.apple.provenance      <- no quarantine
Homebrew tarball  attrs: com.apple.provenance      <- no quarantine
Safari download   com.apple.quarantine: 0083;...;Safari;...
```

Gatekeeper only evaluates quarantined files, and `brew` fetches via curl, which
never sets the attribute. Only a browser download of a Releases tarball would trip
it. A Developer ID would additionally buy notarization at $99/yr, which buys
nothing for this problem.

## Key custody

The certificate is in 1Password (`granola-cli macOS code signing`, Dev Secrets)
and mirrored to repo secrets. GitHub secrets are write-only, so that item is the
**only** recoverable copy — losing it means future releases sign with a different
certificate, changing the requirement and permanently re-triggering prompts.
Restore commands are in `RELEASING.md`. Expires 2036-07-28.

## Not yet proven

That an "always allow" grant actually survives a version bump. That needs two
consecutive signed releases: grant on 0.5.3, then confirm silence on 0.5.4. I'm
not calling this fixed until that's demonstrated.

body:
Publishes a self-contained canonical v8 specification for the repository's `1.0.0` source state, based on the latest `main` and a parallel audit of the implementation, maintained docs, and current first-party Modal contracts.

## Summary

- replace the active v7 specification with a self-contained v8 contract anchored to `71fc9e6`
- classify stable, Alpha, benchmark-only, application-owned, and historical surfaces explicitly
- document native X11 input, binary and observation transports, safe Modal Function handoff, trajectory leases, durable operation receipts, result-loss reobservation, warm capacity, and hosted run-gateway boundaries
- archive v7 with a structured disposition and update every maintained spec link and ownership test
- add the primary-source Modal upstream audit used to review 1.5.x, V2, snapshots, filesystem APIs, networking, named Images, and Volumes v2
- update the lock from Modal 1.5.2 to 1.5.3
- explicitly scope every daemon Connect Token to port 8080, including sync/async create, attach, Function borrow, runner, and benchmark paths, with regression assertions

## Why

v7 began as the May 14 hardened-daemon truth-up and had become incomplete after 371 commits. It still carried forward v6 placeholders and stale roadmap language while the source had added major safety and orchestration contracts. A canonical document must describe the current source without promoting experimental observation semantics, benchmark candidates, or example control planes into the stable core API.

The upstream audit also found that Modal 1.5.1 added explicit Connect Token port scoping. The code hardening is included here because v8 should not canonically describe daemon-only credentials while the implementation relies on an upstream default instead of binding the token to port 8080.

## Boundary

- no provider-owned model loop or hosted multi-tenant service is added to core
- no public route, action, or response schema changes
- no Modal V2 or VM Sandbox path is promoted to the production default
- the package remains an untagged `1.0.0` source state and is not presented as a PyPI release
- three pre-existing untracked research notes were excluded from the commit

author: skearnes
body:
Works the open decision from #17 dimension by dimension. Both candidates carry the same normalizations settled in #16 — united messages to canonical floats, structural identifiers collapsed to one `smiles`, every other identifier kept — so this compares shapes, not coverage.

**EAV wins the axes that decide whether a consumer gets an answer at all.** Selection 13× (0.068 s vs 0.90 s). Wide analysis 2–3×, against expectation, because ORD is sparse enough that a fact table touching 7,026 pressure rows beats a columnar scan of 2.43M mostly-null ones. Flat predicates with no `UNNEST` trap. And schema discovery via `SELECT DISTINCT path` — 81 paths in 0.013 s, reporting what is populated rather than what is declarable.

**The projection wins the axes that decide whether the answer is right.** Declared types, where EAV splits across `value_text`/`value_double`/`value_bool` and reading the wrong one returns nulls rather than an error. A schema that is its own contract, where a typo in an EAV `path` yields zero rows instead of a planner error. And co-membership by construction: "a component that is both named THF and over 5 mL" is native at 0.80 s, where EAV needs `entity_key` in the join and silently answers "a reaction containing an X and a Y" if you omit it — measured, those return 0 and 5,021.

**The finding neither shape was chosen for** is that the projection's core argument does not survive leaving DuckDB. Parquet does store each struct leaf as its own column chunk — but `pandas.read_parquet` cannot select a nested leaf by dotted path at all (`ArrowInvalid`), so a pandas consumer reads the whole `conditions` tree as `object` dtype and traverses dicts per row. The columnar-pruning advantage is DuckDB- and pyarrow-specific; polars sits in between; the flat table reads identically in all four.

Size and build time are still measuring and the entry says so rather than guessing — that measurement decides which artifact ships, and the conclusions section will be rewritten when it lands. Two conclusions hold regardless: the `UNNEST` trap must be documented wherever the nested form ships, and an entity key must be carried wherever the flat form ships. The tier-1 view survives either way as the flat starter table, and is the only one of the three that previews usefully in Data Studio.

author: benpeter
body:
Two small fixes from watching the first live run, neither needing a chain relaunch.

**The boot window.** `barn` gives the worker no boot prompt, so until her driver hands her something
she has no transcript of her own. The sweep then matched the newest file carrying her boot phrase,
which was the previous run's, and she read `stuck` on a transcript that had stopped moving before this
run began. Observed live at 00:57, self-healing at her first hand, but it recurs at every launch and
two of her nine historical sessions carry the phrase nowhere at all.

`.barn-panes` is written by barn at `up`, so its mtime dates the run: anything last written before it
belongs to an earlier run and is now skipped. A role that then resolves to nothing yields
`turn_open=0` and therefore `parked`, which is the right answer for an agent nobody has handed
anything. The floor is per-caller and optional, so the no-floor path is byte-unchanged.

**A resolution miss now says so.** Both `$PWD` bugs (#42, #44) hid for hours because "cannot resolve"
degrades silently to the screen-reading path this was written to replace. Safe, and completely
invisible. One line to stderr, rate-limited to once per process so a per-beat caller cannot flood.
Diagnostics only, the verdict is unchanged.

Tests: 445 green, was 436. The boot-window case is a direct reproduction, asserting `parked` where the
live chain produced `stuck`.

Verified against the running chain: run floor reads 00:51:00 and all three roles still resolve
correctly through both the function and the CLI path stuck-check uses.

No relaunch needed. `liveness-read.sh` is re-execed per call, so this lands on the next beat.

author: boarqing
body:
Stacked on #596 (base: `feat/linattn-scratch-mem`). Review the last commit only; retarget to `main` once #596 lands.

## What

The chunk-parallel gated_delta prefill (#589) sizes its device scratch by `nchunks = seq_len / 32`, so the arena grows without bound with prompt length. #596 made that arena session-scoped instead of per-call, which removed the per-layer alloc/free churn but not the growth. This bounds the growth itself: the three passes now run over a fixed window of `LA_WINDOW_CHUNKS = 64` chunks (2048 tokens) at a time, so the arena is sized per window rather than per sequence.

Measured through the exported `hip_linear_attention_prefill_scratch_bytes` (B=1, Hkv=32, dk=dv=128, i.e. Qwen3.5-9B):

| seq_len | before | after | reduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1842 | 116.2 MiB | 116.2 MiB | 1.00x (single window) |
| 4096 | 256.5 MiB | 129.3 MiB | 1.98x |
| 13529 | 847.7 MiB | 129.3 MiB | 6.56x |
| 16384 | 1026.1 MiB | 129.3 MiB | 7.94x |
| 32768 | 2052.1 MiB | 129.3 MiB | 15.9x |

The arena is flat at 129.3 MiB from 2049 tokens up. On a 128 GB APU where host and device share the pool this is the difference between the prefill fitting alongside the weights and not.

## How

Each kernel gains `nchunks_win` and `chunk_begin`. The scratch index becomes window-local (`cw`) while the query/key/value/decay/output index stays global (`chunk_begin + cw`), so only the addressing splits — the math per chunk is untouched.

The scan (pass 2) was already sequential over chunks, so windowing only changes where its running state lives between launches. Across windows it hands off through a small fp16 carry buffer rather than re-reading `state`: the running state is fp16 in LDS, and a round trip through a narrower `T` (bf16 keeps 8 mantissa bits vs fp16's 10) would perturb it at every window boundary. `is_first` seeds from `state`, `is_last` publishes to `state`, and the carry (1 MiB) is only allocated when there is more than one window.

Ordering needs no extra synchronisation: the three passes are issued back-to-back on one stream, so pass 3 of a window has finished reading `Uloc`/`W`/`S0` before pass 1 of the next window overwrites them.

**Single-window prefills are bit-identical to before** — `is_first == is_last`, the carry is never touched and never allocated, and the layout is unchanged (116.2 MiB at 1842 tokens, above).

64 chunks was chosen so a window still launches `B*Hkv*64` = 2048 blocks at Hkv=32, ~51 blocks per CU on the 40-CU gfx1151 — far above what it needs to stay saturated, so the chunk-parallel decomposition keeps its parallelism.

## Test

Local, Qwen3.5-9B (bf16) on Strix Halo / gfx1151:

- 13529-token prompt: 24 chunk-parallel dispatches per forward (one per LA layer) under `HIPDNN_EP_DEBUG`, zero fallbacks to the per-token path, i.e. all 7 windows go through the windowed path.
- Output stays coherent at both short (274-token) and long (13.5k-token) prompts.
- Scratch numbers above read back from the built DLL, not computed on paper.

TTFT, 13529-token prompt, interleaved before/after (DLL swapped in place, 20 s settle, 3 rounds, arms alternating within a round) — full numbers and caveats in [this comment](https://github.com/ROCm/hip-ep/pull/606#issuecomment-5139478794):

| round | before | after | delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 (cold) | 35032.6 ms | 35807.7 ms | +775 (+2.2%) |
| 2 | 41478.6 ms | 39842.1 ms | −1637 (−4.0%) |
| 3 | 41149.9 ms | 39947.2 ms | −1203 (−2.9%) |

The `before` arm alone drifted +6446 ms between rounds 1 and 2 on identical code, so round 1 is a cold machine and the drift is several times the effect size. Across the settled rounds 2-3 the windowed path is 1420 ms faster (−3.4%); a drift-corrected estimate over all three rounds agrees in direction (−1960 ms). The claim I'd stand behind is **no TTFT regression**, with a likely small gain — the memory bound is the point of the change, and that number is exact rather than measured.

Draft until #596 lands.

author: agent-smith-ddp
body:
## Summary

Companion to [ddp-open-states#40](https://github.com/Digital-Democracy-Project/ddp-open-states/pull/40) — `run-scrape.sh` no longer archives bill documents at all; that's now a standalone `run-archive.sh <state>` script, which needs its own independent schedule here.

**Why this needed to happen:** the old design coupled the scrape job's incremental-cutoff marker write to the archive step finishing too. A run whose archive step ran long or died left the cutoff stuck, making the next run slower and more likely to also miss its own archive window — a compounding failure mode, observed live (a WA run's archive step took 1h45m+ after scrape+import had already finished cleanly). Full writeup in `ddp-open-states/PLAN-incremental-scraping.md`, "Reopened 2026-07-31."

## Changes

- `src/ddp_sync/pipelines/openstates_archive.py` (new) — `run_archive_jobs()` fans out `run-archive.sh` across every `ARCHIVE_ENABLED_STATES` jurisdiction concurrently, mirroring the existing secondary-states scrape job's `asyncio.gather` shape.
- `scheduler.py` — new `_register_openstates_archive_jobs()`, registered alongside (not inside) the scrape registration.
- `config/sync_schedule.yaml` — new top-level `openstates_archive` block (`05:00` UTC daily, same jurisdiction list as `ARCHIVE_ENABLED_STATES`).
- `triggers.py` — matching `POST /trigger/openstates-archive/{target}` manual trigger (`all` or a single jurisdiction), same shape as the existing scrape trigger.

## Not done yet

The live scheduler process (uvicorn, already running) registers jobs once at startup — this needs an explicit restart to take effect, which affects every other job that scheduler runs (Voatz sync, Webflow batch, votebot eval, etc.). That's a deliberate separate decision, not bundled into this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m py_compile` on all changed/new files
- [x] `yaml.safe_load` on the config

author: solotzg
body:
<!--

Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: ref #66658

Problem Summary:

For an ordered query with a small `LIMIT`, asynchronous executors below the Limit can admit much more work than the result needs. In #66658, the query returned 1,000 rows, while the ordered outer `IndexRangeScan` read 392,857 rows and the table lookup processed more than 273,000 rows.

The excess work consumes TiDB and TiKV CPU, memory, network, I/O, and RU. With `keepOrder=true`, a slow leading task also prevents completed later tasks from being returned, so continued prefetch can amplify a transient slowdown and increase cluster load further.

### What changed and how does it work?

This PR introduces statement-local adaptive admission control for eligible ordered LIMIT scans. It is guarded by an experimental GLOBAL/SESSION Boolean variable. Freshly bootstrapped clusters persist the variable as ON. Clusters upgraded from an earlier bootstrap version materialize it as OFF when the value is absent, while an existing explicit value is preserved. It can be disabled to restore the existing executor behavior for subsequent statements:

```sql
tidb_enable_adaptive_limit_scan
```

The split rollout policy uses three defaults: the generic SysVar fallback is OFF, initial cluster bootstrap writes ON, and bootstrap version 284 writes OFF only when an upgraded cluster has no persisted value.

The first version supports these executor shapes:

```text
Limit
└─Projection*
  └─IndexLookUpJoin (ordered outer property)
    └─Projection* (outer)
      └─IndexLookUp (keep order)

Limit
└─Projection*
  └─IndexLookUp (keep order)
```

Only cardinality-preserving Projection operators may appear between Limit and a recognized executor. The IndexLookUp must keep order, use concurrency greater than one, and must not use partition-table mode, grouped ranges, a merge-sort double-read path, or IndexLookUp pushdown. A direct IndexLookUp with an existing pushed-down LIMIT is also skipped because that path is already bounded. Unsupported plans retain the existing execution path.

The controller is owned by one statement execution and does not use SQL digest history or shared state. Its demand is:

```text
demandRows = LIMIT offset + count
```

For IndexLookUpJoin, the controller maintains two independent logical budgets because they use different units:

- the outer-row window bounds how far IndexLookUpJoin can read ahead;
- the lookup-handle window estimates how many handles are justified by the remaining outer demand and the observed handle-to-row yield.

For a direct IndexLookUp, there is no Join outer stage, so the controller uses a lookup-only mode and estimates handle demand directly from the remaining LIMIT output.

Lookup admission separates the logical handle budget `B` from the execution batch size `Q`. The physical lookup window is:

```text
min(maxLookupWindow, ceil(B / Q) * Q)
```

This bounds aggregate admission while avoiding a sequence of inefficient tiny table lookup RPCs. `Q` is capped by `tidb_index_lookup_size`, and the aggregate physical window is capped by `tidb_index_lookup_size * tidb_index_lookup_concurrency`.

The initial direct-reader batch respects the existing paging decision. When the physical IndexLookUp uses paging, a small LIMIT can start with the small logical window. For non-paging execution, including plans whose expected count exceeds the paging threshold, the initial execution batch remains at least `tidb_max_chunk_size` and no larger than `tidb_index_lookup_size`. This avoids trading normal scan throughput for a smaller `actRows` value.

After completed work is consumed in result order, the controller observes actual outer-row-to-join-row and handle-to-table-row yields. It combines cumulative feedback with the most recent four productive samples. Windows may shrink immediately, while growth is limited to at most 2x per progress epoch. A fully drained zero-output phase grows the affected logical window; the lookup stage can also grow its execution batch so a long low-selectivity range does not degrade into many tiny tasks.

If one DistSQL chunk returns more handles than the current reservation can admit, the remaining handles stay in a memory-tracked pending buffer. They cannot enter a table lookup task until a later reservation succeeds.

When Limit obtains `offset + count` rows, reaches EOF, or closes, the controller stops new admission and wakes blocked workers. Context cancellation and deadlines remain errors and do not receive new reservations.

The feature does not rewrite `tidb_distsql_scan_concurrency`, change an existing `kv.Request.Concurrency`, or install a shared coprocessor request limiter. Existing batch and concurrency settings remain hard upper bounds.

`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` exposes compact statement-local accounting. IndexLookUpJoin reports both stages:

```text
adaptive:{outer:1000/1000, lookup:1024/718, outstanding:0/1024, blocked:outer=10.4ms,lookup=12.3ms}
```

A direct IndexLookUp reports only its lookup stage:

```text
adaptive:{lookup:1/1, outstanding:0, blocked:0s}
```

The counters describe admitted and consumed work plus admission wait time. They do not expose internal window values because those are controller implementation details.

This mechanism bounds future TiDB-side admission. It does not synchronously cancel work already dispatched, change worker counts inside an existing SelectResult, or hard-limit raw keys, bytes, or time scanned inside one TiKV request. It does not yet support unordered IndexJoin, IndexHashJoin, Apply, IndexMerge, MPP, or an executor-side Selection between Limit and the recognized reader.

The design, correctness invariants, eligibility rules, current limitations, and future extensions are documented in `docs/design/2026-07-31-adaptive-limit-scan.md`.

### Check List

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- [x] Unit test
- [ ] Integration test
- [x] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)
- [ ] No need to test
  > - [ ] I checked and no code files have been changed.
  > <!-- Or your custom  "No need to test" reasons -->

Unit tests and local checks:

```bash
./tools/check/failpoint-go-test.sh pkg/executor/internal/exec -run '^TestAdaptiveLimitController' -count=1
./tools/check/failpoint-go-test.sh pkg/executor -run '^(TestAdaptiveLimitExecution|TestAdaptiveLimitDirectIndexLookUpExecution|TestAdaptiveLimitEligibility|TestIndexLookUpAdaptiveLimitRuntimeStats)$' -count=1
./tools/check/failpoint-go-test.sh pkg/sessionctx/variable -run 'TestNewSessionVars|TestGlobalSystemVariableInitialValue' -count=1
./tools/check/failpoint-go-test.sh pkg/session -run 'TestUpgradeToVerFunctionsCheck|TestAdaptiveLimitScanClusterDefaults' -count=1
make
make lint
git diff --check
```

The tests cover controller accounting and growth, independent outer and lookup budgets, execution-batch rounding, zero-output progress, cancellation and cleanup, pending-handle memory accounting, result and order equivalence, OFFSET and EOF, feature ON/OFF behavior, eligibility guards, unchanged keep-order request concurrency, compact runtime statistics, direct IndexLookUp paging and non-paging initial batch rules, fresh-cluster bootstrap defaults, upgraded-cluster defaults, GLOBAL/SESSION inheritance, and preservation of explicit values.

Manual issue-scale, multi-Region E2E test:

1. Build TiDB and start one TiDB, one PD, and three TiKV stores.

```bash
make
tiup playground nightly --db 1 --pd 1 --kv 3 --tiflash 0 --without-monitor --db.binpath=/Users/solotzg/Work/tidb/bin/tidb-server
```

## Summary

A batch of interaction polish, sharing/SEO metadata, and rendering fixes for the skills marketplace.

## Interaction & Motion

- **Scroll-triggered entrances**: catalog cards and the "Browse skills" heading now animate in via `whileInView` as they enter the viewport, instead of all animating on initial page load (below-fold cards no longer play their animation unseen)
- **Header scroll state**: the header starts borderless and gains a light border + faint shadow (`--shadow-header`) once the page is scrolled past 8px
- **Theme toggle**: the icon spins in with a spring (rotate + scale) when the theme changes
- **Modal back-to-top**: long skill content shows a circular accent button after ~240px of scrolling that smooth-scrolls the content back to top; content scroll resets when the modal opens or the skill changes
- **Modal state transitions**: loading skeleton / error / markdown content now swap through a quick crossfade instead of a hard cut
- Footer top margin reduced (96px → 48px) to tighten the page rhythm

## Sharing & SEO

- **Dynamic document titles**: `generateMetadata` reads `?skill=<slug>` and emits "{Skill name} · Flc's Skills" plus the skill's own description, so shared links open with the correct title (a client-side effect keeps the tab title in sync when opening/closing the modal without a navigation)
- **Open Graph / Twitter Card**: `metadataBase`, OG image (1200×630, brand-consistent, generated from the brand mark), `summary_large_image`; per-skill OG titles/descriptions flow automatically from the page metadata
- **robots.txt + sitemap.xml** added
- Note: the home route moved from static (○) to dynamic (ƒ) because metadata now depends on `searchParams`; the skills dataset is cached in memory so the cost is negligible

## Fixes

- **Markdown tables now render**: `remark-gfm` was missing, so GFM tables (used by `github-release-notes-writer` and `github-release-pr-writer`) rendered as raw pipe text. Tables render in a rounded bordered wrapper with horizontal scroll for wide content. Strikethrough, task lists, and autolinks are also enabled
- **Body-text links underlined** (45% accent decoration) — links in skill content no longer rely on color alone (WCAG 1.4.1)
- **Modal no longer overflows on mobile**: the panel is a flex column capped at `calc(100dvh - 2rem)` with a fixed header/footer and an internally scrolling content area (`dvh` accounts for mobile browser chrome)

## Validation

- `npm run build` passes (Turbopack + TypeScript)
- Headless Chrome verification: scroll-triggered card entrances, header scroll state, modal back-to-top behavior, table rendering, link underline computed styles, document title on open/close, SSR titles for valid/invalid slugs, OG/Twitter meta output, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, og.png (200, image/png)

## Summary
This PR refactors operator token validation across constant evaluation functions and improves the selection logic for universal type interpretations in overload resolution.

## Key Changes

- **Operator Token Validation**: Introduced consistent use of `Is_Operator_Token()` function across `Eval_Const_Numeric_Impl()`, `Eval_Const_Rational()`, and `Eval_Const_Uint128()` to validate operator tokens before processing. This replaces ad-hoc symbol checks and ensures operators are properly validated.

- **Universal Type Selection Enhancement**: Modified `Select_Interp()` to track whether a universal type candidate has all universal operands (`pu_fully_universal`). The selection now prefers fully universal interpretations over partially universal ones, improving overload resolution accuracy.

- **Helper Function Extraction**: Moved `Hides_Type()` and `Is_Instance_Formal_Binding()` from nested functions inside `Select_Interp()` to module-level functions for better code organization and reusability.

- **Discrete Type Collection**: Extracted `Note_Discrete()` as a standalone function from `Require_Determinable_Case_Expression()` to improve code modularity.

- **Documentation Updates**: Enhanced readme.md with a building section including platform-specific build commands and notes.

## Implementation Details

The operator validation refactoring centralizes the check for whether a symbol represents a valid operator token, replacing scattered conditional logic. This improves maintainability and ensures consistent behavior across all constant evaluation contexts.

The universal type selection improvement addresses edge cases in overload resolution where multiple universal interpretations exist, now preferring those where all operands are universal types.

author: doublegate
body:
## Motivation

Step 2 of task #64, following #231's extraction. `Pipeline::step_instruction` runs **one instruction to completion** — fetch, gate, execute, memory, commit — and returns what it cost in `PCycles`, instead of advancing four inter-stage latches once per `PClock`. `pipeline.rs` is **36.1% of a rendering frame**; this is the change that addresses it.

Behind the default-off `fast-exec` feature, authorized by [ADR 0013](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyN64/blob/main/docs/adr/0013-fast-execution-mode.md).

## It executes the same instruction stream

`decode`, `exec::execute`, `alu`, `cop0`, `tlb`, `addr`, `softfloat`, the caches, the TLB, and the exception model are all shared — and the **commit runs through the accurate path's own `wb_stage`**, by staging the instruction into `dc_wb` first. Nothing about *what* an instruction computes is reimplemented. Only the timing model is relaxed, which is exactly and only what ADR 0013 authorizes.

## The cost model is the accurate path's own stall requests

This is the design decision the rest follows from. Every documented cost already exists in the tree, and the accurate path *spends* them as cycles:

| cost | source |
| --- | --- |
| `MULT` 5, `DIV` 37, `DMULT` 8, `DDIV` 69 | `alu::muldiv_stall_cycles` (UM Table 3-12) |
| FPU add 3, mul 5/8, div/sqrt 29/58 | `fpu::stall_cycles` (UM Table 7-14) |
| micro-ITLB miss 3 | `tlb::ITLB_MISS_PCYCLES` (UM §4.6.2) |
| RCP register access 22 | `M_RCP_REGISTER` — **measured** |
| exception epilogue 2 | `exception::EPILOGUE_STALL` (UM §4.7 p. 114) |
| I-cache fill 46, D-cache fill 40 | `M_ICACHE_FILL`/`M_DCACHE_FILL` — **fitted, not measured** (ledger C-1) |

So the fast path **drains `Pipeline::stall` after each phase and charges it**, rather than carrying a table of its own. There is nothing to keep in step, and no constant is invented — a number wrong here is wrong in the accurate path too, which is the only arrangement under which the two are comparable at all. The last row is flagged in the module docs: inheriting fitted anchors is right, but a timing result from this mode is no more trustworthy than `M(RDRAM)` is.

## No new state, deliberately

**A branch and its delay slot execute in the same call.** The alternative — a `pending_redirect` field on `Pipeline` — would be state the fast path owns, which makes ADR 0011 §4's save-state mode marker fall due and breaks the layout. Executing the pair together costs nothing and owes nothing. A delay slot that is itself a branch continues the loop rather than recursing; MIPS calls that UNPREDICTABLE and the loop reproduces the cascade's sequence.

Not modeled, each deliberately, and each a *timing* structure rather than a semantic one: the bypass network (sequential execution makes operands current), the load interlock (a load's value is always ready), the `prev_was_run` interrupt gate (an instruction boundary is always legal), the flush cascade (nothing younger has been fetched).

Also extracted **`apply_cop0_read`** from `dc_stage` — the fourth latch-independent primitive. #231 left it alone on the grounds that a seam guessed without a second caller is a guess; this is that caller.

## Two findings from building the gate

**The fast path sets the boundaries and the accurate path follows.** One call can retire *two* instructions, so the oracle is advanced to meet the fast path — the reverse is structurally impossible.

**Neither PC-like quantity is comparable across the modes.** Both were tried, and each reported a divergence on the *first* boundary of a run that agrees on everything else:

- `Cpu::pc` is the **`IC` fetch pointer**, up to four instructions ahead of the retiring one;
- `dc_wb.pc` is off by exactly one, because the reverse cascade has already moved the next instruction in by the end of the tick that retired.

The architectural PC of a retiring instruction is simply **not observable from outside the pipeline** in the accurate mode. `EPC` is where it surfaces, and that *is* compared, as part of COP0. What carries the weight instead: every test program writes a **distinct value to a distinct register per instruction**, so a skipped, repeated, or reordered instruction shows in the GPRs within one boundary.

## The cost assertion had to become an A/B

The first version asserted `cost >= 8 + 5 + 37` on the multiply program, and **passed with the charge deleted** — eight cold I-cache fills cleared the bar on their own. That is the converging-test hazard, and mutation caught it, not review.

It is now the difference between two programs of the **same length** differing only in `MULT`/`DIV` versus `NOP`, which cancels every shared cost. Asserted as `==` (42) rather than `>=`, since anything else in the difference would be an operand-dependent cost this model does not have.

**Mutation-checked, both restored afterwards:** skipping the delay slot fails three tests; deleting the muldiv charge fails the A/B (`54 with them, 54 without`) where the threshold version had passed.

## Disclosure: a fifth doc-comment theft, shipped in #231

Adding `sample_interrupt_lines` above `fn dc_stage` in the previous PR put it between `dc_stage`'s doc comment and the function, so **`dc_stage` has been undocumented on `main` since #231** and its `/// \`DC\` — the data-cache access…` block merged onto `sample_interrupt_lines`. The bot caught the `ex_gate` and `fetch_word` instances in that PR; this one slipped through. Fixed here, and I swept `pipeline.rs` for others — the only remaining undocumented items in `impl` blocks are two test helpers.

## Verification

One guarded conditional, no pipes: `cargo fmt --all --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo clippy -p rustyn64-cpu --features fast-exec --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace`; `cargo test -p rustyn64-cpu --features fast-exec`; `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`; the `no_std` build for both crates; `scripts/check_en_us.sh`; `pre-commit run markdownlint --all-files`.

**The oracle, on the accurate path**, which this must not move:

```text
Phase 1 categories: 0 failing (suite ran to xioctl(EXIT)). 90 failing suite-wide
across 950 tests started (the remainder are RSP/RCP -- Phase 2's criterion).
```

**CI gains four entries** for the new feature (test + clippy on the light leg, plus the `no_std` build), mirroring `fast-scheduler` — CI runs clippy exactly once and feature-gated code is invisible to every other job, so without them the gate would be a gate that never runs.

## What this PR does not do

It does **not** wire `fast-exec` into `System` or the scheduler, so nothing in a shipped build reaches it and there is no throughput number yet — deliberately, so the execution path and its wiring are reviewable separately. Wiring, the core-level differential predicate on the ADR 0012 machinery, and the A-B-A measurement are the next slice.

## Summary

- publish the exact manifest, wheels, and sdist to GitHub in a hard-fail GitHub-only step

Exact-tag release run `30600070105` finished GitHub publication but hit the old 15-minute `release-manifest` ceiling while Gitee was still uploading. That coupled a successful GitHub release to a slower secondary provider and reported the whole job as cancelled.

body:
Retro zur Session vom 30./31.07. (platform + dev-hub), Footprint `deep` wegen Prod-Schritt.

**13 Befunde, 10 überlebt, refuted_rate 0,23** — im gesunden Band.

## Die zwei schwersten Befunde treffen Code, der in dieser Session gemergt wurde

**#1 (kritisch):** `_ohne_doppelten_namen` löscht Fließtext. `str.startswith(GRUSSFORMELN)` prüft keine Wortgrenze — "Grüße deine Frau von mir." matcht, die Folgezeile verschwindet aus der versandfertigen Mail. Reproduziert gegen `origin/main`. Der PR-Text von #1568 behauptete ausdrücklich, die doppelte Bedingung verhindere genau das.

**#2 (hoch):** Der Guard aus #1558 erlaubt den Swap, sobald `MANAGED_BY`/`manifest.json` im Ziel liegen. Genau diese zwei Dateien hinterlässt der Unfall, gegen den der Guard gebaut wurde. Auf dieser Maschine dormant (Marker wurden entfernt, per `ls` geprüft), die Logiklücke besteht fort.

## Was die Falsifikation kassiert hat

Drei von dreizehn Anklagen haben die unabhängige Prüfung nicht überlebt — zwei davon zugunsten des Ausführenden: der Vorwurf, #1558 verstecke Security-Tooling (der Titel nennt es wörtlich), und der Vorwurf, die MEiKI-Folgearbeit habe kein Tracking (das Board existiert mit Pfadangabe im Handover).

## Längsschnitt

`claim-before-cheapest-check` ×30 → ×31, `deferred-item-no-tracking-issue` ×5 → ×6. Beide seit Langem gate-pflichtig. Befund #10 ist eine Variante, die der bestehende Stop-Hook strukturell nicht fängt: eine **Wiederholungs-Behauptung über zwei Zeitpunkte** ("zweites Mal am selben Tag" — es waren zwei Kalendertage).

## Meta-Review

Der Meta-Reviewer fand einen Regelverstoß: die Invariante `|Soll-Schritte| == |überlebende Befunde|` stand bei 9:10, weil zwei Befunde in eine Zeile gefasst waren. Vor dem Commit behoben, nachgezählt.

Vier Maßnahmen sind sofort umsetzbar und stehen im Action-Board des Reports; zwei brauchen eine Owner-Entscheidung.

author: shibinraj-cr
body:
## Problem

HR has two approval queues, but only one enforced no-self-approval:

| Flow | Self-hidden in queue | Server-side self-approval block |
|---|---|---|
| Attendance Corrections (`HrAttendanceRegularization`) | ✅ | ✅ |
| **Leave** (`HrLeaveRequest`) | ❌ | ❌ |

On the Leave Requests page an approver could see their **own** leave request with live Approve/Reject buttons, and `POST /api/hr/leave/[id]` only checked `canApproveHr` — never whether the approver *was* the requester. So an approver could approve their own leave, and it never routed up to a second approver. This is live on `main`.

## Fix

Brings the leave flow to parity with the already-correct regularization flow:

- **`/hr/leave` page** — excludes the reviewer's own employee from the queue, so a request surfaces only to *another* approver (admin).
- **`POST /api/hr/leave/[id]`** — returns 403 when `approver == requester`, enforcing it server-side even against a direct API call.

Admins with no linked employee record are unaffected (they still review everyone).

## Notes

- No schema/data changes.
- Existing self-approved leave requests (from before this fix) are **not** auto-reversed — review the Approved filter on `/hr/leave` for any request approved by its own requester.

author: wehos
body:
## 关联 issue

关联 #2500。本 PR 是 `prompts_memory.py` 的独立分批，不关闭仍有其他文件欠账的总 issue。

## 变更内容

- 为 `config/prompts/prompts_memory.py` 补齐 57 个 `zh-TW` prompt 模板，采用台湾用词，并保留占位符及 system prompt 水印
- 让 memory prompt locale normalizer 保留 `zh-TW`，避免 `_loc` 缺键时回退英文
- 从会话级 `user_language` 解析 prompt locale，不依赖进程级系统语言；补齐 HTTP/WebSocket/session 建立与恢复路径的语言传递
- 让聊天记忆、检索问题改写、情感记忆、主动聊天、Minecraft/MetaHuman 记忆等消费链路实际可达 `zh-TW`
- 为 recall/persona hint 增加繁中措辞
- 增加自动发现式模板护栏、session locale 隔离/恢复测试，以及 prompt 欠账门禁夹具

## 用户可感知变化

繁体中文界面下，记忆抽取、事实判断、检索改写、情绪记忆与记忆检索等流程会稳定使用繁中提示词；在应用内切换界面语言后也会跟随当前会话语言，不再受 Steam/系统 locale 干扰或因缺键回退英文。

## 验证

- `uv run python scripts/check_prompt_zh_tw.py --count`：325 → 267
- `uv run python scripts/check_prompt_zh_tw.py --full`：`prompts_memory.py` 欠账为 0
- 相关 pytest：1243 passed
- `uv run ruff check`：通过
- `uv run python scripts/check_docstring_no_cjk.py --base origin/main`：通过

## 回归报告

### 改动与必要性

`prompts_memory.py` 的繁中模板与调用链可达性必须作为同一个原子改动交付：该模块的 `_loc` 缺少 locale 键时会直接回退英文，而调用点若仍把 `zh-TW` 折叠成 `zh`，新增模板又会成为死代码。本 PR 因此同时补齐模板、保留 locale，并把会话级 `user_language` 传到所有实际消费路径。

### 改动前后行为

- 改动前：繁中界面下，memory prompt 可能因为模板缺键直接使用英文，或因为调用点只识别为 `zh` 而无法命中繁中模板；应用内切换语言还可能与进程级 Steam/系统 locale 不一致。
- 改动后：各 memory 消费链路使用当前会话的 `user_language` 解析完整 prompt locale，`zh-TW` 稳定命中繁中模板；非繁中 locale 的既有派发行为保持不变。

### 潜在回归与防护

潜在风险包括简中被误判为繁中、不同会话的 locale 相互泄漏、恢复会话后丢失界面语言，以及翻译破坏占位符或 system prompt 水印。对应防护包括 session/ContextVar 隔离与恢复测试、locale normalizer 测试、自动发现式占位符/水印/台湾用词护栏、逐条删除变异验证，并对相关路径执行 1243 个 pytest 用例。

## 不拆分理由

本 PR 已按 issue #2500 的要求限定为 `prompts_memory.py` 单文件批次；代码侧涉及的多个消费者并非独立功能扩张，而是让同一批模板在聊天记忆、检索改写、情感记忆、主动聊天及游戏集成等既有调用链上可达的必要配套。若再把模板、normalizer、会话语言传递或各消费点拆开，会产生“模板缺键回退英文”或“已有模板不可达”的中间状态，违反本次修复的原子性；测试和门禁也需要与这组行为同时落地。

author: 13angs
body:
Implements [ADR-0027](https://github.com/13angs/my-projects/pull/683) § Handoff.

## Problem

Switching browser tabs or leaving the browser leaves the terminal frozen — cursor blinking, keystrokes going nowhere — and the only recovery was Kill + resume, which throws away session state.

The server was already right (detach ≠ kill, identity-guarded attach). The defects were: nothing reopened the socket after `close`, `send()` dropped input silently when not `OPEN`, the UI had no way to show any of it, and output produced while detached was discarded so even a manual reload landed on a blank screen.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts` | Reconnect with jittered backoff; app-level ping/pong watchdog; `visibilitychange`/`pageshow` revalidation; `stopped` option; `RECONNECTING` state |
| `src/pages/Agent.tsx` | `onClose`/`onError` → `reconnecting` status; restate window size on every reopen; stop the transcript poll from overwriting socket state |
| `src/hooks/useXterm.ts` | Debounce observer-driven `fit()` 50 ms trailing |
| `server.py`, `control_plane/ws_handler.py` | Answer the client's JSON ping; ping attached clients every 30 s |
| `control_plane/terminal.py` | Bounded 256 KiB ring buffer, written while detached, replayed by `attach()` |

## Two decisions worth reviewing closely

**The heartbeat does not run in a hidden tab.** This is deliberate and inverts the obvious approach. Chrome throttles a hidden tab's timers to ~1 wake-up/minute, so a heartbeat left running there fires late and severs a *healthy* connection — the naive fix makes the bug worse. It also drains battery measurably. With a loopback bind there is no NAT or proxy to keep alive, so the heartbeat's only job is detecting a half-open socket, which only matters while someone is looking at the screen.

**Input typed while disconnected is dropped, not queued.** Standard reconnection advice is a draining queue with idempotency keys. That is unsafe for a PTY: terminal input is positional, and replaying a half-typed command into a prompt that has since moved executes something the user never asked for. The status line says `reconnecting… (input is not being sent)` so the loss is visible rather than silent.

## Test change to look at

`tests/test_terminal_lifecycle.py` previously asserted `assert b"ping" not in sub2.data, "unexpected replay to reconnected sub"` — it encoded the v2.1 "no replay buffer" behaviour that ADR-0027 §SD3 overturns. Updated rather than left failing, plus two new tests: output produced while detached is replayed, and the buffer stays bounded.

## Known limitation, stated up front

Replay is best-effort. Full-screen TUIs use the alternate screen buffer, which discards anything scrolling out of the viewport, so a byte buffer beginning mid-stream can render a cosmetically wrong screen until the next full redraw. Documented on `attach()`. A wrong screen the user can fix with a keypress beats today's empty one, but the buffer is not authoritative.

## Verification

- `python3 -m pytest tests -q` → **194 passed**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → clean
- `npm run check:lib` → 4/4 OK
- `npm run build` → fails at rollup's native binding (`ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED`) — the known PRoot/Termux limitation from ADR-0019, not a regression. CI runs the real build on this PR.

body:
## What was broken `state/deals_history.json` is `web/`'s only input, and `App.jsx` re-renders the numbers itself rather than reusing the email's `headline` string. It reads **26 entry fields**; `build_history_entries` emitted **11**. The 15 missing fields meant, the moment real data arrived: - every card rendered with no price line, no score ring, no discount - the **class filter matched nothing** (`e.sku_class !== skuClass` against `undefined`) - the "best saving" stat and "last run" date were both dead - `entryKey()` degenerated to `` `sku|""` `` — so two entries for the same sku on different dates collide, giving duplicate React keys and a drawer that opens the wrong one Among the missing was **`the_math`** — a `required` field of `STAGE_AUDIT_SCHEMA` ([config.py:830](../blob/main/config.py#L830)) that the prompt teaches with a worked example ([config.py:697](../blob/main/config.py#L697)), and the centrepiece output carried over from the user's own `promotion_reviewer.md`. It was absent from `ITEM_BLOCKS` too, so it was generated and paid for on **every run** and rendered in **neither the email nor the UI**. Nothing caught this because `test_stub.py` asserted the *count* of `deals_history` entries, not their *shape*. The PR #1 review flagged "the field list is duplicated three times" and fixed it for the two email renderers — but `web/` is a third consumer with a **wider** contract, and no test joined them. ## The fix - **`ITEM_DATA_FIELDS`** — the structured half of the item contract, as `ITEM_BLOCKS` is the prose half. Both are consumed by `_item_dict`, so there is still one list per half and no per-renderer copy. Add a field to a list, never to `_item_dict`. - **`the_math` added to `ITEM_BLOCKS`**, so it now renders in the email as well as the UI. - **`bulk_total_eur` computed in Python.** `App.jsx`'s stock-up line wants `unit_price × bulk_qty`, but `price_eur` is the *pack* price. A naive passthrough printed `buy 5 kg = €9.80` instead of `€49.00` — wrong in a way that looks entirely plausible. Python keeps owning all arithmetic, in the UI's numbers too. - **A contract test that cannot drift.** `test_stub.py` greps `App.jsx` for `e.` and asserts each is emitted, rather than comparing against a hand-copied list — a copy being the exact thing that drifted here. ## Verification All six offline suites pass (`test_match`, `test_sources`, `test_prefilter`, `test_history`, `test_verdicts`, `test_stub`). The new guard was checked for vacuity: removing a single field (`fit_score`) from `ITEM_DATA_FIELDS` makes it fail with `App.jsx reads fields deals_history.json never emits: ['fit_score']`, and reverting the whole change fails with all 16. Verified live in the browser against realistic data generated through `build_history_entries` itself: - `€9.80/kg vs €12.00 par (18% under) · buy 5 kg = €49.00, saves €11.00` — bulk total correct - score rings render (88 / 68 / 91 / 74); stats show `4 deals tracked · 2 strong buys · €170 best saving` - drawer shows `Kaufland · Consumable`, `fit score = 88/100`, and **`The math: Perceived saving 30% off a 13.99 EUR anchor; against your 12.00 EUR par the real saving is 2.20 EUR/kg, 18%.`** - class filter set to Durable returns exactly the 2 durables (was 0) - console clean, no errors Screenshots are not included because the Browser pane cannot composite frames in this environment; verification above is via the accessibility tree, page text and DOM queries. ## Note `web/src/App.jsx:190` renders `

Shop Hunter

` while `web/index.html` sets the tab title to `Shopping Assistant`. Left alone — product-name vs repo-name is a branding call, not a defect. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: yakupatahanov
body:
The **source end** of mid-execution interaction (JarvisOSLinux/Project-JARVIS#210) — the piece that actually raises the question. dmcp (#47 merged, #48 open) and dispatch (#35) carry the elicitation and the answer; the daemon decides who answers; this makes a shell command *ask*, so `pacman -Syu` without `--noconfirm` can be answered instead of aborting.

## What it does

`execute_interactive` (new tool on **both** `jarvis-shell` and `jarvis-shell-system`) runs a command under a **pseudo-terminal**, so a program that checks `isatty()` still prompts and reads its answer. When the child blocks for input it raises `elicitation/create` with the prompt line; dmcp relays it (`--interactive`), the answer is written back to the pty, and the command continues.

The three outcomes map to the terminal:
- **accept** → write the answer to the pty
- **decline** → EOF the pty so the command aborts, exactly as `execute_command`'s closed stdin does today
- **cancel** → kill the process group

It advertises interactivity only when the client declared it can elicit; otherwise it falls back to `execute_command`'s closed-stdin + `needs_input` behavior, never hanging on an answer that cannot come. A per-call prompt budget (`JARVIS_INTERACTIVE_MAX_PROMPTS`, default 24) bounds a program looping on a question.

**`execute_command` is untouched** — its output shape and `needs_input` report are byte-for-byte what they were, and the two servers' shared bodies stay byte-identical (`selftest_needs_input.py` and `selftest_interactive.py` enforce both).

## The hard part: knowing when a program is *waiting*

A quiet-tail regex alone is not enough — the adversarial review proved it (this was built and hardened by an Opus 5 fleet). It **hangs forever** on `fdisk`'s `Command (m for help): ` (no `[Y/n]` shape) under the default no-timeout, and **false-fires** on a `?`-ending status line printed *while the program is busy* — auto-answering the wrong prompt, or killing a healthy long-running command on decline. Both are strictly worse than `execute_command`.

So detection is anchored to the truth, not the output shape. `_pty_read_state` reads `/proc/<pid>/syscall` to confirm a group member is actually parked in `read(2)` **on our pty** (matched through `/proc/<pid>/fd`). Three-state, mirroring the platform gate's absent/declared/malformed reading elsewhere in the ecosystem:

- **True** — blocked reading → a prompt awaiting an answer
- **False** — busy or sleeping → leave it running, exactly as `execute_command`'s closed stdin would
- **None** — host not introspectable (no `/proc`, unknown arch) → fall back to the `[Y/n]` shape heuristic

Because that *proves* the child is waiting, detection isn't limited to `[Y/n]` shapes: once blocked in `read`, whatever line the program printed is the question, so **fdisk's colon menu, a REPL banner, and numbered menus are elicited and answered** rather than aborted. A bare `read` that printed no prompt has nothing to show and still EOFs. This is the difference between *working on* a command and merely *not hanging on* it.

## The question text is untrusted

The prompt is the command's own output (pacman's, fdisk's), relayed verbatim as the elicitation `message` — not editorialized. dmcp attributes it to the server and the daemon gates it (a password prompt never reaches the model).

## Verification — real dmcp, end to end

Every case driven through the **real** dmcp binary (`--interactive`, one-shot — the path a root command takes):

- a real `read a` in a real `sh` receives a real `y` → **`GOT=y`**, `outcome: completed`
- the fdisk-shape colon menu is elicited and answered → **`CHOSE=p`**
- a bare `read` with no printed prompt returns `no-prompt` instead of hanging
- a busy command with a prompt-shaped **status** line runs to completion, uninterrupted, output intact
- an echoed prompt-shaped answer is not re-detected as a new prompt
- both `jarvis-shell` and `jarvis-shell-system` carry an answer through

Gates: `py_compile` clean · `selftest_interactive.py` (unit + read-state + 24 byte-identity checks + the real-dmcp e2e suite) green · `selftest_needs_input.py` green (no `execute_command` regression) · `sync_registry.py --check` idempotent · `validate_registry.py` · `selftest_platform_format.py` all pass.

**Deliberate limit:** the `/proc/syscall` read-state anchor is Linux/x86_64 with a readable `/proc`; elsewhere it degrades to the `[Y/n]` shape heuristic (still safe, just narrower).

## This closes the chain

With this merged alongside dmcp #48 and dispatch #35, the full path works: `pacman -Syu` → shell server elicits `[Y/n]` → dmcp relays → dispatch parks → daemon's `smart` gate says SAFE → the LLM answers "y" → pacman proceeds. A password or a dangerous prompt stops for the human instead.
