author: rheev21
body:
## O problema relatado

> "o fluxo de solicitação de acesso parece não estar funcionando, os usuários ao solicitar o acesso na pagina de login não está criando uma solicitação para aprovação"

## Causa-raiz: `this` perdido — **não era o banco**

A action nunca chegava ao banco. O commit `8863a69` (13/07, 14h13) refatorou `/solicitar-acesso` para reusar a referência da RPC no fallback e, nisso, trocou

```ts
await (supabase.rpc as unknown as AdminRpc)('solicitar_acesso_admin', {...})   // funcionava
```

por

```ts
const rpc = supabase.rpc as unknown as AdminRpc    // ← a ATRIBUIÇÃO destaca o método
await rpc('solicitar_acesso_admin', {...})
```

**Parênteses em torno de um acesso a membro preservam a referência-base** (`(obj.m)(x)` ≡ `obj.m(x)`); **atribuir o método a uma variável a destrói.** `SupabaseClient.rpc` é método de protótipo cujo corpo é `return this.rest.rpc(...)` — destacado, o `this` é `undefined` (porque `rpc` vive num corpo de `class`, que é **sempre** strict, e não por causa do módulo chamador) e a chamada estoura `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'rest')`.

**A ironia:** o commit que quebrou era um *fix defensivo*, e o fallback legado usava a **mesma** referência quebrada — os dois caminhos morreram juntos.

### Por que ficou 18 dias invisível

Três silêncios empilhados: o `catch` da action é anti-enumeração **por design** (ADR-0110) e engoliu o `TypeError`; a tela **sempre** redireciona para `?enviado=1`; e o erro do fallback era descartado sem checagem. O único rastro era um `console.error` que ninguém tinha motivo para olhar — a tela dizia sucesso.

### As 5 evidências (independentes)

| # | Evidência | Prova |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Log da Vercel: o `TypeError` exato em **100%** dos `POST /solicitar-acesso` — 18 tentativas só na retenção de 7 dias | falha total, não intermitente |
| 2 | Fonte do supabase-js 2.105.1: `rpc(fn,…) { return this.rest.rpc(…) }` | explica o nome `rest` no erro |
| 3 | **Todos** os outros call-sites do repo bindam (`.bind` / `.call(db,…)`) | este era o único fora do padrão |
| 4 | Base via REST/service_role: 8 pedidos, todos `aprovada`, **zero pendentes**, mais recente `criado_em` **13/07 11h26** | nada criado após a regressão |
| 5 | Diff datado do `8863a69` | data exata da quebra, coerente com (4) |

A evidência (4) **refutou** minha primeira hipótese ("nunca funcionou", já que o padrão existia desde a v4.14): os pedidos de 23–26/06 provaram o contrário e me levaram à distinção parênteses × atribuição.

## A correção

Uma linha — `.bind(supabase)`, o padrão que o repo já usa em `admin/uploads/actions.ts`. Mais o segundo buraco fechado: cada caminho loga, e a falha dupla grita `PEDIDO PERDIDO` **com o e-mail e o nome** do solicitante (para o follow-up manual). A resposta ao usuário segue sempre de sucesso — anti-enumeração intocada.

## Guard novo (8 casos, 1º teste de Server Action do repo)

O dublê do cliente é uma **classe** com `rpc` no protótipo tocando `this.rest` — replica a armadilha. **Um `vi.fn()` solto passaria com o bug presente** e seria teatro. **Verificado que 7 dos 8 casos reprovam** o código antigo (o 8º é o de e-mail inválido, que nunca toca o banco).

## Revisão

`revisor`: **aprovado com ressalvas — zero CRÍTICO, zero ALTO.** 1 MÉDIO + 2 BAIXO, todos corrigidos no 3º commit:

- **MÉDIO:** os logs não traziam o e-mail do solicitante — sem saber *de quem*, o log perdia o propósito. Corrigido, e o guard agora exige o e-mail na linha.
- **BAIXO:** o comentário do fallback ancorava numa janela de deploy já extinta. O revisor mostrou que o fallback **não** é código morto (protege contra permissão revogada, drift, regressão futura) — generalizei a redação e **mantive** o fallback, revertendo minha recomendação inicial de avaliar remoção.
- **BAIXO:** eu atribuíra o `this === undefined` a "módulo ESM"; a strictness que decide é a do **método chamado** (corpo de `class` é sempre strict). Corrigido nos 4 lugares onde escrevi a versão imprecisa.

**Contraprova que pedi explicitamente:** varredura de `.rpc`/`.storage`/`.auth`/`.functions` em todo o `src/` — **nenhum outro método destacado sem `this`**. `solicitar-acesso` era a única exceção do repositório.

## Gates

`tsc` ✅ · `lint` ✅ · **549 testes** ✅ · `build` ✅ (re-executados após as correções da revisão)

## Depois do merge

1. **Prova de ponta a ponta:** submeter um pedido em `/solicitar-acesso` e ver a pendência aparecer em Usuários & Acessos (depois rejeitar para não deixar lixo).
2. **Os pedidos dos 18 dias são irrecuperáveis** — nada foi gravado. Quem tentou precisa pedir de novo; vale avisar quem estava esperando.
3. **D5 — enforcement bloqueado pelo harness:** a regra de lint que pegaria esta classe de bug não pode ser aplicada pelo agente (o hook `protecao-config` protege `eslint.config.*`). Diff pronto no §7 do out-briefing.

Lição levada para a skill `contrato-rpc-front` (destino 4 da régua): o `.call(db,…)` do exemplo já estava certo, mas a skill nunca dizia **por que** o `this` é obrigatório — agora diz, com a sutileza que engana e a regra de teste.

author: arcabezudo
body:
Add phy_id values (0xc and 0xd) to the Versal 2 GEM0 and GEM1 entries, matching the original Versal configuration.

Without phy_id set, the generated device tree uses a **fixed-link** node with _cdns,zynqmp-gem_ compatible string. VxWorks requires a **genericPhy** child node (produced when phy_id is non-zero) with the _cdns,versal-gem_ compatible string to successfully probe and attach the GEM network interfaces.

The 10Gb GEM2 (usxgmii) is intentionally left without phy_id — the VxWorks GEM driver does not recognize usxgmii as a valid phy-mode (**phyConnectTypeGet()** in endMedia.h has no mapping for it), so the interface cannot be used regardless.

## What

- replace link-like stack expanders with muted placeholder controls
- render up to three skeleton bars to represent hidden notifications, PRs, or issues
- label collapsed groups by the number of additional items rather than the total group size
- indent revealed children and add a subtle nesting border
- apply the same interaction model to notifications and repository PR/issue lists
- preserve keyboard focus and `aria-expanded` behavior

## Why

The existing blue inline link reads like navigation and does not communicate that more rows are hidden beneath the representative notification. Expanded rows also look like unrelated top-level items.

## Impact

Collapsed groups now look like compact placeholder rows. Expanding them reveals visibly nested children, while the representative item remains a normal notification or list row.

## Checks

- `mise exec -- aube install --frozen-lockfile`
- `mise exec -- aube run test`
- `git diff --check`
- visually checked collapsed and expanded states against a GitHub-shaped dark-mode fixture
- confirmed the selectors against the live GitHub Notifications DOM

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: OpenAI/GPT-5; version: unavailable.*

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> UI and client-side caching/DOM decoration only; no auth or server changes, with regression coverage in grouping and dsl source assertions.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Redesigns collapsed notification and PR/issue list groups** so they read as expandable stacks rather than navigation links: muted full-width controls with skeleton placeholder rows, a separate chevron on the representative row, labels that describe *additional* hidden items (e.g. “2 more PRs in stack”), and indented nested styling when expanded.

On load or DOM refresh, groups can render immediately from cache via `decorateCachedNotificationStacks` / `decorateCachedQueryListCollapses`, then full metadata is refetched in the background.

body:
## Task

> - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** Coverage: let any aspect be manually confirmed, alongside its derived status

<!-- id: 6c94edc8-ac2f-4a23-bbc2-54e172a22d39 -->

## Changes

- **Every aspect row now carries a confirmation tick.** `buildCommitTick` was already generic (persists to `aspect_submissions`, reverts on failure, registers in `ctx.ticks` for the async hydrate). It's now rendered on every non-process, non-shipped aspect row — in-progress, proposed, blocked, and not-started — with rubric-appropriate copy ("Confirmed"), so any aspect can be signed off by hand.
- **Confirmation and derivation stay independent axes.** The tick reads/writes `aspect_submissions`; the row's derived status (`aspectStatus` from queue rows) is untouched. So the four combinations read distinctly: shipped-and-confirmed, shipped-but-unconfirmed, unshipped-but-confirmed (work done by hand), and neither.
- **Blocked rows pair the tick as a sibling.** The blocked row is itself a jump `<button>`; a tick `<button>` can't nest inside it, so both share a small `.coverageDetailConfirmable` flex wrapper. Clicking the tick does not fire the jump (verified in tests).
- **Shipped and manual lanes unchanged.** Shipped aspects keep confirming through the commit lane's "Committed to GitLab" tick (avoids a duplicate tick bound to the same aspect id); manual Git/process aspects keep their "mark done" tick.
- **Headline / count — deliberate decision:** chose the *both-shown* option the task permits. The detail modal's header already shows two counts — the derived coverage line ("N outstanding · M of T covered") and a confirmation count ("N committed to GitLab"), the latter computed across **all** aspects via `committedCount()`, so it now reflects confirmations on any row, not just shipped ones. The card/pane headline and the segmented bar stay **derived** (they render synchronously and don't perform the async `aspect_submissions` read), so derived and confirmed never contradict on one surface — each surface shows a single consistent basis, and the modal shows both explicitly. The tab's compact pane summary remains derived and therefore agrees with the card headline and the bar.
- **Scoping / hydrate:** `setAspectSubmitted` / `getAspectSubmissions` key on `(project_id, aspect)` (pinned by existing tests), so confirming A1 on one project doesn't leak to another's A1. The modal's existing hydrate populates every registered tick — including the new non-process rows — because it reads all committed ids for the project.

## Files modified

- `toDoList_main/src/assignmentCoverage.js` — render a confirmation tick on every non-process, non-shipped aspect row; sibling-wrap the blocked row's tick; update the two doc comments.
- `toDoList_main/src/style.css` — `.coverageDetailConfirmable` flex wrapper for the blocked row + tick pairing.
- `toDoList_main/src/changelog.js` — changelog bullet (see Bookkeeping).
- `toDoList_main/tests/coverageConfirmAspect.test.js` — new test file (9 tests).

## Testing

- Command: `npm run test:run` from `toDoList_main/` → **4413 passed | 4 skipped** (295 files). Baseline before the change was 4404 passed.
- New tests in `tests/coverageConfirmAspect.test.js` exercise the new behavior: a "Confirmed" tick renders on in-progress/proposed/not-started rows; the blocked row pairs its tick as a non-nested sibling; the manual row keeps only "mark done"; the shipped row confirms through the commit lane; confirming a not-started/proposed aspect persists via `setAspectSubmitted` and updates the header count (and reverts on write failure); confirmation does not alter the derived status; clicking the blocked tick doesn't close the modal; and a stored submission hydrates a non-shipped aspect's tick.
- Existing `agentGitlabTick.test.js`, `agentCoverageDetail.test.js`, and `coverageDetailRepaint.test.js` remain green — no existing tests were modified.

## Bookkeeping

- Category `added` (net-new capability: aspects that couldn't be confirmed now can). Today's PDT date (2026-07-31) matches the topmost entry → **merged** into it.
- Bullet added: *"Every rubric aspect in the coverage breakdown can now be confirmed by hand, with your confirmation shown alongside its derived status."*
- Cap enforcement: the merge took the entry to 6 bullets. Per the pruning algorithm the just-added bullet is protected and `added` is the oldest position, so the first prunable bullet is `changed[0]` — the "desktop task-list filter is now ALL / IN PROGRESS / DONE" bullet was pruned and the now-empty `changed` key removed. Total back to exactly 5.

## Notes

- **Headline choice** documented above: kept the card/pane headline + bar derived, surfaced confirmation as the modal's per-row ticks and its existing confirmation count, rather than switching the synchronous card headline to a confirmed count that would require an async submissions read on the render path.
- **Blocked confirmation** is included for fidelity to "let *any* aspect be manually confirmed"; a blocked aspect is one waiting on a needs_words question, and the tick records a by-hand sign-off without touching that derived state.
- Focus across a repaint: a tick toggle writes to `aspect_submissions` and does **not** trigger `onQueueChange`, so it does not repaint the modal — focus is preserved during normal ticking. A concurrent queue settle repaints the body (rebuilding all ticks) and would drop focus, but that is pre-existing behavior shared by the shipped/manual ticks and out of scope here. Rapid tick/untick is already serialized by the tick's `btn.disabled` guard during the async write.
- No follow-up items added to TODO.md.

- **RED → GREEN 与 mutation 证据（临时改动→测试变红→还原→复绿）**: M1 唯一索引降级非唯一 → 6 failed；M2 索引缩错列（仅 reconcile_generation_id）→ 4 failed（另一变体多 status 列 → 1 failed 列序断言）；M3 IF NOT EXISTS 改 IF EXISTS 绕过升级重装 → 3 套件全 fail；M4 删除开机重复行探针 → 1 failed（裸 UNIQUE 错误替代具名 fail-closed）；还原后 focused 18/18 复绿。
- **lint / build-discipline**: eslint src/ 2 errors/1421 warnings 均为 base 既有（owned DatabaseManager.ts 与 base 文件逐项一致 15 problems，零新增）；build-discipline run-all exit 0（存量 warn 新增 0、C4 PASS）、selftest 1 失败为 base 既有（C1 fetch 变量回溯，base worktree 同款失败）。

## 迁移、回滚与边界
- **迁移方式**: 每次开机 upgrade 事务内：先探针存量重复行（具名 fail-closed）→ CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS；fresh、clean predecessor（无 generation 列旧形状重建）、当前形状存量库同一幂等路径；重复启动 no-op；同一事务失败整体 ROLLBACK 零部分升级。
- **回滚方式**: revert PR（2 commits：RED 测试 bc562f5d + GREEN 实现 a6b507f0）；DB 层面 DROP INDEX 即回旧行为（重复行未自动删除，零数据改写）。
- **未覆盖边界**: 生产/真实业务数据库未操作（未授权）；存量重复行的受治理处置工具不属于本票（Issue #83 工具线）；NULL/legacy 行不受唯一约束（系统既有合法形状，保持）；双进程并发测试在 Windows/Node 22.23.1 实测 3 轮稳定，未在 Linux CI 复跑；eslint 存量 2 errors 位于 excluded 文件；preflight 两项环境/基线 FAIL 详见上。
- **我现在最没把握的是什么？ / Least confidence**: risk-v1; anchor=name:并发双签时序稳定性; uncertainty=unverified:双进程并发测试在 Linux CI 不同 SQLite 文件锁实现上的稳定复现
- **关于当前局面，我可能遗漏的最大问题是什么？ / Biggest missing**: risk-v1; anchor=name:supplement 写路径未来演进; uncertainty=unknown:未来新增 supplement 写路径是否在 INSERT 前依赖应用层重签删除逻辑，本 PR 只保证 DB 终态单活

## PM 大白话
- **做了什么**: 给补收单表加了数据库层唯一约束：同一核对代次、同一条漏收差异最多一张存活补收单；老库若有重复单，启动时明确报错点名，绝不偷偷删或合并，由人处置后再启动。
- **结果是什么**: 直接 SQL 绕过界面重复开补收单被封死，收款汇总不再对同一笔漏收计两次钱；正常改判（先删旧单再重签）完全不受影响。
- **对业务或用户意味着什么**: 金额真值更稳——同笔漏收只对应一张补收单、一笔实收；升级安全可逆，重复行不会静默消失。
- **merge authority**: PM retains merge authority（required checks + 固定 SHA 异构复核 + PM 明确批准后合并；实现代理不自动合并）

author: lesmartiepants
body:
## Categorization distillation (v3) — record + refresh runbook

This is the **canonical record** of the categorization distillation (it supersedes the working
PR #649, whose code already shipped to `main` via #652). The file change here is the refresh
runbook; the sections below document the whole feature so the record lives in one place.

### The problem
v2 over-tagged: avg **7.59** mood/topic/motif labels per poem, "love" on **46%** of poems, synonym
stacks (grief+melancholy+despair piled together) — so filters barely discriminated.

### What distillation changed
- Caps **4/4/5 → mood 2 / topic 2 / motif 2** (ceiling 13 → 6).
- **Dominant-concept** prompt + **no-synonym-stacking** rule (≤1 of {melancholy,grief,despair,bittersweet}; ≤1 of {amorous,passion,yearning}).
- **Confidence floor 65** enforced at import.
- `taxonomy_version=3` / `prompt_version=distill-1`. Migration adds `category_dimensions.min_labels/max_labels` (mood 1/2, topic 1/2, motif 0/2) + reconciles the dead `accessibility_level` column.

### Results (full corpus, 9,073 poems — live in the DB)
- avg labels/poem **7.59 → 4.41** (−42%); poems with ≥8 labels **62% → 0%**.
- synonym stacks collapsed (passion 24.7%→8.2%, amorous 25.5%→17.4%); broad "love" **46.4% → 38.9%**.
- 0 orphaned/duplicate rows, JSONB matches the join table, every poem keeps its primary mood.
- Gap-fill: 2 no-topic poems fixed; **~23% correctly have no motif** (optional dimension — not forced).

### Where it all lives now
- **Code on `main` via #652**: distilled `config.py` + `import_categories.py` (floor) + `classify_poems.py` + `classify_new.sh`, the v3 migration, `test_distillation.py`, the audit (`ideas/categorization-audit.md`, `categorization/audit/`), and the spot-check viewer's **v5 · distillation** comparison column.
- **DB re-tagged to v3 on 2026-07-28** (shared Supabase corpus; pre-change backups retained).
- **Migration tracking reconciled 2026-07-31**: the v3 migration (and the two other applied-but-unrecorded categorization migrations) were recorded in `schema_migrations` via `supabase migration repair --status applied` (records without re-running — they're idempotent + already applied). Ledger now matches reality. Going forward, apply schema via `supabase db push`, never direct `pg`.

### This PR's change
Adds the **"Refreshing the categorization (v3 distillation)"** runbook to
`poetry_quality_and_curation/categorization/README.md`: when/how to re-run (`classify_new.sh` for new
inserts; full `--scope all` re-tag on taxonomy/prompt change), the **spend-cap concurrency gotcha**
(keep it low ~6, it's checkpoint-resumable — raise the cap and rerun on 429), verification counts, the
`supabase migration repair` reconcile recipe, and why motif gaps are expected (don't force them).
Docs-only; single file.

Closes the loop on #649 (that PR can be closed — its content is on `main`; this is the record).

author: thatcrispytoast
body:
## Linux installers

Firestarter ships for Windows and macOS. This adds Linux: a `.deb` for Ubuntu
and other Debian systems, and an AppImage for everything else. Both are built
and attached by the same release run that already builds the other two.

### What changed

- **`studio/package.json`** — a `linux` block with the two targets, x64. Plus
  three fields a deb has nowhere to leave blank and without which the build
  stops: `homepage`, `maintainer`, and a description. `desktopName` with
  `syncDesktopName` is what makes a running window attach to its menu entry.
- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — `ubuntu-latest` in the matrix, and the
  two new extensions added to the "did anything installable come out" count and
  to the upload. Nothing else needed changing: `latest-linux.yml` is already
  covered by the `latest*.yml` glob.
- **`README.md`** — which file to download, how to install each, and the one
  difference that bites (below).

### Both self-update

electron-updater reads the package type out of the app's resources, so a copy
installed from the deb fetches a deb and a running AppImage replaces itself.
`latest-linux.yml` names both files, which is why both have to be attached to
the release — the existing "the update feed must name files that exist" check
covers it. Verified locally, feed and all:

```
checking latest-linux.yml
  ok      Firestarter-0.6.4-linux-amd64.deb
  ok      Firestarter-0.6.4-linux-x86_64.AppImage
```

Installing an update from a deb runs `dpkg`, so it asks for a password. The
README says so.

### The dependency list needed fixing, and only running it showed that

electron-builder's default `depends` for a deb omits two libraries Electron
loads. The package installs cleanly and `ldd` is quiet about neither, but the
app dies at launch:

```
firestarter: error while loading shared libraries: libasound.so.2: cannot open shared object file
```

Adding `libasound2` and `libgbm1` fixed the first failure into a second one:

```
firestarter: symbol lookup error: undefined symbol: snd_device_name_get_hint, version ALSA_0.9
```

On Ubuntu 24.04 `libasound2` is a virtual package with two providers, and apt
picked `liboss4-salsa-asound2` — an OSS shim with a partial ALSA API. Hence
`libasound2t64 | libasound2`, which names the real package first and still
resolves on 22.04 and Debian, where no `t64` package exists.

### AppArmor, and why the deb is the one to recommend on Ubuntu

Installing the deb also installs the AppArmor profile the Chromium sandbox
needs on Ubuntu 24.04 and later, and fixes up `chrome-sandbox`. An AppImage
installs nothing, so on those systems it can refuse to start until it is run
with `--no-sandbox`. The README recommends the deb there and says why.

### Verified

Both artifacts were built and exercised in containers, not just built:

- `.deb` and `.AppImage` build from a clean tree (`node:22` container)
- `latest-linux.yml` names both, and the release job's feed check passes on it
- the deb installs on a bare `ubuntu:24.04` with dependencies resolving
  (`libgtk-3-0` → `libgtk-3-0t64` and so on), registers the menu entry and the
  `/usr/bin/firestarter` alternative
- with the fixed depends, `libasound.so.2` comes from `libasound2t64`, `ldd` is
  clean, and the app starts under Xvfb and reaches `Checking for update`, which
  is the updater initialising from a packaged Linux build
- `node verify.js` — 20/20

Not verified: nothing here was run on a real Ubuntu desktop, so the first launch
from the menu and the AppArmor profile taking effect are still untested. The
Windows and macOS builds are untouched, but the first tagged release after this
is the proof.

### One thing to check before merging

`maintainer` is `Anuj Attri <anuj-attri@users.noreply.github.com>`, derived from
the GitHub account on the remote, because a deb refuses to build without an
email and `package.json` has no address in `author`. Change it if you would
rather a real one. Same for `homepage`, which is hardcoded to
`https://github.com/Anuj-Attri/prod-imagen-studio` — the `publish` block keeps
an `OWNER` placeholder that CI rewrites, but a deb needs the URL at build time.

author: loid345
body:
## Summary

- add an environment-gated PostgreSQL integration target for persisted reconciliation schema admission
- require an unregistered tenant schema to return `SchemaNotRegistered` before job creation or source scan
- yield one active-schema reconciliation page and retain one pending job with cursor `{ "offset": 1 }`
- retire the exact schema and require `SchemaRetired` before pending-job claim, attempt increment, source scan, or durable writes
- reactivate the schema and require the same pending job UUID to resume as attempt 2 and complete
- retire the succeeded scope and require `SchemaRetired` before `AlreadyComplete` resolution
- reactivate again and require `AlreadyComplete` without another source scan
- add focused documentation and a standalone fail-closed verifier

## Admission order

The current reconciliation acquisition transaction takes the schema-scope advisory lock and calls `verify_schema_registration` before selecting, claiming, completing, or inserting `index_jobs` rows.

The fixture keeps the in-memory source and schema registries complete while leaving the tenant schema unpersisted. The first invocation must return:

- `IndexReconciliationRunError::SchemaNotRegistered`
- zero source scans
- zero reconciliation jobs
- zero entities
- zero inbox rows

This isolates persisted tenant admission from source ownership and in-memory schema compilation.

## Retired pending scope

After the schema is persisted as active, worker A processes one of two pages and yields with:

- one pending job
- attempt count 1
- `completed_passes = 0`
- `pages_processed = 1`
- source cursor `{ "offset": 1 }`
- one entity and one inbox row

The harness changes only the exact `index_schemas.status` value to `retired`.

Worker B must then receive `SchemaRetired` before the pending job can be claimed. PostgreSQL and the counted source must retain:

- the same job UUID
- attempt count 1
- the same cursor and progress
- cleared lease ownership
- one total source scan
- one job, one entity, and one inbox row

## Reactivation and resume

After the schema returns to `active`, a newly constructed runner must claim the same pending job instead of inserting another row. It resumes from `{ "offset": 1 }` and completes with:

- the same job UUID
- attempt count 2
- one page processed in the resumed invocation
- one completed pass
- one applied mutation
- durable `pages_processed = 2`
- null terminal source cursor
- one job, two entities, and two inbox rows

## Retired terminal scope

The schema is retired again after success. Another invocation must return `SchemaRetired` before the retained succeeded job is resolved as `AlreadyComplete`. Source scans and durable counts stay unchanged.

Once active again, the same request returns `AlreadyComplete` for the succeeded job without another source scan.

## PostgreSQL isolation

The target reads `RUSTOK_INDEX_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, with PostgreSQL `DATABASE_URL` as a fallback. Without a PostgreSQL URL it reports a skip and succeeds.

Each invocation creates a unique schema, creates the tenant owner fixture, applies every real `IndexModule` migration, materializes canonical source/schema registries, reads durable evidence, and drops the schema.

No sleep, polling, elapsed-time expiry, or concurrent race is used.

## Scope boundaries

- no production code, migration, reconciliation SQL/state-machine, schema registration API, source/cursor contract, mutation identity, diagnostic, or public API change
- no authorized schema retirement/reactivation transport
- no automatic scheduler behavior for retired scopes
- no retry/backoff, dead-letter admission, or operator requeue
- no cancellation, lease-loss, heartbeat, takeover, or restart race
- no source-call timeout or pending-future preemption
- no digest comparison, orphan cleanup, targeted/full/shadow repair, locale/partition dimensions, or complete drift repair

The canonical M6 reconciliation and drift-repair item remains open.

## Compatibility

- nine new test, documentation, and verifier files; final diff is add-only
- no changed-file overlap with open Index PRs #2636, #2639, #2642, #2644, #2648, #2649, #2652, #2656, #2660, #2663, #2667, #2679, #2684, #2689, #2693, #2698, #2703, or #2719
- no implementation-plan edit while PR #2636 owns the canonical plan
- merge base: `main` at `4b9789b31831010aa3d23055350e862a529cf4b6`
- current `main` advanced through unrelated Forum/Distribution/Admin changes to `f0a342a8713fd9a29ce485e6e1481a7099810b77`

## Validation

Not run per maintainer instruction:

- Cargo formatting/checks/tests/Clippy
- JavaScript verifier
- PostgreSQL integration target
- CI workflows

Suggested maintainer commands:

```bash
RUSTOK_INDEX_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://... \
  cargo test -p rustok-index \
  --test source_reconciliation_schema_admission_postgres_test \
  -- --nocapture

cargo check -p rustok-index --all-targets

node scripts/verify/verify-index-reconciliation-schema-admission-harness.mjs
```

## Branch state

Branch: `agent/index-m6-reconciliation-schema-admission-harness-20260731`

The connector produced eleven sequential commits. One accidental temporary `.contract` add/delete pair remains in branch history but is absent from the final diff. Squash merge is recommended after maintainer validation.

author: juchengquan
body:
Phase 3b step 2, partially. **The VC is complete; the compact tab root is deliberately not wired**, for a reason that applies to all four remaining tabs.

## The blocker (the important part)

The tab chrome — the add-transaction FAB and the focused-tx sheet — is a SwiftUI `ViewModifier` (`TabChrome`) applied to *hosted* roots. A native `UINavigationController` tab root gets none of it, so swapping the root in **silently loses the FAB**. I found it by writing a `TabChromeHost.wrap` that doesn't exist and letting the compiler say so.

That's a visible regression, and it isn't Scheduled-specific. **A UIKit tab-chrome equivalent has to land before any tab root converts** — otherwise every converted tab ships missing its `+`. Recorded in `uikit-migration-plan.md` as a prerequisite.

## What's here

`ScheduledListVC`, complete: list/calendar mode picker, month-grouped sections with the "Ended" bucket, detected recurring charges, name search, empty and no-result states, swipe actions (Edit/Delete trailing, Post leading — that order is deliberate, see the SwiftUI row), context menu, and selection mode.

`ScheduledRow`, `ViewModePickerRow` and `ScheduledCalendarView` are **hosted as leaves**. The `UICollectionView` remains the scroll view, so this is not reproducer B, and none of the three can drift from the copy the Mac still renders. Same split as `AccountDetailVC`, which this is modelled on.

`ScheduledPostSheetContent` goes private → internal so the UIKit path presents the **same** sheet `.scheduledPostSheet` does. Posting deliberately opens a prefilled sheet rather than posting instantly — `postNow` has to resolve *which* occurrence is meant first.

## Known cost of merging this alone

The iPad column uses `ScheduledListVC` while iPhone still renders `ScheduledTab` — the temporary duplication the Phase 3b correction warns about. Deliberate and short-lived: it's strictly better than a tab that lost its `+` button, and it resolves as soon as the tab chrome exists.

## Verification

iPhone and iPad builds succeed. **`ci-local.sh` was NOT run on this branch** — I ran out of session before it. Worth running before merge; the risk is the i18n guards, since this adds several `String(localized:)` sites.

author: dannbleeker
body:
Adversarial bug hunt over everything merged in #224–#228. Five hunters ran; this PR fixes the findings that **destroy work**. Every one was reproduced against the real functions first, and every guard added here was proven to go red without its fix.

## 1. Same Scale could blank every chart after the first slow one

`updateChartsInSlides` deleted **every** chart's old shapes in one shared sync, committed that, then redrew them one at a time. A single stalled redraw rejected the whole `PowerPoint.run` — leaving every chart *after* it in the batch empty: old shapes gone, new ones never queued.

This is not exotic. Same Scale runs across the whole deck and therefore always includes the chart on the visible slide, which is the one condition this repo has documented as reliably stalling a redraw.

Deleting per chart costs one extra sync each (against the many `renderShapesChunked` already spends) and bounds the damage to the chart that actually failed. The pane now names the chart instead of printing a generic failure. A **total** failure still throws, because `updateChartResilient` needs that throw to reach its slide-swap and picture fallbacks.

Fixing it exposed a second bug in the same function: with a chart dropped from the batch, the returned edit targets were read out of a now-shorter array *by position*, so every chart after a failure was handed the **next** chart's shape id — a target pointing at somebody else's chart, which the following update would overwrite.

## 2. Inserting the demo deck twice deleted one of the runs

Slot indices restart at 0 every run and the demo titles are fixed, so slot+title names an **item**, not an occurrence of one. Every slide of run 2 had a perfect twin in run 1, which the repair pass read as "this item landed twice" and fixed by deleting one of them.

`repairDeckSpan` scans the whole presentation, so this needed no unusual setup — just clicking the button a second time. PowerPoint's own **Duplicate Slide** copies the tag part too, so a demo slide the user duplicated to reuse was deleted on the next pass.

Every slide a run adds now carries a token identifying that run. A slide whose token does not match is reported as an orphan and never claimed.

## 3. The same pass deleted the user's own blank slides

`dropOrphanBlanks` is documented as safe because "the pane turns it on for its own run's range, where every slide is known to be ours" — but `repairDeckSpan` passed it over a span drawn around **every** PowerChart tag in the deck. A blank slide the user added between two demo slides sat inside that span and was swept as our own litter.

The span is now this run's own slides, and a blank slide carrying anyone else's tag is never deleted.

## 4. A half-finished slide swap left the chart on two slides, then drew a third

`replaceSlideWithDeck` answered the same `false` for "nothing landed" and "the new slide landed but the old one would not go". The caller treated them alike and fell through to its picture layer, which rasterized the chart onto the **surviving original** — one stall, the chart twice over, and a success message.

It now reports which happened, and the pane stops and says so. Its delete call is bounded now, like the insert above it — it runs on a host that has already stalled once, so leaving one call unguarded made it the one most likely to hang.

## Also

- An unmeasurable orphan no longer reports the `-1` "cannot tell" sentinel as a shape count.

## Verification

- `npm test` — 1649 passing (1641 before; 8 new guards, no test moved or removed).
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run coverage` — thresholds hold.
- Each guard stashed against its pre-fix source and confirmed red: 4/5 reconcile guards, the batch-isolation guard, the duplicated-swap guard. The two that pass either way are explicitly compatibility guards (an untokened old deck stays repairable; a single-chart failure still throws) and say so.
- **Showcase deck unchanged.** The run token is written only when a caller supplies one, so the skill's byte-deterministic output is untouched — verified part-by-part: only `docProps/core.xml` (pptxgenjs's own build timestamp) differs on a rebuild, every slide XML is identical.

## Not in this PR

The hunt also returned non-destructive findings — the run log never being enabled on the default fast path, two unbounded `rasterizeScene` calls that can hang the pane, and a stale late-sync signal that degrades a healthy run to pictures. Those are next, separately.

No manifest change — **no re-install needed**.

author: davidliedle
body: Two read-only lenses over the IRC client, the Browser DevTools and Svelte, then fixes for everything they proved. IRC — TLS was decorative against an active attacker. A raw SSLSocket validates the certificate CHAIN but not the HOSTNAME (unlike HttpsURLConnection, that check is off by default), so any CA-valid certificate for any domain completed a clean handshake and then received the SASL payload or the NickServ password sent moments later. setEndpointIdentificationAlgorithm(HTTPS) closes it; source-gated and mutation-proven. IRC — the bounded-reads law stopped at the line. The engine caps a line at 8k, but nothing capped what the WINDOW retained, and an IRC connection deliberately outlives its window: a busy channel left overnight grew an EDT-owned document until the IDE ran out of memory. Transcripts now drop whole head lines at a 1M-char ceiling; the same drop-dont-grow ceiling covers auto-created query tabs, nick sets, pending NAMES and WHOIS channels. DevTools — Swing rendered page-controlled text as HTML. Every string in these panes comes from the inspected page, and a JLabel whose text starts with renders it: a page naming a component made the IDE own JVM fetch that URL. Every tree, table and list now disables the HTML view; a source gate fails the build if a pane is added unguarded. Editor — the comment toggle could eat the next line. A line that both starts with the open marker and ends with the close one while being shorter than the pair () looked commented, and stripping that many characters swallowed the newline and the head of the following line: silent file corruption, proved with a scratch run of the real method. Also: long IRC messages split at UTF-8 boundaries instead of being silently truncated by the server while the local echo lied; a quit racing the reconnect timer cannot resurrect a zombie connection that identifies to NickServ invisibly; echo-message no longer bounces the NickServ password into the transcript; executeScript results are capped on OUR side of the page border; closing the Browser tab now actually stops the page; DOM labels re-capped Java-side; 19 unreachable Svelte completions fixed (prefix walk steps over # @ / : on text/x-svelte only). Installers: LICENSE and NOTICE now ride the assembled app, so DMG/tar.gz/deb/Windows inherit them from one Maven execution and the portable zip gets them appended in the workflow. PackagedLicenseGateTest checks the real assembled output at integration-test time, proven failing-first. The first verify caught my own wiring bug — the gate needs BOTH halves (excluded from the default test phase AND included in the packaged-app execution) or it runs before the app exists. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:
## Summary

Process-only: true

**Stacked on #54** — base is `fix/BES-ci-rails-and-client`, because the CI-failure alert edits the same `ci-summary` job. Merge #54 first, then this retargets to `main` cleanly. Scope: `/docs`, `.github`.

The Slack work was written but never committed, and would not have run if it had. All three entry points gated on `if: secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL != ''` — **the `secrets` context is not available in `if:` expressions**. GitHub rejects the workflow with `Unrecognized named-value: 'secrets'`.

## What changed

- **Webhook check moved inside the step** (env + shell guard). No webhook configured now means "log a skip and stay green" — it never fails a PR.
- **Payloads built with `jq`** instead of hand-quoted JSON inside a `curl` argument. Two reasons: any PR title containing a quote or apostrophe broke the JSON outright, and interpolating `${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` straight into a `run:` block is a **script-injection path** — titles are attacker-controlled. Values now reach the shell through `env:` only.
- **Routing by urgency**, matching the matrix in `docs/slack-integration.md`: `SLACK_ALERTS_WEBHOOK_URL` for CI-broke-`main`, urgent/blocked issues and `scope:contracts` PRs; `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` for ordinary PR traffic. One incoming webhook posts to one channel, so the matrix genuinely needs two secrets — the docs previously implied one could serve every row.
- **CI alerts only for `main`.** A failing PR is the author's business and stays out of Slack.
- **Double-posting documented.** `/github subscribe` and this workflow both announce PRs; `docs/slack-setup.md` now says to pick one (recommended: leave `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` unset, keep the GitHub app for ambient traffic, and let the workflow escalate contract changes only).

## How to test

1. Set `SLACK_ALERTS_WEBHOOK_URL` (see `docs/slack-setup.md` §5).
2. Open a PR labelled `scope:contracts` → alert lands in `#bpc-alerts`.
3. With no secret set at all, both workflows should run **green** and log a skip.

## Open questions

- Which channel each webhook binds to is yours to decide — the docs assume `#bpc-alerts` and `#bpc-prs`.
- Linear and Notion rows in the routing matrix are configured **in those tools**, not here. `docs/slack-integration.md` now says so explicitly, so nobody debugs this repo looking for them.

## What was implemented

This PR implements a unified diff parser and model for the Terminal UI Kit project (Issue #32).

## Changes

### New Files

- include/terminal_ui_kit/diff/diff_model.h - Diff model structures per PRD section 28.3
- include/terminal_ui_kit/diff/unified_diff_parser.h - Unified diff parser header

### Modified Files

- src/terminal_ui_kit/CMakeLists.txt - Added diff module as compiled library
- tests/terminal_ui_kit/unit/CMakeLists.txt - Added diff_parser_test to unit tests

## Architecture Decisions

1. **Model-View Separation**: The diff model is completely independent of any UI framework. It provides pure data structures that can be consumed by rendering components.

2. **No External Dependencies**: The parser uses only standard library features (C++20).

3. **UTF-8 Safety**: The parser operates on std::string_view for efficiency without copying.

4. **Simple Path Normalization**: The parser removes a/ and b/ prefixes from paths for cleaner display.

## Testing

All 173 tests pass, including 8 new tests for the unified diff parser.

This PR addresses issues identified by the review subagent:
- Removed unused ParseFileHeaders() and ParseHunkRange() methods
- Fixed unsafe spans()[0] access by adding GetLineText() helper
- Fixed path parsing to handle a/ and b/ prefixes

author: agnaldo4j
body:
**GAP-DY reaberto.** Ele foi para Done com metade feita — colhido no pós-merge do #394 e verificado por mim antes de agir.

## O sítio que ficou

A política *"nome de `ServiceClass` desconhecido → `STANDARD`"* vivia em **dois** lugares do `sql_persistence`, em formas diferentes:

| arquivo | forma | #394 |
|---|---|---|
| `LegacyDecode.kt:30` | `ServiceClass.fromNameOrDefault(...)` | convertido |
| `SimulationSerializerScenarioMappings.kt:106` | `decodeEnum(serviceClass, ServiceClass.STANDARD)` | **ficou para trás** |

Mudar o default num não mudava no outro. É o modo de falha do #388 (sítio adjacente da mesma classe deixado para trás) e exatamente o que o `migrations.md` avisa: *"o mesmo tipo decodificado em dois lugares precisa dos dois consertos"*.

Teste novo no eixo do **card** — o `SimulationSerializerTest` já cobria o eixo da **decisão**, e foi essa separação que escondeu o sítio. Probe: trocando por `ServiceClass.valueOf`, o teste falha ✓

## Os dois guards que deixaram passar

**1. O par não-vácuo media o nome, não a política.** Ele se chama *"a politica de parse tolerante de ServiceClass tem exatamente um ponto de declaracao"* mas assertava `functions.filter { it.name == "fromNameOrDefault" }.size == 1` — unicidade do **nome**. Ficava verde com a política duplicada.

Agora ancora na **constante de fallback**: `ServiceClass.STANDARD` fora do domínio significa política reimplementada, seja com `?:`, `decodeEnum` ou qualquer outra forma. Dentro do domínio ela é legítima (é o default declarado de `Card` e de `Decision.AddItem`).

> Nome de fitness function é lido como a garantia. Este prometia mais do que media.

**2. O conjunto derivado era mais largo que o nome.** A derivação por `= Tipo.CONSTANTE` raspa toda **atribuição**, não só default declarado — **13 entradas para 4 defaults reais**, entrando `MovementType.MOVED`, `CardState.DONE`, `AbilityName.TESTER` do corpo do `SimulationEngine`/`Card`/`Worker`.

Não dava falso verde (era mais **estrito**), mas o primeiro alarme pareceria bug do guard e não problema do código. Exigir a **declaração de tipo** antes do `=` deixa exatamente os 4: `CardState.TODO`, `ServiceClass.STANDARD`, `SimulationStatus.DRAFT`, `Instant.EPOCH` — e o defeito original do GAP-DT (`DRAFT`) segue coberto.

## Probes

| probe | esperado | obtido |
|---|---|---|
| o sítio que escapou volta (`decodeEnum` + `STANDARD`) | vermelho | ✅ — **o guard novo o vê** |
| adapter escolhe `DRAFT` com `?:` (defeito do GAP-DT) | vermelho | ✅ — segue mordendo após estreitar |
| `?: MovementType.MOVED` (**não** é default declarado) | verde | ✅ — over-reach removido |

## Verificação

`./gradlew testAll` verde. Mutação com `--rerun-tasks`:

| módulo | score | gate |
|---|---|---|
| `sql_persistence` | 537/729 = **73,7%** | 65 |
| `domain-kanban` | 284/337 = **84,3%** | 78 (módulo não tocado) |

author: atepem
body:
## Why

Two new HIGH advisories are failing the `yarn audit (production deps)` gate on `main`, blocking every open PR.

## postcss — fixed by bump

**GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849** — path traversal in previous-source-map auto-loading (`sourceMappingURL`) leading to arbitrary `.map` file disclosure.

Bumped the **existing** resolution `8.5.12` → `8.5.25`. Same minor line, no API change. Reached via `next > postcss` and `@binance/w3w-* > tailwindcss > postcss`.

## brace-expansion — allowlisted, with a tested reason

**GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg** — DoS via unbounded expansion length causing an OOM crash.

I tried the resolution first. It does not work:

- The fix exists **only on the 5.x line** (`>=5.0.8`). The `maintenance-v2` line tops out at `2.1.4`, still inside the advisory range — so there is no in-major upgrade path.
- Resolving to `5.0.9` **breaks the build**: `NX  expand is not a function`. brace-expansion 5.x's CJS export is not a drop-in for the 2.x default export that `minimatch` 5.x calls.

So it is allowlisted with a review date of 2026-10-31, on the same reachability argument as the two existing `js-yaml` entries. All 10 paths sit behind `minimatch` in build-time tooling:

```
@nx/next > @nx/js > minimatch > brace-expansion
@nx/next > @nx/devkit > ejs > jake > minimatch > brace-expansion
@binance/... > tailwindcss > sucrase > glob > minimatch > brace-expansion
@solana/... > expo-constants > @expo/fingerprint > minimatch > brace-expansion
```

Those globs are our own config patterns, never untrusted input, and none of this is in the shipped Next.js runtime bundle. Revisit when `minimatch` ships a release depending on `brace-expansion >=5.0.8`.

## Verification

- [x] `yarn audit:prod` — OK (3 allowlisted, no unlisted high/critical)
- [x] `yarn lint:lockfile` — no issues
- [x] `yarn audit:install-hooks` — OK (8 allowlisted); regenerated allowlist is byte-identical, so no new install hooks
- [x] `nx run marketplace:build` — succeeds on postcss 8.5.25 (this is what caught the brace-expansion break)

CI will exercise the remaining app builds.

## Note

This unblocks #441, which is currently red only on this gate.

# How to reproduce
- Create a product with a tag that is not visible to customers
- Go to the website shop page
- Search for the tag's name

# The issue
The product & the tag are displayed even though they should
be invisible to customers

# Cause
This commit introduced the search on tags :
https://github.com/odoo/odoo/commit/9394e17a07cb125914fba137405c152bee2d7618

It did by simply adding `product_tag` to the fields searched by
the autocomplete :
https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/9394e17a07cb125914fba137405c152bee2d7618/addons/website_sale/models/product_template.py#L901

The issue is that when building the domain to do the actual search, we
simply do a big OR with an ilike search for all the searched fields :
https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/f8d82f481b575a7a009234d9628fc8c604d0cf22/addons/website/models/mixins.py#L680-L686

# Proposed solution
Move the domain creation for search fields in a new function. This
allows us to override the simple ilike domain creation and create a custom
domain based on the `visible_to_customers` field of tags

Furthermore, we also need to prevent the invisible tags from being rendered
because a product may contain visible & invisible tags

author: vitalyvorobyev
body:
The follow-up to 0.3.1 is a **minor bump, not the 0.3.2 the roadmap named** —
that open question (REL-07) is now answered and the answer is recorded in both
docs rather than left implied by the version number.

## Why it has to break

- `StreamBuilder::auto_packet_size` is removed (SR-10).
- The Python `open_stream(auto_packet_size=)` argument is renamed to `packet_size=`.
- `viva-camctl stream --auto` becomes `--packet-size <BYTES>`.
- GA-09 adds variants to `NodeDecl` and `Node`.

Cargo reads `^0.3` as any 0.3.x, so shipping these as a patch would break
dependents on their next `cargo update`. **Consequence: roadmap Phase 5's "0.4.0
API consolidation" renumbers to 0.5.0**, and its heading now says why.

## Contents

TC-17 (GVSP trailer offset), TC-20 (Linux link-local discovery), TC-19 (chunk
path reachable end to end), DX-08 (`stream`/`bench`/`events` without `--iface`),
SR-10 (probed MTU no longer discarded), SR-11 (unnamed pixel format sized from
its PFNC code), DC-01 (Zenoh bridge stops truncating unsizeable frames), the
GA-09 first cut (`<Register>` with a plain `<Length>`), and `#[non_exhaustive]`
on the five public enums that actually grow.

## The mechanical part is larger than the six documented touchpoints

A minor bump makes the intra-workspace caret ranges unsatisfiable once
published, so **27 `version = "0.3"` ranges across 8 `crates/*/Cargo.toml`
manifests** go to `"0.4"`. Two things a blind sweep gets wrong, both now
recorded in REL-07:

- **`studio/` is not among them.** It references the viva crates by `path`
  alone, with no version — as does `viva-pygenicam`.
- **Four of the 31 repo-wide `version = "0.3"` matches are `tracing-subscriber`**,
  a third-party crate genuinely at 0.3. Bumping those would be wrong.

**All four lockfiles are refreshed**, not just the root: `studio/`,
`studio/apps/viva-studio-tauri/src-tauri/` and `crates/viva-pygenicam/` each
pin the workspace crates by version.

## Also in here

- The changelog entry **#107 landed without** — the `#[non_exhaustive]` change,
  including what was deliberately *not* marked and why, and the cost (it binds
  only other crates, so our own cross-crate matches lose compile-time
  exhaustiveness and each new arm fails loudly instead).
- **REL-07 moved back into the REL table.** It had drifted below the REL-01
  detail table, where it rendered as a row of the wrong table.

## Gates

All three Rust workspaces, run from the repo root:

| Gate | Result |
|------|--------|
| `cargo fmt --all --check` (root) | PASS |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` (root) | PASS |
| `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps` | PASS (exit 0, 0 warnings) |

body:
Summary

This pull request adds a reproducible, leakage-safe evaluation of the
training-only popularity recommender on the Microsoft MIND-small dataset.

Implemented

  • added a popularity evaluation pipeline using the strict chronological split;

  • fitted popularity scores exclusively on training interactions;

  • evaluated validation candidate rankings with the common ranking evaluator;

  • added the evaluate-popularity CLI command;

  • added unit, integration, smoke, and CLI tests;

  • generated a machine-readable evaluation report;

  • verified deterministic results across repeated runs;

  • updated the README and project roadmap; and

  • added detailed evaluation methodology and limitations.

Reproduction

python -m newslens evaluate-popularity \
  --data-dir data \
  --k 10 \
  --validation-fraction 0.20 \
  --output reports/popularity_metrics.json

Results

Metric | Result -- | -- NDCG@10 | 0.2853 MRR@10 | 0.2308 Recall@10 | 0.5047 Hit Rate@10 | 0.5705 Catalog Coverage@10 | 0.0402 Evaluated impressions | 31,393 Empty rankings | 0 Unique recommended articles | 2,061 Unseen candidate occurrence rate | 30.36%

The model was fitted using 125,572 chronological training records and evaluated
on 31,393 later validation records. Validation interactions were not used for
model fitting.

Validation

  • python -m ruff check .

  • python -m pytest — 120 passed

  • git diff --check

  • repeated evaluation produced an identical JSON report

  • GitHub Actions

Artifacts

  • reports/popularity_metrics.json

  • docs/EVALUATION.md

  • updated README.md

  • updated ROADMAP.md

Limitations

  • this pull request formally evaluates only the popularity baseline;

  • popularity reflects historical exposure as well as user interest;

  • catalog coverage is limited to approximately 4.02%;

  • content-based and fallback evaluation remains future work;

  • the official MIND-small development split remains reserved as a final
    holdout;

  • no confidence intervals or subgroup analyses are reported; and

  • offline ranking results do not establish online product impact.

Next steps

  • evaluate the content-based history recommender;

  • evaluate and measure the cold-start fallback;

  • compare all baselines using identical validation impressions;

  • analyze warm-start, cold-start, and unseen-article performance; and

  • add confidence intervals and subgroup analysis.

author: estebanzimanyi
body:
This PR is the inert first phase of bringing the value-domain layer (`Set<T>` / `Span<T>` / `SpanSet<T>`) under the inherited SQL generator. It adds a manifest axis and documentation only: **it emits no SQL**, changes no `.in.sql` or `.c` file, and `python3 tools/codegen/inherited/generate.py --validate` output is unchanged (all self-regen checks OK).

## `manifest.yaml`: new `setfamilies:` axis

A descriptive axis with one row per set type (16 rows), carrying the tokens a later generation phase consumes:

- `set` / `base` — the set type and its base type (`MEOS_SETTYPE_CATALOG`, `meos_catalog.c:265-280`)
- `ordered` — the base has a semantic total order (int, bigint, float, text, date, timestamptz); this flag is what decides whether position operators are emitted at all
- `posops_spelling` — `value` (`<< >> &< &>`) for numbers + text, `time` (`<<# #>> &<# #&>`) for date + timestamptz; omitted when not ordered
- `metric` — `<->` / `setDistance` is deployed (derived from the live `.in.sql`: all ordered bases except text, plus geomset/geogset/npointset/poseset/cbufferset)
- `spatial` — the set is `spatialset_type()` (`meos_catalog.c:909-914`): geomset, geogset, npointset, poseset, cbufferset, h3indexset, quadbinset; pcpointset/pcpatchset are `pointcloudset_type()` (`:950-954`, no bounding box) and are therefore not marked spatial

The axis has no `files:` entries and no template; the generator ignores unknown manifest keys, so no parsing change is needed and the emitted output is byte-identical.

## `INHERITANCE_MAP.md`: new §9 for the value-domain classes

- Class membership with catalog cites: 16 set types, 5 span types, 5 spanset types.
- Why the 16-vs-5 asymmetry: every base type has a set type because `getValues` returns the range of a temporal value as a set, while `Span<T>` needs a total order **and** a meaningful contiguous interval (`span_basetype()` = numbers + time; `span_canon_basetype()` marks the discrete bases that canonicalize with +1). Order alone is not enough: text is ordered but has no textspan.
- The section-by-section state of `doc/set_span_types.xml`: all twelve `<sect1>` groups are hand-written today.
- The template-class principle: `Span`/`SpanSet`/`TBox` are one C struct parameterized by a basetype field, so generation happens at the template level — one `span<T>` template covers every instantiation.
- The per-family SQL file map (the `temporal/001–015` reference layer plus the 8 per-family set files) and a table of what each axis token encodes.

The document header now names `doc/set_span_types.xml` as the ordering authority for the value-domain classes, and §4a points to the new section.

author: rickfelix
body:
## The QF's diagnosis was wrong, and its prescribed fix would have broken a healthy session

QF-20260729-704 reads *"a dead process is writing its own liveness"* and instructs: **find and stop the writer.**

I reproduced the symptom live on session `e7c92ad8` using the QF's own acceptance measurement — two readings 60s apart, `heartbeat_at` advancing 15:47:45 → 15:48:45 — then checked the OS on every PID involved:

| PID | role | OS |
|---|---|---|
| 6888 | tick daemon | RUNNING (node) |
| 13028 | watched parent | **RUNNING (claude)** — what the daemon verifies |
| 35464 | `claude_sessions.pid` | **NOT RUNNING (ESRCH)** — what every consumer checks |

**The writer is alive and correct.** The session is genuinely alive under a *rotated* parent PID; the row is lying about which process owns it. Stopping the writer would have killed the heartbeat of a working seat that was holding `SD-LEO-FIX-UNOWNED-PARENT-SLICE-001`.

## Root cause

`rediscoverParentPid()` adopts the rotated PID and persists it to the **marker file only**. The steady-state PATCH deliberately writes just the two timestamps and never `pid`, so the row advertises the original PID forever.

`QF-20260727-703` already found this exact defect and fixed the marker. **This is that fix, one field short.**

It also *inverts with usefulness*, for the reason `session-tick.cjs:554` already warns about: only long-lived sessions rotate their PID, so the seats that have done the most work are precisely the ones advertising corpses.

Not the same bug as the original corpse in the QF — `70ae81ad` is now frozen at 1344m, so the self-adoption guard at `:185` did close that path. Same signature, different mechanism, which is why three sessions read that row three ways.

## Fix

`persistAdoptedPid()` writes the adopted PID back to `claude_sessions.pid`, scoped exactly like the steady-state PATCH (`status=in.(active,idle,stale)`) so a released row is never resurrected, and fail-soft so telemetry correctness can never stop a healthy tick. The PID written has already been proven live by `process.kill(pid,0)` inside `rediscoverParentPid`.

Also corrected the live row (`e7c92ad8`: 35464 → 13028) after re-verifying both PIDs at the OS immediately before the write. That seat was one claim-sweep away from being reaped as dead while working.

## Verification

- Mutation-tested: removing the call reproduces the pre-fix state and kills all three new assertions.
- The hot-path guard asserts the steady-state body is **exactly** the two timestamps — asserting the exact shape rather than the absence of `pid`, since absence also passes if the body is deleted, and the first-tick POST legitimately carries `pid`.
- Test-side CRLF normalisation with a length guard: a `\n`-anchored slice on this repo's CRLF source returns nothing and would make every assertion vacuous rather than failing.
- Fleet/liveness surface: **1,825 passing, 0 failures**.

author: skyline10124
body:
## 概述

把 `observe.workspace` 的 read/list/grep/find 四种 mode 从 native handler 迁成独立维护的 WASM Component Tool。Component 只负责 typed mode dispatch 与 result shaping；全部 filesystem authority（System Path Exclusion、safe symlink/root containment、read denial、ignored-path inclusion、bounded result、observation budget、effects/audit）经 Tool Host `workspace-observe` imports 强制执行。

不得重新引入 `ExecutionBackend`、Upper、projection、ambient WASI filesystem 或 native fallback。四种 observation operation 共享同一 visibility decision。

## 核心变更

### Local Workspace 下移
- `lancet-native/src/workspace/` 整体 git mv 到 `lancet-runtime/src/workspace/`（host imports 不能向上跨层调用）
- async 原语抽成 `*_blocking` 同步方法，一份实现同时服务 sync host import 与 async native handler
- `lancet-native` 经 `pub(crate) mod workspace { pub(crate) use lancet_runtime::workspace::*; }` 路径别名继续使用同一具体类型
- 分层图新增 `lancet-runtime -> lancet-authority` 边，无环

### Tool Host workspace imports（核心权限模块）
- 新 `crates/lancet-runtime/src/host_workspace.rs`：`WorkspaceObservationHost` 实现 WIT `workspace-observe` interface（read-file/list-dir/grep/find-files 四函数，一个 interface 保证四 mode 不可拆分链接）
- 每次调用：parse project-relative path → authorize `alloc:read:workspace` → budget charge → `resolve_facts_blocking`（symlink/root containment）→ `VisibilityEngine` 可见性裁决 → `ObservationLimits` 截断
- `composition.rs` 的 `channels_for_domain_imports` 把 `workspace-observe` import 映射到 Workspace channel，组合门禁 fail-closed

### Guest 只做 dispatch 与 shaping
- `tools/observe-workspace/`（no_std）：按 `mode` const 判别分发四分支，结果整形（行窗口 + `[TRUNCATED]` 标记）
- manifest 顶层声明 `imports = ["workspace-observe"]`，params/result 为 oneOf 四分支 union schema

### 三态截断证据
- `ObservedEffect.truncated: Option<bool>`（None = 无边界 / Some(false) = 有界未截 / Some(true) = 截断），host 计算、guest 不可伪造
- `EVIDENCE_SCHEMA_VERSION` 2→3，`evidence_effects` 加 `truncated INTEGER` 可空列，走 `ALTER TABLE` 可加性迁移

### 错误直通与措辞契约
- host 拒绝经 `take_refusal`/`host_refusal` 以结构化 `CepError` 直达调用方
- `PathRejection` 结构化枚举 + `classify_path_error`，钉住模型可见措辞
- symlink 逃逸拒绝用固定措辞，不泄漏宿主绝对路径

### catalog 与 authority 同步摘除
- `lancet-catalog` 降为三个 native 方法（Create/Edit/Fetch）
- authority 删 `observe.workspace` policy arm 与 `extract_observe_workspace_path`
- native handler/registration/executor render/effect-contract observation fixtures 全部删除

## 迁移中对抗验收发现并已修的三处真缺陷

1. **symlink 逃逸拒绝泄漏宿主绝对路径**（`/tmp/.tmpXXX/escape.txt`）→ `observation_io_error` 穷举匹配 `LocalWorkspaceError` 变体，`SymlinkRejected` 用固定措辞，加防泄漏断言
2. **host 结构化拒绝被 guest 包装**（`tool X guest error:` 前缀 + 错误码退化为 `ExecutionFailed`）→ `take_refusal`/`host_refusal` 直通通道
3. **v2 evidence 文件因缺 `truncated` 列被形状守卫拒绝** → `truncated` 移出阻断守卫，走 `ALTER TABLE` 可加性迁移

## 语义变化

root 逃逸的错误码从 `GuardDenied`（legacy policy hook 归一化）变为 `PathContainment`（host 路径解析自报，与 native workspace 层对同类失败已用代码一致），harness 场景断言已更新并在 `FINDINGS.md` 记档。

## 验证

- `env -u LATTICE_BIN cargo xtask ci` 全部通过（fmt、clippy `-D warnings`、build、harness-boundary、lancet-boundary、tool-codegen `--check`、29 个 crate 测试、tool-build `--verify`）
- 对抗性验收 11 条 body 标准 + 4 条执行说明标准 + 审查 comment 边界建议，全部通过
- 测试统计：lancet-runtime 141+16、lancet-audit 88、lancet-native 76+10、lancet-catalog 26、lancet-cep 8、lancet-authority 138、harness 141

> **注意**：本机交互 shell profile 导出 `LATTICE_BIN=/home/astrin/Dev/lattice/target/debug/lattice`（主仓库旧二进制），会让 harness 场景测到旧分发路径。跑 harness/CI 前须 `env -u LATTICE_BIN`。

Closes #30

author: taras
body:
Stack: PR 6 — the last slice of #195. Base is `main` at 68f446f, which includes #252 and #254.

## Why

Everything #195 needs existed after PR 5, and no document could use it: `<WebForm>` was registered by nothing the CLI ran. This wires it in, publishes the package that holds it, and documents it.

Playwright coverage is split out to **#256** by agreement.

## What a document can now write

```md
<WebForm schema={reviewSchema} as="review">
# Review required

Read the plan above and decide.
</WebForm>
```

Verified end to end through `xmd run`, not by inspection: the real 620 KB client bundle is served, `validator.js` registers, and a submission returns 204.

## The release was forced, not chosen

This is worth reading before the diff, because it explains most of it.

`build-npm.ts` resolves internal sibling versions from **`deno.json`**. A member with no `name` there cannot be a dependency of a package that is itself published to npm — the CLI's npm build fails outright with *"no workspace version found for internal dependency @executablemd/web"*. So wiring the CLI required `packages/web` to become a real, published package. There is no variant of this PR that ships the CLI integration and defers publication.

Publishing it then surfaced two things the earlier slices left implicit:

- **`deno publish` refused the package.** The generated bundle is gitignored, so it was excluded, and JSR rejects a module that sits in the graph but would not exist at runtime. A negated `publish.exclude` glob puts it in the artifact while the repository still does not track it.
- **Nothing built it.** `deno task build:web` appeared in no workflow, so the npm build of any dependent would have failed. It now runs in `test-deno` — which builds the CLI's npm artifact — and unconditionally in `publish-one`, because dnt packages a package's workspace siblings too.

The generated publish workflow derived the order itself: `web` needs `[version, core, durable-streams]`.

## A bug PR 5 shipped

`assets.ts` read `CLIENT_JS`/`THEME_CSS`; the generator writes **`clientJs`/`themeCss`**. `<WebForm>` could never have served a real page.

Nothing caught it because every test substitutes the `FormAssets` seam, so the real reader never met real generator output. The new contract test evaluates actual `generatedModule()` output against `readAssets`, and I confirmed it discriminates by reintroducing the old names — it fails, then passes when restored.

A missing bundle now reports *"run `deno task build:web`"* rather than a raw module-not-found naming a path nobody chose.

## Two tests that were wrong about the world

- **`build-web-client.test.ts` deleted the real generated module** in its cleanup. That made the npm build test pass or fail depending on which ran first — I hit it. It now restores whatever it found.
- **`publish-workflow-private.test.ts` asserted `packages/web` was withheld.** That stopped being true, and with no private member left its own `withheld.length > 0` vacuity guard failed. Rewritten as `publish-workflow-membership.test.ts`, asserting what holds — and saying plainly that **the private-exclusion path is now unexercised** until a private member exists again, so that guarantee currently rests on the release spec alone.

## Documentation

- `specs/executable-mdx-spec.md` §6.15 — the component in the spec's own catalogue, pointing at the full one.
- `specs/web-form-spec.md` — a bundled-client section recording the real sizes: **`clientJs` 620,803 bytes, `themeCss` 37,258**.
- `specs/release-process-spec.md` §8 — which jobs build the bundle and why, and the `publish.exclude` and its reason (Code Rule 8).
- `site/routes/docs/components.tsx` — an "Asking a person" section with a human-review example and the `uiSchema` variant.

## Verification

With Deno 2.9.1:

- `deno task lint` — 0 errors; `deno task check` — 0; `deno task test` — **300 passed, 2086 steps**; `deno task check:jsr` — success
- `pnpm test:node` — **2047 passed**; `pnpm exec tsc --project tsconfig.node.json` — clean
- `bun run test:bun` — **2047 passed**
- `deno task gen:publish-workflow` — committed copy matches
- `git diff --check` clean
- Compiled binary: registers `<WebForm>` and fails preflight with no browser, added as a CI smoke step
- `cd site && deno task check && deno task build` — both pass

## Known gaps, stated rather than left

- **`xmd test packages/web/src` fails**, because the colocated `src/WebForm.ts` is resolved as a *repository* component and exports no default. It fails fast with a clear message rather than hanging, and no CI step runs it — but it is a wart worth knowing about before anyone adds one.
- **`WebForm.test.md` still does not run under `xmd test`**, for the reason established in PR 5: a responder is installed by a host, never a document. It runs through `tests/document.test.ts`.
- **The private-member exclusion is unexercised** — see above.
- **No browser has rendered the page in CI** — that is #256.
- **The manual smoke check has not been run.** Playwright drives a Chromium it launched; only a human running `xmd run` exercises the platform opener finding the real default browser.

## For whoever releases this

`@executablemd/web` is new to the publish set. Per release spec §4 the JSR package must exist before the first tagged release — confirmed created. §6 notes that a package with `workspace:*` siblings cannot build its first npm artifact until those versions are on the registry (**#152**), which applies here.

author: martinhalvorson
body:
## Ownership claim

- Machine ID: `martin-mbp`
- Agent/session ID: `claude-r3-discovery`
- Task: discovery estimate labels
- Claimed paths: `src/bin/ai_eval.rs`, `docs/EVAL_INTEGRITY.md`
- Coordinated with: **#679** — it changes *construction* (`builtin_ai_strict`, seat dispatch) and owns §2/§3 + row 2 of the §9 table. This changes *reporting* (one helper, one flag parse, one `println!`) and owns §4/§8 + rows 3 and 6. No line overlap; split recorded at https://github.com/MartinHalvorson/CIVVIS/pull/679#issuecomment-5144971606
- Related issue/request: operator request; **item 3** (evaluator half) and **item 6** (recompute) of #661

## What changed

Two things, both making the evaluator tell the truth about a number: the reporting half of R3 (item 3), and a recompute of §8's restatement worklist (item 6).

### Part 1 — the evaluator half of R3

A gate accepts when the observed effect is large enough, so conditioning on
"passed" conditions on the estimate being *large*. Every headline size here is
inflated by an amount that grows as the true effect shrinks — `+207`→`+86`,
`+92`→`+61`, `+45`→excluded at `−8`. Direction and significance replicate; the
size fails, always downward.

```
promotion gate: PASS — advanced's effect interval ... clear parity after 24 maps
effect size:    +307 (DISCOVERY ESTIMATE — selected on passing the gate, so biased
                upward; not quotable until confirmed on a disjoint seed: rerun
                with --seed <new> --confirm 811000)
```

`--confirm <prior-seed>` marks a run as the replication of one already made. It
**refuses a seed equal to `--seed`**, because a rerun on the same maps confirms
nothing. A verdict the gate did not select on says so explicitly, so no reader
has to remember which verdicts condition on size.

### The two halves of R3 are pinned to each other

Every branch of `effect_size_line` names a seed — a token
`unevidenced_effect_sizes` (merged in #685) accepts as provenance — and
`every_effect_size_line_carries_provenance_the_docs_gate_accepts` asserts it
across all eight verdict/confirmation combinations. Verified end to end:

| line | merged docs gate |
|---|---|
| the `DISCOVERY ESTIMATE` line | accepted |
| the `CONFIRMED` line | accepted |
| the `not gate-selected` line | accepted |
| `Search is worth +307 Elo.` | **rejected** |

Without this, the tool would print numbers the repository's own docs check then
refuses.

### Part 2 — §8's worklist, recomputed (item 6)

§8 was counted **by hand**, before `ai_eval` could report axes. It is wrong on
**five of six rows, in both directions**:

| comparison | §8 counted | tool reports | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strategic` v `advanced` | 2 | **3** — architecture, weights, evaluator | undercount |
| `production` v `advanced` | 2 | **3** | undercount |
| `strategic_cheap` v `advanced` | 2 | **4** | undercount |
| `policy_wide` v `advanced` | 3 | **1** — weights | **overcount** |
| `policy` v `advanced` | 1 | 1 | correct |
| `advanced_evolved` v `advanced` | 1 | 1 | correct |

The missing axis is the same every time: a netless `strategic`/`production`
falls back to score-share terminal evaluation, so it differs in **evaluator** as
well as architecture — invisible to a reading of entrant names, which is exactly
why a hand count produced it wrong.

**And the prescribed fix does not fix them:**

| replacement pairing | axes remaining |
|---|---|
| `strategic` v `advanced_evolved` | architecture, evaluator — still 2 |
| `production` v `advanced_evolved` | architecture, evaluator — still 2 |
| `strategic_cheap` v `advanced_evolved` | + search-cheap — still 3 |
| `policy_wide` v `advanced_evolved` | **none** |

That last row is the sharpest result: `policy_wide` and `advanced_evolved`
differ on **nothing**. The recorded `policy_wide` result is a **self-comparison**
— not a mislabelled architecture result — and the same holds for
`policy_wide_frozen`. §8 filed it as the worst-confounded of the eight; it is
the one row that measures nothing at all.

The only entrant pairing that isolates search on one axis is
`strategic_cheap` v `strategic_score` (`search-cheap`). `strategic_deep` v
`strategic` — the comparison that produced the promoted **+45** — varies *two*
treatment components, so that number was never attributable to a single
mechanism, a defect prior to and separate from #482 excluding it on size.

**Standing rule recorded with it:** ask the tool. Read `arms differ on:` before
designing or citing a comparison.

## Validation

- [x] Branch started from current `origin/main`
- [x] Ownership/overlap is coordinated above
- [x] Latest `origin/main` merged before ready
- [x] `git diff --check origin/main...`
- [x] `cargo test --profile ci --locked` — **1,441 passed, 0 failed, 22 ignored**
- [x] Focused: 4 new tests in `src/bin/ai_eval.rs`; all four CLI paths exercised by hand (PASS→discovery, `--confirm`→confirmed, same-seed→exit 2, no-value→exit 2, INCONCLUSIVE→not-selected)
- [x] Cross-check against the merged #685 gate (table above)
- [x] Soak: not applicable — no engine code changed; the diff is one reporting helper, one flag, and a doc section. Agent construction and game play are untouched.
- [x] No unrelated formatting, generated output, or runtime artifacts

## Notes for integration

Squash merge only. Delete the branch after merge.

author: barmengolli
body:
Finishes the job Bite 4E started: every surface that renders a lead- or MQL-derived number is now audited, classified, and labeled, so no surface silently mixes the two counting models. Adds the lead drawer's campaign touch history. **No calculations changed in this bite.**

## Lead drawer: campaign touch history

The lead detail drawer gains a read-only "Campaign touches" section listing every membership recorded for the contact: channel name, touch date, provenance (parent / sub campaign), source badge (`import`, `n8n_sync`, `manual`, and `backfill` shown as "seed"), a **primary** marker on the contact's `source_channel_id` row, and a **(corrected)** disclosure whose tooltip carries the original Salesforce date whenever the Bite 4D importer applied Marketing's locked `marketing_sourced_date` instead of the report's. Newest first; undated memberships sort last and are labeled rather than dropped.

**Four distinct query states.** The page passes the real `useLeadCampaignTouches` status, so the section shows: "Loading campaign touches…" while in flight; "Campaign touches could not be loaded. Try refreshing the page." on failure (raw error text never rendered); the empty state **only** after a successful load with zero rows; and the history otherwise. An error is never reported as an empty history, and the rest of the drawer stays open and visible in every state.

## The audit

`docs/counting-basis-audit.md` classifies every surface as one of three bases, each now stated in the UI:

- **Memberships (overlapping)** — funnel lead/MQL reporting counts campaign memberships from `lead_campaign_touches`. A contact in several campaigns counts in each, so channel totals intentionally overlap and exceed distinct contacts. Covers the Data Entry grid and drilldown, the three year lead charts, Actuals vs Projections, Channel Distribution, Conversion Funnel, and Quarterly Trend. All were already switched in Bite 4E; this bite labels them. The dashboard's unassigned notice now correctly says "campaign touches … have no channel".
- **Primary source** — one channel per person. Spend, Events, Opportunities, Channels, and the Campaigns scorecard.
- **Unique contacts** — distinct people. The Leads utility page and the grid's unique-contacts line.

**No currently visible, in-scope surface required a calculation switch in Bite 4F**: every channel x lead/MQL count already flowed through the 4E computation path.

## Locked decision: Spend stays primary-source-based

Spend, CPL, CPMQL, acquisition-efficiency denominators, and ROI remain primary-source-based per the locked decision in `docs/lead-multi-attribution-program.md` section 2. This is recorded, not open. Membership denominators would credit the same contact to several channel budgets at once, lowering every channel's CPL and CPMQL without a cent of spend changing or a single new person acquired. Consequence, stated on the Spend page itself: **Spend figures and funnel membership totals come from different models on purpose and will not reconcile** — the grid's lead count for a channel is expected to exceed the count behind that channel's CPL, and that gap is the multi-campaign overlap, not an error.

The Campaigns scorecard likewise stays primary-source-based for now, pending the Bite 4H influence report where campaign overlap is the explicit subject. Deal-side surfaces (Opportunities, velocity) keep primary-source channel inheritance per program decision 1.4.

## Hidden legacy surfaces

The Funnel Flow Sankey and the Funnel Compare page are hidden today and were **not** audited. Both carry the legacy primary-source basis and neither is wired to the 4E path (`computeFunnelSankey` has a bespoke per-lead derivation). Per the bite rule, no new logic was built for a hidden surface. Both are recorded as hidden legacy surfaces that must be classified, and either switched or explicitly labeled, before restoration.

## Scope and safety

No database, schema, migration, RLS, n8n, dependency, environment, CI, or production-data changes. No new network writes; the touch history is read-only. Calculation modules (`compute.ts`, `campaignScorecard.ts`, `computeChannelSpend.ts`, the Sankey, Compare, and Velocity surfaces) show zero diff against main.

## Verification

715 tests across 41 files (26 new: touch-history selection, drawer rendering and all four query states, and an audit-completeness guard that fails if a new lead-consuming page appears without a classification). Typecheck and production build pass; lint holds the pre-existing 41-error / 5-warning baseline; `git diff --check` clean.

**Production-data preview validation remains a manual acceptance step** once the preview is available: confirm multi-campaign contacts appear under each of their channels on the switched surfaces, and that person-level surfaces are unchanged.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
