author: steipete
body:
## Problem
Photo batches validated structure before processing but postponed base64 and URL checks until each image was written. A valid first private image remained on disk if the second was malformed or unsafe, while dual URL plus invalid base64 could incorrectly succeed.

## Fix
Validate every representation through the shared camera owner before publishing: bounded canonical base64, HTTPS, trusted resolved node host, and required host identity. Preserve the current atomic publisher and valid iOS, Android, and macOS behavior. Superseded outcome/writer changes from the original branch were removed.

## Proof
Five actual node-tool/filesystem regressions first reproduced leaked images or false success; five parser regressions independently failed before the fix. The repaired CLI, parser, real artifact lifecycle, and node owner now pass 158 tests. Repository guards, formatting, dead-export scan, and independent review are clean. Full local typechecking is blocked only by preexisting linked dependency versions older than the lockfile; hosted CI installs pinned dependencies. Production growth: 21 lines.

author: annesodub
body:
Adds two Brainstorm processes so the MIA group workflow runs from the pipeline editor, plus the reader and GUI work they depend on.

Independent of #6 — zero file overlap, so the two can merge in either order.

## Brainstorm processes

**`MIA: Export data to MIA2`** (`process_mia_bst2mia.m`) wraps `mia_bst2mia`, which gains `Subjects`/`SubjectsToSkip` filtering and an `Atlas` option. Contact matching handles the `Subject__Contact` naming that `process_mia_channel_concat` gives the group channel file, which is a different convention from the single-underscore bipolar montage names used elsewhere. When nothing matches at all the error prints both the table and channel-file names — that case is a naming mismatch rather than missing data, and would otherwise surface as a silently empty group result.

**`MIA: Visualize Averages`** (`process_mia_group_gui.m`) wraps the group viewer. `mia_group_gui` takes one ROI structure per condition plus the condition names, and needs R2020a or later for menus on `uifigure`.

## Supporting changes

**`mia_read_loc_tsv_table` now reads two table layouts.** It handled only Brainstorm iEEG atlas exports — one patient per file, contacts in a `Channel` column, laterality inferred from the label text. MIA coregistration tables have several patients per file with `Subject`/`Contact` columns, and carry labels like "amygdale" that name no side, so the text heuristic discarded every row. The layout is now detected from the columns present; for coregistration tables laterality comes from the sign of X, the duplicated `Prob` header (read back as `Prob`/`Prob_1`) is dropped case-insensitively, and numeric atlas index columns are filtered out. The apostrophe survives in contact names there, since SEEG prime notation is significant (`A'1` is not `A1`) and the names are matched against the channel file.

`OPTIONS` gains `.patient` and `.atlas`; supplying both skips the selection dialog so processes and scripts run without a window appearing. A missing atlas name now fails with the list of available ones instead of returning an empty table.

**The group channel folder has a stable name.** `import_raw` named it after the simulated signal (`matrix_sim_<date>_<time>`), which changed every run, so nothing downstream could point at it. It is now `GroupChannel`. The rename moves the files, so the study is re-read from the database — returning `sFilesNew.FileName` afterwards would hand back a path that no longer exists.

**Shared GUI palette.** Colours are factored out of the GUIs into `mia_palette`. The values match the website's `:root` tokens, so the toolbox and the site read as one brand. Colour distinguishes actions rather than decorating them: terracotta for the main action, cream for secondary, gold for comparing conditions.

## Housekeeping

`show_brainstorm.m` and `start_brainstorm.m` were unversioned working files (`.gitignore` excluded the first outright); they are now tracked, and `brainstorm3/` — a local install each user supplies — is ignored instead.

`CITATION.cff` is added, and `README_bst.md` now asks for the version actually run alongside the introductory paper, with `mia_get_version` to obtain it and the Westner et al. (2024) rationale. The repository URL is corrected from `MIA-iEEG/mia` to `MIA-iEEG/mia2`; every other reference in the tree already used `mia2`.

## Review notes

- **Not executed.** None of this Matlab was run — no Matlab available here. The commits are a grouping of existing working-tree changes, so the code wants testing against a real protocol before merge, particularly the two table layouts and the `GroupChannel` rename against an existing database.
- `README_bst.md` also **drops the Wang et al. (2025) reference** that was previously listed. Flagging in case that was not intended.
- `icons/example_snapshopt_mia.png` (1.7 MB) is deliberately **not** included. #6 ships a 49 KB WebP derived from it; say the word if the original should be tracked as the source.

author: mikelward
body:
Amethyst's focus-follows-mouse implementation is unusable because it dismisses popovers and panels — a known issue (ianyh/Amethyst#277) since 2015. The script now disables it, and the documentation explains why it can't carry over from the KDE setup.

## Changes

- **setup-macos**: Changed focus-follows-mouse from `true` to `false`. The setting is now explicitly written as false rather than left unset, because machines configured by earlier runs retain the old `true` value in preferences.

- **docs/MACOS.md**: Substantially expanded the window manager evaluation section:
  - Added new subsections for "Focus follows mouse" and "Layout model" to explain the key trade-offs between Amethyst and yabai
  - Documented why Amethyst's focus-follows-mouse breaks popovers (hit-tests only tracked windows before checking what's under the pointer, unlike yabai which checks first)
  - Explained that yabai 7.1.25 restored throw-to-space support with SIP enabled, removing the previous disqualifier
  - Clarified that yabai has no master/stack or column layout and upstream doesn't plan to add them, making it unsuitable despite better focus handling
  - Updated the recommendation to reflect that Amethyst still wins, but now as a genuine trade-off rather than a walkover
  - Updated "What doesn't carry over" section to clarify that focus-follows-mouse is Amethyst's own limitation, not a platform limit

- **setup-macos_test**: Updated tests to verify focus-follows-mouse is disabled:

author: storkme
body:
## Intent

Fixes #488. `check_belt_dead_ends` is dispatched from `validate/mod.rs` as the
live check, but only iterated `is_surface_belt` entities — an underground-belt
OUTPUT whose downstream tile was empty was never examined, so a genuine
dead-end passed validation silently. The abandoned duplicate in
`belt_flow.rs` (never dispatched) caught this case, and carried two orphaned
regression tests (`ug_output_dead_end_detected`, `ug_output_with_receiver_ok`)
that failed against the live check.

## Scope

- **In:** strengthen the live `check_belt_dead_ends` (`belt_structural.rs`) to
  examine UG outputs; port the two abandoned tests plus a new regression test
  found while re-running the full suite; delete the confirmed-dead
  `belt_flow.rs` duplicates of `check_belt_dead_ends`, `check_belt_loops`, and
  `check_belt_item_isolation`.
- **Out:** `belt_flow.rs` still has three other shadowed duplicates
  (`check_belt_throughput`, `check_output_belt_coverage`,
  `check_belt_inserter_conflict`) — the issue notes these "redirect cleanly"
  to their `belt_structural.rs` counterparts, but that cleanup wasn't part of
  this task's scope and is left for a follow-up.

## The fix

Added a second loop to `check_belt_dead_ends` in `belt_structural.rs`: for
each UG output, compute the downstream tile from its direction and flag it
(`Severity::Error`, `belt-dead-end`) unless a receiver sits there. Unlike
surface belts, a UG output has no "orphan segment" case — it only exists
because a paired UG input fed it, so it's always treated as a real flow
source (matches the existing `supplier_tiles` treatment one loop above).

**A false positive turned up while verifying against the full suite** (see
Verification below) and is fixed in the same commit: a UG output's own tile
is a full belt-like surface segment, so an inserter reaching *that* tile
drains it directly — the item never needs to reach the downstream tile at
all. This is exactly the "leapfrog" pattern the kovarex self-loop template
uses (alternating UG-output/UG-input pairs along one row, each output's tile
picked up by an inserter in the row below). The live surface-belt loop
already had the equivalent exemption (`chain_has_pickup`, which checks the
tail tile itself before walking upstream); the UG-output loop needed the
same check against `pickup_tiles` for its own `(e.x, e.y)`. Added
`ug_output_drained_by_own_tile_inserter_ok` to lock this in.

## Verification

- [x] `cargo test --manifest-path crates/core/Cargo.toml` (`--no-fail-fast`,
      one clean invocation): **all green** — 918 lib tests, 68 e2e (0
      ignored-as-failed), and every other test binary in `crates/core/tests/`.
      Confirmed `ug_output_dead_end_detected` **fails** (0 errors found, 1
      expected) against the live check before the fix, and **passes** after.
- [x] **New fixture errors found by the strengthened check, then resolved —
      not suppressed:** the first version of the fix (checking only the
      downstream tile) surfaced a real false positive in three fixtures, all
      the same underlying kovarex-self-loop layout accessed three ways:
      `tier_kovarex_self_loop`, `quality_differential_kovarex_self_loop_normal_vs_legendary`,
      `stacking_kovarex_family_exempt_s2` — each reported
      `[belt-dead-end] UG output at (23,7) facing East has no receiver at
      output tile (24,7)`. Decoded the snapshot: the UG output at (23,7) is
      the last of a leapfrog chain, drained directly by the inserter at
      (23,8) (pickup tile = (23,7), the UG output's own position) — not
      actually a dead end. Root-caused to the missing own-tile-pickup
      exemption (above) and fixed properly rather than weakening or
      re-blessing; all three pass cleanly on the corrected check.
- [x] `cargo clippy --manifest-path crates/core/Cargo.toml --all-targets` —
      zero warnings in either touched file; pre-existing warning count/shape
      elsewhere unchanged (verified against a `git stash`d baseline).
- [ ] WASM rebuild + browser eyeball — not done; this is a validator-logic
      change with no layout/geometry output, and the affected fixtures are
      exercised structurally by the e2e suite above.

## Deviations from intent

- Left `check_belt_throughput`, `check_output_belt_coverage`, and
  `check_belt_inserter_conflict` duplicates in `belt_flow.rs` alone — out of
  this task's scope (see Scope). The comment left in `belt_flow.rs` at the
  deleted `check_belt_loops`/`check_belt_item_isolation` site and the
  `check_belt_dead_ends` site explains what was removed and why, for whoever
  picks up that follow-up.
- Added one test beyond what was asked (`ug_output_drained_by_own_tile_inserter_ok`)
  to cover the false positive found during verification — flagged in the task
  instructions as something to report rather than silently absorb, so it's
  called out explicitly here rather than folded in quietly.

## Models / contracts touched

`docs/validator-reporting.md` — this check already emits one positioned
issue per instance (unchanged); the new UG-output loop follows the same
convention. No other contract docs affected.

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four generic media boundaries currently lose facts that users and models need: oriented JPEGs report encoded instead of displayed dimensions, common AVIF/M4V/M4B/HEIC containers lack complete canonical MIME mappings, quoted/extended attachment filenames are truncated or mishandled, and PNG-to-JPEG conversion retains a misleading source extension.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Normalize EXIF orientation at the two existing metadata owners while preserving the raw probe contract.
- Extend the canonical media MIME owner using actual installed `file-type` brand contracts, including AVIF image hydration and M4B audio classification.
- Replace fragile Content-Disposition matching with a dependency-free quote/escape-aware top-level parameter parser, validated UTF-8/Latin-1 extended decoding, safe plain fallback, and legacy Windows basename preservation.
- Route both direct and loaded JPEG conversion results through the existing JPEG filename normalizer.
- Preserve MIME sniffing, SSRF, traversal, existing `audio/mp4 -> .m4a` preference, public SDK surfaces, and plugin ownership. Matrix-specific video work is intentionally excluded.

## User Impact

- Photos taken in portrait orientation now display their actual dimensions to model, channel, and preview consumers.
- AVIF images, M4V videos, M4B audiobooks, and HEIC/HEIF sequences keep correct type and extension metadata.
- Downloaded attachment names survive quoted semicolons, escaped punctuation/spaces, international extended values, malformed fallback, and Windows drive/UNC/relative/mixed paths without weakening filename sanitization.
- Opaque images converted to JPEG are consistently returned as `*.jpg` from both optimization entry points.

## Evidence

- Frozen base: `e051a7bb4a6ba69b87391e990b00813114b1d482`; isolated candidate: `9eb53c2fcd7bbb2fef94c281a1d31cf4e75a012e`.
- Exact-head focused owner suites: **262 passing tests** across MIME, EXIF, full fetch/security, and current-turn image owners.
- Exact-head web-media/security cases: **5 passing tests**; 81 unrelated cases intentionally skipped.
- Final complete fetch/security suite: **77 passing tests**, including spoofed quoted parameters; escaped quote, semicolon, comma, space, hyphen, and multiple punctuation; malformed/unsupported extended fallbacks; and drive, UNC, nested, mixed, Unicode, punctuation, and space-prefixed Windows basenames.
- Actual installed `file-type` recognizes six exercised ISO-BMFF brands; actual installed Rastermill reports a real EXIF-orientation-6 JPEG as raw **568×269**, with both metadata owners and real JPEG output reporting **269×568**.
- All nine changed paths pass `oxfmt --check`, targeted `oxlint`, and `git diff --check`; sparse checkout remains clean and 16 MB.
- Genuine official TruffleHog exact-commit preflight: **clean**. Independent Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` / high structured exact-commit review: **zero findings**, **patch is correct**, confidence **0.99** (`review-q2mediatransforms-9eb53c2fcd7.json`).

author: captainpacket
body:
A customer's `ipam.ipaddress` merge failure reported `on invalid field(s) __all__` — a field name meaning "no field". 2.6.9's diagnosis was working and still said nothing.

## What this changes

- **Non-field rules name themselves.** NetBox interpolates the message before raising, putting the address inside the string, so it cannot be persisted as-is. Known rules resolve to slugs this plugin defines; anything uncatalogued is reduced to wording with every value-bearing token masked, so a rule nobody has read yet is legible on sight rather than a release later.
- **The ingestion log download carries the issues.** Asking the customer for logs could never have worked — the merge recorder logs the model and exception class and discards the message, so it reached neither log, database, nor support bundle. The download now includes the issue rows with an explicit truncation flag past 200.
- **A validation-rejected row no longer wedges the baseline.** Any failed row blocks baseline promotion, and retrying cannot change a validation rejection because the rule belongs to the destination, not the incoming data. Those rows are recorded and skipped; integrity and other errors still fail and still block.
- **The baseline delete refusal reads as expected**, as a warning rather than an error. Reported as a defect twice.
- **2.6.9 promoted from candidate to current** in all three tables — it was tagged by hand, so the finish step never ran and the tables described a published release as unpublished.

## Note

The new tests found a real defect rather than confirming the implementation: `getattr(exc, "message_dict", None)` yields `None` for a bare `ValidationError`, so a failure raised outside `full_clean()` recorded nothing but its exception class — the exact failure this release removes, one layer down.

This makes the customer's rejection visible and non-blocking; it does not stop the rejection happening. Root cause follows once his next run names the rule.

author: axel-damage
body:
## Problem

The `_consume_vault_events` function used `asyncio.gather` with `return_exceptions=True` on bare coroutines. When the consumer was cancelled mid-batch (e.g. on shutdown), the child `process` tasks were not cancelled — they became orphaned and continued running without supervision.

## Fix

- Track in-flight process tasks in a `set[asyncio.Task]`
- On `CancelledError`: cancel all in-flight tasks, await them with `return_exceptions=True`, then drain the queue
- Clean up completed tasks from the tracking set after each batch

## Known issue
Fixes known issue #7 from AGENTS.md: *Vault watcher can leave orphaned tasks in edge cases*

author: wrburgess
body:
Closes #49

## Summary

`team_memberships` was append-only, so a player who left a team stayed on **every** roster read forever
— and could be predicted onto a court by `tn lineup plan`, since their old court matches for that team
are legitimately scoped evidence after #47's team-scoping fix.

This adds a **soft-retire**: a nullable `retired_at` column, set when a team pull no longer observes a
player and cleared the moment they are observed again, filtered out of every current-roster read and
write gate while remaining fully visible as history.

## Changes

1. **Schema + migration** — nullable `team_memberships.retired_at`; migration `0006` is DDL-only,
   backfilling every existing row to *current*.
2. **Write primitives** — `upsertMembership` un-retires on conflict; new `retireAbsentMemberships`
   retires absent, non-event-scoped, not-already-retired rows, with an empty-observed-set no-op guard.
3. **Reconcile** wired into `pullTeam`'s existing transaction (so a partial or aborted roster never
   retires anyone), with `retiredCount` surfaced in the result and the `tn team pull` summary.
4. **Current-roster reads** — `getTeamProfile` and `getLineupPlan` filter retired members, including
   the versus-team roster and the head-to-head cross pairs.
5. **Write gates** — `setAvailability` and `addCaptainNote` (both the subject-player and
   pairing-partner call sites) refuse for a retired member.
6. **History preserved** — `getPlayerProfile` keeps a retired team in `teamMemberships`, carrying
   `retiredAt`; `tn player show` renders it `<Team> (former)`; the MCP `player_show` wire shape gains
   the field additively.
7. **Prose sweep** — `team-profile.ts`'s roster doc comment, `availability.ts`'s roster doc comment,
   `upsert.ts`'s now-stale "genuine no-op" comment, and the new schema comment all state the new
   behavior; closed the `docs/findings.md` review note (#17 PR B round 7) this issue was filed from.

**Added during review** (self-review plus three rounds of independent adversarial review — see the
disposition comments):

8. **`retiredCount` reaches MCP too** — the `team_pull` handler hand-builds its result, so the CLI's
   `retired=N` did not reach it; an MCP-driven pull could retire teammates silently.
9. **A replayed `--from` page never reconciles** — an archive's vintage is unknowable, so a replay may
   add and refresh but never remove.
10. **Retirement is ordered by observation time** — new nullable `teams.roster_observed_at`
    (migration `0007`); a snapshot that is not strictly newer than the last applied one refreshes
    without retiring.
11. **…and by source** — new nullable `teams.roster_observed_url` (migration `0008`); a roster from a
    different URL (e.g. a prior season) re-baselines instead of retiring.
12. **`fetchedAt` stamps send time, not body completion** (`src/ingest/fetch.ts`) — a cached stale
    body that finishes downloading last must not outrank the fresher response that overtook it.

## Technical Approach

**Soft-retire rather than delete.** NULL means current, a timestamp means retired, and un-retiring is
just clearing it back to NULL — no data is ever destroyed, and both existing unique indexes
(`membership_unique`, `membership_unique_no_event`) are untouched, since retirement is a column update
and never a second row. A hard `DELETE` would have been FK-safe today, which is exactly what made it
the tempting wrong move: a departed player's *match history* must survive, and so must the statement
that they were once on the team.

**The migration invents no facts.** `retired_at` is nullable with no default — following the
`players.nameKey` precedent, where SQLite rejects `ADD COLUMN … NOT NULL DEFAULT '' CHECK(…)` on a
populated table and the un-checked form is fail-open. Because NULL already means "not retired", the
backfill *is* the absence of one: every pre-existing row keeps its present meaning. That is the
fail-**open** direction on purpose — a wrong "current" reproduces the known bug for one pull cycle and
self-corrects, whereas a wrong "retired" would silently delete a real roster from every read.

**Both reconcile guards live in `retireAbsentMemberships`, not in its caller,** so a future second
caller inherits them:
- an **empty observed set is a no-op** — you cannot conclude "everyone left" from a roster page that
  parsed to zero members, since a changed page shape is the far likelier cause (this also sidesteps
  SQLite's `NOT IN ()` empty-array footgun); and
- `retired_at IS NULL` in the predicate means a repeated pull never rewrites an already-retired row's
  original timestamp.

**The reconcile runs inside `pullTeam`'s existing transaction,** after the full roster loop — so an
ambiguous-identity abort partway through can never retire against a partial roster. That dependency was
previously incidental and is now load-bearing, so it is recorded in a comment at the reconcile site:
any future change making ambiguity non-fatal would silently make this destructive.

**Retirement is ordered by evidence, not by commit order.** SQLite serializes the writers, but
serialization orders the *writes*, and a reconcile is a claim about the *inputs*. Two live pulls whose
fetches resolve out of order would otherwise let the older complete roster commit last and retire a
player the newer one listed — reachable inside a single process, since the MCP server `await`s
`fetchPage`. So a reconcile requires the incoming snapshot to be **strictly newer** than the last
applied one **and** to come from the **same source** that set it. Ties fail closed. Anything that
fails those tests still upserts and un-retires: **evidence we cannot order may refresh, never remove.**

**The three read categories are split deliberately.** Current-roster reads (dossier, predicted lineup,
availability/note write gates) filter `retired_at IS NULL`. `getPlayerProfile` deliberately does not —
"teams this player has been on" is a legitimately historical statement, and their court-match history
lives in a separate table this change never reads or writes.

## Testing

36 scenarios, all written red-then-green:

- **Migration** (`test/db-membership-retirement-upgrade.test.ts`) — upgrade from a DB migrated through
  0005 with existing rows, asserting every pre-existing row reads as **current**; `runMigrations`
  idempotency; the nullable-insert contract ~20 existing test files depend on.
- **Write primitives** (`test/ingest-upsert-membership-retirement.test.ts`) — the empty-set no-op
  asserted on **database state**, not just a return value; the already-retired timestamp invariant; the
  `event_id` scope boundary; the `teamId` scope boundary; un-retire without creating a second row.
- **Ingest end-to-end** — retire, un-retire, empty-roster guard, and an aborted ambiguous pull leaving
  memberships exactly as they were (the regression test for the transaction dependency above), plus the
  CLI summary line.
- **Current-roster reads** — exclusion from the roster, the versus roster and head-to-head; a
  predicted-lineup confidence-degrade case; **and** an assertion that the team's match record is
  *unchanged* by a retirement (the sharp edge of "retired ≠ deleted").
- **Write gates** — refusals asserted **by error class**, never message text, covering both
  `captain-notes` call sites.
- **Historical preservation + wire shape** — the retired team still listed with `retiredAt`, the
  `(former)` label, and an explicit MCP `player_show` pin (parity tests check name/command only and
  would not have caught a silent change here).

- **Ordering and provenance** (added in review) — an older snapshot committing after a newer one
  retires nobody; a newer one still retires normally; a stale snapshot does not advance the watermark;
  an equal stamp fails closed; a prior-season URL retires nobody but re-baselines, and the next pull
  from that source reconciles normally; `--from` records no observation time; and `fetchedAt` is
  pinned to the send time through an inject

body:
Two live test rounds produced **no `§GHOST_GROUND` line at all**, while the served bytes were correct every time (sw v896, `tmGroundSchedule`, `groundIfcZ`, arm call site — all verified live). So the fault was structural, not deployment:

**1. The feature spans three files and had a single point of version failure.** A service worker can serve one of `cinema_maxq.js` / `time_machine.js` / `tools.js` from an older cache, and a missing `tmGroundSchedule` made the whole thing return false. It now **degrades** to a coarse proxy on `tmPlacedCount` (present since the buildup shipped), and the arm log states which rule is in force.

**2. Arming was hostage to ordering.** It ran once, before the frame loop, in a regime where the ground plane isn't even visible yet — photoreal staging turns it on *inside* the loop, which is the exact ordering that disabled it in #1113. The first per-frame tick now arms itself.

Both new behaviours are **gated, not assumed**:

| gate | measured |
|---|---|
| G-GG-10 | `tmGroundSchedule` hidden the way a stale cache would → still arms, early=0.22 late=1 |
| G-GG-11 | `ghostGroundArm()` never called → first `ghostGroundAt()` arms itself, returns 0.22 |

Witness **11/11** on Duplex (was 9/9 before these gates existed). sw v897→v898.

author: arimu1
body:
## Impact

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes expected existing functionality)
- [ ] Enhancement/New feature (adds functionality without impacting existing logic)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

## Description

Fixes #3876

On Oracle (and other databases that uppercase unquoted identifiers), `createIndex` quotes index names that need quoting (for example names containing `-`) and preserves the original case:

```sql
CREATE INDEX ADMIN."index_-id" ON ADMIN.test_table(name)
```

But `indexExists` looked up the index via `database.correctObjectName(indexName, Index.class)`, which uppercased the name to `INDEX_-ID`. The snapshot therefore never found the index, the precondition passed, and a second run of a `runAlways` changeset failed with ORA-00955.

This change skips case normalization in `correctObjectName` when the object is an `Index` and `mustQuoteObjectName()` is true, so create and lookup use the same stored case. Unquoted index names (and other object types) still use the previous upper/lower behavior.

Matches the approach suggested by @nvoxland on the issue and the patch reported as working by the issue author.

## Release note

Fixed `indexExists` failing to detect Oracle indexes whose names require quoting (for example names containing `-`), which caused second-run failures for conditional `createIndex` changesets.

## Things to be aware of

- Fix is in shared `AbstractJdbcDatabase.correctObjectName`, scoped to `Index` only when quoting is required, so it does not change table/column/schema case correction.
- Covered with unit tests only (no Oracle Docker required).

## Things to worry about

- None expected; unquoted index names still normalize as before.

## Additional Context

**Tests run (JDK 17):**
- `OracleDatabaseTest` — 34 tests, 0 failures
- `OracleDatabaseSpec` — 23 tests, 0 failures (includes new index name cases for #3876)

author: nhorto
body:
Closes #42. 38 new tests; **402 in total** with the three honesty PRs merged in. `src/mcp/` is four files and **no new dependency** — `package.json` is untouched.

### No SDK, and the numbers are the argument

`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.0` installs **93 packages and 24 MB** — express, hono, cors, jose, ajv, zod, eventsource, express-rate-limit, pkce-challenge — to give this command three methods and a `\n`. Everything that tree drags in exists for transports we do not use: HTTP, SSE, OAuth, rate limiting.

MCP over stdio is JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line. `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call` is the whole surface a tools-only server needs. This is the same reasoning that put `node:sqlite` in over better-sqlite3 and a hand-rolled tar extractor in over a package with an install script: the person this is for types `npx app-atlas`, and every megabyte between them and the map is a real cost paid by everyone to save one afternoon here. **Revisit it the day this server needs to be reachable over HTTP** — that is when the SDK starts earning its tree.

### The six tools

`unguarded_doors` (first, because it is the one no competitor in LANDSCAPE.md answers at all), `list_doors`, `what_calls`, `where_is`, `data_stores`, `env_vars`.

Driven over a real pipe against a fixture before merging:

```
handshake -> {'name': 'app-atlas', 'version': '0.7.0'} 2025-06-18
unguardedCount: 3 of 6 routes
   /healthz     | open | writes: False | src/server.ts:12
   /live        | open | writes: False | src/live.controller.ts:9
   /open/status | open | writes: False | src/public.routes.ts:7
```

### An empty list is the failure this surface exists to avoid

A directory nobody has analysed returns `isError: true`, **no** `structuredContent`, and a sentence naming the command that fixes it. Verified:

```
isError: True
has structuredContent: False
No atlas in /…/never. This server reads an analysis that has already been run; it never
runs one itself. Run `app-atlas analyze /…/never` in a terminal, then call this tool again.
```

An agent handed `{"unguarded": []}` will report that the app has no unprotected routes — the single sentence this whole product exists to stop somebody saying to a customer. **"Could not look" and "looked and found nothing" have to be distinguishable by the client**, not by a sentence the model may skim. For the same reason `unguarded_doors` keeps *"nothing is unguarded"* apart from *"there is nothing to guard"*, branching off the same `authHeadline` the CLI and the export branch off rather than testing `routes === 0` a fourth time.

### The server never analyses, and says so

Three reasons, any one sufficient: an MCP client starts its servers at session start and will not wait forty seconds for a first answer; analysis writes into the user's project, which a background process spawned by an agent has no business doing unasked; and on a metered backend the enricher asks about money, to a stdin that belongs to a protocol.

### Provenance on every result, not once at the handshake

A model reads the result in front of it, not the `initialize` it saw an hour ago. Every answer ends with which app answered, when it was analysed, that `(ai)` sentences were model-written, and how to refresh — plus the tree-sitter caveat when a grammar rather than a compiler read the language. The staleness line earns its tokens: an atlas from before the agent's last three edits answers confidently and wrongly, and nothing else in a transcript says so.

Every guard keeps its `confidence`; a test asserts none is ever emitted without one, and an unsure check never renders as a plain "checked". A name matching two things returns both rather than picking one.

### stdout is taken away from the rest of the process

Anything on stdout that is not a message is a parse error inside somebody's agent, reported as "App Atlas is broken" — and not everything that writes there is ours. `claimStdout` captures the stream once and points `process.stdout.write` at stderr, **diverted rather than dropped**, so a person reading their client's server log still sees it. Verified three ways, including `ping` alone producing the byte-exact single line `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{}}`.

No `outputSchema` is declared — that is a promise to conform on every future result, and the text block is the contract that can actually be kept. The atlas is re-read on the mtime of `atlas.db`, so `analyze --watch` in another terminal reaches the agent.

Grain: G1/claims-outputs -- lane myia-po-2023:CoursIA -- prev: G1/claims-outputs #9061 (hmm_alpha)

## Defect #8052 — second-order stochastic timing drift

App-11-Picross: two interpretation cells of the naive solver cite Stopwatch timings from a prior run. PR #3605 (merged c7d582f0, audit #3164) aligned them once (1.86 ms / 0.93 s), then code cells idx17/idx22 were re-executed (new timings 0.66 ms / 0.19 s) and the MD was never re-synced.

## Re-prise §D.5 (fresh re-exec, CAUSE_FIXED) — replaces the markdown-only commit

ai-01 review rejected the prior markdown-only approach (commit cc02b256d): a perf/timing number in a **locally re-executable** notebook must come from a **fresh re-execution**, never from a byte-surgical markdown-align on stale committed output. Rationale (§D.5): the aligned value will move again on the next kernel pass — engraving the old-run number produces the *next* drift. Correct path: re-exec → commit real outputs → prose follows.

Re-executed end-to-end with papermill (kernel python3, ortools 9.15.6755, cwd = notebook dir so `../..` resolves `search_helpers`). Timings moved exactly as §D.5 predicts a wall-clock metric would on a fresh run:

| Cell | Metric | Stale committed | Fresh re-exec (this PR) |
|------|--------|-----------------|-------------------------|
| #17 (5x5 naive) | Temps | 0.66 ms | **0.43 ms** |
| #22 (10x10 naive) | Temps | 0.19 s | **0.15 s** |
| #32 benchmark | debit | 119,976 comb/s | **151,724 comb/s** |
| #32 benchmark | 10x10 naive estimé | 496.22 ms | **392.39 ms** |

Combinatoire is **deterministic** and stable across runs: 225 / 59,535 total combinations, 113 / 23,153 checked — unchanged. The MD prose is now **sourced by the committed run** (MD + outputs of the same commit, identical values).

## Diagnostic dérive (§D.5 required section)

- **Cause (e) — wall-clock non-reproductible.** `time.perf_counter` on naive backtracking; the benchmark derives `real_throughput` from cell#22, so any timing drift cascades into every estimated naive column. This is intrinsic to a Stopwatch-on-a-solver pedagogical setup, not an env/kernel defect (a/b/c/d excluded).
- **Verdict: CAUSE_FIXED.** Fresh local re-execution; MD aligned to the committed outputs of the same run. The numbers will still drift on the *next* kernel pass — that is expected; what this fixes is that the MD is no longer a stale copy of a run that predates the committed outputs.
- **C.1/C.2 forensics:** 21 code cells, **0** with `execution_count=None`, **0** error outputs, **0** forbidden patterns (`raise NotImplementedError` / `assert False` / `1/0`).
- **Stop & Repair (rule 6):** no cell output hand-edited. Only `metadata.papermill.output_path` normalized to basename (anti machine path-leak — the sole tolerated exception).

## Non-duplication

#3605 (merged) aligned these cells to the outputs of its time (1.86/0.93). A later re-exec changed the outputs (0.66/0.19); the prior markdown-only commit re-aligned to those — but that was the superseded gesture. This re-prise does the re-exec §D.5 demands. Complementary, not duplicate.

## Integrity

- MD speedup/perf CP-SAT cells (analogies: "marche vs fusée") NOT touched — deliberately approximate pedagogy, the graph (cell#35) carries the true e24 magnitude → illustrative-pedagogy FP risk, left as-is.
- Catalogue byte-identical to `origin/main`.
- Notebook-only change, 1 file. `papermill` output_path normalized; no machine path in any output.

See #8052, #3801.

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Five independently reproduced Control UI chat defects silently damage ordinary operator workflows:

1. Streaming Markdown splits loose lists, indented continuations, and reference links into unrelated fragments, so live replies briefly display different content and links from completed replies.
2. Workspace file references look clickable but cannot receive keyboard focus or open from Enter/Space in either the transcript or Markdown detail sidebar.
3. Cancelled session navigation continues requesting up to five Gateway session pages after the operator has already moved elsewhere.
4. Tool-card caching reuses a `read` presentation for an `edit` or `write` when calls share an arguments object.
5. Tool completion events without a repeated name overwrite an authoritative started name with generic `tool`, corrupting transcript labels and skipping named result effects.

## Why This Change Was Made

Repair each canonical owner directly. Cache only the independent prefix before the first Markdown list, keep every subsequent list/container fragment intact, and render reference definitions with the complete document that owns them. Generate sanitized, href-less file anchors with explicit button semantics, tab focus, and shared Enter/Space activation used by both chat surfaces. Make the existing session-resolution cache subscriber-aware: cancel a paginated producer only when its last route navigation aborts, while preserving live shared callers. Include normalized tool identity in the presentation cache. Resolve result identity from the authoritative existing tool-call entry before applying result effects or rebuilding its transcript.

The change preserves the Markdown sanitizer, external-link policy, href-less local-file security boundary, session lookup limits, Gateway/public protocol, configuration, authentication, and persistent-state contracts.

## User Impact

- Live replies preserve whole-document list structure, indented Markdown, and reference-style hyperlinks.
- Keyboard and assistive-technology users can focus workspace references and open them with Enter or Space from both the transcript and detail preview.
- Rapid session navigation stops obsolete Gateway pagination without interrupting another navigation sharing the same lookup.
- Read, edit, and write tool cards retain the correct file presentation, diff, and action affordances.
- Completed tools keep their started names; nameless `session_status` results continue updating the visible model override.

## Evidence

- Frozen source: `e051a7bb4a6ba69b87391e990b00813114b1d482`; isolated sparse branch: `codex/qa200-ui-chat-stream-ownership`; exact candidate: `a7f00d9918ea0c513635d31b3d3b3d950539ba4f`; 15 MB worktree; frozen canonical checkout unchanged.
- Actual owner-level red proof: **27 newly added regressions failed before the fixes** across Markdown structure, escaped/multiline/list-nested reference labels, tab-expanded and stale-boundary list continuation, all three file-link generation forms, real focused transcript/sidebar keyboard activation, aborted/shared Gateway lookup, shared-arguments tool presentation, omitted/empty/blank/conflicting result names, placeholder upgrades, and nameless/conflicting `session_status` effects.
- Actual exact-source green proof: all **27 focused regressions passed** after the canonical-owner fixes.
- Eight complete affected owner and sibling suites: **328/328 tests passed** in `ui/src/components/markdown.test.ts`, `ui/src/components/markdown-details.test.ts`, `ui/src/lib/chat/tool-call-view.test.ts`, `ui/src/pages/chat/route.test.ts`, `ui/src/pages/chat/tool-stream.node.test.ts`, `ui/src/pages/chat/tool-stream-fallback.node.test.ts`, `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-sidebar.test.ts`, and `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-thread.measure.test.ts`.
- Actual sanitizer/XSS assertions remain green in the complete Markdown owner suite; href-less file-link invariants and external HTTP-link behavior are preserved.
- All 15 changed files pass targeted `oxfmt --check`, single-thread `oxlint`, existing max-lines enforcement, and `git diff --check`.
- Exact-commit TruffleHog 3.96.0 secret scan: **clean**.
- Independent review found genuine escaped/multiline/container-indented reference-label, Markdown-tab-column, stale list-boundary, and conflicting terminal-name gaps. Every finding failed with an exact red regression; direct inspection of markdown-it's reference, list, and tab-expanded block-state owners confirmed the dependency contract. The final streaming owner deletes the brittle list-indent/boundary state machine and preserves every case with green behavior proof.
- Exact-commit structured independent Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` high-reasoning autoreview: **CLEAN**, zero accepted/actionable findings, **patch is correct**, confidence **0.87**.

No public API, Gateway protocol, configuration, authentication, migration, SQLite, dependency, generated locale, live Gateway, or publishing changes.

author: ulisescm
body:
Closes #265
Closes #285

Dos bugs de la auditoría en la misma zona de `packages/cli/src/lib/marker.ts`, agrupados para no chocar.

## #265 — `stripOrphanMarkers` destruía un bloque managed válido
`slice(-orphanOpens)` con `orphanOpens === 0` equivale a `slice(0)` → marcaba TODOS los opens para borrar cuando había 0 opens huérfanos pero ≥1 close huérfano (edición-a-mano típica: un close de más debajo de un bloque bueno). El open del bloque válido se destruía y `injectManagedSection` inyectaba un duplicado.

Fix: el pareo open/close ahora rastrea los índices huérfanos **concretos** (no los cuenta) y los quita en una sola pasada sobre el string original, de mayor a menor índice. Esto también cierra el **bug secundario**: un close huérfano en medio de dos pares válidos (`open close close-orphan open close`) ahora elimina el correcto, no el último (que era un cierre válido y corrompía el bloque siguiente).

## #285 — citar un marcador en la zona de usuario la partía
`locateManagedBlocks` y `extractUserProse` ahora son conscientes de code fences:
- Un bloque managed citado dentro de un ` ```fence``` ` ya no se toma como ancla en `splitUserSection` → no barre la user-zone real ni inyecta un segundo `user-start`. El contenido de un bloque managed real se trata como **opaco**, así que un fence dentro de él nunca desincroniza el escaneo ni descarta un bloque posterior.
- Una línea que **es** exactamente `user-start`/`user-end` dentro de un fence se conserva verbatim en vez de borrarse. Docstring corregido (antes describía lo contrario).

## Tests
4 tests nuevos en `marker.test.ts`, todos rojos antes del fix:
- #265 primario (bloque válido + close huérfano extra → sobrevive, sin duplicado)
- #265 secundario (close huérfano en medio → se quita el correcto)
- #285 caso 1 (bloque managed en fence → no ancla, idempotente)
- #285 caso 2 (líneas de marcador en fence → conservadas)

Los 3 tests de huérfanos existentes siguen verdes.

author: stranske
body:
## What

Hand-reviewed pass (`scripts/normalize_titles.py`) that rewrites the `title` field for a fixed cluster of works whose titles were photo-caption fragments, Wikimedia filenames, or catalogue lines with the artist / year / a leading list number folded into the title string. Surfaced during the category backfill (PR #361).

Examples:
- `30. Calvin Coolidge, 1919` → `Calvin Coolidge`
- `Baturraden_overview_from_ridge` → `Baturraden overview from ridge`
- `Rocky Landscape in the Elbe Sandstone Mountains - Friederich` → `Rocky Landscape in the Elbe Sandstone Mountains`
- `Griet Jans -` → `The Shipbuilder and His Wife`

17 of the 23 candidates actually changed; the other 6 already had clean titles (e.g. "An Old Woman Cooking Eggs") and are intentionally absent from the map.

## Design

- **Reviewed static map keyed by `work_id`**, not a fuzzy rule stripper and not a live LLM call. For a fixed, identifiable set of 23 works this is reproducible, testable, and needs no credentials/network. Each entry stores the exact `expected` current title, so the pass **refuses to clobber a drifted sidecar** and is idempotent.
- **Scope is `title` only.** Several of these works also have junk in `artist.name` (`1907-1908Oil on canvas`, `_Ingushetia`, a wrong `Federico Barocci` QID on the Friedrich landscape). That belongs to the artist-resolution pipeline (`backfill_artist_qids`) and is left for a follow-up, not fixed here.
- Follows the standard pass shape: `sidecar.validate` → `sidecar.write` → mirror to `Art/works` → append `operations.log` → record `field_provenance` for `title` (status `available`, source `curated`). Dry-run by default; `--apply` writes.

## ⚠️ This is data hygiene, not a categorization unlock

The follow-up note expected that re-running `backfill_categories` after normalization would categorize many of these. **It categorizes 0/23** (verified before and after). The categorizer's title tier only matches `altarpiece / stained glass / fresco / tapestry`; these works have null `medium` and no valid work QID (the two that have QIDs are mis-resolved — `Q30668804` → "scholarly article", `Q18869` → the Caucasus region). Recovering `medium` and/or the correct work QID is the real follow-up if categorization is the goal.

## Applied to local data

Dry-run then `--apply`: **17 updated, 17 mirrored**, re-run idempotent (0), 17 `title_normalization` entries in `operations.log`.

## Tests

`tests/test_normalize_titles.py` — map integrity, dry-run non-writing, apply rewrites title + records provenance, mirror + log, drift-skip guard, idempotency, missing-work reporting, empty-title schema rejection. `ruff` + local suite green.

author: bo2
body:
`knowledge/` is now a fixed name, like `workspaces/` has always been.

## Why the affordance had to go

It was presented as an instance choice: `create-instance` asked which name to
use, offered alternatives, and carried a whole section — § 5, "If the user
renamed the durable-content dir" — listing the files that must move together.
Docs spoke in a `<durable-content-dir>` placeholder rather than a path.

Nothing read the value. Every consumer hardcodes the name:

| consumer | how it resolves the name |
|---|---|
| `connect-agent.sh` | literal `knowledge/*/README.md` glob |
| `skills-registry.sh` | literal `"$repo_dir"/knowledge/*/` |
| `validate-exobrain.sh` | literal `knowledge\|knowledge/*` content-tree case |
| `authoring-review.sh` | literal `knowledge/*.md` file filter |
| `.gitleaks.toml` | literal `^knowledge/.*/_raw/.*` allowlist |

No config file carries it — not `scopes.json`, not `.exobrain.json`. So the
"choice" was a documented find-and-replace across the tree, offered at the one
moment the user knows least about the system. It bought nothing even here:
renaming the directory in the seed last week got no help from the mechanism.

Contrast the scope collections, which *are* real config — `validate-exobrain.sh`
and `authoring-review.sh` both read collection names out of `scopes.json`. Those
vary because principals differ: a solo user has no group, a household has one, an
org may call it something else. A singleton every instance has exactly one of
varies only by taste.

And the tell was the sibling: `workspaces/` is equally universal, equally a
content tree, and was never offered as negotiable.

## What was removed

- `create-instance` § 1's Vocabulary question, and § 5 in full (later sections
  renumbered, cross-references updated)
- `<durable-content-dir>` placeholders in `create-instance` and `exobrain-evolve`
  → literal paths
- "if you renamed the durable-content dir" from `exobrain-evolve`'s path-mapping
  note, which still covers restructured scopes
- the durable-content dir as the lead example of expected divergence in
  `propagation.md` and the meta-domain README — groups and restructured scripts
  still make the point
- the vocabulary answer from the `seed-tests` builder prompt, which was only
  there to answer a question that is no longer asked

## Divergence is still handled

Fixing the name doesn't forbid renaming. `exobrain-evolve` already re-synthesizes
into local names and structure wherever an instance has diverged — the general
mechanism the special case was duplicating. An instance that renames anyway
follows the same path as one that restructured its scopes.

## Feed card 0095

This one carries a pattern worth publishing: configure what genuinely varies
between instances, fix what doesn't, and treat "does anything read the value?" as
the test. An unread knob is a rename procedure with a settings prompt attached.

## Verification

`scripts/validate-exobrain.sh` clean; `skills/exobrain-tests/unit/run.sh` 52/52;
`scripts/authoring-review.sh` clean; `bash -n` on the changed script.

author: robotsix-mill[bot]
body:
## Summary

`is_openrouter_upstream_payment_error` is a public, tested, in-repo-consumed transient-signature predicate that is the one odd sibling **missing** from the `openrouter/` package's public re-export surface (`src/robotsix_llmio/openrouter/__init__.py`). Its three direct siblings in the same module are all re-exported; it is not.

## Evidence

**The predicate is defined, public, and functional** — `src/robotsix_llmio/openrouter/transient.py:29`:
```python
def is_openrouter_upstream_payment_error(exc: BaseException) -> bool:
```
It recognises a 402 raised by the *upstream* provider (not our account), and is composed into the package's canonical transient check at `transient.py:86` (`or is_openrouter_upstream_payment_error(cur)`) inside `is_openrouter_transient`. It is thoroughly unit-tested (`tests/openrouter/test_openrouter.py:23,105,115,122,133,139`).

**All three siblings ARE re-exported from the package public surface** — `src/robotsix_llmio/openrouter/__init__.py:15-18`: top-level import
```python
from .transient import (
    is_deepseek_reasoning_400,
    is_openrouter_transient,
    is_openrouter_upstream_error,
)
```
and all three names appear in `__all__` (L50-52). The module docstring (L1-4) explicitly frames these as the lightweight public helpers. Only `is_openrouter_upstream_payment_error` is omitted.

**The sibling-pattern mismatch is the gap.** `is_openrouter_upstream_error`, `is_deepseek_reasoning_400`, and `is_openrouter_upstream_payment_error` are all peer predicates that (a) live in the same `transient.py` module, (b) are each composed into `is_openrouter_transient`, and (c) each carry a public docstring. Two of the three are individually re-exported at package level; the `_payment_error` one is the odd one out. A consumer using the documented `robotsix_llmio.openrouter` surface to recognise transient OpenRouter failures can import `is_openrouter_upstream_error` or `is_deepseek_reasoning_400` but cannot import `is_openrouter_upstream_payment_error` — it is only reachable via the private submodule path `robotsix_llmio.openrouter.transient` (exactly what the tests do at `test_openrouter.py:23`).

Contrast with `claude_sdk/transient.py`, where the convention is to export only the aggregate `is_claude_sdk_transient` and keep the individual signatures internal — but `openrouter/` has explicitly chosen the opposite convention (individually exporting the peer predicates), so the missing one violates this package's own established pattern.

## Proposed fix

In `src/robotsix_llmio/openrouter/__init__.py`:
1. Add `is_openrouter_upstream_payment_error` to the top-level `from .transient import (...)` at L15-18.
2. Add `"is_openrouter_upstream_payment_error"` to `__all__` alongside its siblings (L50-52).
No `__getattr__` change is needed — `transient` is already eagerly imported at module top (lightweight, no pydantic-ai/OTel), matching how the other three helpers are surfaced.

<!-- completeness_check-gap-id: OPENROUTER-PAYMENT-REEXPORT -->

---

author: vencil
body:
Closes #1219

`guard-defaults-impact.yml` 以 `paths: ["**/_defaults.yaml"]` 觸發，用意是「任何 `_defaults.yaml` 變更都跑一次 blast-radius 檢查」——實際上它驗的是一個 PR 根本沒動過的目錄，然後貼上綠色 sticky comment。

## ⛔ 為什麼能活下來：兩個缺陷互相遮蔽

1. `actions/checkout` 未設 `fetch-depth`（預設 shallow）⇒ 工作區沒有 `origin/<base>` ref
2. `git diff --name-only "origin/${BASE_REF}"...HEAD` 因此 `fatal: bad revision`，被行尾的 `|| true` 吞掉
3. 變更清單成為空集合 ⇒ scope 退回自動偵測到的那個 conf.d 根
4. da-guard 驗那個目錄 ⇒ `errors=0` ⇒ 貼綠

**因為 scope 永遠算不出來，所以永遠踩不到「scope 落在 `--config-dir` 之外」那條路**（`config.ScopeEffective` 會拒絕、`da-guard` 回 exit 2、workflow 視為硬失敗）。⇒ 單獨修 `fetch-depth` 會把 fail-open 換成「所有 try-local／tests 的 defaults PR 一律硬紅」。**兩者必須同一次處理**，這也是本票從一開始就標明的。

## 修法形狀由實測決定

先量了兩件事再動手：

**(a) 這個 repo 不是一棵 conf.d 樹，是九棵。** 15 個 `_defaults.yaml` 分佈在：

| conf.d 樹 | 檔數 |
|---|---|
| `components/threshold-exporter/config/conf.d` | 1 |
| `rule-packs/recipes/examples/conf.d` | 2 |
| `try-local/seed/conf.d` | 1 |
| `tests/e2e-bench/fixture/{synthetic-v1,synthetic-v2}/conf.d` | 2 |
| `tests/golden/fixtures/*/conf.d`（6 棵） | 9 |

**其中只有 1 個在自動偵測到的根底下。** ⇒ scope 不是「一個目錄」，而是「每棵被碰到的樹各一組 (config-dir, scope)」。

**(b) 全部都驗會不會把 fixture 變成誤報？** 這是我原本最擔心的——`tests/golden/fixtures/full-l0-l3` 有四層串接 defaults，正是 redundant-override 檢查的目標。**實測：把 da-guard 對 11 棵樹逐一跑過，全部 `exit 0`。** ⇒ 疑慮被推翻，**不需要 allowlist 或 skip 清單**。

## 改了什麼

- `fetch-depth: 0`
- base ref 取不到 ⇒ **fail-loud**（`::error::` + exit 1），不再退回猜測
- 每棵被碰到的樹各跑一次 da-guard，報告串接、取最差 exit code
- **不在任何 conf.d 樹底下的檔案顯式回報「NOT CHECKED ＋ 原因」** ＋ `::warning::`——⛔ 不靜默略過，靜默正是本票要消滅的形狀
- 零個 `_defaults.yaml` ⇒ 對偵測到的 conf.d 跑**全樹**，不是錯誤（見下方「我自己踩的第二個坑」）
- 往上找 conf.d 根的邏輯抽成 `scripts/ops/guard_defaults_scopes.py`——那正是先前失效的那一步，它該有測試釘住，而不是留在 inline bash

實跑輸出（15 個檔全改的話）：分組正確，`full-l0-l3` 的四個檔收斂成一組（scope 用根，才驗得出跨層 redundant-override）、`mixed-mode` 單一目錄則收窄到 `conf.d/db`。

## ⭐ 變異測試抓到我自己測試的一個真洞

`tests/ops/test_guard_defaults_scopes.py` 16 條斷言：單元規則、live-repo 探索（**任何新增的 `_defaults.yaml` 自動納入**，非硬編清單）、#1219 的原始情境（只改 try-local 那份必須解析到 try-local 的樹）、三條 workflow 契約斷言。

契約斷言原本逐行檢查「含 `git diff` 的那一行有沒有 `|| true`」——但該指令用 `\` **跨兩行**，`|| true` 加在**續行**上時完全逃過斷言。而更早一版用整段字串比對，又會咬到我寫的解釋註解（「原本是 `|| true`」那句）而誤報。

**同一個病的兩個方向**：比對法比目標窄＝假陰性，比目標寬＝假陽性。現在先接續行、再濾註解。

三個變異逐一實測（每次都從已驗證存在的備份還原）：

| 變異 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| 拿掉 `fetch-depth: 0` | 1 failed |
| `\|\| true` 加在續行上 | 1 failed ← 修好前這個是綠的 |
| 拿掉 resolver 呼叫 | 1 failed |
| 還原 | 16 passed |

附帶教訓：這個洞是因為我第一輪的備份指令失敗、三個 mutation 疊加才暴露的——變異測試要先驗備份真的存在再繼續。

## ⭐ 我自己踩的第二個坑：第一版會讓這支 PR 擋下自己（commit 2）

第一版把「PR 事件下解析不出 `_defaults.yaml`」寫成硬錯誤，理由（寫在註解裡）是「this workflow only runs on that path filter」。**那句話是錯的**——`paths:` 有**六條**，其中五條是 da-guard 的原始碼與這支 workflow 自己：

```
**/_defaults.yaml
components/threshold-exporter/app/cmd/da-guard/**
components/threshold-exporter/app/internal/guard/**
components/threshold-exporter/app/pkg/config/scope.go
components/threshold-exporter/app/pkg/config/hierarchy.go
.github/workflows/guard-defaults-impact.yml          ← 本 PR 改的是這個
```

⇒ 只改那些的 PR 合法地不會動到任何 `_defaults.yaml`。**本 PR 自己就是這個情境**（`_defaults.yaml` 變更數 = 0），第一版會被自己擋下。

改為：零結果時對偵測到的 conf.d 跑全樹——那不是退讓，而是「改完 guard 之後它還能不能用」的煙霧測試，正好對應那五條觸發路徑的語意。並補一條契約斷言釘住：只要觸發面還有非 `_defaults.yaml` 的 path，就不允許把零結果寫成 `::error::`（變異實測轉紅）。

## 驗證

- `da-guard` 對 11 棵 conf.d 樹實跑皆 exit 0（修法擴到全部樹的依據）
- `tests/ops/test_guard_defaults_scopes.py` 16 passed
- workflow YAML parse 通過
- `verify_diff.py --write-map` 已於 host、所有編輯之後重生
- `bump_docs --sync-counts --check` 綠（新增的 `scripts/ops/*.py` 不計入 tool-map／README 工具數）

Refs: #1219

author: fukuemon
body:
## Summary

- 文書の鮮度を手書きの日付ではなく git の差分で担保し、読み取り索引を生成物にする方針を ADR-0008 として起案する
- その入力側 (各文書の frontmatter 整備と索引の改名) を #40 のスコープへ取り込む
- 索引の設定を `context/project.yml` の `reading_index` ブロックで持つ (sdd-template#17 の追随)

**本 PR に実装は含まない。** 決定と要求の確定までを扱い、スクリプトの実装は #45 が担う。

## Background

文書は「docs が正本、コードが導出物」で運用しているが、**正本であること自体は、正本が実装と一致していることを保証しない**。実測で 2 つの構造的な穴が確認された。

- **鮮度が手書きに依存**: `> 最終更新: YYYY-MM-DD` は人が書くため、更新忘れも実態との食い違いも機械的に検出できない (対象 14 ファイル)
- **手書きの索引が育たない**: `context/impact-index.yaml` はテンプレートのプレースホルダのまま一度も埋まっていない

一方で本リポジトリには同じ問題を解いた実例がある。`scripts/depgraph.sh` は依存図を `go list` の実 import から生成し、再生成 diff で drift を検出する。ADR-0008 はこのパターンを文書運用へ一般化する。

外部ツール (OpenWiki 等) も調査したが、「コードが正本・docs が導出物」という逆向きの前提に立つため導入せず、設計思想のみを取り込んだ。

## Changes

### adr/0008-doc-freshness-and-reading-map.md (新規)

| 決定 | 内容                                                                                                                       |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | 文書メタ情報を YAML frontmatter 化し、`> 最終更新` を廃止する。鮮度は `governs` と `verified_commit` の git 差分で判定する |
| 2    | `governs` はコードパスに限らず設定ファイルも指す (対象 14 本の割り当て表を持つ)                                            |
| 3    | 検査は「生成物は FAIL、本文は通知のみ」で二分する                                                                          |
| 4    | 逆引き表を生成物にし、`context/reading-map.yaml` へ改名する                                                                |

判定が不確実な検査を FAIL にすると「内容を読まずに `verified_commit` だけ進めて通す」運用へ堕ちるため、本文の鮮度は通知に留める。移行時は `unverified` を正規値として許容し、未確認の文書を初回から stale として点灯させる (虚偽の初期値で一覧を空にするより、未確認を明示するほうが消し込みリストとして機能する)。

### specs/40-docs-reorg/requirements.md

frontmatter 化と改名をスコープへ追加し、業務ルール 3 件・出力 3 件・バリデーション 2 件・受け入れ基準 3 件を追記した。未決事項のうち 2 件が ADR-0008 で解消した。

- 論点 2 (索引を集約するか) → 階層 README を残し、索引部分だけを生成マーカー区間へ生成する
- 論点 5 (README の更新トリガー) → 規約の文言ではなく `governs` + `verified_commit` の stale 通知で担う

### context/project.yml

```yaml
reading_index:
  path: context/impact-index.yaml # #40 で context/reading-map.yaml へ
  generated: false # #45 で生成器を入れたら true にする
  generate_command: null # #45 で scripts/reading-map.sh を設定する
```

索引の path が共有 skill 4 箇所にファイル名で直書きされており、改名すると全て解決不能になることが判明したため、sdd-template#17 でキー参照へ一般化した。本 PR はその追随。

### 生成物の追随 (2851aaf)

再生成で、depwalk の生成物が sdd-template より遅れていることが判明した。本題と無関係な 84 ファイルを独立した commit に分離している。原因 (消費 repo に生成物 drift の検査がない) は #46 として起票済み。

## Testing

- `bash scripts/generate.sh` 実行後に再実行し、意図した差分のみが出ることを確認
- lefthook pre-commit (format / protected-branch / repo-analysis) と commit-msg (ticket-number) が全 commit で pass
- コード変更を含まないため Go / Java のテストは対象外

## Related Issues

- Refs #40
- Refs #45 (生成器と鮮度検査スクリプトの実装。本 PR が前提)
- Refs #46 (生成物 drift 検査。2851aaf で顕在化した問題)
- 上流: Fukuemon/sdd-template#17 (merge 済み)

## Notes

レビューで見ていただきたい点。

1. **ADR-0008 決定 3 の二分**が妥当か。「生成物は FAIL / 本文は通知のみ」は強制力を意図的に捨てている
2. **`unverified` を初期値に許す**判断。移行直後は stale 一覧が未確認文書で埋まる
3. **`governs` の割り当て表** (決定 2) が実態と合っているか。特に `context/ai-agents.md` は正本が sdd-template 側にあるため、検出できるのは生成物の変更までという限界がある

author: liuytgithub
body:
## What this does

Fills the `risk_agent` placeholder with a working collective reviewer for the settled trader batch, implementing the team's 3-way cherry-picking checklist (CP-1 … CP-13).

Follows the Reporting agent's convention: `risk_agent.py` stays the Protocol, `risk_agent_impl.py` is the implementation. **Six lines of existing code changed** — one export line in `src/agents/__init__.py` and two fields in the agent card. Nothing in `protocols/`, `graph/`, `tools/`, or any teammate's agent was modified. That was possible because the scaffold already exposes injected node boundaries; the graph never imports the Risk class, it receives it.

## How it works

Two stages, in order:

1. **Deterministic gate.** Every mechanically checkable item is computed from engine-produced evidence — the `BacktestRunLedgerEntry` embedded in each result, request counts, package identity. No model call.
2. **Model judgment (optional).** A `ModelClient` reviews what code cannot judge — sweep severity, lens similarity, cosmetic resubmission — grounded in stage 1. It may *escalate* severity with justification; equal-or-lower proposals are discarded, so judgment can never soften a deterministic verdict. A model failure degrades to deterministic-only review instead of aborting the round.

Evidence that cannot be reached returns FLAG with `requires_human_review=True`, never a manufactured PASS.

## Check status

Working today with no new dependencies: CP-3 (full-period metrics), CP-5 (canonical metric set), CP-6 (same-terms baseline), CP-7 (multiple-comparison disclosure), CP-8 (lens duplication, exact-rule proxy), CP-9 (no borrowed evidence), CP-11 (validation-touch budget), CP-13 (test-set lock).

Degrading to human review until adapters exist: CP-1, CP-2, CP-4 (need `RoundAuditReader`), CP-10, CP-12 (need `RoundHistoryReader`).

## What I need from other workstreams

**Ledger owner — two small adapters.** `WorkflowState` already carries `round_audit_summary_reference` and `round_history_reference`, but nothing dereferences them. Risk needs injected readers returning the round's `BacktestRunLedgerEntry` list and prior-round summaries. This is the single highest-value dependency — it unlocks five checks.

**Trader owners — three optional disclosure keys** in `TraderStrategyPackage.additional_fields`: `declared_backtest_run_count` (CP-1/2/7), `stability_evidence` (CP-11), `parent_strategy_id` (CP-12). Omitting the run count means "one hypothesis", so a trader that sweeps silently gets vetoed once the ledger is readable. That is the intended incentive.

**Reporting owner.** `RiskReviewResponse.required_reporting_flags()` returns every flag the memo must carry verbatim, including how many hypotheses competed this round. Dropping a flag is itself cherry-picking the critique.

Full detail in `docs/risk_agent.md`.

## Bug found and fixed

The test-set-lock check reads the validation split out of the ledger's `additional_fields`, which is a `date` in-process but an **ISO string** after the graph's JSON checkpoint round-trip. CP-13 was therefore silently passing on exactly the path production uses. Fixed, with a regression test (`test_test_set_lock_survives_a_json_round_trip`) that fails without it.

## Tests

21 tests, all passing against current `main` (merged in).

16 unit tests cover each check, including the QA workstream's planted fixture: a 50-variant sweep reported as a single hypothesis draws a CP-1/CP-2 veto while the two honest candidates are approved.

5 integration tests run the real agent through `compile_production_workflow` with a `MemorySaver` checkpointer, proving the vetoed candidate never reaches Reporting and never becomes PM-selectable, and that a benched Risk agent escalates to the PM rather than silently approving.

## Two things worth discussing

**Import weight.** On current `main`, `from agents import anything` pulls in numpy and pandas, because `agents/__init__.py` eagerly imports `quant_trader`, whose `__init__` imports `discovery`, which imports numpy at module level. Importing the Risk agent should not require pandas. A lazy import inside `discovery` would fix it. I did not change this — it is the Quant workstream's call.

**Shared model interfaces are in the wrong place.** `ModelClient` / `MetricsSink` live in `agents/technical_trader/model_client.py` but are written as provider-neutral shared infrastructure. Risk now imports them from inside another agent's package, which is backwards. Suggest moving that module somewhere shared, but that restructures a teammate's package so it belongs in a team decision.

**Still open:** `pytest` is not declared anywhere in `pyproject.toml`, so there is no documented way to run the suite. Happy to add a `test` extra in a follow-up.

## Policy thresholds awaiting ratification

`RiskPolicy` holds every value the checklist left open, so a meeting ruling is a one-line change: round budget (default 3), sweep flag threshold (default 20), duplication overlap (default 0.7, not yet wired — current CP-8 test is exact rule equality), and the canonical metric set.

🤖 Generated with Claude (https://claude.com)
### ###

author: zephyrnova
body:
Two bugs found while debugging a broken HyperInsight on the freshly-released v0.1.10. Bumps to 0.1.11.

## 1. Every addon is broken in the shipped v0.1.10

There were two committed esbuild configs:

- `esbuild.config.mjs` — `main`, `preload`, `secure-wallet-import-preload`, `addon-preload`. Wired to `npm run build:electron`.
- `esbuild.config.js` — `main`, `preload` only, plus the MCP server. Dated May 17.

`forge.config.js`'s `generateAssets` hook ran `node esbuild.config.js`. That hook is what CI runs, and `dist/` is gitignored, so a clean CI checkout only ever emitted what the stale config listed.

Confirmed against the published v0.1.10 DMG:

```
$ npx asar list .../app.asar | grep dist/main
/dist/main
/dist/main/main.js
/dist/main/mcp-server.js
/dist/main/preload.js
```

No `addon-preload.js`. `ADDON_PRELOAD_PATH` (`electron/addons/webviews.ts`) points at a file that isn't in the asar, the preload fails to load, and `window.addonAPI` is undefined in every addon webview — HyperInsight throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'invoke')` on its first call. `secure-wallet-import-preload.js` (`electron/main.ts`) is missing for the same reason.

This never reproduced locally because a stale `dist/main/addon-preload.js` from an earlier manual `build:electron` was sitting on disk.

Fix: merge both configs into `esbuild.config.mjs` (all four entry points, the MCP server build, union of externals), delete `esbuild.config.js`, point the hook at the survivor. Also widened the packager `ignore` rule, which still named `esbuild.config.js` and was letting the `.mjs` ship inside the asar.

## 2. Addon tabs disappear after quitting

`before-quit` → `deactivateAll()` → `deactivateAddon()` → `setActivated(id, false)`. That field is the *desired* state `initAddons()` converges to on the next launch, so a clean quit was indistinguishable from the user deliberately switching the addon off: next launch skipped activation, and `listAddonTabs()` only emits tabs for live addons, so the tab silently vanished.

Intermittent, because `before-quit` doesn't await `deactivateAll` — the write only landed when the process outlived it.

Fix: `deactivateAddon(id, { persist: false })` for shutdown teardown only. User-initiated deactivate, uninstall and upgrade still persist as before.

## Verification

- Deleted `dist/main` and ran the exact command the hook now runs: all five artifacts emit, `mcp-server.js` byte-identical to the previous build.
- `npm run typecheck` clean.
- Confirmed no packager `ignore` rule touches `dist/main`, and `bundled-addons/` is present in the shipped asar.

Not yet verified: a full packaged build of this branch — `npm run package` doesn't write in this environment. The asar contents should be spot-checked after the release build.

author: adv11
body:
## What
Root-causes the "topbar/sidebar reads grey, page reads dark" bug the user reported twice after #435/PR #436 merged — #435 fixed the opaque *fallback* paths only; the live, at-rest glass surfaces (topbar, sidebar) were still reading a mismatched token family and stayed visibly lighter than the page at all times, not just during scroll.

## How
- `app.css` has two parallel color-token families: the real production `--color-*` tokens (hex, warm-neutral hue) and a `--v3-*` HSL-component layer from the v3 rollout. `.app-topbar`/`.app-sidebar`/`.card`/etc. read `--v3-surface`/`--v3-bg`/`--v3-surface-elevated` directly for their live translucent glass fill — these had a cool blue-gray hue (`220deg`) with no relation to the real `--color-bg`/`--color-surface`/`--color-surface-raised` hex values, so the topbar (always sticky+blurred, never in the fallback state) read a persistently different shade.
- Root-cause fix: retuned `--v3-bg`/`--v3-surface`/`--v3-surface-elevated` (both themes) to the exact HSL-component equivalent of the real hex values. Every one of the dozens of `hsl(var(--v3-surface...` readers app-wide now resolves consistently — no per-selector patch needed.
- Follow-up feedback after the first fix: even with matching hue, `.app-topbar`/`.app-sidebar`'s scroll/no-backdrop-filter fallback still used `--color-surface-raised` ("elevated" chrome, slightly lighter than the page by design) — split that fallback onto `--color-bg` specifically for nav chrome only; card-shaped surfaces (`.card`/`.phase-card`/`.template-card`/`.tag-chip`) keep `--color-surface-raised`, since those are meant to read as distinct cards.

## Testing
- [ ] Unit/integration/E2E tests — N/A, token-value-only CSS change, no new logic
- [x] Manually tested in browser — golden path and edge cases listed below

**Manual test notes:** Verified live against `npm run dev`, dark theme: at rest, topbar/sidebar/page all read one consistent color. Forced `[data-scrolling]` on `<html>` and confirmed topbar/sidebar stay pixel-identical to the page background (screenshot attached) instead of flashing to a lighter fill. `npm run lint` / `npm test` (1484 tests) / `npm run check:cache-version` all green.

## Docs updated
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md`
- [x] `docs/architecture.md` Build Log entry added

## Breaking changes / rollback notes
None. Token-value-only CSS change.

Sidebar/topbar during a forced `[data-scrolling]` state — now pixel-identical to the page:
![consistent dark bg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adv11/ascent/fix/issue-440-v3-surface-token-hue-mismatch/docs/screenshots/issue-440/consistent-dark-bg-fixed.png)

Closes #440

author: amandeepsingh29
body:
Closes #39128

This PR adds an optional `length_function` parameter to `RecursiveJsonSplitter`, allowing users to provide custom chunk size measurement logic (e.g. token counting) instead of the default `len(json.dumps(data))`.

### Changes

**`langchain_text_splitters/json.py`**
- Added `length_function: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], int] | None = None` keyword argument to `__init__`, falling back to `self._json_size` when not provided.
- Replaced hardcoded `self._json_size` calls in `_json_split` with `self._length_function`.
- Removed the additive size assumption in the **dict branch** — now tentatively merges, measures the actual result, and reverts on overflow.
- Applied the same tentative-merge-and-measure pattern to the **leaf branch** (`elif current_path:`), ensuring non-additive size functions (like tokenizers) don't produce oversized chunks.

**`tests/unit_tests/test_text_splitters.py`**
- Added `test_recursive_json_splitter_with_length_function` — verifies custom length function drives chunk splitting.
- Added `test_split_json_non_additive_length_function` — verifies chunks respect `max_chunk_size` with a non-additive size function (simulating tokenizer behavior).

### Testing
- Backward compatible — existing usage without `length_function` is unaffected.
- Passed `make format` and `make lint`.
- All tests pass with no regressions.

author: david-driscoll
body:
Comment-only companion to **david-driscoll/.github#2**, which is the actual fix for the four permanently-stuck `pin image ...` entries on the Renovate dashboard.

Research: david-driscoll/vault#104

**No behaviour change.** Parsing both revisions with JSON5 and deep-comparing yields identical objects — this PR only corrects comments that were wrong, and that caused the same wrong conclusion to be reached twice.

### What was wrong

1. **`helmfile: { pinDigests: false }`** was believed to suppress the pins. It cannot: `applyPackageRules(depConfig, "pre-lookup")` runs *after* the manager config is merged (`lib/workers/repository/process/fetch.ts`), so the shared preset's `docker:pinDigests` rule (`{ matchDatasources: ["docker"], pinDigests: true }`) overrides it. helmfile's `oci://` charts use the `docker` datasource, so they match. Annotated as a no-op.

2. **The "Don't pin digests on flux-managed OCI Helm charts" rule** was believed to cover this. It lists `flux`, `helm-values`, `kubernetes` — not `helmfile`, which is the manager that actually emits these (confirmed by the `renovate/helmfile-*` branch prefix). Also noted: `matchUpdateTypes` is a post-lookup matcher, so that rule suppresses by generating the update and then discarding it at `flatten.ts`'s `enabled !== false` filter, rather than preventing it.

3. **The `additionalBranchPrefix: "helmfile-"` comment** attributed `Error updating branch: update failure` to a rebase race between managers. It is not. The helmfile extractor never sets `currentDigest` and the manager exports neither `updateDependency` nor `autoReplaceStringTemplate`, so `doAutoReplace` can never satisfy `confirmIfDepUpdated` for a `pinDigest` update and throws `WORKER_FILE_UPDATE_FAILED` on every run. The rule is kept — separate branch namespaces are still correct — but the reason is corrected.

4. **The "Excess registryUrls ... benign" comment** blamed overlapping managers. The real cause is two `HelmRepository` documents sharing a name + namespace: `resolveHelmRepository` in `modules/manager/flux/extract.ts` filters *all* HelmRepositories on name+namespace and returns both, yielding the same URL twice.

All references verified against **renovate 44.3.2**, the version actually running these repos.

body:
`GET /api/products` no mesmo contrato do `catalog-lookups`. **164 testes**, CI verde.

## O que ele acrescenta

`catalog_lookups` é global dentro da organização — bastava a fronteira de organização, que vem da sessão. **`products` tem `tenant_id` e RLS**, então o recorte por empresa chega ao HTTP pela primeira vez.

E com ele chega o modo de falhar que a Etapa 0 provou: **sem empresa no escopo, o SQL devolveria zero linhas**. Correto lá dentro, e **indistinguível de "esta empresa não tem produtos"** — o operador olharia uma tela vazia e concluiria a coisa errada. Por isso um guarda recusa **antes** da consulta, para o erro ser visível.

## Desvio deliberado do contrato — e registrado nele

O contrato de listagem diz **500** para empresa ausente. Foi escrito quando a empresa viria sempre pronta na sessão, e aí a ausência só poderia ser defeito de programação.

Depois do ADR-010 D4, **escolher empresa é ação da pessoa** (`PUT /auth/active-tenant`). "Ainda não escolhi" virou estado legítimo do cliente — e responder 500 mandaria fluxo normal para o monitoramento de erro. **500 é o alarme que não pode tocar à toa.**

Ficou **409**, com `type: .../empresa-nao-escolhida`. **A exigência do contrato está intacta:** recusar alto, nunca devolver vazio. Muda só o código, e o contrato foi atualizado explicando por quê — se preferir o 500 literal, é uma linha.

## Detalhes

Whitelist `code`/`description`/`active`; ordem padrão por código (é como o operador do legado enxerga o catálogo); busca cobre **código E descrição**, porque quem procura digita um dos dois e obrigar a escolher o campo é a tela que o operador reclama; `total` sai **de dentro do RLS** — a empresa nunca sabe o total do schema.

## Verificado por mutação

Remover o guarda → quebra exatamente o caso da lista vazia silenciosa.

## Duas decisões de teste

**Não testei acento aqui.** É propriedade da função `vitra_busca`, já provada no `catalog-lookups`; repetir só acoplaria este teste ao dado semeado. Cheguei a semear um produto acentuado, **e ele quebrou três testes de outras classes** que contam linhas do fixture — o seed é compartilhado, e poluí-lo é dívida. Removi.

**O desempate por `id` é asserido no `ORDER BY` gerado**, não no resultado: com poucas linhas o Postgres devolve ordem estável por acaso (medido antes, no `catalog-lookups`).
