author: farizanjum
body:
Fixes #4563

#### Describe the changes you have made in this PR -

Adds Google Cloud Storage as a second built-in object-store provider for remote sync (`OPENSRE_REMOTE_SYNC_PROVIDER=gcs`), plus the `opensre remote-sync setup` command from the issue's Onboarding section. Engine, CLI sync paths, REPL, and gateway are untouched; everything goes through the existing open/closed registry.

**Provider (`platform/filestorage/providers/gcs.py`)**
- Four-method `ObjectStore` implementation over `google-cloud-storage`, registered via `_BUILTIN_MODULES` (lazy import).
- Change detection: converts GCS's base64 `md5Hash` to the hex tag the engine compares. Strict decode (`validate=True`, exactly 16 bytes); composite, foreign, or malformed objects fall back to timestamp comparison, same as S3 multipart. The version-style `blob.etag` is never used - it is not a content hash.
- Credentials are ambient (Application Default Credentials). No new env vars; nothing credential-shaped is stored anywhere.
- All vendor and transport failures wrap to `RemoteSyncUnavailableError`. The catch is broad on purpose: `google-resumable-media` / `requests` exceptions (DataCorruption, InvalidResponse, connection errors) do not inherit `GoogleAPIError`, and the engine and chat surfaces may only ever see `RemoteSyncError` (CWE-209 boundary unchanged).
- `list_objects` force-materializes the lazy listing inside the try and maps to `RemoteObject` outside it, so provider-side mapping bugs can never be masked as availability errors.

**Setup (`opensre remote-sync setup --provider gcs`)**
- New `platform/filestorage/setup.py`: validates the provider against the registry first, then persists exactly six non-secret values (enabled/provider/bucket/prefix/region/profile) into the `remote_sync` section of `~/.opensre/config.yml`. `update_section` merges, so pre-existing keys survive.
- CLI flags for everything; TTY prompts for provider/bucket/prefix when omitted (region/profile are flags-only); clear error when run in a pipe without `--bucket`.
- Provider-aware credential hints (`gcloud auth application-default login` for GCS, profile/SSO for AWS) via a small `credential_hint_for_provider` registry helper and a `CREDENTIAL_HINT` constant per provider module.
- `--disabled` writes `enabled: false` and the confirmation correctly reports "Remote sync is off."
- REPL slash setup is intentionally out of scope here (interactive wizard is #4554); `/remote-sync setup` gets the existing "unknown subcommand" reply. Environment-variable configuration ("and env") is unchanged.
- `DISABLED_HELP` now advertises the setup command and computes the built-in list from the registry, so it stays correct when more providers land.

**Docs**
- GCS provider section: ADC setup, IAM note - `storage.objects.list/get/create/delete`; GCS requires delete to *replace* an existing object (changed sessions re-upload), even though opensre itself never deletes. Default encryption at rest.
- `.env.example`, package docstrings, constants comments, and the "Turn it on" section updated for the second built-in provider.

### Demo/Screenshot for feature changes and bug fixes -

**[ VIDEO PLACEHOLDER - full zero-to-working recording (bucket create, setup, first sync, second-sync etag skip, restore, cleanup) will be attached here by the contributor ]**

Terminal evidence (live, personal GCP account via ADC; every bucket deleted after its run):

```
$ opensre remote-sync setup --provider gcs --bucket opensre-setup-verify-fariz --prefix opensre
Remote sync is on. Settings saved to ~/.opensre/config.yml:
  provider   gcs
  bucket     opensre-setup-verify-fariz
  prefix     opensre
GCP credentials stay ambient: run `gcloud auth application-default login` once per machine with the account that owns the bucket; opensre stores nothing.
Run `opensre remote-sync status` to check, `opensre remote-sync sync` to mirror now.

$ opensre remote-sync status          # no env vars set; reads stored config
Remote sync is on (gcs) -> opensre-setup-verify-fariz/opensre

$ opensre remote-sync sync
Sync complete - 0 downloaded, 3 uploaded (486 B), 0 already current (486 B total).

$ opensre remote-sync sync            # second run, no changes: etag skip path
Sync complete - 0 downloaded, 0 uploaded, 6 already current.

# after editing one local session file (overwrite path):
Sync complete - 0 downloaded, 1 uploaded (267 B), 5 already current (267 B total).
# next run: 0 uploaded, 6 already current (etag matches on overwritten objects)

# restore: sessions dir moved away, then `sync --pull-only`
Sync complete - 2 downloaded (450 B), 0 uploaded, 1 already current (450 B total).
# all restored files verified byte-identical (matching Get-FileHash MD5 pairs)
```

Stored `remote_sync` section - no credential material anywhere:

```
remote_sync:
  enabled: true
  provider: gcs
  bucket: opensre-setup-verify-fariz
  prefix: opensre
  region: ''
  profile: ''
```

Additional live checks from independent QA runs: a planted `credentials.json` in the sessions dir is refused by the deny-list (`Sync failed: refusing to upload ...`), and an unknown provider fails with `known: aws, gcs`.

## Code Understanding and AI Usage

**Did you use AI assistance (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc.) to write any part of this code?**
- [ ] No, I wrote all the code myself
- [x] Yes, I used AI assistance (continue below)

**If you used AI assistance:**
- [ ] I have reviewed every single line of the AI-generated code
- [ ] I can explain the purpose and logic of each function/component I added
- [x] I have tested edge cases and understand how the code handles them
- [x] I have modified the AI output to follow this project's coding standards and conventions

**Explain your implementation approach:**

The issue required a GCS ObjectStore registered as a built-in, proven by a real push-and-restore cycle, plus a setup command that never stores secrets. I mirrored the existing `aws.py` provider because the registry was designed for exactly that shape (open/closed: new module plus one register call). The one GCS-specific problem is change detection: `blob.etag` is a generation tag, not a content hash, so the provider converts the listing's base64 `md5Hash` into the hex MD5 the engine compares; composite or malformed objects degrade to timestamp comparison, the same as S3 multipart. Credentials are ambient ADC, so setup persists only six non-secret values and points the user at `gcloud auth application-default login`. Alternatives considered and rejected: using `blob.etag` directly (breaks skip-on-unchanged), CRC32C (would require engine changes, which the issue forbids), storing a service-account path in config.yml (violates "never store secrets"), and catching only `GoogleAPIError` (google-resumable-media/requests exceptions bypass it and would crash the sync).

---

- [ ] I have considered potential edge cases and how my code handles them
- [x] If it is a core feature, I have added thorough tests
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines and conventions

- Tests: 13 provider tests + 10 setup tests + 6 CLI setup tests + registry/enum/message coverage. Full filestorage/CLI/REPL/gateway/surface suites pass; ruff, ruff format, and mypy (1541 files) are clean.
- Four pre-existing test failures reproduce on *unmodified* `main` on Windows only (text-mode `write_text("\n")` writes CRLF; byte assertions then mismatch): `test_community_style_gcs/azure_registration_drives_the_engine`, `test_older_remote_does_not_clobber_a_newer_local_edit`, `test_pull_writes_atomically_leaving_no_partial_file`. Linux CI is unaffected.

author: mbilokonsky
body:
Re-opened against `main` after its base ([#296](https://github.com/bombadil-labs/loam/pull/296), the isolated fixture edit) merged. GitHub auto-closed [#295](https://github.com/bombadil-labs/loam/pull/295) when that branch was deleted and will not let a closed PR be retargeted; this is the same commits, rebased.

## Summary

- A session's writes carry that user's own author, not the store's. Two operators are distinguishable in the ground — the point of the phase, since two people writing under one name stops being fine the moment a second holds the role.
- The minted identity carries the user's seed AND the operator flag. Dropping the flag would be a silent narrowing dressed as attribution.
- A user with no usable key is refused by name; falling back to the store's seed would be a lie about provenance no later reader could detect.

## Review guide

- The seam: the seed read and the identity in `postToken` (`src/server/session.ts`).
- Read closely: the three-state seed check (absent / unreadable / present-and-not-a-key).
- Two limits stated rather than hidden: the constitutional doors still sign as the STORE, and a struck grant still lets a user log in and mint — authorization is refused at admission instead.

## Evidence

- P1: spec-lint 14/14. An independent premortem returned 8 causes, all folded in — including a live fail-open in my own diff: a zero-byte seed read as "present" and minted `{actor: ""}`, which is not nullish, so nothing fell back.
- P5: two independent lenses found 9 more. The sharpest: the 409 told the operator to run `assign-role`, a command guaranteed to refuse in that exact state (the user already holds the role) — it names the `remove-role`/`assign-role` pair now. And a signing seed outlived every sweep, so the token table is now swept on session-ending too.
- **Myk's correction, folded in:** I claimed that sweep closed the residency. It does not — every sweep path needs a request, so on an untouched server the last copy sits until the process ends. Both specs now state the bound as TRAFFIC, not time.
- 6/6 hand-mutants killed.

## Honest gaps

- `adlc hollow-test` cannot mutate TypeScript at 1.7.0 — hand-mutants stood in. ([#303](https://github.com/bombadil-labs/loam/pull/303) fixes the tool.)
- `adlc prosecute` will not record this P5: trust-root tier wants a cross-model reviewer and this box has only the Claude CLI.
- The REST door is a named gap in the rail file: it addresses schemas by a version alias only a delta-borne registration mints, so a rail there would assert on a 404.

author: dereuromark
body:
`Profile.full()` deleted content. A node type carve-js had no canonical mapping for was denied before the deny and allow lists were ever consulted, so a construct whose type was unmapped rendered as nothing: ``` plain:

x oldnew y ... full :

x y ... ``` Both the old wording and the new one, destroyed by a profile that denies nothing. markup-carve/carve#419 settled that the three resolution steps are exhaustive - an unmapped type cannot be in a deny list, an allow list excludes it, and otherwise it is allowed. There is no fourth "deny the unrecognized" step. markup-carve/carve-php#503 fixed carve-php the same way and is the reference this follows. ## What changed `canonicalType()` is now total - it returns the type itself when there is no fold, instead of `undefined`. Returning `undefined` *was* the defect: the filter read "no mapping" as "deny". Resolution then happens on the node's own axis, which is the only place block-vs-inline is unambiguous for a type the vocabulary does not know. `to_text` no longer deletes what it cannot read. It deleted any node whose payload lived in fields rather than children, so denying a substitution destroyed both wordings. It now substitutes non-empty text, or removes a node that renders nothing, and records a `to_text_yielded_nothing` violation with a visible `[type]` marker if an extractor arm is ever missing. ``` plain :

x oldnew y and a :smile: and “quoted”

full : identical comment:

x oldnew y and a :smile: and “quoted”

``` **The security posture is unchanged.** An allow-list profile still denies every type not in its list, including unknown ones - step 2 excludes them by construction. `Profile.comment()` and `Profile.minimal()` behave identically for every type they list. ## A second-order fix worth flagging Making `canonicalType` total removed the `undefined` that `isBlockNode`'s `BLOCK_JS_TYPES` fallback silently depended on, which cost `abbreviation_def` its block-axis classification. It is re-added to `BLOCK_CANONICAL` and the fallback is deleted, having become unreachable. All 15 of its entries were checked by hand: only `abbreviation_def` ever reached it. ## Known divergence from carve-php, not introduced here `Profile.denyBlock(['frontmatter'])` is a **silent no-op in carve-js**, while carve-php strips the node. carve-js models frontmatter as a plain field on `Document`, never entered through the child walk, so the filter cannot see it. markup-carve/carve#418 says frontmatter is a block node in the tree; carve-js does not model it that way. This is pre-existing and architectural rather than a regression, but it is exactly the silent-no-op that a normative vocabulary is supposed to prevent, and the two engines now disagree. Worth its own issue. `escaped_text` remains folded to `text` here, so denying it is likewise a no-op even though the spec lists it as nameable. Also pre-existing, also out of scope.

author: gitchrisqueen
body:
Closes #804. Refs #406, #747, #771.

Option **1A** from the Decision Comment: run the live probe, paste the verdict, add the resolving routes + unit tests.

## The live run

Ran on the prod VPS from a Selenium worker with user 1's real session (cookies + residential proxy, 429 breaker clear). **Read-only** — nothing typed, no control clicked, nothing published.

| Step | Verdict | Route | Live element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `article_title` | **OK** | `title_placeholder` (1st route) | `<textarea placeholder="Title">` |
| `article_body` | **OK** | `body_aria` (1st route) | `<div role="textbox" aria-label="Article editor content">` |
| `article_next` | **OK** | `next_text` (1st route) | `<button type="submit">Next</button>` |
| `article_publish` | **UNKNOWN** | none resolved | *not on this screen* |

Every checkable route resolved on its **first** route, so **no selector needed changing** — the #771 ladder is correctly grounded. Full JSON on the issue.

Every visible control on `/article/new/`: `Me`, `For Business`, `Christopher Queen / The Growth Brief`, `Style`, `Manage menu`, **`Next`**, `Upload from computer`. No publish-like control among them. **The editor is two screens** — Publish only exists in the "Ready to publish?" dialog Next opens.

## What the run actually found: a defect in the gate

`fill_article_editor` pre-flighted **all four** steps before typing:

```python
failed = editor.first_missing()      # included article_publish
if failed:
    return None, failed              # aborted before typing a character
```

Publish is never on the editor screen, so **that gate could never pass**. Every newsletter edition publish would have returned `(None, "article_publish")` — #747's alert firing with a step name for a button that was not supposed to be there yet, and #771's ladder never reached. User 1 has newsletter publishing enabled with a live series, so the next scheduled edition would have hit it. Caught before the first real edition published.

## Changes

- **`article_editor.py`** — pre-flight (and the typing-failure re-check) scoped to `EDITOR_SCREEN_STEPS`; Publish is still required, at the point it is re-resolved *after* Next. `first_missing(steps=…)` takes the screen scope.
- **`ResolvedElement.expected_on_screen`** — a step absent from the current screen is **`UNKNOWN`, never `MISSING`**. `StepVerdict.UNKNOWN` was defined but nothing ever returned it; "we did not look" must not read as "the selector is broken".
- **`article_editor_verdict(..., on_editor_screen=True)`** — what a read-only probe passes. Adds `editor_ready` ("can publishing start") and `graded_steps`. Default is unchanged (whole-flow view), so existing callers keep their semantics.
- **`linkedin_live_validation.py`** — the probe ships `buttons` (every visible control) beside the verdict, so the two-screen claim is **checkable rather than assumed**, plus each winning element's attributes as selector provenance and a one-sentence `verdict`.
- **`docs/LIVE_VALIDATION_FORMAT_AND_STATS.md`** — §3 selector rows with live provenance, §4 the run command, new §6 with the result and the defect.

## Testing

- `tests/unit/utilities/linkedin/test_article_editor.py`: **45 pass** (was 30). New `TestTwoScreenGrading` covers screen-scoped `first_missing`, the three-valued verdict, the editor-screen vs whole-flow grading, a genuinely broken editor step still failing, publish reading OK if LinkedIn ever moves it to screen 1, and the **#804 regression** — the flow now types, clicks Next, and only then requires Publish.
- `TestProbeEvidenceHelpers` covers the probe's evidence capture (dedup, hidden skip, limit, stale elements).
- `article_editor.py` at **100%** line coverage.
- `tests/unit/test_linkedin_live_validation.py` (28) and `tests/unit/app/test_newsletter_publish.py` + `test_newsletter_catchup.py` (44) all pass — 109 green across the affected suites.

## Not validated, deliberately

The **publish dialog** — `article_publish`'s two routes and `_fill_edition_description`. Reaching it means clicking Next on a real draft, one control away from publishing to the live account. It stays a **supervised first publish** per `docs/FORMAT_API_FEASIBILITY.md` §4; `failed_step` now names the dialog step honestly if it fails.

https://github.com/theforeman/puppet-pulpcore/actions/runs/30661608422/job/91258977370

```
Problem: package python3.12-pulpcore-3.105.12-3.el10.noarch from pulpcore requires
  (python3.12dist(django-import-export) < 5~~ with python3.12dist(django-import-export) >= 2.9),

 - nothing provides python3.12-diff-match-patch needed by python3.12-django-import-export-4.4.1-2.el10.noarch
```

**python-diff-match-patch** — listed in `tier4_packages`, but its COPR package (`python3.12-diff-match-patch`) was only ever built for `rhel-9-x86_64`. Slipped through all 24 tier4 waves. Bumped release to trigger an EL10 build.

While sweeping every package in `package_manifest.yaml` against COPR's actual latest-succeeded-build chroots (resolving each package's real RPM `Name:`, not the source directory name) to check for other silent gaps like this one, also found:

- **python-lxml** — still hardcoded `%global python3_pkgversion 3.11`, so `python3.12-lxml` never existed here, breaking `python3.12-aiohttp-xmlrpc`'s plain `Requires: python3.12-lxml` (a dependency of `python-pulp-rpm` and `python-bandersnatch`). `python3.12-lxml` is already provided natively by CentOS Stream 9 and 10 (confirmed: `python3.12-lxml = 5.2.1-2.el10`), so the plan is to drop our custom build entirely rather than rebuild it — tracked separately, not part of this PR.
- Ten other packages (`python-ecdsa`, `python-future`, `python-colorama`, `python-commonmark`, `python-contextlib2`, `python-dataclasses`, `python-idna-ssl`, `python-pycryptodomex`, `python-pyjwkest`, `python-toml`, `python-types-cryptography`, `postgresql-debversion`, `postgresql-evr`) also never got past `rhel-8-x86_64`, but aren't referenced by any current spec and mostly already have their own `Obsoletes` entries from the python 3.11→3.12 transition — likely retired packages whose manifest entries were never cleaned up. Not touched here.

author: mkcyberlabs
body:
🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: The Express rate limiting middleware used strict string equality `req.path === '/analyze'` without normalizing the path. Since Express routing is case-insensitive and ignores trailing slashes by default, attackers could trivially bypass the rate limiter by using varied casing (e.g., `/Analyze`) or trailing slashes (e.g., `/analyze/`).
🎯 Impact: Attackers could bypass DoS protections and flood sensitive endpoints indefinitely.
🔧 Fix: Normalized the request path in the middleware using `req.path.toLowerCase().replace(/\/$/, '')` prior to comparison. Also appended `.unref()` to the cleanup `setInterval` to prevent tests/processes from hanging.
✅ Verification: Ran `bash tests/test-upload.sh` to confirm standard routing works, and manually verified that uppercase/trailing slash requests are successfully blocked by the rate limiter after the threshold is reached.

author: ondreu
body:
## What does this PR do?

Sorting a tasks card by priority could put a **High** task above a **Highest** one.

`priorityRank()` was built on `priorityLevel()` — the coarse three-bucket mapping that exists to pick the *colour* of the priority dot. That bucket deliberately folds `highest` into `high` (and `lowest` into `low`), so two tasks one level apart compared **equal** and the order fell through to the next rule (the smart-sort chain, ultimately created date). The result looked arbitrary, which the reporter read as alphabetical.

`priorityRank()` now ranks on `priorityKey()`, the exact five-level mapping already used for the CSS class and the editor pickers, indexed into the descending key order: highest → high → medium → low → lowest → unranked. Loose synonyms (`urgent`, `p1`, `minor`, …) still fall back to their coarse level, as `priorityKey()` already did.

This affects three places that share the rank: the **Priority** sort, the priority step of a **custom multi-field sort**, and the priority tiebreak inside the default **smart sort**. Colours and the priority filter chips are untouched — they keep using the coarse level on purpose.

The priority helpers were pure string logic buried in `src/cards/tasks.ts`, which can't be imported under test (`tasks → editors → cards/index → tasks` is circular at module init). They move to `src/priority.ts`, following the existing `checkboxes.ts` / `taskscope.ts` pattern, so the ordering can be pinned by unit tests. No behaviour moved with them; the only incidental change is that `priorityKey()` now trims before comparing words.

### A note on TaskNotes mode

Checked, and stock TaskNotes is fine — its default `low` / `normal` / `high` values rank correctly under this fix, and TaskNotes tasks never open the quick-view editor, so its hardcoded five-level dropdown can't clobber a priority. Custom TaskNotes priorities are a separate, pre-existing gap (Hearth doesn't read TaskNotes' configured priority list or weights, so unrecognised values all tie in the unranked bucket and read as "None" to the filter chips). Not addressed here — worth its own issue.

## Related issue

Closes #145

- [ ] 📝 Docs
- [ ] ✨ Feature / behaviour change (discussed in an issue first)

`npm run build`, `npm run lint` (0 errors) and `npm test` all pass; the suite is 204 tests including the new `test/taskpriority.test.ts`, which pins the ordering for words and emoji, the synonym fallbacks, and unranked-last. Not exercised in a live vault — the ordering is covered by unit tests, but a sanity check on a real card would be worth it before release.

author: daniel-frenkel
body:
Five commits from the 2026-07-31 bench session. Two real device bugs, a version bump, and the tooling for the 50-unit pilot burn.

## fix(device): USB-CDC backpressure froze the loop every 30 s

Reported symptom: the screen froze ~3 s every 30–60 s, and cards were slow to open and close. Those are the **same event** — touch is polled once per loop pass, so a stalled loop reads as dead touch.

Not the network. `HWCDC::write` blocks when the port is enumerated but nothing drains it (a board plugged into a computer with no terminal open). `isPlugged()` stays true, so the disconnect guard never fires and the driver falls back to `max_consec_timeouts(20) x tx_timeout_ms(100)` = **up to 2 s per `write()`**. `RecordFrameUs` emits two printfs every 30 s, on the loop task.

`setTxTimeoutMs(2)` caps that at ~40 ms. Guarded on `ARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT`; `blipscope-pro-s3-21` (UART0) builds green.

Ships to customers, not just the bench: anyone powering the device from a laptop or monitor USB port hits it.

## fix(logbook): persist failures were silent

```
putString(): nvs_set_str fail: operators NOT_ENOUGH_SPACE
[logbook] persisted (70 types, 86 airlines, ...)     <-- said this anyway
```

No write's return value was checked and `dirty` was cleared unconditionally, so a failed store was both forgotten and reported as saved. Now every write is checked, `dirty` only clears when all four land, and the line reports the failing key, its size, and NVS entries free.

**The storage change in this PR did not fix the underlying failure, and the commit message overstates it.** I diagnosed NVS string contiguity and moved the stores to blobs; blobs fail too, and so does a 4-byte `putUInt`. The 20 KB partition is genuinely full (`freeEntries=126` — one page, the one NVS reserves for GC). The blob migration is kept because it is still the more robust storage for these sizes, but the real fix is a bigger NVS (being verified separately, ahead of the pilot burn) plus a hard logbook footprint budget (post-burn, OTA-able).

The honest reporting is what surfaced all of this, and it is the part that matters here.

## release: FW_VERSION 5

Pilot boards must ship carrying a version the v5 Release can supersede. Bumping ships nothing on its own.

## tooling: parallel batch provisioning

`provision-batch.py` — N boards at once, each with its own HMAC-derived key. One build up front then esptool directly (concurrent `pio run -t upload` would race on `.pio/build`), one esptool call per board writing the merged factory image and that board's NVS together, idempotent by MAC rather than port since COM numbers are recycled on unplug. Failures are isolated. Dry-run verified against the bench s3-128.

Also gitignores `provisioned.csv` (factory MACs — a fleet roster, not for a public repo).

## Testing

- `blipscope-s3-128-cloud` and `blipscope-pro-s3-21` build green
- CDC fix flashed to the bench s3-128; serial output verified healthy by reading the port directly
- Logbook diagnostics verified live — they are how the full-partition condition was found
- Batch provisioner dry-run derives the same device id whose key production accepted

author: morcen
body:
## What was broken

`config/probe.php` defines two redaction field lists: `redact.body_fields` and `redact.query_bindings`. `body_fields` explicitly includes `credit_card` and `ssn`, but `query_bindings` did not.

`QueryWatcher::interpolate()` only redacts a bound value when its column name matches an entry in `probe.redact.query_bindings`. Since the `queries` watcher is enabled by default (`probe.watchers.queries` defaults to `true`), any statement like `INSERT INTO payments (credit_card, ...) VALUES (?, ...)` or `UPDATE users SET ssn = ?` was captured with the raw credit card number or SSN in plaintext in `probe_entries.content.sql`, even though the package already treats those exact fields as sensitive for the request/response body redaction path.

## What changed

- Added `credit_card` and `ssn` to the default `redact.query_bindings` list in `config/probe.php`, matching `redact.body_fields`.
- Added a test in `tests/Watchers/QueryWatcherTest.php` covering an INSERT statement with `credit_card` and `ssn` columns, asserting both are redacted in the recorded SQL.

Fixes #44

author: guyettinger
body:
Builds `src/replay/` and `native/ax-exec.swift` — the first component in DeskRAG that *acts* rather than records — and fixes four defects found by driving real recordings through the trace pipeline for the first time.

## Why the fixes are in the same PR

The spec's design decisions are grounded in numbers measured from real recordings, and those numbers were not obtainable before these fixes. Splitting them would leave the spec citing figures no one could reproduce.

Driving two real recordings through capture → lift → graph (the prior end-to-end proof was `SyntheticInputProducer` in tests) produced a graph of **2 nodes, 3 edges, 0 slots** — one state with two self-loops.

1. **AX role prefix mismatch.** `ax-dump.swift` strips the `AX` prefix, so real data carries `Button`/`Window`/`TextField`, but `trace/predicates.ts` matched *prefixed* literals with an exact `Set.has()`. `extractPredicates` emitted **zero `ax_exists` and `ax_focused` predicates from real data, ever** — so every boundary inside an app looked like the same state, and every idle gap was dropped as *"no newly-true predicate"* (a constant predicate set has nothing that can become true). `represent/regions/ax.ts` already normalizes for this reason; `predicates.ts` had regressed it. Roles are now canonicalized for matching *and* in emitted args, so both spellings key identically.
2. **Region proposal was fused to region embedding.** `imageEmbedder` and `patchEmbedder` are mutually exclusive, and the Regions stage was gated on the former — so selecting ColSmol skipped it entirely and `Anchor.visual` could never be populated. Proposal is geometry plus the AX tree; only the crop needs a model. `RegionInsert.vector` is now optional, which is the same state a crash between the SQLite commit and the Lance add already leaves behind and which `reconcile()` already finds.
3. **The visual anchor took its pHash from the AX snapshot** while taking its regions from the nearest frame. Two thirds of real snapshots are boundary-triggered (`focus_change`, `dwell_resume`) and carry no frame, so the layer was dropped on 31 of 32 actions. `RegionsAtFrame` now carries both, making the mismatch unrepresentable.
4. *(Environment)* the built `ax-dump` binary predated `--keymap`/`--displays` and returned an AX tree for both.

### Result on the same two recordings

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nodes / edges / slots | 2 / 3 / 0 | 18 / 21 / **2** |
| `ax_exists` predicates | 0 | 245 |
| `wait` actions | 0 | 13 |
| `type` actions | 0 | 4 |
| Nodes with a visual signature | ~1 | 16 / 18 |

Slots merged as `textfield=["Test 1","Test 2"]` and `textarea=["This is test 1","This is test 2"]` — two recordings differing only in typed text collapsed into shared edges with two samples each. That is the graph model's central claim, confirmed on real data.

## The executor

`src/replay/` is pure TypeScript that spawns a subprocess, so it belongs in the barrel — the repo's line is *native module, not subprocess*.

- **Dry-run by default, one arming gate.** Planning has no side effects beyond reading the AX tree; an armed plan then runs end-to-end, aborting on predicate mismatch.
- **A five-rung anchor ladder ranked by measured availability**: `identifier → path → label → visual → point`. Of anchors carrying an AX layer, **71% have an `AXIdentifier` but only 29% have a label**, and the positional path (mean depth 3.8) shifts whenever the UI gains a sibling. A rung resolving to a box wildly unlike the recorded one is rejected rather than trusted.
- **Verification is subset, not set equality.** `samePredicateSet` is exact because *merging* needs it; verification asks "is this still true?", so extra observed predicates are not violations. Equality here would fail on any screen that gained anything since recording.
- **Brittleness gates arming.** An edge whose targets are majority point-only cannot be armed without an explicit override. 45% of real targets resolve to coordinates alone today.
- **`wait` polls a predicate, never sleeps a recorded duration.**
- **Clicks use CGEvent, never `AXPress`** — `AXPress` is a different action (no hover, no mouse-down, different event stream), so replaying with it would be a silent divergence from what was recorded.
- **`native/ax-exec` is a separate binary from `ax-dump`.** `ax-dump` is read-only and two of its modes are permission-free by design; folding actuation in would mean every AX read is done by something that can also click.

## Safety

`execute.ts` depends only on an injected `Actuator`, and a test asserts no module in `replay/` except `sidecar.ts` mentions `spawn`/`child_process` — **the suite is structurally incapable of posting a real event.** The sidecar tests only exercise `dump`, `quit`, and an unknown command; none actuate. `ax-exec` gates on `AXIsProcessTrusted()` and refuses to start without `--plan`.

## Known limitations

- **The visual rung fires on 6% of targets**, because all 154 region rows are `source: "ax"` — grid tiles score 0.5 against AX's 2–5 and never survive the 14-region budget in `fuse.ts`. The layer therefore only exists where AX already worked, which inverts its purpose. Recorded as a derived requirement on `represent/` rather than tuned blind: whether a grid tile resolves usefully at replay is a question the executor now exists to answer.
- **The ladder percentages come from two recordings of one task in TextEdit.** They are real and they contradict what a label-first ladder would assume, but they are one app.
- Nothing wires the executor into DeskRAGApp yet; this is the library seam only.

## Verification

- **639 tests passing**, 14 skipped (sidecar tests skip cleanly without `swiftc`)
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, and `npm --prefix app run typecheck` all clean

Specs: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-executor-design.md`, plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-31-executor.md`.

body:
## GitHub Issue

**Issue:** [#11](https://github.com/Portal-Doctor/Book-Oracle/issues/11)

---

## Description

Added title/author fuzzy search to the mobile scan screen so readers without the physical book (eBook, library borrow, Kindle) no longer have to type a 13-digit ISBN by hand. Roadmap milestone **M5**.

**Web API.** Added `GET /api/books/search?q=…`, a thin handler that parses an inline Zod `querySchema` (`q: z.string().min(3).max(120)`), checks `getUserId` per-route, and delegates to the new `apps/web/src/lib/books/searchBooks.ts`. Failures are caught per-route and mapped to the standard 400/401/500 shape, with `logger.error()` before the 5xx. `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` is set, matching every other route.

**Search logic.** `searchBooks(query, limit)` calls Google Books first and only augments with Open Library when Google returned fewer than three usable hits, then dedupes by `isbn13` and caps the merged list at `limit`. Hits with no ISBN-13 are discarded, since the mobile tap-through hands the ISBN straight to the existing resolve-by-ISBN flow. An upstream failure or malformed payload is logged and degrades to no hits from that provider — a half-typed query never surfaces a 5xx.

**Provider modules.** Extended the existing `googleBooks.ts` and `openLibrary.ts` rather than adding new ones: `searchGoogleBooks(query, limit)` reuses `parseYear` and `pickIdentifier`, and the inline http→https cover rewrite was lifted into a shared `toHttpsCover` helper now used by both the ISBN lookup and the search path. `searchOpenLibrary(query, limit)` hits `search.json` and maps `docs[]` entries that carry a 13-digit ISBN.

**Shared type.** Added `BookSearchResult` to `packages/shared/src/types.ts` so the route and the mobile client agree on the result shape.

**Mobile.** Added a debounced (300 ms) search bar above the camera preview in `apps/mobile/app/scan.tsx`, built from Restyle primitives — a `Card variant="outlined"` wrapping a plain `TextInput`, with suggestion rows as an inline `SuggestionRow` subcomponent (cover thumbnail from `theme.sizes`, title in `variant="body"`, author + year in `variant="caption"`). Queries fire at three characters or more, each keystroke aborts the previous in-flight request, and tapping a row reuses the existing lookup handler so the resolve → add to library → navigate to `/book/[isbn]` flow is unchanged. The barcode scanner keeps running untouched while the field is empty. Every value comes from a theme token — no hex colours, no raw pixel numbers, no `StyleSheet.create`.

**Roadmap.** Bumped the M5 row in `ROADMAP.md` to in-progress; the ✅ mark is left for after merge.

**Test notes:**

Added `apps/web/test/searchBooks.test.ts`, targeting the `src/lib/` function rather than the HTTP endpoint per the testing convention. `fetch` is stubbed with `vi.stubGlobal` and routed by hostname so Google Books and Open Library can be driven independently. Coverage: Google Books passthrough (and Open Library never called), Google Books thin → Open Library fills with dedupe by `isbn13`, both providers empty → `[]`, malformed JSON and a 503 → `[]` without throwing, hits missing an ISBN-13 filtered out before the limit is counted, and the merged list capped at the requested limit.

author: felickz
body: pr-compile.sh: replace unconditional full-language compile with a three-way gate. A PR that only touches leaf .ql files now gets a fast, strict per-file recompile instead of compiling every query in the language. Any change to a shared library (.qll anywhere, not just lib/), qlpack.yml/lockfile/suite metadata, or a dependency/CLI version bump (.codeqlversion, .release.yml) still triggers a full, strict recompile - this also fixes a latent gap where a deleted dependency file was silently ignored. .github/** changes get a lenient full compile (matching the prior no-PR-context behavior) plus a strict per-file recompile of any touched queries. ci.yml Test Queries step: mirror the same classification to scope codeql test run to just the .qlref file(s) that test the touched .ql file(s), resolved via each .qlref's authoritative query: line (not folder-name convention, which is unreliable - see CWE-089/ CWE-208 test layouts). Falls back to the full 4-way sliced suite for any non-fast-path change. Also fixes test-step stderr always being discarded on success: the child's progress output now goes to a real per-slice log file that is always printed after the process exits, instead of being captured via communicate() and only shown on failure. Upload test results now also picks up these log files for post-hoc debugging. author: u2giants
body:
Companion to `u2giants/shared-db` PR #357 (merged as `c7321b5`). **Do not merge without Albert's say-so.**

## Why

A fresh coordinator read the (empty) `REQUEST QUEUE` / `INTAKE QUEUE` / `IN PROGRESS` sections of `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md` — exactly as `shared-db-orchestrator` instructed — and reported **"there is no pending work"** while ~20 real jobs sat in `HANDOFF.md`'s `## BACKLOG`. Every word was true; the conclusion was completely wrong.

Root cause: the outgoing coordinator wrote a narrative handover and never populated the queue, **because nothing in the handover standard required it**. The skill and the intake file agreed with each other and were both incomplete. The repo-side banner fix only helps on one machine — these skill changes are the durable fix.

## `shared-db-handover` (primary fix)

- New **"Seed the queue — REQUIRED, and a handover without it is INCOMPLETE"** section in path (B): the outgoing coordinator must seed/refresh the `REQUEST QUEUE` with every outstanding item — opening agenda, waiting-on-Albert list, and every `B<n>` backlog item — as **short** entries pointing at `HANDOFF.md`, never duplicating its content. Cites the 2026-07-31 failure.
- Rewritten "The handoff has TWO halves" statement so an un-seeded queue makes a handover incomplete with **exactly the same weight** as a missing per-sub-agent block.
- Added as pre-handover sweep step **2b** and before-you-call-it-done checklist item **8**.

## `shared-db-orchestrator`

- Session start is now **five ordered steps**, with reading `HANDOFF.md` (most recent `COORDINATOR HANDOVER` incl. opening agenda + waiting-on-Albert list, and `## BACKLOG`) as a **required step BEFORE** the queue sweep.
- Verbatim: *"An empty REQUEST QUEUE / INTAKE QUEUE / IN PROGRESS does not mean there is no work. `HANDOFF.md` is the authoritative record of outstanding work; the queues track only incoming requests and handovers."*
- States plainly: **where the queues and `HANDOFF.md` disagree, `HANDOFF.md` wins.**
- Step 3 now requires reconciling the queue against the backlog just read, and seeding anything missing before dispatching.

## Also

`docs/skills-map.md` updated to match both descriptions.

## Trigger safety

**Neither skill's frontmatter `description:` was touched** — all edits are in the body — so trigger behaviour is unchanged by construction.

author: higherorderfunctor
body:
## What

`stacked-workflows.enable = true` fans two things into the `ai.*` pools ([`mkSkillPackageModule.nix`](../blob/main/lib/ai/mkSkillPackageModule.nix)): the six `stack-*` skills, and a router instruction that is **always-loaded** in every ecosystem (`paths = null` → Kiro `inclusion: always`, Claude no `paths:` key).

Most of that instruction was a 9-row operation → skill table, which duplicated the skill descriptions that are *already resident* — Claude and Kiro both surface `name` + `description` for every installed skill and load the body on demand.

Measured against the live install:

| | bytes |
|---|---|
| routing table (of the 2205-byte fragment) | 1700 |
| `stack-*` frontmatter already in context | 2670 |
| **rendered consumer artifact, before** | **2205** |
| **rendered consumer artifact, after** | **626** |

`stack-plan`'s description already reads *"…INSTEAD of manual git rebase -i, git reset --soft, or ad-hoc git move sequences"* — verbatim the table row for `/stack-plan`.

What survives is the one thing a skill description cannot express: the check has to happen **before** the model considers a skill, and a description is matched only once it already has.

## Alternatives evaluated and rejected

Both are recorded in `router.nix` so they aren't re-proposed.

**Kiro `inclusion: auto`** — description-matched by the same matcher that fires skills, so it cannot fire in the case this rule exists for. (`auto` is a real Kiro mode; the transformer can't emit it — see follow-up below.)

**A `PreToolUse` hook** — cannot distinguish freelancing from a skill running. The skills' own bodies execute every command the old table named as a thing to use a skill *instead of*:

| skill | command it runs |
|---|---|
| `stack-fix` | `git absorb --and-rebase` |
| `stack-split` | `git rebase -i`, `git reset HEAD^` |
| `stack-plan` | `git reset --soft`, `git commit --fixup` |

So a command matcher fires mostly on **correct** behavior — `deny` breaks the skills outright, `ask` prompts inside every correct run — and `PreToolUse` sees only `tool_name` + `tool_input`, with no signal for whether a skill is driving. Separating them needs session-transcript inspection, which doesn't pay for itself against a few hundred bytes of prose.

There is also an engine gap: Kiro v3 hooks are TUI-gated, so a hook would not fire under `acp` at all, whereas steering injects on every engine.

## Also in this change

- Fragment renamed `routing-table.md` → `skill-routing.md`; it no longer holds a table. Propagated through `overlay.nix`, both backend modules, dev fragments, `dev/generate.nix`, `checks/module-eval.nix`, and the repo-review personality prompts.
- Stale **rationale** corrected in `lib/ai/mkSkillPackageModule.nix` and `packages/living-workflow/modules/homeManager/default.nix`: both justified the router as *"sibling disambiguation"*, which was the table's job. Replaced with the actual bar for adding an always-loaded router.
- Dropped one dead line in `consistency-auditor.md` that referenced both the removed table and `INSTALL.md`.

## Verification

- `nix flake check` — all checks passed (includes `instructions-drift`, which asserts the generated ecosystem files match the fragments).
- Rendered the consumer artifact through `lib/ai/transformers/kiro.nix` to confirm the emitted frontmatter and the 2205 → 626 byte delta.
- Regenerated all instruction files via `devenv tasks run --mode before generate:all`; `treefmt` clean; prek hooks green.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

`lib/ai/transformers/kiro.nix` is a two-way branch and can only express 2 of Kiro's 4 documented inclusion modes — `auto` and `manual` are unreachable. Wiring them needs a typed option on `instructionModule`/`ruleModule` plus HM/devenv parity and check coverage. Filed as a follow-up rather than conflated here.

## Note for reviewers

Pre-existing drift, deliberately **not** fixed here: `INSTALL.md` is referenced 7 times across 4 `dev/skills/repo-review/personalities/*.md` files and does not exist anywhere in the repo.

author: jake-kramer
body:
Several commits improving the symbolizer's debuginfod client

**1. `fix(symbolizer): retry connection-level debuginfod failures and count attempts`**
The failure message counts attempts actually made instead of the backoff wait counter.

**2. `fix(symbolizer): stop dropping not-found cache config in the client constructor`**
The constructor rebuilt its config field-by-field and silently dropped `NotFoundCacheTTL`/`NotFoundCacheMaxItems`, so cached 404s never expired instead of expiring after the configured seven days.

**3. `feat(symbolizer): circuit-break debuginfod after consecutive network failures`**
Five consecutive network-level failures open the breaker for a minute, then a single half-open probe decides. Trips are logged and counted (`pyroscope_symbolizer_debuginfod_circuit_breaker_trips_total`); open-state rejections surface with an `error:unavailable` metric status.

**4. `fix(symbolizer): trace debuginfod fetches, classify cache-probe misses`**
The fetch gets a `debuginfod_fetch` span via dskit tracing, carrying build ID and outcome (404s and breaker skips are expected outcomes, not span errors) (previously the dominant cost of a slow resolve appeared only as unexplained gaps between bucket operations). The bucket cache probes now classify a missing object as a distinct `errObjectNotFound` instead of treating every `Get` error as a miss.

**5. `refactor(symbolizer): budget upstream fetches separately from cache probes`**
`max-debuginfod-concurrency` throttled the entire per-binary resolution pipeline, coupling cheap object-store cache probes to the politeness cap for a third-party service. The cap now lives inside the client as a semaphore around actual upstream fetches (acquired inside the breaker, so an open breaker never consumes a slot), and the frontend pipeline fans out four resolves per fetch slot so cache lookups drain at bucket speed.

**6. `feat(symbolizer): send an identifying User-Agent to debuginfod servers`**
`pyroscope-symbolizer/<version> (github.com/grafana/pyroscope)` instead of Go's default `Go-http-client`, so upstream operators can attribute the traffic and contact us rather than throttle by IP. The reference libdebuginfod client identifies itself the same way.

author: dpmills
body:
`specialize_use`'s memo compared two values produced by two different procedures: a candidate's key was `resolve_var_type(&use_expr.ty)` taken *before* its pin, while an entry's was `clone.ty` — the clone's type *after* the pin and a full re-entrant coalesce. Neither is a faithful identity for what a clone gets specialized to, and the mismatch broke the memo in both directions.

## False hits, i.e. a miscompile

A resolved type is a polarity-correct *rendering*: a domain resolves from upper bounds — what the definition body demands — so a position the body never touches is narrowed away, and an argument's refinement, which arrives as a *lower* bound of that domain, is invisible unless `compact_type`'s opposite-polarity fallback happens to fire at that exact position. The clone's interior reads its parameter at a *positive* position and sees precisely those refinements. So two uses differing only in a key-invisible position shared a clone whose interior was resolved against the first use's argument:

```
h = \a, b -> a + b
h(1, 2) + h(1, 5)
```

Both uses keyed on `((1, Int) ⇒ Int)` — element 0's refinement reached the key, element 1's did not — and the shared clone typed `.1` as `2`. The post-inline consistency wall then panicked with `Type mismatch for Apply: expected 5, found 2`. A difference in the *first* argument keyed apart and compiled fine, so the failure was confined to differences the rendering could not see.

## A write-only table

For any definition whose clone type gains a refinement across the pin, no candidate key could ever equal a stored one, so every call site minted its own clone — including character-identical ones — and the table accumulated several entries under one key. The comment justifying the stored key claimed a later same-typed use would resolve through the first pin's extended chains; it cannot, because every use instantiates its own fresh variables, which the first clone's pin never touches.

## `SpecKey`

`SpecKey` replaces the resolved type. It is the pair of **directed reads** of the use's instantiation, kept apart: the *positive* read is the stamping view (a domain from the definition's demands), the *negative* read is the clone's view (a domain from the argument that flowed in, a codomain from the consumer's demand). The negative read is the load-bearing half — it is the polarity the clone's interior reads its parameter at — and the pair is exhaustive, because use-specific information enters an instantiation through exactly two channels: an `arg <: domain` edge and a `codomain <: demand` edge.

Both reads stay *directed*, which matters: following both bound lists at every variable instead walks out of one use's cone and into every other (two calls' arguments meet at the shared variable of an operator's scheme), so every use keys on the whole program's literals and they all compare equal. Keeping the two views separate matters too — a merged view forgets which direction a contribution came from, and the pin the key stands in for is direction-sensitive. Within a read, merging is always union: a key that narrows can only under-split, and under-splitting is a miscompile while over-splitting is a wasted clone. An under-determined position is one canonical empty view rather than a fresh `Infer` placeholder, so two unexercised uses can now share.

Both sides of the comparison are now taken by one procedure at one point in the pin's lifecycle, and an entry stores the key of the use that minted it, with a `debug_assert` that no two entries share a key.

`poly_used_directly_and_through_wrapper_shares_specializations` drops from five specializations to four: the direct `f(1)` and the `f(y)` reached inside `g`'s `Int` clone instantiate `f` identically, so they now group onto one specialization — which is what the test's name and its "the memo is per frame, not per demanding region" comment always asked for.

Consequences carried along: `ReadPurpose::SpecializationKey` becomes `Instantiation` (that resolution no longer keys anything — it seeds the clone's channel-domain pairings and blames a resolution failure, so its refinement exclusion is now justified by *those* consumers being refinement-insensitive rather than by the false claim that a refinement the read could not see can only cause a miss); `HistoryKind` derives `Ord` so a kind can key a `BTreeMap`; and a `specialize_use` doc block that had detached from its function is reattached.

The remaining imprecision is documented on `SpecializeFrame::specs` and in the new "Keying a specialization" design section: the key summarizes the pin's *input*, so two uses differing only in a position the clone never reads still key apart. Closing that means keying on the pin's *output* — the finished clone, deduped structurally — which cannot be a lookup, only a build-then-dedupe. The two compose, so nothing here has to be undone to get there.

## Retiring "witness"

The second commit is a vocabulary sweep with no behaviour change. `design/type-inference.md` defined a *witness* as "the term for a refinement in its role as a black box to the subtyping lattice", and the word had spread through the solver, the design docs, and four identifiers.

The distinction does not earn a word. We already have `base` and `refinement`; "the refinement as the lattice sees it" is a fact about the lattice, not a second kind of object. Worse, the word names precisely a **limitation** — that the lattice accumulates refinements and matches them by identity instead of reasoning about what they imply — so having a term for it quietly asserts that the limitation is permanent.

So `witness` → `refinement` throughout (185 occurrences, 26 files), including `join_witnesses` → `join_refinements` and `type_carries_witness` → `type_carries_refinement` (`channelize`), `input_witnesses` → `input_refinements` (`coalesce`), the flag on `types_agree_modulo_unread`, and the `#### Refinements as witness sets` section, which becomes `#### Refinements on the lattice` with an opening sentence that states the opacity as a property of the lattice rather than as the definition of a term.

## Testing

Four end-to-end regression cases for the miscompile plus its controls (a difference in a key-visible position, and identical calls that must still share), two unit tests for the memo's two halves, and unit tests for `SpecKey` itself. Full `./ci.sh` passes.

## A function's kind is part of its identity

`KeyView.fun` is keyed by `KindMerge`, the way `KeyView.history` is keyed by `HistoryKind` and for the same reason: `𝐷 ⇒ 𝑉` and `𝐷 ⤇ 𝑉` are one shape that compiles to different code, so a clone pinned at `⤇` — whose body iterates the domain — must not serve a `⇒` use that never supplies one. A union at one position keeps the two apart rather than letting one shadow the other.

The kind is read through `KindMerge::of`, the same resolved-from-bounds view compaction takes, rather than off the `FunKind` itself. That distinction is the whole of it: an inferred kind is a *variable*, freshly minted per instantiation, so keying on its identity would give every use its own key and retire sharing altogether. Its bounds are the answer, and reading them mid-solve is the bargain every other field in the key already makes — the guarantee is agreement with the pin, not omniscience about the graph.

author: nwadams
body:
## Summary

Review follow-ups from #18655. That PR stopped a single orphaned index entry from aborting the `datahub-documents` embedding run. These changes harden the *same* failure family: a run that finishes **SUCCESS having embedded nothing — or a silent subset**.

## Changes

### Missing scroll payload was warn-only

`scrollAcrossEntities` is nullable and `execute_graphql` only raises when the response carries GraphQL `errors`, so `{"scrollAcrossEntities": null}` arrives as an ordinary response. It was reported as a warning, and warnings don't flip `Pipeline.has_failures()` — enumeration could break completely and the run would still finish SUCCESS.

Now `report.failure` + abort (`DocumentEnumerationError`).

### Systemic hydration failure kept going

When every URN in a hydration batch failed the same way (typically a GraphQL schema mismatch — GMS missing a queried field), the code reported a failure and `continue`d to the next batch. Each later batch then repeated the batch call *plus* a doomed per-URN retry for each of its URNs: O(total URNs) failing GMS requests before the run ended.

It now aborts after the first fully-failed batch, so GMS sees `1 + batch_size` doomed requests instead of one per document in the catalog.

### Full URN catalog materialized before hydrating

`urns = list(self._scroll_document_urns())` held the whole catalog in memory before the first hydrate call. Enumeration and hydration now interleave through `islice` windows: `_fetch_documents_graphql` is a generator, `_hydrate_documents` takes an `Iterable[str]`, and at most one `_HYDRATE_BATCH_SIZE` window is held at a time.

### Truncated scroll page was warn-only

A full page with no `nextScrollId` means enumeration stopped early. The page itself is usable, so its documents are still embedded, but the run now **fails** rather than reporting success over a potentially large silent gap.

### Count mismatch / empty entity list

- Empty `entities` for a non-empty batch is a serving problem, not a batch of orphans → `report.failure` + abort, instead of booking every URN as orphaned.
- Hydration now matches entities by **their own URN** instead of a positional `zip(..., strict=False)`. A short or reordered response can no longer attribute one document's content to a different URN, and unresolved URNs are counted as orphans (`num_documents_skipped_orphaned`) rather than dropped off the end of the zip.

## Behavior change

Conditions that previously produced a warning and a SUCCESS run now produce a FAILURE run. That is the point: an embedding run that silently covers an unknown subset of the catalog is worse than a red run, because the semantic index looks populated while queries return nothing.

## Testing

`147 passed` in `tests/unit/test_datahub_documents_source.py`. New/changed tests:

- `test_missing_scroll_payload_is_fatal` — null scroll payload → failure + raise.
- `test_truncated_scroll_page_fails_the_run` — full page, no cursor → failure, page still yielded.
- `test_systemic_hydration_failure_stops_after_first_batch` — 250 URNs, systemic error → exactly `1 + 100` GMS calls, not O(250).
- `test_empty_entity_response_is_fatal` — empty `entities` → failure, zero orphans booked.
- `test_hydration_matches_entities_by_urn_not_position` — short response attributes content to the right URN, missing URN counted as orphan.
- `test_enumeration_and_hydration_interleave` — regression guard that the first window hydrates before the last scroll page is fetched.
- `test_batch_all_urns_fail_reports_failure` now asserts the raise; `test_stops_when_no_next_scroll_id` uses a partial page (a full page is now the truncation-failure case).

Lint: `ruff format` / `ruff check` / `mypy` clean on both files.

## Checklist

- [x] PR conforms to the Contributing Guideline (PR Title Format)
- [x] Tests added/updated
- [ ] Docs — n/a (no user-facing config; internal embedding job semantics)
- [ ] Breaking changes — none for config/API; see "Behavior change" above

author: rhizonymph
body:
## What

Vendors llama.cpp's tensor-core (MMA) MMQ kernels and routes the 2-D quantized
GEMM behind `ggml_mul_mat_a8` at them. Opt-in via `VLLM_GGUF_MMA_MMQ=1`; default
off, so behaviour is unchanged unless it is set.

Decode (`ggml_mul_mat_vec_a8`), MoE (`ggml_moe_a8`) and dequantization are
untouched. Covers Q4_0/Q4_1/Q5_0/Q5_1/Q8_0/Q2_K/Q3_K/Q4_K/Q5_K/Q6_K on Turing
(sm_75) and newer; everything else falls through to the existing path.

`csrc/gguf/llamacpp/` is llama.cpp `b8892` copied verbatim — `mmq.cuh` needed no
modification, so re-vendoring stays a copy rather than a merge. The plugin-side
code is ~380 lines: a launcher, a runtime shim for the handful of ggml functions
the kernels reference, and per-type template instances.

## Why

`csrc/gguf/mmq.cuh` was copied from llama.cpp `b2899` (April 2024). Its Q4_K
output tile is **4 tokens deep** on NVIDIA, so the kernel re-reads the entire
weight matrix `M/4` times. On an RTX 3090 it measures ~5.7 TFLOP/s *flat* from
M=32 to M=8192 — 8% of peak, and batch-independent, so larger batches cannot
help. Nsight Compute confirms the mechanism: Mem Pipes Busy 95.44%, DRAM 46.63%,
`sm__pipe_tensor_cycles_active` **0%**.

That narrow tile is not a bug upstream. At b2899 it was selected only
`#if defined(CUDA_USE_TENSOR_CORES)`, and was paired with a guard —
`MMQ_MAX_BATCH_SIZE 32` — that sent anything larger to cuBLAS. The tile is
correct *because* of the guard. The port took the tile and not the guard, and
keyed it on `USE_ROCM` instead, so every NVIDIA GPU gets the small-batch kernel
with nothing bounding the batch.

Upstream has since rewritten MMQ around int8 tensor-core MMA
(`mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k32.row.col.s32.s8.s8.s32`) with a tile up to 128 tokens
wide, and removed the cuBLAS fallback on Turing+ because it is no longer needed.
This change adopts that kernel.

## Results

RTX 3090, Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL, real tensors, M=2048:

| tensor | current | this PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ffn_down` 5120x17408 Q4_K | 64.13 ms | **4.94 ms** | **13.0x** |
| `ffn_gate` 17408x5120 Q4_K | 63.83 ms | **4.88 ms** | **13.1x** |
| `ffn_down` 5120x17408 Q5_K | 83.66 ms | **5.17 ms** | **16.2x** |
| `ffn_down` 5120x17408 Q6_K | 85.33 ms | **5.61 ms** | **15.2x** |
| `ssm_out` 5120x6144 Q8_0 | 24.28 ms | **1.78 ms** | **13.7x** |

73.8 TFLOP/s against the current kernel's 5.7. It is faster at **every** M tested
(1 through 2048), so no batch-size threshold is needed.

Accuracy is unchanged in aggregate — relative Frobenius error vs an fp32 ground
truth is 1.29e-2 against the current kernel's 1.30e-2 (Q4_K), identical to three
digits for Q5_K/Q6_K/Q8_0. Both paths quantize activations to int8, so this is
the same numerical regime, not a different one.

## Known issue

`tests/test_kernels.py::test_mmq[12-Q4_K-dtype0-1024-2048]` fails with the kernel
enabled: **1 element in 2,097,152**. The worst-case element is ~9% larger than
the current kernel's (1.125 vs 1.031), which crosses the test's `atol=1.0` at an
index where the reference value is too small for `rtol` to absorb. Consistent
with stream-k's split-K fixup adding a rounding step. Aggregate accuracy is
unaffected. This is part of why the default is off. 191/192 pass with the flag
on; 192/192 with it off.

## Notes for reviewers

- **`use_stream_k` must stay true on Turing+.** With it disabled the tiling path
  degrades as M grows — 60.5 TFLOP/s at M=128 falling to 5.1 at M=2048, i.e.
  slower than the kernel it replaces. It is not an optional tuning knob.
- **The two `ggml-common.h` copies must never meet in one translation unit.**
  `llamacpp/ggml-common.h` and the plugin's own are different vintages defining
  the same block structs; hence the separate TU and the ggml-free `mmq_mma.h`.
- **Verify by import, not by build.** Missing ggml symbols still link — shared
  objects tolerate undefined symbols — and fail at `dlopen`, after which
  `ops.ggml_mul_mat_a8` silently falls back to Triton. `nm -u` should report no
  undefined `ggml_*` symbols.
- torch's `-D__CUDA_NO_HALF_CONVERSIONS__` family is undefined for this
  extension; the vendored kernels assume stock CUDA conversion semantics.
- The kernels are fp32-in/fp32-out, so activations and results stage through
  float buffers (`M*K` and `M*N`). Cheap in time (~0.5 ms of 70 at M=2048) but
  real memory. Templating upstream's `quantize_mmq_q8_1` and `mmq_write_back_*`
  on the element type would remove both; deliberately left for a follow-up.
- Only sm_86 has been exercised. Other Turing+ parts should work but are
  untested, which is the other reason the default is off.

## Relationship to #14

#14 added a batch-size threshold routing large GEMMs to dequantize+cuBLAS. This
kernel is faster than that path (1.3–2.1x at M=2048), needs no threshold, and
avoids materializing bf16 weights — #14 costs 7.8–16.4% of KV cache depending on
`max-num-seqs`, and fails outright at 32 on a hybrid SSM model where decode
sequences also need Mamba cache blocks.

The exception is accuracy. #14 leaves activations in bf16 and is ~7.6x more
accurate (1.7e-3 vs 1.3e-2 relative Frobenius). This PR is still MMQ and
quantizes activations to int8, so it inherits the current kernel's numerics
exactly — status quo, not a regression, but not #14's improvement either.

So: this supersedes #14 on Turing+ for throughput and memory; #14 remains
preferable if accuracy matters more than speed, and is the only option on
pre-Turing NVIDIA and AMD, which have no MMA path at all.

author: mmcdermott
body:
Follow-up to the review note on #89. Pure refactor — no behavior change.

### The duplication

`Strptime.strict`, `Cast.strict`, and `Split.drop_empty` each carried a byte-identical 14-line block doing the same four checks: present, is a node, evaluatable outside a polars context, right type. Every future node taking a constant-valued kwarg would have copied it a fourth time.

```python
# ×3, verbatim
strict_node = self.kwargs.get("strict", None)
if strict_node is None:
    return True
if not isinstance(strict_node, NodeBase):
    raise ValueError("The strict argument must be a NodeBase instance that evaluates to a boolean.")
try:
    val = pl.select(strict_node.polars_expr).item()
except Exception as e:
    raise ValueError("The strict argument must evaluate to a boolean.") from e
if not isinstance(val, bool):
    raise ValueError(f"The strict argument must be a boolean, got {type(val)}")
return val
```

becomes

```python
return self.literal_kwarg("strict", bool, default=True)
```

46 lines of triplicated logic → three one-liners, plus one documented helper.

### The messages are unchanged

`literal_kwarg` generates the same three distinct errors the copies did, parameterized by argument name and type name. **The entire suite passes with no doctest edits** — every existing assertion on those messages still matches verbatim. That was the design constraint, and it's the evidence the refactor is behavior-preserving.

| condition | message |
|---|---|
| not a node | `The strict argument must be a NodeBase instance that evaluates to a boolean.` |
| unevaluatable | `The strict argument must evaluate to a boolean.` |
| wrong type | `The strict argument must be a boolean, got <class 'str'>` |
| absent, no default | `The strict argument is required.` |

### One latent bug fixed

`bool` subclasses `int`, so an int-typed kwarg written with the old pattern would have silently accepted `True` as `1`. The helper rejects that explicitly:

```python
Demo(n=Literal(True)).literal_kwarg("n", int)
# ValueError: The n argument must be a integer, got <class 'bool'>
```

No current call site is int-typed, so this is prophylactic — but it's exactly the kind of thing that would have been copied forward.

### Deliberately left alone

`Strptime.format_str`, `Cast.output_type`, and `RegexExtract.group_index` are superficially similar but have bespoke messages and extra rules (non-negativity, accepting raw `int`s alongside nodes). Folding them in would mean either changing user-facing error text or parameterizing the helper until it saved nothing. Happy to revisit if you'd rather unify the wording across all of them.

### Also

Added a `Key Conventions` line in AGENTS.md so new nodes reach for the helper rather than the copy-paste.

body:
## What
Adds a single, owner-authored developer/creator profile page — name, tagline, bio, and contact links (GitHub, LinkedIn, X, portfolio site, email) — reachable at `#/creator` whether or not a visitor is signed in. This is an app-wide product-owner identity surface, distinct from `settings.js`'s per-user "Name" field (issue #267).

## How
- `src/data/developerProfile.js` — a single exported `DEVELOPER_PROFILE` constant (`name`/`tagline`/`bio`/`links[]`), following `changelog.js`'s "one file, one edit, no rebuild" convention. No `avatarUrl` field — no photo-upload layer exists anywhere in the app, so the page derives initials from `name` instead, same fallback `avatar.js` already uses.
- `src/ui/pages/developerProfile.js` — built entirely on the app's real, currently-shipped v3 glass primitives (`.card`, `.icon-tile`, `.eyebrow`) rather than inventing a bespoke visual system for one page. The issue text originally described a v2 "Modernist" flush-left/square-avatar treatment, which predates v3's full rollout (#431) and is superseded — followed the current binding `design-system.md` instead.
- `main.js` registers `/creator` outside `guardApp`/`lazyGuard` (same treatment as `/shared*`, since it renders static content, not the signed-in user's own store-backed data). It's deliberately **not** folded into the existing `publicRoutes` array — that array also drives the "bounce an already-onboarded user off a public route back to `/app`" redirect on a sign-in transition, and folding `/creator` in there would send a signed-in visitor loading the page directly straight back to `/app`. A dedicated `isCreatorRoute` check opts the route out of both the signed-out redirect-to-`/signin` and the signed-in bounce-to-`/app` paths.
- `src/ui/components/icons.js` gained three real brand-mark icons (`github`/`linkedin`/`x`, `fill: currentColor` per design-system.md §5's brand-mark rule — no stroke) plus two ordinary line icons (`mail`/`globe`, `stroke-2` like the rest of the set).
- Every link is validated before being used as an `href`. `isValidUrl()` (`dom.js`) is intentionally http/https-only for every other resource-URL call site in the app — this page has its own small `isValidProfileLinkUrl()` that adds `mailto:` to the allowed set for the one legitimate email link, without widening the shared helper. A link that fails validation is dropped from the rendered list entirely.
- Discoverability: a new "About the developer" link in the landing page footer (signed-out) and a new item in the sidebar account dropdown next to "My reports" (every signed-in identity, including anonymous guests).

## Testing
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Integration tests — N/A, no store/service contract involved
- [x] E2E tests added/updated
- [x] Manually tested in browser — golden path and edge cases listed below

**Manual test notes:**
Verified locally against `npm run dev`: `/creator` renders correctly signed-out (no redirect) and reachable from the landing footer; sidebar "About the developer" navigates correctly for a signed-in guest. Checked both light and dark theme, and 390px/1440px viewport widths — layout stacks to a single column on mobile, 2-column grid on desktop, all touch targets sized per the app's existing conventions. All 5 links render with `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"`; a link with an invalid URL is dropped rather than rendered unsafely (unit-tested). `npm test` (1498/1498 passing), `npm run lint` (0 errors), `node scripts/lint-icons.mjs` / `lint-theme.mjs` (both clean), and the new Playwright E2E + axe accessibility suites (light + dark) all pass.

## Docs updated

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` (pointer file, no change needed)
- [x] `docs/api.md` (documents the `DEVELOPER_PROFILE` shape)
- [x] `docs/architecture.md` Build Log entry added

## Breaking changes / rollback notes
None. Purely additive — new route, new data file, new page, new icons, two small existing-file additions (landing footer link, sidebar menu item). Reverting this PR requires no manual intervention.

author: joni123467
body:
Sicherheits- und Compliance-Release. Schließt eine offene JSON-Schnittstelle, korrigiert die Pausenprüfung fachlich und macht Compliance-Feststellungen nachvollziehbar statt löschbar.

> **Keine rechtliche Garantie.** Die Umsetzung erfüllt technische Anforderungen, ist nicht zertifiziert und ersetzt keine Rechtsberatung. In Betrieben mit Betriebsrat ist die Einführung nach § 87 Abs. 1 Nr. 6 BetrVG mitbestimmungspflichtig.

## 1. Die JSON-Schnittstelle war offen (Security)

**Neun `/api/*`-Endpunkte hatten keinerlei Prüfung** – weder Anmeldung noch Berechtigung:

| Endpunkt | Was ohne Anmeldung möglich war |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/users` | Stammdaten **aller** Personen auslesen |
| `POST /api/users` | ein Benutzerkonto anlegen |
| `GET`/`POST /api/groups` | Organisationsstruktur lesen/anlegen |
| `GET /api/users/{id}/excel` | **vollständige Arbeitszeit** jeder Person herunterladen |
| `POST /api/time-entries` | beliebiger Person Arbeitszeit unterschieben |
| `DELETE /api/time-entries/{id}` | jede Buchung stornieren – ohne Urheber, ohne Grund |
| `POST /api/vacations` | Urlaub für Dritte beantragen |
| `POST /api/vacations/{id}/status` | jeden Antrag genehmigen |

Der CSRF-Schutz war **keine** Hürde: `GET /api/csrf` liefert Sitzung und Token auch ohne Anmeldung (damit die Offline-App sich vor dem Abgleich ein frisches Token holen kann). Ein Angreifer ging denselben Weg.

Der Excel-Export wiegt am schwersten – vollständige Arbeitszeit einer namentlich genannten Person, ein personenbezogenes Datum nach Art. 4 DSGVO, ohne jede Zugriffskontrolle.

**Jetzt:** drei Helfer (`_api_user`, `_api_require`, `_api_require_scope`) als einziger Weg in die Schnittstelle. Anonym **401** (nicht 403 – der Unterschied gehört in die Antwort), fehlendes Recht **403**, Person außerhalb des Geltungsbereichs **403**. Für die **eigene** Person bleibt alles ohne Sonderrecht möglich. Stornieren verlangt Akteur **und** `?reason=…`, beides in der Revisionshistorie; ohne Begründung 400.

Auch das **Einordnen eines Regelverstoßes** war ungeschützt – die Kenntnis einer `flag_id` genügte, und ein Verstoß verrät Arbeitszeit, Datum und Schweregrad. Jetzt wird der Geltungsbereich von `Time.View` geprüft.

## 2. Pausen wurden je Buchung geprüft (Fachlicher Fehler)

Wer von 8 bis 12 für Kunde A und von 12 bis 17 für Kunde B arbeitete, hatte nach alter Rechnung zwei Buchungen unter sechs Stunden – und damit **keine** Pausenpflicht. Tatsächlich neun Stunden am Stück.

§ 4 ArbZG kennt keine Aufträge. Die Prüfung bildet jetzt die **chronologische Schicht** über alle Kunden, Aufträge und Einsatzorte:

1. Buchungen um gebuchte Pausen bereinigen
2. überlappende und anschließende Intervalle zusammenführen
3. Lücken **unter 15 Minuten** = Arbeitszeit, keine Pause → kein Auftragswechsel täuscht eine Pause vor
4. nur echte Unterbrechungen **ab 15 Minuten** anrechnen
5. Grenzen unverändert: >6 Std → 30 Min, >9 Std → 45 Min

Nachtarbeit über Mitternacht bleibt **eine** Schicht; die Ruhezeitprüfung (§ 5) vergleicht ebenfalls Schichten. Die gespeicherte Arbeitszeit ändert sich **nicht**.

## 3. UTC-Stempel wurden behauptet, aber nicht benutzt

`compliance._entry_bounds()` versprach im eigenen Docstring den UTC-Vorrang und rechnete trotzdem nur mit Ortszeit – über eine Zeitumstellung lag die Ruhezeit um eine Stunde daneben. Jetzt haben `started_at_utc`/`ended_at_utc` Vorrang, Ortszeit ist Rückfallebene für Bestandsbuchungen, und ein naiver Wert aus einer `*_at_utc`-Spalte wird als **UTC** gelesen (hier wäre die Korrektur sonst um den Zonenversatz danebengegangen). Durchgehend zonenbehaftet.

## 4. Pausenereignisse in der Historie

Neu: `break_started`, `break_ended`, `break_corrected`, `break_cancelled` – mit Akteur, Quelle, UTC-Zeitpunkt, Zeitzone und Vorher/Nachher. Korrektur und Storno sind **begründungspflichtig**; eine stornierte Pause wird auf null gesetzt statt gelöscht. Web, Mobil/Offline, Terminalimport und API nutzen denselben Pfad.

## 5. Feststellungen werden fortgeschrieben statt gelöscht

Offene `ComplianceFlag`-Datensätze wurden bei jeder Neuberechnung **physisch gelöscht**. Neuer Lebenszyklus: `detected`, `changed`, `resolved`, `acknowledged`, `reopened`.

**Eine Bestätigung gilt nur für den geprüften Datenstand** – gebunden an eine SHA-256-Prüfsumme. Ändert sich Arbeitszeit, Pause oder Schweregrad, öffnet sich die Feststellung automatisch wieder. Ohne Änderung bleibt die Bestätigung bestehen.

## 6. Kunden sind keine Arbeitgeber

`Company`/`CompanyLocation` sind Kunde und Auftragsort. **Die Prüfung ergab, dass `compliance.py` und `services.py` bereits nirgends darauf zugreifen** – die Trennung hielt. Sie ist jetzt in beiden Modulen und an beiden Modellklassen dokumentiert und durch Tests abgesichert: Feiertagsregion, Sollzeit, Pausen-, Höchstarbeitszeit- und Ruhezeitregeln kommen ausschließlich aus der zentralen Konfiguration.

## Datenbank

**Migration 18** (`_add_compliance_lifecycle`) in **beiden** Mechanismen (`ensure_schema()` + `MIGRATIONS`). Sieben neue Spalten an `compliance_flags`. Idempotent und datenerhaltend: bestätigte Kennzeichnungen behalten ihren Zustand, alle übrigen werden `detected`; die Prüfsumme bleibt zunächst `NULL` und gilt nicht als Änderung. Portables DDL für SQLite/MySQL/MariaDB/PostgreSQL; die Spalten wandern automatisch in logisches Backup und Cross-Database-Restore. Bestehende Migrationen unverändert.

## Offene fachliche Entscheidung

**Wann endet eine Schicht?** Das ArbZG kennt den Begriff nicht – es kennt Ruhepausen (§ 4, max. 45 Min) und Ruhezeit (§ 5, 11 Std). Dazwischen klafft eine Lücke: Ist eine Unterbrechung von vier Stunden eine lange Pause oder das Ende des Arbeitstags?

Diese Umsetzung legt die Grenze bei **sechs Stunden** (`models.SHIFT_BREAK_MINUTES`): Ein geteilter Dienst bleibt eine Schicht mit Pausenpflicht; ab sechs Stunden greift die Ruhezeitprüfung. **Das ist eine Festlegung, keine Gesetzesvorgabe.** Ein niedrigerer Wert erzeugt mehr Ruhezeit- und weniger Pausenwarnungen, ein höherer das Gegenteil. Die Entscheidung gehört in die Mitbestimmung.

## Auswirkungen auf den Betrieb

- **Bestehende API-Integrationen brechen**, wenn sie sich ohne Anmeldung bedient haben. Beabsichtigt.
- `DELETE /api/time-entries/{id}` verlangt `?reason=…`.
- **Mehr Pausenwarnungen**, vor allem bei Arbeit für mehrere Kunden am selben Tag.
- Offline-Aktionen, Terminalimporte, Backup und Restore unverändert.

## Datenschutz

- Kein Logging von Passwörtern, PINs, Tokens – und **keine IP-Adressen** (Art. 5 Abs. 1 lit. c DSGVO).
- Lesende Zugriffe auf fremde Zeitdaten erzeugen einen Eintrag im Zugriffsprotokoll.
- Keine GPS-Ortung, keine Bewegungsprofile – auch nicht neu eingeführt.

## Tests

**593 Tests grün** (`PYTHONPATH=. pytest -q`), davon 42 neue in `tests/test_v0150.py`: anonyme Zugriffe (401), fehlende Rechte und Scope-Umgehung über fremde IDs (403), Storno mit Akteur und Begründung, Protokollierung ohne Geheimnisse; Teilbuchungen ohne echte Pause, Kunden-/Standortwechsel, 14 vs. 15 Minuten, Grenzen 6:00/6:01/9:00/9:01, Nachtschicht; Pausenhistorie inkl. Begründungspflicht; UTC-Vorrang, Bestandsfallback, **beide** Zeitumstellungen in `Europe/Berlin`; erledigte Feststellungen bleiben, Änderung nach Bestätigung öffnet erneut; zwei Kunden = ein Arbeitstag, Feiertag am Kundenstandort wirkt nicht, eigener Feiertag wirkt auch bei Kundenarbeit; Migration 18 registriert, Aufstieg von 0.14.x ohne Datenverlust, doppelte Ausführung unschädlich, neue Spalten im Backup.

## Bekannte Grenzen

- Schichtgrenze von sechs Stunden ist eine Festlegung (siehe oben).
- Ausnahmen nach §§ 7, 10 ArbZG, Tariföffnungen, Bereitschaft kann die Anwendung nicht bewerten.
- Bestandsbuchungen ohne UTC-Stempel werden über die Anlagenzeitzone umgerechnet – eine Annäherung, wenn die Zeitzone seit der Erfassung geändert wurde. Geraten oder umgeschrieben wird nichts.
- Revisionssicherheit endet an der Anwendungsgrenze (direkter DB-/Dateizugriff).

body:
## Meldt feil

En rytter bygde en rundtur (start = slutt, via et mellompunkt) og fikk værkort som så duplisert ut — samme navngitte rutepunkt dukket opp to ganger med bare 32 minutter mellom. Ikke en datafeil: hvert kort hadde et genuint ulikt tidspunkt og temperatur (13°→14°). Det egentlige problemet ligger et hakk før — `loadWeather` samplet alltid nøyaktig 5 punkter ved faste 0/25/50/75/100 %-distansebrøker, uansett hvor lang turen faktisk er. For en ~2-timers rundtur betyr det et sjekkpunkt hvert ~25. minutt, og «nærmeste navngitte rutepunkt innen 15 km»-logikken gjentar naturlig et navn når ruten passerer nær samme sted to ganger — noe en rundtur per definisjon gjør.

## Fiksen

`pickWeatherFractions` skalerer antall sjekkpunkter til omtrent ett per time kjøring, med grense 2–6: en 30-minutters tur får bare start og slutt, ~2t08m-rundturen fra feilrapporten får 3 jevnt fordelte punkter i stedet for 5, en 6-timers dagstur får fortsatt full dekning. Start og slutt er alltid med.

Trukket ut til `src/utils/weatherCheckpoints.ts`, i tråd med hvordan resten av kodebasen holder rute-/værlogikk testbar utenfor `App.tsx`.

## Testing

128 tester grønne (6 nye), typecheck og bygg grønt.

Kunne ikke verifisere selve UI-en lokalt — den offentlige OSRM-demoserveren (brukt for punkt-til-punkt-ruting i dev, siden ingen ORS-nøkkel er satt lokalt) svarte 503 og deretter en ruteberegningsfeil, urelatert til denne endringen og trolig et resultat av dagens omfattende testing mot den. Verifiserer på produksjon mot rundtur-stien (ORS-basert, allerede bevist pålitelig der) etter deploy.
