author: malkreide
body:
## Problem

Beim Verifizieren des Katalog-Modus (PR #173) zeigte ein manueller Lauf `RESEARCH_QUERIES_INCLUDE_CATALOG: false` im Job-Env — obwohl die Repo-Variable `RESEARCH_QUERIES_INCLUDE_CATALOG=1` gesetzt war. Der Katalog-Modus wurde übersprungen (8 statt 24 Abfragen).

**Ursache:** Der Ausdruck nutzte `github.event.inputs.include_catalog`, und `github.event.inputs.*` ist **immer ein String**. Der String `"false"` ist in GitHub-Ausdrücken **truthy** (nicht-leer), also gewann bei jedem manuellen Dispatch der Input-String und **überschattete `vars.RESEARCH_QUERIES_INCLUDE_CATALOG`** — die Variable griff nie.

(Der geplante Montagslauf war nicht betroffen: dort ist der Input leer/`null` → falsy → fällt korrekt auf die Variable durch. Der Bug traf nur den manuellen Pfad und machte die Verifikation unmöglich.)

## Fix

Statt `github.event.inputs.include_catalog` das **typisierte** `inputs.include_catalog` (echter Boolean) verwenden:

```yaml
RESEARCH_QUERIES_INCLUDE_CATALOG: ${{ inputs.include_catalog || vars.RESEARCH_QUERIES_INCLUDE_CATALOG }}
```

Damit komponiert der Ausdruck in allen Fällen korrekt:
- **manuell, Checkbox an** → `true`
- **manuell, Checkbox aus** → `false || vars.X` → Repo-Variable
- **geplant** → `inputs` leer → Repo-Variable

`RESEARCH_QUERIES` (String-Input) ebenfalls auf `inputs.queries` umgestellt (Konsistenz; Verhalten unverändert).

## Verifikation (Branch-Lauf #16, ref = dieser Branch)

```
RESEARCH_QUERIES_INCLUDE_CATALOG: 1
Appended 34 new OpenAlex candidates … from 24 queries (353 filtered as irrelevant)
Appended 1 new Crossref candidates … from 24 queries (336 filtered as irrelevant)
Appended 155 new Semantic Scholar candidates … from 24 queries (52 filtered as irrelevant)
Appended 1 new arXiv candidates … from 24 queries (435 filtered as irrelevant)
Appended 199 new ERIC candidates … from 24 queries (130 filtered as irrelevant)
```

Alle fünf Importer liefen mit 24 Abfragen (8 Config + 16 Katalog); der Relevanzfilter sortierte Off-Scope zuverlässig aus.

## Hinweis

Nur eine Zeile Workflow-Logik (plus Kommentar) — keine Code- oder Teständerung. Neuer Branch frisch von `main` (PR #173 enthalten).

author: mralanlee
body:
Migrates Jellyfin off the Dockge compose stack (Proxmox LXC) onto the k8s cluster, preserving Intel iGPU hardware transcoding, existing TrueNAS NFS media, and the current Jellyfin config.

## What's in this PR (repo side)

- **`charts/intel-device-plugin`** — core-infra chart wrapping `intel-device-plugins-operator` + `intel-device-plugins-gpu` (0.36.0). Advertises `gpu.intel.com/i915` on node `k8s-w-2`; NFD disabled, pinned by node label. Registered in `charts/argocd-apps` (serverSideApply).
- **`charts/jellyfin`** — leaf chart wrapping the official `jellyfin/jellyfin` 3.2.0 (mirrors the `charts/paperless` pattern):
  - GPU: pod requests `gpu.intel.com/i915: 1` → scheduler auto-pins to the GPU node.
  - `securityContext`: runAsUser/Group 1000, fsGroup 1000, `supplementalGroups: [44, 104]`.
  - Storage: config on `truenas-iscsi` PVC (RWO), cache as emptyDir, 3 **direct NFS** media mounts (`/movies` RW, `/series` RO, `/private` RW) — existing TrueNAS exports reused, no reprovisioning.
  - Ingress: Gateway API HTTPRoute at `jellyfin.k8s.shimmerlabs.xyz`. DLNA dropped.
- **Runbooks** — `docs/runbooks/jellyfin-gpu-passthrough.md` (Proxmox VFIO iGPU → `k8s-w-2`) and `docs/runbooks/jellyfin-config-migration.md` (seed config PVC from Dockge).
- Design spec + implementation plan under `docs/superpowers/`.

## Operator action required before/after merge (not in this PR)

1. **Proxmox passthrough** (runbook): VFIO the iGPU to `k8s-w-2`, then record the real render GID (`stat -c '%g' /dev/dri/renderD128`) and update `supplementalGroups` if it isn't `104`.
2. **Fill placeholders** in `charts/jellyfin/values.yaml`: `<NFS_SERVER>` + the three `<EXPORT_*>` paths (TrueNAS address isn't in-repo).
3. **Seed config PVC** (runbook), then repoint Infuse to the new URL.

## Validation

`helm lint` + `helm template` pass for `intel-device-plugin`, `jellyfin`, and `argocd-apps`. Rendered Service/Deployment name is `jellyfin` (subchart fullname dedup); HTTPRoute backendRef and runbooks use it correctly.

body:
## What

The Auftragskorb backend for the Werkbank (stage W1): a `work_items` table plus an admin API, so the admin can file a structured optimization task instead of screenshotting a bad glyph and describing it in prose — and a working session can read the basket, work it off and mark each item done.

- **Table `work_items`** (migration `0020`, additive, nothing seeded): one row per marked element. `kind` names the level (`letter` | `pair` | `word`), `glyph_key` / `left_key` + `right_key` / `word` name the element, `specimen_kind` + `specimen_id` name the words.json sample the issue was seen in (same id-namespace semantics as `pair_instances`), `note` carries the observation. `status` runs `open` → `done`, `resolution` holds the session's completion note (what changed, PR reference). Plain autoincrement rows — no unique constraint: two notes on the same letter are two observations, not one overwritten row.
- **Endpoints** `GET/POST /sources/{id}/work-items` + `PATCH/DELETE /sources/{id}/work-items/{item_id}`. `GET ?status=open` is the round's queue, `?status=done` the archive; `POST` returns the stored row incl. its `id` (the handle the closing PATCH needs); `PATCH` is partial (`exclude_unset` — an omitted note is not an empty note); `DELETE` is for a misfiling, a worked item is closed with `done` so the archive stays readable.

## Why

Per the hand-model/Werkbank plan (`docs/proposals/handmodell-stufenplan.md`), the optimization rounds are bottlenecked on how a finding travels from the admin's eye to a working session. W1 makes that channel structured and durable: the finding names its own target, so a session can act on the row alone, and the closed rows document what was done.

## Notes on design

- **Every route is admin-gated**, including the list — unlike the occurrence reads, these are internal work notes, not measurement derived from PD specimens and not public content.
- **Validation in two layers**, mirroring the occurrence writes: the schema rejects an unworkable target (a letter item without its `glyph_key`, a pair missing a side, a word without text or specimen), the router rejects glyph keys that are not registry glyphs (`core.shaping.is_registry_glyph_key`) — a typo'd key would file fine but point at nothing.
- Model, migration, repository, schemas, router and tests follow the occurrence layer (#250) file-by-file.
- Nothing here touches rendering; the composer path is untouched.

## Verification

- `uv run --extra test pytest` — 465 passed, 17 skipped (incl. the new `tests/test_api_work_items.py`: create+list per kind, status filter, partial PATCH closing an item, delete, all-routes-401, and the 422 battery for unworkable targets / unknown keys / an unknown status filter).
- `uv run --extra dev ruff check .` + `ruff format --check .` — clean.
- Migrations against a throwaway local Postgres (never the shared Cloud SQL DB): `alembic upgrade head` through `0020`, `alembic check` → "No new upgrade operations detected.", `downgrade -1` → `upgrade head` roundtrip, `alembic check` clean again.
- `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `[Unreleased]/Added`; `CLAUDE.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` kept in sync (router enumeration, migration map, tables list).

author: jceddy
body:
## Summary

Adds a final "Announce deploy on Discord" step to both `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (production) and `.github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml` (dev), so a deploy that lands posts a message to a shared Discord channel using the app's own existing bot token — the same bot already used for per-user DM notifications (`DiscordNotificationChannel.php`), just posting straight to a fixed channel this time instead of opening a DM.

- Posts **after** the migration + health-check steps both succeed (implicit `success()` in the step's own `if:`), so a broken deploy is never announced as if it worked.
- Message includes the deployed `VERSION`, the environment's own `SITE_URL`, and the commit subjects (`--no-merges`, capped at 15 with a "…and N more" tail) introduced since the previous deploy on that branch — diffed via `github.event.before..github.sha`, which needed switching `actions/checkout` to `fetch-depth: 0` (full history) in both workflows.
- Both environments post into the **same** shared channel (production's `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`, dev's own `DEV_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` — two separate Discord Applications per the existing `DEV_`-prefix convention, both needing to be members of that one channel).
- Entirely opt-in: the step no-ops (not fails) unless a new `DISCORD_ANNOUNCE_CHANNEL_ID` repo variable is set — documented in the root `README.md`'s "Deployment" section, including the "invite the bot to the channel" step that's easy to miss since the existing OAuth2 scopes for account linking don't add the bot to any server on their own.

No app code changes — this is entirely GitHub Actions workflow YAML plus README docs.

## Test plan

- [x] Validated both workflow files parse as valid YAML
- [x] Unit-tested the shell logic in isolation (commit-list truncation at 15 lines, the "no new commits" fallback, and the final Discord JSON payload via `jq`) outside the workflow, since the real `github.event.before`/`github.sha` values only exist in an actual Actions run
- [ ] Not yet exercised end-to-end against real Discord (needs `DISCORD_ANNOUNCE_CHANNEL_ID` set as a repo variable, and both bots invited to that channel with Send Messages permission — first real deploy after this merges will be the first live test)

author: dkaliakin
body:
## Summary

Adds a complete set of worked examples to the repository, introduces an energy-only density-assembly route that makes large single-point calculations tractable, and documents both. 27 commits.

The examples cover the three things a new user needs: how to describe their own HPC site, what a geometry optimization looks like end to end under three different solver strategies, and what the workflow does at production scale on a real protein. The Trp-cage material doubles as a regression benchmark against published results.

## What is included

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `Examples/Geometry_Optimization/` | Acetone optimized three ways — EWF-(FCI,SCI), EWF-(FCI,SQD), unfragmented SCI — 3,068 files, 0.45 GB |
| `Examples/Trp-cage_Single_Point/JCTC_2026/` | Published EWF-(FCI,SQD) and EWF-CCSD reference data — 8,806 files, 3.34 GB |
| `Examples/Trp-cage_Single_Point/Latest_Implementation/` | Both conformers re-run with the current code — 35,372 files, 2.92 GB |
| `Examples/HPC_Settings/` | Two real cluster definitions (CCF, MSU) plus three Slurm submission templates |
| `Source/` | New `cluster_energy` assembly route; HPC-preset fallback; stale folder references removed |
| Documentation | Three README files, two comparison figures, corrected links throughout |

## Code changes

`Source/EWF-CI_Geom_Opt_HPC.py` (+189) adds the **`cluster_energy`** assembly route: an energy-only fast path that sums per-fragment energies instead of assembling a global density matrix, which is what makes a 303-fragment single point practical. A new `resolve_assembly_for_task()` makes it the default for `run_task: energy` and raises a hard error if it is requested for `geomopt` or `gradient`, since no gradient can be taken from it. Explicit user choices are preserved — the resolver tracks whether `ewf.assembly` was set deliberately rather than defaulted.

`Source/calculation_setup.py` (+74) fixes the shipped-preset fallback, which broke when the HPC settings files moved out of `Source/`. It now resolves `Examples/HPC_Settings/` and, when it falls back, warns that the run is being configured from another site's definition — a config generated from a preset looks complete but fails at submission time, so the warning names the directory searched, the presets found, and what to review.

Small cleanups to `embedding_lagrangian.py`, `sqd_solver.py`, `sqd_quantum_sampling.py`, and `zigzag_layout.py` remove documentation references to folders that no longer exist. `.gitignore` gains `Trp-Cage_Comparison/` and `.snakemake/`.

## Scientific result

The Trp-cage comparison is the substantive outcome. The published calculations used the CPU SBD eigensolver, which was slow enough to force a loose Davidson convergence threshold. The GPU-accelerated diagonalizer allows a much tighter threshold, so each cluster converges lower and closer to its CCSD reference — most visibly for clusters above roughly 28 orbitals.

| Method | ΔE (unfolded − folded) | Error vs reference |
|---|---|---|
| DLPNO-CCSD, unfragmented (reference) | 52.05 kcal/mol | — |
| EWF-(FCI,SQD), published | 55.43 kcal/mol | +3.38 |
| EWF-(FCI,SQD), this branch | 52.89 kcal/mol | +0.84 |

The error against the unfragmented reference falls fourfold, bringing the fragmented calculation within 1 kcal/mol. Per-cluster curves for both conformers are in `Examples/Trp-cage_Single_Point/README.md`, with the reasoning behind the improvement.

Reference: [*J. Chem. Theory Comput.* **2026**, *22* (12), 6041–6056](https://pubs.acs.org/jctcce/article/22/12/6041/5166449/Molecular-Quantum-Computations-on-a-Protein)

author: rapunzlnflt-afk
body:
## Summary

Adds a per-family-member **Profile** tab, placed directly after Dashboard in the sidebar (`IdCard` icon, route `#/profile`).

**Personal details** — profile photo, DOB with calculated age, blood type, height, allergies, conditions, and a primary care physician picker populated from that patient's existing Physicians. Weight is deliberately not duplicated here; it stays in Vitals.

**Insurance card** — front/back card photos that open full-screen with a fit ⇄ zoom toggle, plus structured plan fields (carrier, plan type, member ID, group number, policy holder, effective date, RxBIN/RxPCN/RxGroup) and a member services phone rendered as a `tel:` link matching the app's existing pattern.

All new `Patient` fields are optional, so records created before this tab keep working untouched. **No Dexie version bump** — only plain, non-indexed fields were added, so the existing schema handles them as-is.

### Image downscaling

Every attachment is inlined as a base64 data URL into the Dexie record and, in turn, into every "Save My Data" backup. A raw phone photo is ~4 MB, which becomes ~5.3 MB of base64.

New `client/src/lib/image.ts` downscales to ~1600px on the long edge and re-encodes as JPEG (q0.8) before storage. It uses `createImageBitmap(..., { imageOrientation: "from-image" })` so EXIF-rotated phone photos aren't stored sideways, fills white before drawing so transparent PNGs don't come out black, and passes PDFs through untouched. Undecodable files (HEIC, corrupt) throw a user-facing message shown inline rather than crashing.

This is also **retrofitted into the existing medical-records uploader**, which previously stored raw multi-megabyte photos.

Measured: a 3024×4032 source photo stores as 1200×1600 / **81 KB**, with the member ID still legible when zoomed. A full backup carrying two card images is 218 KB.

### Backup compatibility

`exportAllData()` bumped **v3 → v4**. `importAllData()` needed no changes — it destructures `const { id, ...rest }` and spreads field-for-field, so new optional fields round-trip automatically and older backups import cleanly. Verified with a hand-crafted v3 file.

### Unrelated fix included

`defaultReminderSoundPreferences` in `client/src/lib/db.ts` had a stale `enabled: 0` key instead of `appointmentsEnabled` / `medicationsEnabled` / `vitalsEnabled`, which made `npm run check` fail on `main` before this branch. Fixed so typecheck passes clean. Runtime behavior is identical — both `undefined !== 1` and `0 !== 1` mean sounds off.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run check` — clean
- [x] `npm run build` — clean
- [x] Interactive Playwright run at 375×812 mobile viewport, 38 assertions, all passing:
  - Nav routes to `/profile`; personal details save, title-case the name, and show calculated age
  - Card photos upload, downscale to 1200×1600 / 81 KB, and persist across reload
  - Full-screen viewer fits the viewport (341px) and zoom enlarges to 785px
  - Member services renders as `tel:5551234567`, auto-formatted to `(555) 123-4567`
  - Backup exports at version 4 carrying all new fields + card images, and re-imports them
  - Legacy v3 backup imports cleanly and its patient shows the empty profile state without crashing
  - A fake HEIC shows the inline error and the app stays alive
  - Medical-records uploader now downscales; PDFs still pass through un-converted
  - Zero horizontal overflow at 8 distinct states on mobile, and at 1280px desktop
  - Dark mode verified on the profile view, the full-screen viewer, and the edit dialogs

No network calls, no new dependencies.

## Deliberately left out

- **No rotate control** in the full-screen viewer — EXIF orientation is already applied at upload time, so it would be dead weight for the common case.
- **Zoom is an explicit toggle**, not pinch — native pinch-zoom inside a fixed-position Radix dialog is unreliable on phones.
- **`FieldSection` is duplicated** with `EcFieldSection` in `emergency-contacts.tsx`. The repo's convention is per-page presentational helpers, and consolidating would mean refactoring an unrelated file.
- **No Dexie version bump**, per the note that adding plain fields doesn't require one.

Fixes #60 (commented there before starting, per CONTRIBUTING.md).

## What changed

1. **`moon_cli.py`**: added `--version` via `argparse`'s built-in `action="version"`, importing the existing `VERSION` constant from `moon_download.py` (no second copy). Since `action="version"` short-circuits before argparse's required-argument check, it works without `--urls`/`--output`.
2. **`moon_download.py`**: `Telemetry._save_cli` now includes `VERSION` in its log header and as a `"version"` field in its JSON report (previously had neither). `_save_engine`'s log header already had it; added the matching `"version"` field to its JSON report for parity.
3. **`docs/CLI.md`**: documented the new flag in the arguments table.

One version constant (`moon_download.py:23`), imported everywhere it's used — no circular-import issue since `moon_cli.py` already imports from `moon_download`.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/ -q` — 11 passed.
- `python moon_cli.py --version` → prints `v2.0`, exit 0, with and without other args.
- `python moon_cli.py` (no args) → still correctly errors requiring `--urls`/`--output`, exit 2 (no regression).
- Direct smoke test of `Telemetry.save()` for both `flavor="cli"` and `flavor="engine"`, confirming the generated `.log` header and `.json` field actually contain the version (not just eyeballing the diff):
  ```
  CLI json version field: v2.0
  CLI log header line: MOONTECH CLI v2.0  --  PERFORMANCE LOG
  Engine json version field: v2.0
  Engine log header line: MOONTECH v2.0  —  PERFORMANCE LOG
  ```

All acceptance criteria from the issue are met.

Implemented with Claude Code (Claude Sonnet). Scope: the three files above only; no changes to extraction, download, or GUI logic.

author: dpmills
body:
The constraint solver relates type variables in exactly one way: subtyping. `α <: β` is the only fact it can record. That is enough whenever a rule's result type *is* one of its input types — `max(xs)` returns an element, `x.f` returns the field — because "is one of" is expressible as sharing a lattice position.

It is not enough for a rule whose result is **computed from** its inputs. Addition is the smallest example: the result of `a + b` is neither operand.

## What went wrong without it

The encoding available was to share a variable: `∀α. α → α → α`. A variable carries every lattice dimension, so this states far more than intended, and it is wrong in both directions at once.

| Program | Inferred | Should be |
|---|---|---|
| `\x -> x + 1` | `{Int \| __elem == 1} ⇒ Int` | polymorphic in `x` |
| `y = 1; z = 1; y + z` | `{Int \| __elem == 1}` | `Int` |
| `1 > "a"` | `Bool`, then panics in the interpreter | rejected |

The first two are the two polarities of one mistake. Operand occurrences are *domains* — negative positions, where refinement sets **union** — so one operand's refinement becomes a requirement on the other. The result occurrence is positive, where refinement sets **intersect**, so a refinement both operands carry survives onto the result. The second row needs two operands carrying the *same* refinement (intersecting a set with itself returns it), which is why it stayed hidden.

## The mechanism

`Type::App { fun: TypeFn, args }` is the type "whatever `fun` computes from `args`" — `1 + x` types as `Add({Int | __elem == 1}, α)`.

An `App` **denotes** a type rather than constructing one: `Add(Int, Int)` *is* `Int`, written in a form that does not yet know it. It adds no inhabitants and no subtyping edges to the lattice, so reduction is *normalization*, and it is transient in the same sense as `Infer` — every `Type` that escapes inference is `App`-free.

Reduction is **demand-driven**: materializing an `App` resolves each argument through the ordinary pipeline and applies the rule. Nothing is deposited, so no phase ordering can make the answer wrong. A rule is a pure function of resolved argument types — no inference context, no access to the bound graph — which is also what leaves room for user-declared type schemas on UDFs later.

Four laws make a rule sound: pure, monotone in the subtype order, **declares a `CycleTolerance`**, and normalizing. They are stated in `src/ccl/infer/solver/reduce.rs` with what each buys inference, and summarized in `src/ccl/design/type-inference.md`, "4.7 Type functions".

### A cycle is a recurrence in the program, and a rule says whether it can answer through one

An argument arrives cyclic when resolving it would re-enter the resolution already computing it, which is what a self-read is: `x += 1` makes `value(x) = join(seed, Add(value(x), 1))`, a fixpoint equation, because an accumulator *is* one. Measured: 1,910 cyclic arguments across the suite, and adding a self-read is exactly what creates them.

So `Option<Type>` is `Arg::Known(_) | Arg::Cyclic` — the distinction a rule must reason about is not "absent" but *cyclic*, and there is no later point at which more is known. `TypeFn::cycle_tolerance()` declares `Any` or `AllKnown` and `reduce` enforces it centrally, so a rule that cannot answer cannot forget to say so. It is deliberately **not** per-position: every rule's condition is about *how many* arguments are cyclic rather than which.

Both of today's rules are `Any`, for reasons worth keeping apart — a comparison is constant on its domain so a cyclic operand costs nothing, while arithmetic loses the agreement check but keeps a usable type, which is what lets an accumulator have one.

### The cut is an unrolling, not an iteration

Traced, one materialization of `x := 0; x := x + 1; x` reduces `Add(⟨cyclic⟩, 1) → Int` and then `Add(Int, 1) → Int`, and stops; `x + x` reaches three levels because each operand re-enters separately. The depth is fixed by the shape of the program, never by an iteration count, and in every shape measured the outermost frame — the one whose answer becomes the node's type — sees every argument known.

The consequence is the opposite of the familiar one. Because nothing iterates, whatever a rule answers at a cut is **what the unrolling carries**; there is no later pass that widens it. A rule must already be sound at the cut, not merely improvable. Both current rules are, for free: arithmetic drops to the shared base — the top of the chain the missing operand could have contributed to — and comparison is constant on its domain. A sharper rule that kept what it could see would return whatever a bounded unrolling happened to reach, sound only by accident of how far the program unrolled.

## The operand requirement lives in the result rule

An operator's operands are two **unrelated** scheme variables. Nothing relates them, and nothing needs to: what checks them is the rule that reduces the result.

That works because of one property, which is silent when violated and so is recorded where schemes are defined: **a scheme that wants its operands checked must mention them in its result.** A rule runs when something materializes the application it belongs to, and an application is materialized only when some node's type reaches it. A scheme's operand variables are nobody's node type — a use records `left <: α` and `right <: β`, so `α` and `β` are reachable *from* the operands, but nothing walks *from* them. The only thing that can reach them is the result.

So `1 + "a"` is rejected because the addition's result is `Add(α, β)`; materializing the node runs the rule and finds the conflict. A comparison declaring a bare `Bool` mentions neither operand, so nothing ever materializes them, the rule never runs, and `1 > "a"` types cleanly and then panics. A comparison's result is therefore `Compare(kind, α, β)`, reducing to `Bool` for operands that share a base and to an error for those that do not.

### What that costs

`\x -> x + 1` no longer infers `x : Int`. Its result still resolves — the rule answers from the literal operand — but the parameter is determined by nothing.

That is the honest answer rather than a regression. The lambda works for any two things `+` accepts, so it is polymorphic in its parameter, and `Type` has no `∀` to say so. As a program value it is an **ambiguous program**, rejected downstream exactly as `\x -> [x, x]` already was. Inferring `Int` read as precision; it was a single-numeric-type lattice showing through, and it would have become wrong the moment `Int + Float → Float` existed.

An earlier revision of this branch bought that inference back with a self-referential bound on the scheme's own variables (`α <: CommonBase(α, β)`), so that resolving one operand pulled the other's base. It is gone: redundant as a guard, wrong as a claim about what makes two values addable, and — as a pull — compensating for two defects elsewhere that are fixed below it. `src/ccl/design/type-inference.md`, "Why not a bound on the operand variables" records the argument so it is not re-added.

## Obligations that are not decidable yet are parked

`constrain_go` cannot compare an unreduced `App` against anything: reduction resolves the arguments off the bound graph, and emission runs while that graph is still being built, so an answer read there could be superseded by the next edge.

The obligation is therefore **parked** rather than dropped. `constrain_go` records it with the in-flight substitutions applied, `require_sub` tags it with the node to blame, and `InferCtx::check_parked_obligations` retries it between emission and coalesce — the point at which every edge the program implies exists. Only fully-determined obligations are checked, which keeps the retry from perturbing the graph it reads: a side still holding a variable is one the program never determined, and coalesce reports that as `UnresolvedInfer`.

This is what makes `(1 + 2) and True` and `sum(["a" + "b"])` ordinary d

author: effortlesssteven
body:
## Claim

After this lands, `__CLASS__` emits a `PL900` **Warning** unless the file both declares Perl v5.40+ **and** has the `class` feature lexically enabled — the only combination that actually compiles. The message names the construct, the v5.40 minimum, and the declared version; the remediation names whichever requirement is missing.

## Controlling issue

Relates to #5279 — remaining scope after lexer/parser support landed in PR #5280. Parent issue #5279 stays open for follow-up.

## Governing contract

Parity with the existing version-compat lint pattern: each version-gated construct gets one match arm in `check_version_compat` that calls `make_diagnostic_with_details` and emits a structured Warning. Same shape as `class {}` (v5.38), `try/catch` (v5.34), `say` (v5.10), `defer` (v5.36).

## Changed production path

`check_version_compat` in `crates/perl-lsp-rs-core/src/providers/diagnostics/lints/version_compat.rs`, called by the diagnostics provider for every open document. A new match arm fires when the AST walker visits a node named `"__CLASS__"` (`NodeKind::FunctionCall` or `NodeKind::Identifier`).

## Gate: two independent requirements

```rust
let version_ok = declared_version >= PerlVersion::new(5, 40);
let feature_ok = pragma_state.has_feature("class");
if !version_ok || !feature_ok { /* emit */ }
```

Compiling `__CLASS__` needs **both**, and neither implies the other:

1. **declared version >= v5.40.** The `class` feature shipped in v5.38, but the `__CLASS__` keyword did not arrive until v5.40 — see [perl5400delta](https://perldoc.perl.org/perl5400delta): "code inside a method, `ADJUST` block or field initializer expression is now permitted to use the new `__CLASS__` keyword." So `use feature 'class'` cannot backport it to v5.38/v5.39.
2. **`class` lexically enabled.** `class` is still experimental, so it is in *no* version bundle — `:5.40` included. The repository already encodes this: `BUNDLE_5_40_FEATURES` (`crates/perl-pragma/src/version.rs:213`) omits `class`, matching [perldoc feature](https://perldoc.perl.org/feature). `use v5.40;` alone leaves `__CLASS__` a bareword, rejected under `strict subs`.

Gating on either alone is a false negative. Both were found and fixed during review:

| Source | Compiles? | Original (feature-gated) | `ffcc01c` (version-only) | Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `use v5.36;` | ✗ | warns, misleading fix | warns | warns |
| `use v5.36; use feature 'class';` | ✗ | **silent** | warns | warns |
| `use v5.40;` | ✗ | **silent** | **silent** | warns |
| `use v5.40; use feature 'class';` | ✓ | silent | silent | silent |
| no declared version | — | silent | silent | silent (early return) |

## User-visible output

Message (all cases): `'__CLASS__' requires Perl v5.40+; declared version is vX.Y` — names the construct, the minimum, and what the file actually declares.

Remediation, per missing half — following it always produces compiling code:

```
use v5.36;                      → Update 'use v5.36' to 'use v5.40' and add
                                  'use feature "class";' — __CLASS__ requires both
use v5.36; use feature 'class'; → Update 'use v5.36' to 'use v5.40' —
                                  'use feature "class";' does not provide
                                  __CLASS__ before v5.40
use v5.40;                      → Add 'use feature "class";' — 'use v5.40' does not
                                  enable the experimental 'class' feature
```

The v5.40 case deliberately avoids degenerate "Update 'use v5.40' to 'use v5.40'" advice, and the pragma is never offered as an *alternative* to the version bump. Both are pinned by negative assertions.

## Suppression parity

No new mechanism. The arm emits `DiagnosticCode::VersionIncompatFeature` (`PL900`) through the same `make_diagnostic_with_details` path as every other version-compat construct, so whatever suppression applies to PL900 applies here unchanged. `PL900` is already registered in the `perl-diagnostics` catalog (`codes/metadata.rs`, incl. explanation + docs URL); no new code was added, so no catalog entry was needed. `cargo test -p perl-diagnostics --all-targets` passes, including the code/catalog completeness guards.

## Proof (on `5e712ae`)

```
cargo fmt -p perl-lsp-rs-core -- --check                        # clean
cargo clippy -p perl-lsp-rs-core --lib --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo test -p perl-lsp-rs-core --lib --locked version_compat    # 20 passed, 0 failed
cargo test -p perl-lsp-rs-core --lib --locked                   # 2820 passed, 0 failed
cargo test -p perl-diagnostics --all-targets --locked           # all green
cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked                  # compiles
```

Tests covering the `__CLASS__` arm — one per row of the table above, so a regression identifies which requirement broke:

- `class_token_without_class_feature_emits_pl900` — exactly one PL900 per occurrence; Warning; message names `__CLASS__`, `v5.40`, and the declared `v5.36`.
- `class_token_with_explicit_class_feature_still_emits_pl900_below_v5_40` — the pragma does not backport the keyword.
- `class_token_on_v5_40_without_class_feature_emits_pl900` — the bundle does not enable the feature; also asserts the remediation is not a no-op.
- `class_token_on_v5_40_with_class_feature_suppresses_pl900` — the only compiling shape is silent.
- `class_token_suggestion_never_offers_the_pragma_as_an_alternative` — asserts on `Diagnostic::suggestion`, the field the author acts on.
- `class_token_without_declared_version_no_pl900` — undeclared version stays silent.

## Test hardening notes

Two tests asserted false negatives and were **inverted or split, never deleted**:

- `class_token_with_explicit_class_feature_suppresses_pl900` → inverted to `…still_emits_pl900_below_v5_40`.
- `class_token_on_v5_40_suppresses_pl900` → split into the `…without_class_feature_emits_pl900` / `…with_class_feature_suppresses_pl900` pair.

A `message.contains("v5.40")` assertion is vacuous for remediation, because `message` always reads `'__CLASS__' requires Perl v5.40+; declared version is vX.Y` regardless of the suggestion. The suggestion test reads `suggestion` instead.

Mutation-checked: flipping the minimum from v5.40 to v5.38 fails `class_token_without_class_feature_emits_pl900` and `class_token_with_explicit_class_feature_still_emits_pl900_below_v5_40`, confirming the version threshold is actually pinned.

## Review history

Both false negatives were found by review, not by the original author:

- [gemini-code-assist](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/perl-lsp-swarm/pull/5430#discussion_r3693178660) / [chatgpt-codex-connector](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/perl-lsp-swarm/pull/5430#discussion_r3695940691) — the pragma was offered as a fix that does not fix; led to `ffcc01c`.
- [factory-droid](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/perl-lsp-swarm/pull/5430#discussion_r3696024122) — `use v5.40;` alone was wrongly suppressed; led to `5e712ae`.

## Claim boundary

**Proven:** `__CLASS__` emits a structured PL900 Warning through the standard lint path in every source shape that does not compile on the declared Perl, and is silent in the one that does.

**Out of scope:**
- Scoping the diagnostic to `class` method bodies only (the parser accepts `__CLASS__` anywhere; a false positive in non-class context is a parser-level gap).
- Resolving `__CLASS__` to the runtime class name.
- The pre-existing `class` arm false positive on `use v5.38` — same defect shape, found while finishing this PR, filed at [#5279 (comment)](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/perl-lsp-swarm/issues/5279#issuecomment-5152246128).

## Non-goals

- Runtime class-name resolution or completion.
- Constraining `__CLASS__` to class-body scope.
- Changing the `class {}` v5.38 gate.

## Risk and rollback

**Risk:** Low. Single file, lint-only path, no protocol or parser changes. The arm is only reached when `__CLASS__` appears in the AST, which requires the lexer keyword from #5280 (merged)

author: aytey
body:
#680 added `isqrt64` to seed the ground-path collapse's backward hint chain. Its Newton seed `(n + 1) / 2` overflows to zero at `n == UINT64_MAX`, and the next iteration then divides by it.

`hintBackStep` calls it for a `(bvmul t t)` step of width 64, so any chain whose back-propagated target is all-ones takes a SIGFPE inside `RemoveUnconstrained`. That needs nothing but plain QF_BV — no floating point, no arrays — and crashes master today, 2.4.0 included:

```smt2
(set-logic QF_BV)
(declare-fun x () (_ BitVec 64))
(assert (= (bvmul (bvlshr x #x0000000000000001) (bvlshr x #x0000000000000001)) #xffffffffffffffff))
(check-sat)
```

```
$ stp --SMTLIB2 crash.smt2 ; echo $?
136
```

(136 is a hardware trap, so there is no assertion text.)

Fixed here by seeding with `n / 2 + (n & 1)`: the same `ceil(n/2)` without the overflow. Every smaller `n` keeps the seed it had, so no existing result — or the CNF built from it — moves, and `UINT64_MAX` now returns the exact root `2^32 - 1`. Checked against the old function over ~11M inputs.

Two regression tests, both SIGFPE without the fix: a unit test that back-propagates all-ones through a width-64 square and checks the recovered root is really used, and `unconstrained-ground-path3.smt2`.

Found by a murxla campaign that was fuzzing a downstream floating-point branch; the trace was FP-heavy but minimises to this bit-vector core, and the crashing code is FP-free.

author: krystophny
body:
Fixes #2943.

## Problem
The source-character rejection rule from #2929 rejected the first byte of a UTF-8 BOM (`Invalid character 0xEF at line 1, column 1`). gfortran accepts BOM-prefixed sources (its own `gfortran.dg/bom_*.f90` tests), and so did fortfront before that wave. Blocks ffc PR #545.

## Fix
New leaf module `src/lexer/source_bom.f90` with `decode_source_bom`: strips a UTF-8 BOM, decodes UTF-16/UTF-32 BOM-prefixed ASCII payloads, returns anything else unchanged. It is applied in `validate_source_characters` and both `tokenize_core_safe*` entry points; `decode_bom_if_needed` in the transformation pipeline now delegates to it instead of keeping a second copy.

## Preserved invariant
Only a *leading* BOM is consumed. Bytes that are not part of one are still rejected: negative controls in the new test cover a stray 0xEF mid-line and a bare NUL in a BOM-less source.

## Evidence
Red (unmodified main): `test_issue_2943_bom_source` FAIL — `FAIL: utf8_bom_example.f90 rejected / Invalid character 0xEF at line 1, column 1`.
Green: `fo test test_issue_2943_bom_source` PASS; full `fo` pipeline green (483 tests, lint OK, fmt OK).

Corpus gate:
- `make check-rejection-gate` (examples, 784 files): OK, zero newly rejected; `examples/f90/utf8_bom_example.f90` REJECTED -> ACCEPTED (baseline fixture updated).
- Full gfortran.dg (7857 files) against a probe built at origin/main: OK, zero newly rejected, accepted 7522 -> 7527. Newly accepted: bom_UTF-8.f90, bom_UTF-8_F.F90, bom_UTF16-BE.f90, bom_UTF16-LE.f90, bom_UTF-32.f90 — all accepted by `gfortran -fsyntax-only`.

author: remote55
body:
The supervisor read the site and replied that it is written in GenAI language, as though nobody had edited it, and asked to be walked through what each section is trying to say. She quoted two sentences back, and about one of them asked a sharper question:

> "อะไรที่ freeze และบอกข้อจำกัดได้ทุกขั้นเลยหรอคะ"
> *(What exactly is frozen, and can you really state the limitation at every step?)*

**She was right, and the second question found a real overclaim.** The demo header said the page states its limits at every step. It does not — there are limitations recorded for three validation sets and several stages with no validation at all.

Reading the code found worse: design rationale shipped as body copy, and a note to whoever wrote the code rendered to visitors.

| Was on the page | What it actually was |
|---|---|
| "หนึ่ง narrative ต่อเนื่อง…**แทนการแยก feature เป็นการ์ดที่ดูมีน้ำหนักเท่ากัน**" | why the layout is a list instead of cards |
| "Measured evidence / **do not round**" | an instruction to the developer |
| "Field observation / 01" | a decorative label naming nothing |

## The approach

Each section is renamed to the question a reader actually has. A section called **วัดยังไง** cannot be filled with layout rationale — it can only be filled with how it measures.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `01 / Problem` — ปัญหาที่การวัดแบบเดิมทิ้งไว้ | **ทำไมต้องวัดใหม่** |
| `02 / Measurement journey` — เส้นทางการวัดจากจุดสู่คาร์บอน | **วัดยังไง** |
| `03 / Inspect the structure` — หลักฐาน 3D ที่เปิดให้ตรวจสอบ | **ขอดูของจริง** |
| `04 / Evidence with limitations` — Validation ที่รายงานตามขอบเขต | **เชื่อได้แค่ไหน** |

Jargon is not deleted — NSC judges need it. It moves under a native `<details>` closed by default, labelled `รายละเอียดทางเทคนิค`.

Section 04 now splits **ทดสอบแล้ว** from **ยังไม่ได้ทดสอบ**, which is the honest answer to the question that was asked.

## Two stale claims fixed along the way

- The hero CTA said "เข้าสู่ระบบเพื่ออัปโหลดไฟล์" → `/login`. That stopped being true in #70 when the viewer was opened to visitors. Now "ลองอัปโหลดไฟล์ของคุณ" → `/dashboard/viewer`, and the browser test that asserted the old journey now asserts the stronger thing it was always after: the action arrives at a page with a real file input.
- The menu still read Technology / Method / Evidence — words that appear nowhere at the destination after the rename.

## The font trap, caught by its own test

`.editorial-eyebrow` is `font-mono`, and JetBrains Mono carries no Thai glyphs. This project already shipped that bug once and had it reported as unreadable. A test was added that scans **rendered markup** for Thai under a mono class — and it immediately caught a second, still-live instance in the hero badges that nobody had noticed:

```
expected [ 'แยกลำต้น–ใบ ที่ใช้จริง', 'จำแนกชนิดพันธุ์' ] to deeply equal []
```

Both are fixed. The test was proven able to fail before anything was built on it.

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| web unit | **151 passed** (was 147) |
| browser journey | **42 passed** |
| type-check · lint · build | PASS |
| forbidden-claim scan | none |

Every truth still on the page, checked by hand: estimates not certified credits · PointNet++ experimental and unused · species classification a stub · Wood IoU `0.418`, Leaf IoU `0.808`, DBH MAE `1.1673846154` unrounded · `NOT A LIVE RUN` in frozen mode · the TGO 2017 citation, which one pass dropped and was put back.

Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-31-plain-language-copy.md`

body: ## Summary This PR fixes how EndpointSlice condition values are interpreted when they are omitted from the Kubernetes API response. Kubernetes defines missing `ready` and `serving` values as `true`, and a missing `terminating` value as `false`. Headlamp previously relied on JavaScript truthiness, causing omitted `ready` and `serving` values to be displayed as failures. The change applies the Kubernetes-defined defaults consistently in the EndpointSlice list and details views. ## Related Issue Fixes #6784 ## Changes - Added a shared helper for resolving EndpointSlice condition defaults. - Updated the EndpointSlice details view to use the resolved condition values. - Updated the EndpointSlice list to use the resolved `ready` value. - Updated the EndpointSlice condition types to allow omitted values returned by the Kubernetes API. - Added regression tests for missing, empty, partial, and explicit condition values. ## Steps to Test 1. Start Headlamp and connect it to a Kubernetes cluster. 2. Create an EndpointSlice without explicit endpoint condition values: ```yaml apiVersion: discovery.k8s.io/v1 kind: EndpointSlice metadata: name: headlamp-missing-conditions namespace: default labels: kubernetes.io/service-name: headlamp-condition-test addressType: IPv4 ports: - name: http protocol: TCP port: 8080 endpoints: - addresses: - "10.244.0.250" hostname: no-conditions nodeName: minikube ``` 3. Open `headlamp-missing-conditions` in the EndpointSlice details view. 4. Verify that `Ready` and `Serving` are displayed as success. 5. Verify that `Terminating` is displayed as false/error. 6. Open the EndpointSlice list and verify that the endpoint is displayed as ready. The automated regression tests can be run with: ```bash cd frontend npm test -- --run src/components/endpointSlices/utils.test.ts npm run tsc ``` Validation completed locally: - Focused regression tests: 4 passed - TypeScript checks: passed - Scoped ESLint checks: passed - Prettier checks: passed - Manual verification with Minikube: passed ## Screenshots (if applicable) ### Before ### After ## Notes for the Reviewer - The defaults follow the Kubernetes EndpointSlice API semantics: missing `ready` and `serving` values are interpreted as `true`, while a missing `terminating` value is interpreted as `false`. - Explicit boolean values are preserved. - The change does not add dependencies or modify public APIs.

author: the-marauder101
body:
One commit. The console wore the marketing brand; it should follow Vyom instead, because a recruiter moves between the two internal tools all day and they should feel like one toolset rather than two products.

## Split by audience, not by tool

| Stylesheet | Used by | Language |
|---|---|---|
| `css/nikash.css` | console, keying, verification call | **Vyom's** — navy `#0F3460`, cyan `#00B4D8`, 10px radius, navy-tinted shadows, gradient primary |
| `css/brand.css` | client role brief, candidate supplement | **v-bog.com's** — warm off-white, orange, zero radius, zero shadows |
| `css/assess.css` | candidate assessment | v-bog.com's, mobile-first |

Only the *internal* surfaces moved. A client filling in a role brief, or a candidate taking a test, should see V-BOG — not the internal tooling. `brand.css` is the previous stylesheet kept intact so those pages did not follow the console inward.

Every class name is unchanged, so no HTML or JS needed rewriting.

## One correction to Vyom's palette

Cyan `#00B4D8` measures **2.4:1** on Vyom's light ground, below the 3:1 floor for a UI component that carries meaning. So cyan does what Vyom uses it for — gradients, the nav hairline, decoration — while anything that actually signals (a selected option, a checked box, a progress fill) uses navy at 12.5:1. Same look, meaning that survives.

The four form-follows-function rules were untouched, since they govern hierarchy rather than colour. QA asserts them against the new palette: the figure is still 26px, concerns still render beside reasons at equal weight, there is still no reject control.

## Three bugs the screenshots exposed

1. **Ranks read 1 and 13** on a real two-candidate shortlist, under a heading saying "1 eligible of 2" — ranking ran over a pool that included golden-case fixtures which the view then hid. `v_console_clean` now ranks the rows it actually returns, with a migration assertion that every visible shortlist is contiguous from 1.
2. **"10 of 14 eligible"** — the same bug in the requirements list. Counts now agree with the shortlist, also asserted in the migration.
3. **"Quality 102.6%"** read as a broken percentage. It isn't: quality is a ratio to the requirement, capped at 1.15. Now labelled "of what this role requires".

Also removed a 3px coloured left border on notices — a thick side tab is decoration standing in for hierarchy, and the mono label already says what kind of notice it is.

## Verification

**11/11** in light and dark, including a check that the client-facing intake still renders on the warm brand ground rather than the console's. Golden cases pass; `v_c10_audit` empty.

`sql/15` only replaces two views — no schema, no data, no scoring change — and is already applied to the live project, so merging brings the repo in line with the database rather than changing it.

## Note for next time

This is the third PR merged at a commit earlier than the branch head, because I created the PR and then pushed more work to the same branch. From here I will open the PR **after** the final push, so what you review is what you merge.

author: dpmills
body:
A mutable variable could not keep a refinement that every one of its contributions establishes. The three contribution sites — `MutWrite`, a mutable binding's initializer, and a `Transact` key's seed — stripped refinements at emit, and two later checks read a refined variable as drift. The strip was compensating for an *incomplete join*: a write reaching a mutable variable through a `Mut` parameter never contributed to it at all. This records that contribution, deletes all three strips, and fixes both checks, so `x := 5` with no other writes types as `Mut(5)` and reads as `5`, while `x := 0` written only through a `Mut(Int)` parameter joins to `Int` instead of being rejected against that parameter.

## The missing contribution

`Typing::apply` records `arg <: d` against a **fresh** variable, so a `Mut` argument meets an `Infer` and takes the deliberate deref arm — right for a bare read like `cnt + 1`, wrong here: the handle is gone before the invariance rule can relate the two value types, and the parameter's `V` arrives only as an upper bound. `emit_apply` records it directly instead (`contribute_pbr_writes`), reading the parameter off the **head of the application spine** (`parameter_type`), since a curried call leaves the immediately-applied type a bare `Infer` for every argument past the first. Why the lattice's join is the whole rule: `src/ccl/design/type-inference.md`.

## Two checks that made a refined mutable variable look unsound

- `types_agree_modulo_unread` counted refinement layers *before* reading through a handle, comparing a refined value's one layer against the handle's zero. The read-through runs first now, split out as `histories_agree`.
- `inline`'s `refinement_discharged_by` compared the parameter's demand against the argument's `Mut` stamp — which the mutability phase needs in order to find the read — so it asks what the argument *denotes* instead.

`MutWrite` also stopped relaxing its **target**: the constraint is skipped outright when the target is not a mutable variable, leaving that diagnosis to `check_mut_write_targets`, so `Mut(Int)` genuinely demands `Int` of its writes.

## Mechanical, and one known gap

`Type::peel_refinements` / `mut_value_type` / `as_feed` / `is_handle` replace the hand-rolled peel-then-`matches!` at every site dispatching on a handle shape, retiring `peel_refinements_outer` and `peel_mut` with no behavior change.

An unstripped seed also keeps a filtered comprehension's extent, which then hangs in join planning's `insert_iterate_markers` — the same unfinished area where a *write* to a collection-valued mutable variable panics. Mutable collections are unsupported either way; recorded as a planning bug, not a restriction in the type system.

New end-to-end cases cover the computed seed with writes and without, and the pass-by-reference contribution at a non-first argument and through a forwarding chain; the accessors and the read-through are unit-tested, since no program can refine a handle.

author: utkarshmankad
body:
## Summary
- On WAL object prepare failure, fail the upload future and invoke the storage failure handler instead of silently swallowing the exception.
- Fix a resulting deadlock: the failed context was never polled off `walPrepareQueue`, so the prepare pipeline stayed permanently non-empty and never accepted new prepare cycles once a failure occurred (only masked when the handler halts the JVM; `ForceCloseStorageFailureHandler` just sets a flag and doesn't drain the queue).
- Fix a test bug: `prepareObject(int count, long ttl)` was stubbed with `any()` against its primitive `int` param, which corrupted Mockito's matcher stack and broke an unrelated test (`testAppend`) in the same class. Switched to `anyInt()`.

## Test plan
- [x] `./gradlew :s3stream:test --tests "com.automq.stream.s3.S3StorageTest"` — all 4 tests pass
- [x] Verified `prepareDeltaWALUpload`'s exceptional path now drains `walPrepareQueue` and fails all queued contexts

body: Unsigned simulator builds seed a deterministic device ID in UserDefaults because they cannot read Keychain. The restore-safety witness check treated that seeded mirror as foreign before the development identity file existed, so Iroh activation deferred and the app stayed Not Connected.\n\nThis treats the seeded mirror as same-device evidence only under the iOS Simulator target. Physical devices keep the Keychain and backup-restore safeguards unchanged.\n\nCommits are split red then green: the first adds the simulator regression test, the second fixes the probe. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes identity recovery in unsigned iOS Simulator builds by treating the deterministic `UserDefaults`-seeded device ID as same-device evidence in MobileIrohDevelopmentFileEvidenceProbe, enabling Iroh activation without a development identity file. Physical devices are unchanged and still rely on Keychain/backup-restore safeguards; adds an isolated, simulator-only regression suite that seeds the device ID and verifies adoption under DEBUG. Written for commit 700d9a24aba9f6bc6c5d819908067727a81d5a0e. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved DEBUG iOS Simulator builds so seeded device identities are recognized even when the durable identity store or development identity file is unavailable. * Preserved existing identity verification behavior on physical devices. * **Tests** * Added regression coverage for simulator builds that adopt a launcher-seeded device identity when identity storage is unavailable.

author: batkins33
body:
## Summary

Rebase of #10 onto current `master`. #10 itself was stale (base from 2026-07-15, `master` has moved substantially since via canary/execution-constraints work) and had a `null` merge state with no CI ever run.

Confirmed the underlying bug is still live before rebasing: current `master`'s `startAdapterExecutionTargetPaperclipBridge()` calls in each adapter's `execute.ts` still have no `hostApiUrl` field, so this fix is not superseded or already-applied elsewhere.

## Changes (identical to #10's intent)

- `hostApiUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:3100"` added to the `startAdapterExecutionTargetPaperclipBridge()` call in all 6 local adapters: `claude-local`, `codex-local`, `cursor-local`, `gemini-local`, `opencode-local`, `pi-local`.
- `.github/workflows/pr.yml`: adds a "Typecheck adapter packages" CI step (`pnpm --filter '@paperclipai/adapter-*' typecheck`).
- `pnpm-lock.yaml`: regenerated against current `master` (large diff is expected — lockfile format is verbose and was 3+ weeks stale; not hand-merged, regenerated via `pnpm install --lockfile-only` after the code changes were rebased in).

## Rebase process

- `git rebase origin/master` on #10's branch: all 6 adapter code changes applied cleanly via 3-way merge, no conflicts.
- Only conflict was `pnpm-lock.yaml` (expected for any 3-week-stale lockfile) — resolved by taking `master`'s lockfile and regenerating with `pnpm install --lockfile-only`, not manual conflict resolution.

## Verification

- `pnpm install` — clean
- `pnpm --filter '@paperclipai/adapter-*' typecheck` (the exact gate this PR adds to CI) — all 12 adapter-scoped packages pass `tsc --noEmit`
- Diff against `master` outside the lockfile: exactly 6 one-line adapter additions + 3-line workflow addition, matching #10 precisely

## Relationship to #10

Superseding #10 with this rebased version is the intent — recommend closing #10 once this is reviewed, to avoid two open PRs for the same fix.

body:
## Kötelező cégnév

A négy űrlapból eddig csak a termékoldali ajánlatkérőn volt kötelező a cégnév. Mostantól mind a négyen az:

| űrlap | eddig | mostantól |
|---|---|---|
| Kapcsolat | „Cég (opcionális)" | **Cégnév \*** |
| Címke ajánlatkérés | opcionális | **Cégnév \*** |
| Szerviz megkeresés | „Cég (opcionális)" | **Cégnév \*** |
| Termék ajánlatkérés | kötelező | változatlan |

A „(opcionális)" utótag mind a hét nyelven lekerült a címkéről — kötelező mező nem hívhatja magát opcionálisnak. A levéltörzsben a cégnév így már nem feltételes sor, hanem mindig ott van.

## Egyeztetés a gép beküldése előtt

A szervizoldal beküldés-csempéje kiegészült: *„Kérjük, mielőtt beküldi a gépet, vegye fel velünk a kapcsolatot."* — mind a hét nyelven.

A kérés szándékosan a **cím elé** került, kiemelve. Aki a címet keresi, azt kimásolja és becsomagolja a gépet; a cím alatti szöveget már nem olvassa el.

## Ellenőrzés

`tsc` tiszta, `STATIC_EXPORT=1` build lefut. Böngészős mérés:

- mind a négy űrlapon a cégnév mező üresen érvénytelen, kitöltve érvényes, a címke csillagot mutat és nem tartalmazza az „opcionális" szót
- a szerviz űrlap kitöltve elmegy, és a cégnév benne van a küldött levélben
- az egyeztetési kérés mind a hét nyelven megvan, és a DOM-ban a cím előtt áll
- mobilon (390 px) semmi nem lóg ki, konzolhiba nincs

Driver-vehicle assignment was stored in two independent DB columns (drivers.assigned_vehicle_id and vehicles.assigned_driver_id) that were never synchronized. Reassigning a driver left stale data on the old vehicle.

## Fix

Made vehicles.assignedDriverId the single canonical source. Removed the duplicate drivers.assignedVehicleId field entirely.

### Changes (8 files, +72/-99)
- Removed assignedVehicleId from Driver type, DB schema, API handlers, store, mock data
- Removed assignDriverVehicle function from store
- Drivers page assignment modal now calls updateVehicle with assignedDriverId
- All driver-vehicle lookups now use vehicles.assignedDriverId

author: copilot
body:
On Windows, startup could fail before rendering the TUI because `PushKeyboardEnhancementFlags` returned an error on legacy console APIs. The binary still parsed CLI flags (e.g. `--help`) because the failure path was in runtime terminal initialization.

- **Startup behavior**
  - Made keyboard enhancement setup non-fatal during `run()`.
  - Added a capability gate (`keyboard_enhancement_enabled`) so cleanup only attempts `PopKeyboardEnhancementFlags` when push succeeded.

- **Lifecycle consistency across SSH handoff**
  - Switched keyboard enhancement push/pop in `launch_ssh()` to best-effort calls as well.
  - Preserved existing raw mode / alternate screen / mouse capture flow; only enhancement-flag error handling changed.

- **Implementation shape**
  - Introduced focused helpers for explicit behavior:
    - `try_push_keyboard_enhancement_flags(...) -> bool`
    - `try_pop_keyboard_enhancement_flags(...)`

```rust
fn try_push_keyboard_enhancement_flags(writer: &mut impl Write) -> bool {
    execute!(
        writer,
        PushKeyboardEnhancementFlags(keyboard_enhancement_flags())
    )
    .is_ok()
}
```

author: jmtcsngr
body:
Closes #108.

## Problem

baton-rs opened one iRODS connection per process and reused it for every
NDJSON record. The only rebuild trigger was the `--connect-time`
wall-clock watchdog — nothing rebuilt in response to an error. So a
single mid-stream connection drop poisoned **every** subsequent record:
each reused the same dead socket and failed, until end of stream.

## Approach

- **`error::is_connection_level_code`** classifies iRODS socket/transport
  status codes (bases from iRODS 4.3.5 `rodsErrorTable.h`, errno sub-code
  stripped) vs per-record errors, as named constants with unit tests.
- **`ReconnectingSession::note_error`** flags a rebuild; the next
  `maybe_reconnect()` rebuilds *before any op runs*, so no operation ever
  touches a dead/null handle. The record in flight when the socket died
  is annotated in-band and **not retried** — a possibly half-applied
  write is never re-issued. Reconnect failure stays fatal, exactly as the
  age-based path already is.
- Wired into the six annotate-and-continue loops (list/get/put/chmod/
  metamod/baton-do). `baton-metaquery`'s main query is already fail-fast
  (`?`), so it has no cross-record cascade and is left as-is.

## Key finding

A mid-stream drop surfaces through the iRODS client as the **generic**
`SYS_INTERNAL_ERR` (-154000), not a tidy socket code (confirmed on
4.2.7). It's included in the classifier; over-inclusion is safe because
`note_error` only flags a rebuild — the record keeps its real error, so
a mis-flagged rebuild costs at most one cheap reconnect.

## Testing

New test-only `fault-injection` Cargo feature gates a
`shim_test_force_disconnect` seam (`shutdown(SHUT_RDWR)`) that drops a
live connection mid-stream. An integration test asserts the record after
the drop recovers on a rebuilt connection. Green across iRODS
4.2.7 / 4.3.4 / 4.3.5. Each of the three commits is individually CI-green
(clean bisect).

## Deferred to `release: 1.1.0`

Per the repo convention (CHANGELOG + version bumps live in `release:`
commits), the `Cargo.toml` bump to 1.1.0 and the CHANGELOG entry are not
in this branch. This is a backwards-compatible new capability → minor
bump.

body:
## STATUS gap #2: Auth roles + immutable audit trail + appeal workflow

Completes the roles system started with the reviewer roles/queue (0008): distinct coarse roles applied to all protected routes, a complete append-only audit trail for moderation actions, and a contributor appeal workflow that records every transition into the audit log.

### What's in this PR

1. **Distinct roles (contributor / moderator / admin)**
   - `db/schema.ts`: new `users` table (role identity, ADR 0013-compatible) with `role` enum, `active`, `mfa_enabled`; `reviewers.user_id` link to the DATA_TRUST reviewer profile (0008).
   - `app/lib/authz.ts`: `requireRole()`/`requireAuth()` guards resolving the coarse role from the session on every protected route.
   - `app/api/moderation/route.ts`: PATCH derives the acting reviewer server-side from the session/user link instead of trusting a client-chosen actor id.

2. **Immutable audit log (extension of `moderation_events`)**
   - `moderation_events` extended with `reviewer_id`, `actor_role`, `recused`, `escalated`, `second_reviewer_id`, `appeal_id`; UPDATE/DELETE remain blocked at the DB layer (0008 triggers).
   - `db/moderation.ts` records reviewer attribution and flags at write time.

3. **Appeal workflow**
   - `db/appeals.ts` + `app/api/appeals/` (list + decide by id): a contributor can contest a final moderation decision; `moderation_appeals` rows are linked to the originating decision event and every transition is appended to `moderation_events.appeal_id`.
   - `docs/decisions/0014-auth-roles-appeals.md` (ADR) + STATUS.md update.

4. **Migration 0010** (`drizzle/0010_auth_roles_appeals.sql`)
   - Regenerated by drizzle-kit against the merged schema (includes PR #57 `contributors`/`sessions` tables) so `drizzle-kit generate` is a no-op; hand-finished with the demo seed (6 role identities, reviewer links). Snapshot chain 0009 → 0010 verified (`prevId` correct).

5. **Tests (end-to-end)**
   - `tests/appeals.test.mjs` (new, 303 lines), `tests/auth-flow-e2e.test.mjs` extended (310 lines): auth → submit → moderate → publish → appeal → audit.
   - `tests/api-moderation.test.mjs`, `tests/correction-record-outcome.test.mjs`, `tests/invalid-inputs.test.mjs`, `tests/moderation-events.test.mjs` updated for role-guarded routes.
   - `scripts/db-migration-smoke.mjs` updated: `users` + `moderation_appeals` tables/indexes, seed counts (5 reviewers / 6 users).

### Verification (local)

- `npm run lint` — clean
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npm test` — 543/543 pass (includes build)
- `npm run db:smoke` — PASS (fresh-DB migration smoke)
- `npx drizzle-kit generate` — no-op (no schema drift)

### Privacy & safety (design constraints)

- No PII beyond the role identity; demo seed is LOCAL-PROTOTYPE only and flagged MUST-replace before public alpha.
- Audit trail is append-only; API exposes no mutation of history.

author: dudarenok-maker
body:
## Summary

`CoquiEngine._infer_from_latents` (`server/tts-sidecar/main.py`) passes `enable_text_splitting=True` to XTTS's low-level `inference()` — config-faithful, mirrors `Xtts.synthesize`'s own build — so a cloned-voice render at or above `tokenizer.char_limits[lang]` doesn't hard-crash the bare low-level assert instead. That path reaches upstream's `get_spacy_lang`, which raises `ImportError` when spacy isn't installed — and spacy was never declared as a sidecar dependency, so **every** such render 500'd (`{"detail":"Internal error."}`).

**Decision (per the implementation brief): Option A, with plain `spacy`, plus Option B's catch as belt-and-braces — not a straight revert to `enable_text_splitting=False`.**

- **Option A, revised placement** — plain `spacy>=3.8,<4.0` (**not** `spacy[ja]`) is installed by `server/tts-sidecar/scripts/install-coqui.mjs`'s third pip step, alongside the existing CJK phonemizers (`pypinyin`/`cutlet`/`unidic-lite`), **not** `requirements/base.txt`. spacy is reached only via the opt-in Coqui/XTTS clone path — never by Qwen or Kokoro — and this repo deliberately keeps Coqui-only dependencies out of the shared manifest (`test_coqui_absent_from_all_overlays` keeps `coqui-tts` itself out of every overlay the same way). Landing it in `base.txt` would have made every CPU-only and Kokoro-only install pay 22.3 MB / 16 packages for a library they never import. Measured in the real sidecar venv: plain `spacy` → 16 packages / 22.3 MB; `spacy[ja]` → 18 packages / 92.5 MB, of which **68.9 MB is `sudachidict-core`** alone (needed only for Japanese). Verified plain spacy actually satisfies `get_spacy_lang`'s ar/en/es/hi/zh branches (zh confirmed working, despite the upstream error message naming `spacy[ja]` generically) — only `ja` needs SudachiPy and stays broken on purpose, filed separately as #2038 (fs-59's call). The manifest guard (`test_spacy_is_explicit_and_not_the_ja_extra`, `server/tts-sidecar/tests/test_requirements.py`) is re-pointed at the new invariant: spacy absent from every manifest/overlay, present in `install-coqui.mjs`, never `[ja]` — verified it actually fails if spacy is put back in `base.txt`.
  - **Known cost, surfaced rather than hidden: this does NOT reach an existing Coqui install automatically.** A `base.txt` dependency is covered by `reqHash`, which re-pips on every version bump — so the original placement would have reached every upgrading user for free. The installer route only runs when a user explicitly (re-)installs or presses **Repair** on Coqui from Model Manager. Anyone who already has Coqui set up keeps hitting the #2017 500 until they do that. Called out in `RELEASE_NOTES.md` (user-facing) and `docs/release-notes-next.md` (operator terms) in this same PR.
- **Option B's catch, belt-and-braces only** — `_infer_from_latents` now catches `ImportError` from the inference call, logs it loudly (`log.error`, never silent), and retries with `enable_text_splitting=False`. Per the brief, this is a fallback for a stale/broken install, not the primary fix; the primary `enable_text_splitting=True` line is untouched.

**Incidental check requested by the brief — the stock catalogue path does NOT share this bug.** `synthesize()`'s `tts.tts()` call goes through `TTS.api.TTS.tts()` → `Synthesizer.tts()`, whose own `split_sentences=True` pre-splits text using `pysbd` (not spacy) *before* ever reaching `Xtts.synthesize()`/`.inference()` — and neither of those ever passes `enable_text_splitting=True` down from that path (`Xtts.inference()`'s own signature default is `False`). So the catalogue path never touches `get_spacy_lang` at all; this bug is confined to the cached-latents (`_infer_from_latents`) branch. No new issue filed for that.

**Other Coqui-provisioning paths checked — none need this change.** `install-coqui.ps1`/`.sh` (the scripted/offline siblings) only pre-fetch XTTS weights via `TTS.api.TTS(...)`; they don't pip-install anything and assume `coqui-tts` (and its deps) is already in the venv, so they're not an independent install path. The in-app installer route (`server/src/routes/coqui-install.ts` + `coqui-install-bootstrap.ts`) spawns `install-coqui.mjs` directly. No Pinokio-specific Coqui installer, no separate "Repair" code path, and no CI/test-setup script independently installs `coqui-tts` exist in this repo.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run verify:fast:branch` — green (pre-push gate; `test:sidecar` ran for real, 449s, 0 failures)
- [x] New regression test `test_synthesize_cloned_voice_recovers_when_spacy_import_fails` (`server/tts-sidecar/tests/test_xtts_clone_voice.py`) — drives a >182-char Russian string (`char_limits['ru']`) through the cached-latents path via a fake `tts_model.inference` that raises `ImportError` on the `enable_text_splitting=True` attempt (mirroring the real upstream shape) and succeeds on the `False` retry. Verified fail-before/pass-after by temporarily reverting the `main.py` catch and re-running: fails with the raw `ImportError` before the fix, passes after.
- [x] Full `pytest -m "not golden"` sidecar suite — 0 failures (2 pre-existing skips), confirming the new `spacy` dependency doesn't break anything else.
- [x] `test_requirements.py`'s `test_spacy_is_explicit_and_not_the_ja_extra` re-pointed at the new invariant and verified to fail when spacy is restored to `base.txt`.

Closes #2017

author: jbailes
body:
Four symptoms from this week's debugging, each of which presents as something else.

| Symptom | What it actually is |
| --- | --- |
| Delegate reports `cannot open` for a file in its own worktree | Its sandbox mounted an **empty directory**: a bind source expressed in aimee-server's filesystem does not exist on a sibling Docker daemon's host, and Docker creates it rather than failing |
| Delegated shell refused as unsandboxed | Correct refusal for a delegate with **no assigned worktree**. Reaching for `sandbox.mode` to silence it authorises an unsandboxed shell on the host holding the Docker socket |
| Settings change appears ignored | The reload **validates before publishing**, so a bad file is rejected and the running config kept. The log says which happened |
| Deploy reports success and changes nothing | A quiet `pull` is a no-op on a tag that looks current, Compose keeps the old container, and every later check tests the previous build |

Each section gives the command that settles it rather than a list of things to consider.

The deploy one also records that `aimee --version` reporting an older commit than your branch is **normal** after a docs-only change, because the image only rebuilds when image-affecting paths change. Without that, the correct state looks like the stale-image failure it is meant to detect.

## On the headings

They stay symptoms rather than becoming assertions. This file is a lookup table, not an argument: a reader arrives knowing what they see and needing the cause, so a heading that asserts the cause is one they cannot search for.

author: neo-opus-grace
body:
Resolves neomjs/neo#16240

A backup that completed is not necessarily a backup you can restore from — and until now every surface collapsed those two facts into one. A bundle finished cleanly, wrote a receipt reading `"status": "success"`, exported **zero rows for every subsystem**, and the health block named it the last successful backup. The bundle's own metadata had already recorded the truth; nothing read it.

Evidence: L3 (live non-destructive probe — the fixed health block run against two real backup series, and the newly-documented command executed against the retained series) → L3 required (#16240's ACs are about what the surfaces report over real bundles; no destructive or operator-gated step is in scope). Residual: a real backup run on a *populated* deployment producing a consistent verdict is post-merge, since producing one now would mean running a backup against the live plane mid-incident.

## What was and was not broken

**`backup.mjs` is not the defect and is essentially unchanged.** Its handling is deliberate and documented in-comment: `fail` throws, `empty` warns and is persisted into `bundle-meta.integrity` expressly *"for a downstream canary/alert to escalate on"*, because a fresh environment legitimately backs up empty. That reasoning is correct and is preserved. **The downstream consumer was never built.** This PR is that consumer.

Three parts, one coherent change:

| | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `HealthService` | walked bundles for `completedAt` only; named a zero-row bundle `lastSuccessful` | reports `lastSuccessful` (restorable), `lastCompleted` (a run finished), and `unusableCount` |
| backup receipt | `"status": "success"` and nothing else | carries the integrity summary, so a receipt-only consumer cannot read `success` as restorable |
| `backupCorruptionTimeline.mjs` | no npm script, no scheduler, no caller anywhere | `npm run ai:check-backup-integrity`, with the runbook naming *when* to reach for it |

## The design decisions worth attacking

**Tri-state, not boolean.** `restorable` is `true` / `false` / `null`. Absent evidence is a third answer: a bundle carrying no integrity block predates the block, and retained series contain them. Forcing absence into `false` retroactively condemns every historical recovery source — a worse outage than the bug. Forcing it into `true` recreates the false-green. Pinned by specs on both sides.

**Any empty subsystem disqualifies the whole bundle.** A partial restore is not a restore: recovering memories while the knowledge base comes back empty is a silently incomplete system, which is the hardest state to notice afterwards.

**The rule lives in exactly one module.** `bundleIntegrity.mjs` owns "is this bundle a usable recovery source?" and both consumers import it. The first commit had the predicate inline in the health block; a second copy in the receipt builder would have put the two halves of one contract an edit apart from disagreeing — the same coupling flagged in neomjs/neo#16238's review, avoided here before it shipped rather than after.

**`empty` is still non-fatal, deliberately.** Making it fatal would break first boot for every new deployment, since a genuinely fresh environment backs up empty and legitimately succeeds. The defect was that the verdict was invisible, not that it was non-fatal. `lastCompleted` is what preserves that, and an AC requires a spec that fails if anyone makes it fatal.

**No `schemaVersion` bump.** `readBackupReceipt` rejects any version it does not recognise, so bumping would make every receipt already on disk unreadable. The field is additive, pinned by a spec.

## Evidence

**Falsifier-first.** Every probe was written and run red before any fix existed. The health probes failed with `Expected: "2026-07-30…" / Received: "2026-07-31T04:57:18Z"` — the defect reproduced verbatim, the empty bundle being named the last successful backup.

**Live cross-validation against an independent instrument.** `backupCorruptionTimeline.mjs` classifies bundles by artifact **bytes**; the health block reads the integrity **verdict**. They were not built to agree, and on the retained series they do:

```
health block   → lastSuccessful 2026-07-30T19-28-57, count 36, unusableCount 4
canary         → 36 backups: 29 artifact-verified-clean, 0 manifest-false-green, 3 export-failed
                 last clean 2026-07-30T19-28-57; four `no-mc-claim` rows
```

Same newest-clean bundle, same disqualified count, from two different signals. On the deployment that produced the incident, the block now reports `lastSuccessful: null, lastCompleted: 2026-07-31T04-57-18, unusableCount: 1` — the honest report that was missing.

**The documented command was executed, not merely declared:** `npm run ai:check-backup-integrity` against the retained series returns the artifact-verified table.

**A scope bug the existing specs caught, recorded because it is instructive.** My first receipt edit read `meta.integrity` at the call site, but `meta` is declared in `runBackup()` while the receipt is written in `runBackupWithOffHostSync()` — a different function, so that was a `ReferenceError` on the real success path. `node --check` reported "parse OK", because syntax checking does not resolve scope. Two pre-existing wrapper specs went red and were the actual signal.

## Deltas from ticket

**None substantive.** All three fix items delivered as scoped.

One shape decision the ticket left open: it said the receipt should carry the verdict but not in what form. It carries a *summary* (`{restorable, emptySubsystems}`) rather than the full check array, because the receipt is deployment-global and duplicating `bundle-meta` there would create a second copy that can drift from the first.

## Test Evidence

```
npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs
  10531 passed, 5 skipped, 1 failed
```

Per surface touched:

- `ai/services/memory-core/HealthService.mjs` — 5 new probes in `HealthService.spec.mjs` (newest-empty, all-empty, partial-emptiness, absent-block, plus a POSITIVE CONTROL that a clean bundle is still reported — without it the assertions are satisfied by a function that reports nothing).
- `ai/services/memory-core/helpers/offHostSyncStore.mjs` — 4 new probes in `offHostSync.spec.mjs`, including the schema-version pin.
- `ai/services/memory-core/helpers/bundleIntegrity.mjs` — new; exercised through both consumers rather than in isolation, so the specs prove the shared rule reaches both.
- `ai/scripts/maintenance/backup.mjs` — one call site; its two pre-existing wrapper specs cover it and caught the scope bug above.
- `package.json` / `RestorationRunbook.md` — 2 static probes reading the committed files.

**On the single failure, stated honestly.** Each full-suite run on this machine produces roughly one failure, and it is a *different* test each time — `SessionSummarization` (live LLM latency), `DreamService`, `MemoryService.Lifecycle` (an unref-d timer). Every one passes in isolation on this branch, and `DreamService` passes in a full-file run on clean `dev`. The runs that failed were also markedly slower (5.0m vs the usual ~2m). That is consistent with load-dependent flakiness in this suite rather than with this change, which touches none of those files. Flagged rather than asserted as unrelated — CI is the tiebreak.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] On a populated deployment, a real backup run produces a receipt whose `integrity.restorable` matches what `ai:check-backup-integrity` reports for the same bundle.
- [ ] The Memory Core healthcheck payload shows `lastSuccessful`, `lastCompleted`, and `unusableCount`, and any consumer reading the old `lastSuccessful` alone still gets a correct (now stricter) answer.
- [ ] Once neomjs/neo#16208 corrects the Chroma persist path, the next backup's verdict flips from `empty` to clean without any further change here — that is the end-to-end proof the two tickets compose.
- [ ] A fresh deployment's first backup still succeeds with e
