author: kurzonmorris
body:
Adds a "saved settings found — press Enter to reuse" prompt at the top of both interactive flows in tavernManager, matching the pattern used by activateShrine / loginDaily / donationBot / activateMiracle (per AUTOSTART_BRIEF.md section 5-6).

On the second and later launches, the user sees:

    Saved settings found for this module:
       Cities: 3 (Alpha, Beta, Gamma)
       Wine level: 60%

    (1) Use these settings   [just press ENTER]
    (2) Reconfigure
    (3) Delete saved settings and reconfigure

Pressing Enter replays the previous cities + percentage (or the previous notification mode + cities + schedule for auto-tune) with zero further questions.

Two module-prefs files, one per flow:

  tavernManager.set          — cities + pct
  tavernManager.equilibrium  — notification_mode + cities + run_hours

Two files rather than one so the two flows can't stomp on each other's last-inputs — they answer different questions.

Foundation: reuses the shared ikabot.helpers.modulePrefs API (load_prefs / save_prefs / prompt_use_saved) exactly. That gets per-account isolation and the sequenceRunner-safe silent-return behaviour for free (prompt_use_saved returns False when config.predetermined_input is populated, so recorded keystroke sequences still win).

Design rules from the brief that are enforced here:

- Validate before replaying. Every field is type-checked and range-checked; malformed or older-schema prefs files fall through silently to the normal questions rather than crashing.
- Stale city IDs (sold, world reset, wrong account) are dropped silently, and the count of dropped cities is surfaced in the summary so the user sees why the reused count is smaller than what they saved.
- If ALL saved cities are gone, no offer at all — no point asking the user to reuse an empty set.
- _-prefixed keys are treated as reserved metadata (test T12 passes an _autostart key alongside real settings; replay ignores it as required).
- Save happens BEFORE the long-running loop in equilibrium mode, so Ctrl+C during a run still leaves valid last-inputs for the next launch.
- The destructive-action confirm ('About to set wine to N% in K cities. Go ahead? [Y/n]') is deliberately kept on the replay path — this UX shortcut skips CONFIG questions, not the intended-change gate.

What this deliberately does NOT do:

- Auto-start at login. The brief covers that separately as a larger feature; the user asked for one-button reuse only. Once settings memory exists (this commit), auto-start would be a small follow-up.

Verified with 14 unit tests: no-saved skip; happy-path replay; user-rejects path; stale-ID drop with note; all-stale silent skip; malformed pct / out-of-range notif / out-of-range hours all skip; empty city_ids skips; hours=0 (one-shot) is valid; per-account isolation (different username → separate prefs); _-prefixed keys ignored; singular/plural in the drop-count wording; save-then- replay round-trip for both flows.

author: karimwitani
body:
## Summary

Adds `reward_programs` as a first-class resource: domain types, repository, in-memory fake, service, controller, and DI wiring, following the same layering as `/rewards` and `/balances`.

- **Schema**: `check_reward_programs_type_reward_id` CHECK constraint enforces the `type` <-> `reward_id` invariant (`point_program` must have no bound reward, `reward_program` must have exactly one) that nothing previously enforced. `fk_reward_programs_reward_id` changes from `ON DELETE SET NULL` to `ON DELETE RESTRICT` - `SET NULL` would violate the new CHECK on a reward delete, and `CASCADE` would delete the whole program (and every balance on it, post-LOY-11) just because a reward was removed. Indexes added on `org_id` and `reward_id`. Migration generated via `supabase db diff --local -f enforce_reward_program_type_invariant`, verified with `supabase db reset`.
- **Atomic inline create**: `fn_create_reward_program_with_reward` (plpgsql, mirrors `fn_increment_balance`'s style) inserts the reward and the program in one function body, so `POST /reward_programs` with `type: "reward_program"` and a nested `reward` object creates both rows atomically in a single call - the client never calls `POST /rewards` for this flow.
- **Discriminated-union create body**: `RewardProgramCreateSchema = z.discriminatedUnion("type", [...])` makes the invalid states unrepresentable - `point_program` has no `reward` key at all (`.strict()` rejects it), `reward_program` requires one. **tsoa handled this cleanly as an `@Body()` type on the first try** (compiles to an OpenAPI `anyOf`), so the brief's suggested fallback (a single type with `reward` optional at the tsoa layer) wasn't needed.
- **Reads always embed the reward**: `GET /reward_programs` / `GET /reward_programs/{id}` return the full `reward` object (`null` for `point_program`), never the raw `reward_id`.
- **In-memory fake** shares the same singleton `IRewardsRepository` instance (constructor-injected) as the `/rewards` slice, so a reward created inline is visible via `GET /rewards` and vice versa - matching the real DB where they're the same table. It reproduces "both rows or neither" atomicity: the reward is created first, and the program row is only added if that succeeds.
- Integration tests assert the CHECK constraint directly (bypassing zod), `ON DELETE RESTRICT` refusing a bound-reward delete (mapped to 409 via the existing `23503` mapping in `postgres-error-handler.ts` - no change needed there), and RPC atomicity via a forced failure leaving no orphan reward row.

## Scoped out of this PR

**PATCH/DELETE are split into a follow-up issue, LOY-23.** The full CRUD implementation (read + create + update + delete, all four test tiers) landed at ~1500 LOC, 50% over the brief's own "~900-1000 LOC, top of the range" target - driven by the DB-level invariant tests, not padding. This PR ships the harder half (atomic create, discriminated union, CHECK/RESTRICT/atomicity tests); LOY-23 covers the more mechanical title-only `PATCH` + `DELETE` plumbing, following the same pattern already established for `/rewards`.

Also out of scope per the original brief: changes to `/rewards` itself (beyond the `ON DELETE RESTRICT` consequence), pagination, auth, and changing a program's `type` after creation.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npm test` (unit + component) - 208 passed
- [x] `npm run test:integration` - 44 passed, including CHECK constraint, `ON DELETE RESTRICT`, and RPC-atomicity assertions against real Postgres
- [x] `npm run test:e2e` - 44 passed
- [x] `supabase db reset` applies the generated migration cleanly from scratch
- [x] `pnpm supabase:gen` regenerated and committed `database.schema.ts`

body:
## What changed

Add an opt-in compiler mode that builds adaptive token masks on first use instead of materializing every parser state during compilation. Serialization materializes missing entries, dynamic insertion is synchronized, and the existing eager mode remains the default. The diff also enables a compiler-checked -fno-semantic-interposition optimization in five CMake lines; it contains no unrelated formatting or renaming.

This commit is based on main at 09a12a11 (#706 merged) and changes 20 files, +4512/-548.

## Why

Eager compilation scans the complete vocabulary for many states that a matcher never visits. On-demand generation moves that work to the first real mask request and provides the foundation for the following focused fast paths.

## Scope and split rationale

This is the smallest independently correct boundary found after repeated diff review. Splitting by historical commits would first expose the older +6375/-464 prototype or temporarily omit known cache-accounting, concurrency, and context-key fixes. The squashed version is about 1,863 lines smaller and keeps those required correctness fixes atomic.

## Correctness

On the current machine, pre-commit passed; Release C++: 61 passed; affected Python files: 143 passed, with 23 hf_token_required cases deselected by the project's default test rule. Tests compare eager and dynamic masks step by step and cover public APIs, serialization, concurrent matcher construction, fork, rollback, reset, budgets, and structural tags. All four benchmark workloads have zero before/after behavior differences.

## Performance

Compile time is in milliseconds and mask time is mean per-step latency in microseconds. Before is this commit's direct parent. A ratio above 1.00x means After is faster than Before.

|---|---|---:|---:|---:|

author: yu-min3
body:
#471 で `docs/` が docs サイト専用になったので、ガードの前提が変わった。その追従。

## 対象は 9 本 — docs サイトが transclude しているファイルだけ

当初 75 本（`docs/` 以外の全 Markdown）にしたが**過剰だった**。この壊れ方は「docs サイト用の記法を、GitHub でも読まれるファイルに書いた」ときにしか起きない。それが起きるのは書き手がサイト側とリポジトリ側を行き来している場所 = transclude 元だけで、`.claude/rules/` や `bootstrap/*/README.md` に Material 記法を書く動機は誰にも無い。

ルート `README.md` も transclude されておらず docs サイトには載らないので、同じ原則で対象外にした。

Markdown 145 本を分類した結果:

| 群 | 本数 | 読まれる場所 | このチェックの対象 |
|---|---:|---|:-:|
| `docs/**` | 70 | docs サイトのみ | — |
| **transclude 元** | **9** | **GitHub と docs サイト** | **○** |
| GitHub 専用ドキュメント（ルート README・`.claude/`・`apps/` ほか） | 46 | GitHub のみ | — |
| サンプルデータ / フィクスチャ / scaffold | 20 | 読み物ではない | — |

## パス固定ではなく導出にした

9 本をリストで持つと、10 個目の transclude が増えたときに黙って穴が開く。`docs/**` の `--8<--` 行を読んで対象を組み立てる。

```python
INCLUDE = re.compile(r'^-{2,3}8<-{2,3}\s+"?([^"\s]+)"?\s*$')
```

## docs.yml から専用 workflow へ

範囲を絞る作業でトリガーの穴が見つかった。`docs/` が検査対象外になった今、このチェックと site build に関連は無いので `.github/workflows/markdown-render.yml` に切り出した。`requirements-lint.txt` も分離（site を build しないので MkDocs 一式は不要）。

## 確認

| 項目 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| 既定スキャン | 9 dual-rendered files clean |
| `kubernetes/auth/README.md` に `<figure markdown>` + `{ width= }` を注入 | image / attr_list の 2 件を検出 |
| `kubernetes/storage/README.md` に `!!! note` を注入 | admonition を検出 |
| 10 個目の transclude を追加 | 自動で 10 本に拡大 |
| 2026-07-12 当時の `showcase.md` | 検出を維持（exit 1） |
| 最小依存環境（`requirements-lint.txt` のみ） | 動作 |
| `mkdocs build --strict` | 従来どおり通過 |
| workflow YAML 2 本 | パース確認済み |

## 併せて訂正

`docs/concepts/doc-layout.md` の "Rendering target" 表で `apps/*/README.md` とルート `README.md` を両面として書いていたが、どちらも transclude されていないので GitHub 専用が正しい。#471 で入れた自分の記述の誤り。

author: camielvs
body:
## Description

A follow-up on top of the **Compare Runs** stack (builds on #2603) that makes the Compare page far more forgiving and easier to drive.

Before this, if you opened the Compare page without two runs already chosen, it dropped you onto a full-screen "pick a run" list and wouldn't show anything else. Landing there with a single run (e.g. from a run's "Compare" menu) was a dead end. Now the **full comparison page always shows**, no matter what:

- **No runs chosen** → the whole page still renders, with each view showing a neutral "select two runs to compare" message.
- **One run chosen** → the run is compared against itself, so every view simply reads "no changes" — you see the page fully populated with one run's data.
- **Two runs chosen** → exactly the same comparison as before.

You can now also **change or clear either run without leaving the page**. Next to each run label (A / B) there's:
- a small **swap/replace** button that opens a pop-up run picker, and
- an **✕** to clear that side back to empty.

The run picker pop-up borrows the look & feel of the dashboard's run list — status, date, who started it — with **search, "created by" and date-range filters** so you can quickly find the run you want. Picking one drops it straight into the comparison without any page navigation.

Net effect: the Compare page behaves like a live workspace — start with nothing, one run, or two, and add/swap/remove runs in place until you're looking at what you want.

## Related Issue and Pull requests

<!-- Link to any related issues using the format #<issue-number> -->

Follow-up to the Compare Runs stack. Builds on #2603.

- [x] New feature
- [x] Improvement

- [ ] I have tested the changes on staging

## Screenshots (if applicable)

<!-- Add screenshots of: the empty compare page, a single-run comparison, and the run-picker pop-up with its filters. -->

## Test Instructions

1. Enable the **Compare runs** flag under Settings → Beta features.
2. **Empty state:** open `/compare` directly. Confirm the full page renders with dashed "Select run A / B" buttons and each tab (Structured / YAML / Graph) shows a "select two runs" message instead of a picker takeover.
3. **Single run:** open `/compare?a=<run-id>` (or use a run's **Compare** menu). Confirm run A is filled in, B shows "Select run B", and all tabs read "no changes" with the single run's data visible.
4. **Add a run:** click the replace button (or the empty "Select run B" button) to open the run picker pop-up. Try the **search**, **created by** and **date range** filters; the run already on the other side is excluded from the list. Pick a run and confirm it drops into the comparison without leaving the page.
5. **Swap / clear:** confirm swap flips A and B, and the **✕** clears a side back to empty (a two-run comparison correctly falls back to the single-run "no changes" state).
6. **Two runs:** confirm the full diffing behaviour across all three tabs is unchanged from before.

body: Follows the org-scoped route migration (#3256) that mounted the trigger-callback endpoint at both the canonical `/api/:org/trigger-callback` (via `createOrgScopedApi`, org-scoped.ts) and the legacy unscoped `/api/trigger-callback`. The route validates the Bearer token (bound to a specific org+connection at `TRIGGER_CONFIGURE` time) but never cross-checked the path-resolved `:org` against the token's bound organization. The sibling `automation-webhooks.ts` route (same trust boundary: an external, unauthenticated caller presenting a bearer credential) already does this exact cross-check for its API-key-based auth (`ctx.organization?.id !== meta.organization.id`) — this route was the one org-scoped-family route missing the analogous guard. **Why it matters:** `configure-trigger.ts` mints the callback URL with the connection's own org slug (`${ctx.baseUrl}/api/${organizationSlug}/trigger-callback`), so a legitimate caller's `:org` always matches the token's org — this change never affects normal traffic. It closes the gap for a leaked/reused token being replayed against a different org's URL path, matching the established defense-in-depth idiom for org-scoped external-webhook auth in this codebase. **Regression test** (`trigger-callback.test.ts`, injects fake `tokenStorage`/`studioContext`, no DB/mocking of internals): - matching path-org + token-org → 202, automation fires - mismatched path-org vs token-org → 401, automation does NOT fire - legacy unscoped mount (no path-resolved org) → unaffected, still fires (mirrors current behavior) **To verify:** `bun test apps/api/src/api/routes/trigger-callback.test.ts` **Locally ran:** `bun run fmt`, `cd apps/api && bunx tsc --noEmit` (clean), the targeted test above (3 pass), and `bunx oxlint` on both changed files (0 warnings/errors). Full CI validates the rest. --- ## Summary by cubic Prevents cross-org replay of trigger-callback tokens on the org-scoped endpoint. A token minted for one org can no longer be used on another org’s URL; normal traffic is unaffected. - **Bug Fixes** - Cross-checks the path org (`studioContext.organization.id`) against the token’s org on `POST /api/:org/trigger-callback`; returns 401 on mismatch (parity with `automation-webhooks.ts`). - Legacy unscoped `POST /api/trigger-callback` behavior unchanged. - Added tests covering match (202), mismatch (401), and legacy (202). Written for commit e8313d4e7550acf038956e0b0609bdc9f83383fc. Summary will update on new commits.

## What this does (plain English)

The DONNA / Falsifiable Finance products section was removed from the canonical page (third parties are involved in those products). This fills the gap it left, at the same mid-page position, with a small illustrated **"Three flagships"** spotlight.

Its honest purpose is **imagery**, which was requested. All three flagships were already described in full elsewhere on the page, so this section does **not** restate them — each tile is one short line, its own hand-drawn SVG, and a link to the fuller section:

- **HAL — AI as a syscall** → links to `#engine` (the client repos + the conformance mark already live there)
- **GRASP** → links to `#grasp` (the moat section)
- **ccflex-skibidi** → links to `#open-work`

## Why it is a visual layer, not new content

While building it I confirmed every flagship is already featured: GRASP has its own section, ccflex-skibidi is in *The Open Work*, and HAL plus its `hal-go/py/js/conformance` clones are in *The Engine*. So the value added here is the three SVG drawings and a mid-page visual focal point — not new words. (An earlier draft duplicated HAL's clone lines; that was trimmed to a cross-link once I found them in `#engine`.) If you would rather I distribute the drawings into those existing sections and drop this band instead, that is an easy pivot.

## Details

- New `<section id="flagships">` at `data-score="52"` — an existing gap in the scroll-progress scale, so nothing was renumbered.
- Reuses the existing design system (`.work-grid`, `.project-card`, `.clone`, `.claim`). No `main.js` or `style.css` changes.
- Each SVG is theme-aware (`currentColor` + `var(--accent)`, no hardcoded colours — the page-wide contrast audit specifically flagged those) and accessible (`role="img"` + a descriptive `aria-label`, decorative internals `aria-hidden`).
- No DONNA / Falsifiable Finance anywhere.

This site deploys live from `main` on merge, so this PR is left **unmerged for your decision**.

author: alicup29
body:
## What
Brings the browser's imageless crash-recovery draft to the **Tauri desktop** runtime, and unifies recovery for both runtimes into the existing Welcome-screen "Restore unsaved work?" card.

## Desktop auto-save (crash-recovery net)
- Debounced (1.5s) imageless draft — `saveSlpStructureToBytes(labels, {embed:false})` — written to `<appLocalData>/sleap-drafts/` + an on-disk JSON manifest. Refs only, no pixels → no memory ceiling regardless of video count.
- Never marks the project clean (⌘S remains the real disk save; the draft is only a net). Cleared on a successful save / discard.
- New modules: `tauriDraft.ts`, `tauriDraftManifest.ts`, `draftRestoreTauri.ts`. Browser OPFS path untouched. Reuses the shipped in-place-save (#220) + OPFS-draft (#239) infra.

## fs capability fix
Auto-save's manifest write (`writeTextFile`) + cleanup (`remove`) were granted nowhere (`fs:default` only covers `mkdir` + reads; `fs:allow-write-file` was the only mutating grant) — so the manifest write would throw, get swallowed, and crash-recovery would **silently record nothing**. Added `fs:allow-write-text-file` + `fs:allow-remove`.

> Note: the same missing grant silently breaks `pathMappings.saveMapping` on desktop today (its `writeTextFile` is swallowed by a `try/catch`) — a separate pre-existing bug worth a follow-up.

## Unified in-app recovery (replaces the desktop `window.confirm`)
Recovery is now the **same in-app card the browser already uses**, for both runtimes — no native dialogs, and it's user-initiated (a click), not an auto-prompt.
- New `recoverableDrafts.ts` normalizes browser-OPFS + desktop-disk drafts into one shape; `WelcomeScreen` lists both and restores/discards via the right per-runtime helper.
- Removed `maybeRestoreTauriDraft` + its auto-restore-on-launch `window.confirm`. This fixes a React-StrictMode double-restore (the auto-restore effect had no single-flight guard) and makes recovery trivially escapable.
- Discard uses an inline in-app confirm — recovery has **zero native dialogs**.

## Tests + verification
- Unit tests for the manifest round-trip, path derivation, the "records a draft without marking clean" behavior, and cross-runtime draft normalization.
- Gate green: build ✓, typecheck:tests ✓, `bun run test` (1158) ✓, changed-file lint ✓.
- **Live-verified in a real Tauri window** (tauri-pilot): draft `.slp` + manifest written to disk via the real debounce path; net semantics; full restore reconstruction (labels rebuilt from disk, re-linked, stays dirty); the Welcome card renders (no auto-restore), **Restore loads the project**, and the inline Discard→confirm→Cancel works.

Manual checks worth doing before merge: the embedded-*pkg*.slp restore graft (verified with a regular .slp + external video, not an embedded pkg), the on-disk-divergence → Save-As path, and a browser spot-check of the shared card.

author: jeremy
body: Closes #527. Split out of #526, which modeled the wire contract (`FieldValidationError` → `{"errors": FieldErrorMap}`) in the spec; this PR makes all six transports honor it. ## The real payload (verified against bc3) `app/controllers/calendars_controller.rb` renders both variants of the field-keyed shape: ```ruby rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e raise unless request.format.json? render json: { errors: e.record.errors }, status: :unprocessable_entity ``` and the up-front enum guard, which pins the exact wire shape: ```ruby render json: { errors: { color: [ "is not a valid color" ] } }, status: :unprocessable_entity ``` (`ActiveModel::Errors#as_json` serializes to `{attribute => [messages]}`.) The route is `resources :calendars, only: [ :update, :show ]` (config/routes.rb:858) and the controller responds to JSON, so `UpdateCalendar` — the operation the spec maps to `FieldValidationError` — hits this rendering. The same `{ errors: e.record.errors }` pattern appears in `google_documents_controller.rb` and `cloud_files_controller.rb`, confirming it as the Rails `RecordInvalid` family shape. Smithy's `FieldErrorMap` (`map>`) matches. ## What changed (identical in all six) Scoped to 400/422 responses: 1. **Parse** the `errors` map: object value; entries whose value is an array keep their string elements; unusable shapes (non-object `errors`, non-array entries, no surviving messages) are treated as absent — flat-body behavior is unchanged. 2. **Flatten** identically everywhere: fields sorted lexicographically, each field rendered `field: msg1; msg2` (messages joined `"; "`), fields joined `", "`. Appended in parentheses after a top-level `error` message (`Validation failed (color: is not a valid color)`), standing alone when only `errors` is present. Truncated **after** flattening via each SDK's existing 500-char message cap. 3. **Structured slot** carrying the raw, untruncated map: - Go: `Error.FieldErrors map[string][]string` - TypeScript: `BasecampError.fieldErrors?: Record` (+ `toJSON`) - Python: `ValidationError.field_errors: dict[str, list[str]] | None` - Ruby: `ValidationError#field_errors` (both construction paths: `Basecamp.error_from_response` and `Http#handle_error`) - Kotlin: `BasecampException.Validation.fieldErrors: Map>?` (trailing default param — source-additive) - Swift: **message-only flattening.** Extending the `.validation` associated values breaks every `case .validation(let ...)` match, so the structured slot awaits a deliberate source break (documented on the case and in SPEC §6). SPEC §6 gains a "Field-Keyed Validation Bodies (400/422)" subsection documenting the shared algorithm and the Swift deviation. ## Breaking: Go (deliberate, pre-1.0) Adding `FieldErrors` to the exported `basecamp.Error` struct. `apidiff base.api pr.api`: ``` Incompatible changes: - Error: old is comparable, new is not Compatible changes: - Error.FieldErrors: added ``` Unkeyed composite literals of `basecamp.Error` also break. The SDK itself uses `*Error` and keyed literals throughout. Labeled `breaking`; consolidate with the upcoming C4 Go type changes so pre-1.0 consumers absorb one break, not two. ## Latent TS bug fixed along the way The TS service path passed the `Response` to `errorFromResponse`, which re-read `response.json()` — but openapi-fetch has already consumed and parsed the error body by then, so the re-read threw and **every service-layer error message silently fell back to `statusText`**. The parsed body was sitting unused in `handleError`'s `error` param. `errorFromResponse` now delegates to a new exported `errorFromParsedBody`, and `handleError` feeds the parsed body through it. The new conformance cases are what surfaced this (unit tests constructed fresh `Response` objects and passed). ## Tests Red-first: per-SDK unit tests were run against the pristine transports and failed as expected before the implementation landed — - Go: build failure, `e.FieldErrors undefined` (compile-level red) - TS: 7 failed / 50 (`vitest tests/errors.test.ts`) - Python: 12 failed, 1 passed (`pytest -k FieldKeyed`) - Ruby: `NoMethodError: field_errors` + message mismatches in both `errors_test.rb` and `http_test.rb` - Swift: 6 XCTAssert failures (`"client error"` / `"Validation failed"` vs flattened) - Kotlin: compile failure, unresolved `fieldErrors` / `flattenFieldErrors` Green, full suites (after all review rounds): Go `go test ./...` ok (lint 0 issues); TS 1031 passed; Python 725 passed (`uv run pytest`); Ruby 963 runs / 0 failures; Swift 267 tests / 0 failures; Kotlin `:basecamp-sdk:jvmTest` BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Conformance: seven new `error-mapping.json` cases on `UpdateCalendar` (single-field, multi-field sort/join, top-level append, non-string-sibling survival, message-key fallback, `__proto__`-as-ordinary-field, mixed-validity map tolerance), asserted via language-independent `errorMessage` substrings — never the structured slot. All five runners green with the new cases passing: Go 129/0, Kotlin 122/0, TypeScript 147 passed, Ruby 113/0, Python 127/0. Swift mirrors the cases as native XCTests in `ErrorTests.swift`. No skip-roster changes. --- ## Summary by cubic Make 400/422 validation errors field-aware across all transports and align error parsing across surfaces. We flatten Rails-style field maps into clear messages, expose the raw map (except Swift), honor a "message" fallback, and harden TypeScript against `__proto__`. - **New Features** - 400/422: parse `{"errors": {field: [messages]}}`, keep string elements only, skip unusable shapes; flatten as `field: msg1; msg2, other: msg`; append to any top-level error; truncate after flattening. - Structured slot for the raw, untruncated map: Go `Error.FieldErrors`, TypeScript `BasecampError.fieldErrors`, Python/Ruby/Kotlin `field_errors`/`fieldErrors`; Swift flattens message only for now. - SPEC documents the shared algorithm; conformance adds sorted/multi-field, append, non-string-sibling survival, `"message"`-fallback, `__proto__` cases, and a malformed-entry tolerance case (Swift mirrors as XCTests). - **Bug Fixes** - Top-level message fallback: Go/TypeScript/Kotlin/Swift now honor the `"message"` fallback when composing field errors. - Robustness: parse scalar members independently so non-string `error`/`error_description` don’t discard field errors (Go `json.RawMessage` + safe string extraction; Kotlin/Python/Ruby string-only reads). - Go generation: 4xx/5xx parsers tolerate undecodable error bodies so wrappers still see the raw body (wired via `go/generate.go` and `scripts/normalize-go-error-response-parsing.sh`); 2xx stays strict. - TypeScript service: stop re-reading consumed bodies from `openapi-fetch` — use `errorFromParsedBody` to preserve server messages and field errors; treat `"__proto__"` as a normal key via a null‑prototype accumulator. - Kotlin consistency: one shared parser (`exceptionFromErrorBody`) powers both services and `Download`. - Go: error message truncation matches SPEC (500-byte cap, last 3 replaced with `...`). - Breaking (Go): added `FieldErrors` to `basecamp.Error`; the struct is no longer comparable and unkeyed literals break. Written for commit d40967442d2ff788442349f4b9df2aec92779729. Summary will update on new commits.

body:
`document('')` is sometimes used as an idiom for returning a node-set
corresponding to the current stylesheet. However, resolving the empty string
against an invalid base URI produces an invalid URI, and per section
12.1 of the XSLT 1.0 standard:

  If there is an error retrieving the resource, then the XSLT processor
  may signal the error; if it does not signal the error, it must recover
  by returning an empty node-set.

The spec is a bit contradictory here; elsewhere, it also states:

  Note that a zero-length URI reference is a reference to the document
  relative to which the URI reference is being resolved; thus
  document("") refers to the root node of the stylesheet; the tree
  representation of the stylesheet is exactly the same as if the XML
  document containing the stylesheet was the initial source document.

But the standard also says:

  The URI reference may be relative. The base URI of the node in the
  second argument node-set that is first in document order is used as
  the base URI for resolving the relative URI into an absolute URI.

And resolving the empty string against an invalid URI should arguably
produce an invalid URI.

In some ways, this brings Chrome behavior closer to Firefox, though it
still differs in other ways: the specific test case here returns a
different result in Firefox, because Firefox appears to ignore an
attempt to set an invalid base URI, while Chrome does not.

author: sajid-ahmed1
body:
## Changes

Each category is now a **swipeable deck** rather than three stacked options: one card at a time, with the next card peeking out behind it and a "1 of 3" counter.

- **Drag right to pick, left to skip.** The card follows your finger/cursor, rotates as it goes, and shows a "Let's go" / "Nope" stamp once you pass the intent threshold. Released short of the threshold, it snaps back.
- **Picking opens the full plan** for that place — travel bubbles, calendar, share, maps — with a "Back to swiping" link to return to the deck.
- **Running out** shows "That's everything here" with a **New suggestions** button wired to the existing refresh (which already excludes what you've seen), plus "Start over" to run the same deck again.

Dragging uses pointer events, so mouse and touch take the same path. The same decisions are available via **Skip / Let's go** buttons and the **left/right arrow keys**, since a drag-only interface is unusable by keyboard; cards are focusable and labelled for screen readers, and the fly-out animation is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

Refreshing resets both decks to the first card via a keyed remount.

## Testing

Full flow driven in a headless browser with real mouse drags:

| Step | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Drag left 160px | advances 1 of 3 → 2 of 3 |
| Drag left 40px (below threshold) | stays on 2 of 3 |
| Skip button | advances to 3 of 3 |
| ArrowLeft on last card | shows "That's everything here" + New suggestions |
| Start over | back to 1 of 3 |
| Drag right 170px | opens the full plan for that place |
| Inside the pick | travel bubbles, Add to calendar and Share plan all present |
| Back to swiping | returns to 1 of 3 |

`npm run build` and `tsc --noEmit` pass; lint holds at the 5 pre-existing `no-explicit-any` errors.

Screenshots caught a styling regression before it shipped: moving the deck markup into a new `SwipeDeck` component silently dropped its card, title and button styles — styled-jsx scopes rules to the component that declares them, the same trap as the earlier `PlaceItem` extraction. Those rules are now `:global`.

## Note

The two decks are independent — you can pick a restaurant and an activity separately. There's no combined "here's your evening" view pairing the two; say the word if that's what you want next.

## CHAOS-3294 — Ask Dev Wave 3.1: intent, resolution, plan, frame, narrative, and answer-v2 contracts

Contracts-only foundation for the Wave 3.1 corrective program (CHAOS-3293). Zero behavior change to the live v1 path — new `contracts_v2` module set beside untouched `contracts.py`.

### What lands

- **Nine versioned contract groups** per Amendment TRD v2 §4: `dev_question_intent.v1` (12 launch intents), `dev_subject_mention.v1` + `dev_resolution_ledger.v1` (append-only, per-mention terminal outcomes), `dev_subject_set.v1` (homogeneous, ≤25, TEAM first-class), `dev_investigation_plan.v1` + `dev_source_requirement.v1` (8 required-source states), `dev_investigation_result.v1` + `dev_source_observation.v1` (measured-zero ≠ no-data), `dev_answer_frame.v1` (completion requires numerator+denominator or `calculable=false`), `dev_narrative.v1` (presentation-only, fact-bound), `dev_answer.v2` (8-value safe public outcome enum), v2 stream events, and a v2→v1 compat projection.
- **Semantic validators**, each with fail-before/pass-after counterexample tests: internal-outcome leakage, contradictory outcome vs frame, completion-without-denominator, narrative fact-ID closure, relationship closure.
- **JSON schemas + positive/negative fixture corpus** (exported via `export_contracts_v2`, drift-checked) in the layout web's contract generator consumes (web regeneration is CHAOS-3298).
- Client `question_class` demoted to a non-authoritative hint in `dev_message_request.v2` (server interpretation lands in CHAOS-3292).

### Adversarial hardening (5 Codex rounds, all findings reproduced by execution before fixing)

Structural closures rather than patches, each with a stated closure argument and partition test:

1. **Allowlist canonical projection** for every no-content outcome (denied/not_found/unsupported/temporarily_unavailable/failed): every string-bearing field programmatically enumerated and classified (canonical / closed-enum / non-text / absent); denied carries no subject identity; a future field addition fails the test until classified.
2. **Deep immutability**: tuple collections across every frozen v2 model *including embedded v1 mirrors* (`contracts_v2/embedded.py`), asserted by recursive introspection; post-validation mutate-then-serialize regressions.
3. **Identifier grammars by mint**: server-minted correlation handles pinned to canonical lowercase dashed UUID (`ServerHandle`, matching the actual `uuid.uuid4()` mints); evidence refs keep their `ev1_<40hex>` HMAC grammar; client-supplied request IDs stay deliberately loose; every one of the 66 identifier cells classified with a live-model-checked reason table.
4. **Fact-bound narrative validation**: per-sentence numeric admission from referenced facts only (no global token pool), completion polarity enforced (completed-stems cite the rate, remaining-stems its complement, both for percentages and bare decimals), token-boundary subject identity, ordinary typography accepted (`75 %`, `3-of-4`, `3 out of 4`).
5. **Stream lifecycle invariant**: exactly one `run.started` at index 0, exactly one `done` at the end, one terminal result, append-only ledger extension enforced across snapshot updates, frame/answer/stream `run_id` closure.

**210 contract tests** (110 → 210 across the rounds). Full `ci/local_validate.sh` gate green at every round (ruff, mypy, go, full unit suite, live-ClickHouse argMax proof).

### Documented residuals (non-blocking, owned downstream)

- Semantic narrative consistency beyond deterministic binding (structural polarity, non-English phrasing) → CHAOS-3297 layer-6 validator.
- Six contract-layer IDs (`frame_id`, `narrative_id`, `ledger_id`, `set_id`, `mention_id`, `observation_id`) pinned to UUID ahead of persistence; CHAOS-3292/3295/3297/3299 must mint them as UUIDs.
- `SourceClass` (12 members) and `PLAN_REGISTRY` (12 plan IDs) are newly defined vocabularies — flagged for domain review before CHAOS-3292/3295 build on them.

SCREENSHOT-WAIVER: contracts/backend only, no rendered surface.

body:
Adds two agent-backend cookbook examples and fixes the Covalent one's full run. All three were run **green against live Tenki** (a `tk_` key) and each **self-terminates** (verified: zero non-terminated sandboxes after each run).

## What's here

**`examples/hermes-tenki` (new)** — the Hermes (Nous Research) terminal backend on Tenki: a persistent cloud shell that pauses when idle and resumes intact.
- `verify.mjs` runs `setup.sh` (clones the **public** PR #1 branch of `LuxorLabs/tenki-hermes-agent` into `./hermes-agent` and repins the SDK to a published version), then `verify.py`.
- Live: **19/19** — boot, exec, exit codes, stderr, cwd tracking, file I/O, stdin (heredoc), and a full pause→reattach→resume roundtrip. `main.py` is the narrated walkthrough.
- Drives the **open PR branch** (the backend isn't published yet); `setup.sh` handles that and the SDK repin. When PR #1 merges, drop the repin.

**`examples/openhermit-tenki` (new)** — an OpenHermit-style per-agent exec backend (TypeScript): one microVM per agent, sticky sessions, pause/resume across a simulated gateway restart.
- `verify.mjs` shims to `tsx verify.ts`. Live: **11/11**, including the ~60s pause/resume roundtrip. Cleans up in a `finally`.
- Self-contained — needs only `@tenkicloud/sandbox` (not an OpenHermit checkout).

**`examples/covalent-tenki` (fix)** — its smoke test already passed, but the headline **`workflow.py` was broken**: with `covalent==0.240.0` + `requests>=2.34` (what `requirements.txt` resolves to) *any* `ct.dispatch()` returns `422` (an upstream Covalent bug — no `Content-Type: application/json`). Added the plugin repo's inline `APIClient.post` monkeypatch, so the full run works — **verified: dispatch → `70.356`**. Also import `covalent` before the plugin in `verify.py` (silences a misleading "executor not found" warning) and documented the 422 in the README.

## CI notes
- **Project id is optional.** All three resolve the project from the key (JS SDK, Python SDK via `who_am_i`, and OpenHermit's now-relaxed config) — I verified each with **only `TENKI_API_KEY`** set (the exact CI scenario), matching the existing Python examples.
- This inherits the pre-existing CI-secret dependency noted in `STATE.md §41` (Python examples want a `tk_` key, or `TENKI_PROJECT_ID`/`TENKI_WORKSPACE_ID` repo vars) — a maintainer setting, not specific to these examples.
- **Plugin repo URL:** the existing covalent example references `TenkiCloud/covalent-tenki-plugin`; I kept that. (Note for maintainers: a `LuxorLabs/tenki-covalent-plugin` repo also exists — worth confirming which is canonical. The PyPI package `covalent-tenki-plugin` is the same either way.)

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

`sim/selftest.sh` stages 2-4 — the toolchain pin check, the end-to-end PVT
sweeps, and the `--sabotage-corners` negative control — only ever ran on a
developer's machine. Stage 4 is the only check that can distinguish a live
corner sweep from one silently simulating typical everywhere, and nothing
automated noticed if it regressed.

This adds `.github/workflows/nightly-pdk.yml`: a scheduled (and on-demand, and
opt-in-per-PR) job that installs a real pinned toolchain on a hosted runner and
runs `sim/selftest.sh --require-pdk`. The default PR path is untouched.

### Why cached PDK on a hosted runner, and not the other two options

The issue costed out three options. The decisive fact is that **the gf180mcu PDK
is distributed prebuilt**: `volare fetch` downloads a released `open_pdks` build,
so the feared "cold build" does not exist — a cache miss is a download. Measured
on the pinned hash: 4.8 GB for all four variants, 1.2 GB for the one this repo
targets, of which 730 MB is `libs.ref` (standard-cell/IO/SRAM GDS/LEF/CDL) that
nothing under `sim/` or `design/` reads. Pruned to one variant's `libs.tech`,
the cache is ~506 MB — comfortably inside a hosted runner's disk and inside the
10 GB repo cache budget.

- **Self-hosted runner** — cheapest per run, but needs a machine and a
  registration token nobody has provisioned. Not implementable from here.
- **Prebuilt container image** — needs somewhere to publish it, and would still
  have to carry the *exact* `open_pdks` hash `sim/toolchain.json` pins. No
  public analog-EDA image happens to. It moves the problem, it does not remove it.
- **Cached PDK (chosen)** — plus a from-source ngspice, because no Ubuntu
  release ships one satisfying the pin (24.04 ships 42; the pin is >= 46). That
  build is a few minutes and is itself cached.

Both cache keys derive from `sim/toolchain.json`, so a pin bump misses the cache
and re-installs. A stale cache cannot silently produce evidence against the wrong
models: stage 2 (`run_corners.py --check-env`) compares what actually landed
against the pins and exits non-zero on drift, before anything is simulated.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/nightly-pdk.yml`** (new) — cron nightly + `workflow_dispatch`
  + `pull_request` labelled `ci:pdk`. Builds pinned ngspice from the upstream
  tarball, fetches + prunes + caches the gf180mcu install, runs
  `run_corners.py --check-env` standalone (so a bad cache is reported as a bad
  cache, not as a mystery failure mid-sweep), then `sim/selftest.sh --require-pdk`.
  Uploads the self-test log as an artifact and writes a job summary.
- **Failure is notified, not just red** — a *scheduled* failure files a GitHub
  issue, or comments on the existing open one (de-duplicated on an HTML marker
  in the body) so it does not open one a night. A stage-4 regression — a
  sabotaged sweep *passing* — gets its own title and `loom:urgent` on top of
  `loom:triage`. Manual and `ci:pdk` runs skip the issue: whoever pushed the
  button is already watching.
- **Nothing writes evidence** — `sim/selftest.sh` is invoked without `--record`,
  so the corner runner runs with `--no-write`; a step then asserts
  `git status --porcelain` is empty, as a structural guard on "`sim/` results are
  append-only evidence".
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — inventory header updated: stages 2-4 move from
  "EXCLUDED" to "NOT HERE, but covered", with where and why; the smoke test's
  entry now states why it stays excluded even with a PDK available.
- **`sim/smoke_test/run_smoke_test.sh`** — new `--no-write` mode (redirects the
  single `tee` sink to `/dev/null` rather than branching at each call site, so
  the two modes cannot drift apart) plus `-h/--help` and unknown-option handling.
- **`.github/labels.yml`** — `ci:pdk`, added *outside* the Loom-managed block so
  an upgrade does not drop it. The label already exists on the repo, so this PR
  can be tested by applying it.
- **`README.md`, `docs/environment-setup.md`, `package.json`** — corrected the
  now-false "cannot run on a hosted runner / excluded by design" claim, pointed
  at the workflow as the worked Linux install path, documented `--no-write`, and
  added `npm run check:pdk` mirroring what the nightly runs.

### Why the smoke test stays excluded from execution

`run_smoke_test.sh` needs **xschem**, which has no Ubuntu package and would put a
second from-source build on the nightly's critical path — to re-prove an
*installation* fact that the nightly's own PDK setup already demonstrates. Its
unique coverage is xschem netlisting; that is worth adding later, as its own job,
where a broken xschem build cannot make the stage-4 signal noisy. The hazard the
issue actually called out is fixed regardless: `--no-write` means an automated
runner can no longer append machine-generated sections to the append-only
`sim/smoke_test/smoke_test.log`. Follow-up filed below.

## Acceptance Criteria Verification

- [x] **Stages 2-4 run automatically at least nightly against a real PDK** —
      `schedule: '23 7 * * *'`, plus `workflow_dispatch` and the `ci:pdk` label,
      running `sim/selftest.sh --require-pdk` (so "no PDK, skipping" is a
      failure, not a pass).
- [x] **Default PR path unchanged** — `ci.yml` is byte-identical below its header
      comment; no step added, no PDK, no ngspice. The new workflow is a separate
      file that never triggers on `push`/`pull_request` except on an explicit
      `ci:pdk` label.
- [x] **A stage-4 regression produces a visible failure notification** — the
      self-test step greps its own log for selftest.sh's regression line and sets
      a step output; on a scheduled failure that becomes a filed/escalated GitHub
      issue titled "corner switching is NOT verified (stage 4 regression)" with
      `loom:urgent`. Verified with a stub, see Test Plan.
- [x] **Exclusion inventory in `ci.yml` updated** — stages 2-4 rewritten as
      covered-elsewhere with a pointer; the smoke test's exclusion restated with
      its current reason.

## Test Plan

Run on this machine, which has the pinned toolchain (ngspice 46 + gf180mcu at
`c6d73a35…`) installed:

- [x] **The self-test step's script, extracted from the YAML and executed
      verbatim against the real PDK** — stages 1-4 all pass, step exits 0, and it
      writes `stage4_regressed=false`:
      `PASS: harness is functional end to end and corner switching is verified.`
      (~9 min, all 8 experiments swept and all 8 correctly FAILED under sabotage.)
- [x] **Stage-4 regression detection, positive test** — same step script run
      against a stub `sim/selftest.sh` that emits selftest.sh's regression line:
      step exits 1 and writes `stage4_regressed=true`.
- [x] **"Nothing was written" assertion** — the tree-clean step, run after the
      full real-PDK self-test above: `ok: working tree clean, no evidence written`.
- [x] **`run_smoke_test.sh --no-write`** — full xschem -> ngspice run against the
      real PDK, correct operating point (`v(vhold) = 1.025608e+00`, matching
      docs/environment-setup.md §5), and `smoke_test.log`'s SHA-256 is unchanged
      before/after. `--help` and an unknown option behave.
- [x] **`actionlint` clean** on both workflow files (includes shellcheck on every
      `run:` block); `node --check` on the `github-script` body; both files parse
      as YAML.
- [x] **`npm run check:ci`** — 100 tests, OK.
- [x] **Prune safety** — `grep` confirms nothing under `sim/`, `design/` or
      `docs/` references `libs.ref`; only `libs.tech` is ever read.

### Verified on a real hosted runner

The `ci:pdk` label was applied to this PR, so the workflow has now run cold on
`ubuntu-latest` end to end
([run 30672961896](https://github.com/2AMLogic/gf180-sar-adc/actions/runs/30672961896)) —
**success**, 13 min 06 s total from a completely empty cache:

| step | cold time | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| build ngspice 46 from source | 5 m 15 s | `ngspice-46 : Circuit level simulation program` |
| volare fe

author: dakra
body:
Follow-up to #589. That PR made `buffer-face-mode` rescale the terminal grid; the cell *pixel* dimensions ghostel reports were still computed from the frame.

## Cells were measured off the wrong thing

`ghostel--reported-cell-width` and `ghostel--cell-height` — the dimensions handed to libghostty and reported to programs through XTWINOPS (`CSI 14 t` / `CSI 16 t`) — used `frame-char-width` / `frame-char-height`. Both are frame-level and ignore a buffer-local `default` face remapping, while the row/column count comes from the remap-aware `window-screen-lines` and `window-max-chars-per-line`. Any local font change (`text-scale-mode`, `buffer-face-mode`, a `ghostel-default` `:height`) therefore left the reported cell at the frame's size while the grid tracked the new font.

The kitty graphics paths shared the base, so a placement asking for 4×2 cells was sized for the frame's cell and drew at the wrong scale inside a scaled grid.

Both now use `default-font-width` / `default-font-height`, which resolve through `face-remapping-alist`.

Two things deliberately keep the frame metric:

- the float `line-spacing` branch, because redisplay scales a float by `FRAME_LINE_HEIGHT` (`xdisp.c`), matching `default-line-height`;
- kitty slice heights, which stay at the font height rather than `default-line-height` — buffer `line-spacing` is applied per glyph, so a spacing-inclusive slice would double-pad image rows.

Measured in a real Emacs before adding any caching: the `default-font-width` + `default-font-height` pair costs ~11 µs even on the `font-info` path, against ~0.06 µs for `frame-char-*`. Not worth caching on the per-placement kitty path.

### Verified live

GUI Emacs 31.0.91 driving a real bash, with a Python helper in the shell reading back the terminal's own `CSI 16 t` / `CSI 14 t` replies. `frame-char-*` stayed 7×14 throughout.

| state | buffer font | term grid | cell (h;w) | text area | kitty image (4c×2r) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | 7×14 | 34×120 | 22;11 | 748×1320 | `:width 28 :height 28`, `(slice 0 0 28 14)` |
| `text-scale-set 6` | 22×41 | 11×38 | 65;35 | 715×1330 | `:width 88 :height 82`, `(slice 0 0 88 41)` |
| `buffer-face-set '(:height 240)` | 14×28 | 17×60 | 44;22 | 748×1320 | — |
| `line-spacing` 4 | 7×14 | — | cell height 18 logical | — | slices still 14 tall |

Every text-area figure equals rows × cell-height and cols × cell-width. Before the change all four rows reported 22;11 and sized the image at 28×28, so at text-scale 6 an image drew at about a third of its declared cell footprint.

## A compile terminal reset its cell to 1×1 px

Found while reviewing the above; it is an independent pre-existing bug, in the second commit.

`ghostel-compile--start` reconciles the VT to the output window after `display-buffer` may have placed the buffer somewhere other than the window `--prepare-buffer` measured. It called `ghostel--set-size` with only rows and cols, and the native binding defaults omitted cell dimensions to 1 px — wiping the dimensions `ghostel--init-buffer` had just seeded. `ghostel--adjust-size` never repaired it, because it only re-sends when the row/column count changes and the reconcile had just made those match. So a compile terminal reported a 1 px cell for the whole run.

The reconcile now goes through `ghostel--set-size-with-cell-dims` like the other resize sites. Verified live: `M-x ghostel-compile` running a probe that queries `CSI 16 t` on `/dev/tty` reports `6;22;11`, where dropping the dimensions again reports `6;1;1`.

## Tests

Stubs in the kitty fixture and the cell-dimension tests now make the frame dimensions differ from the font dimensions, so a revert to `frame-char-*` fails rather than passing on coincidence. New: `ghostel-test-kitty-display-image-sized-from-buffer-font`.

`ghostel-test-compile-reconciles-vt-size-to-outwin` had been masking the compile bug — it stubbed `ghostel--set-size-with-cell-dims` away and recorded only the three-argument `ghostel--set-size`. Both reconcile tests now let the wrapper run and assert at the native boundary.

`make -j8 all` passes from a clean `.build/tests`.

## Not addressed here

The float `line-spacing` branch rounds where `xdisp.c` and `default-line-height` truncate — up to 1 px of over-report at e.g. `line-spacing` 0.25 with a 14 px font. Predates this work; only the base term changed.

author: markdbodman
body:
## Summary

Two changes from reviewing Anthropic's current per-model guidance against what `AGENTS.md` and the DPF skill pack actually do.

**1. A platform limit we were treating as advisory.** The Agent Skills API rejects a SKILL.md `description` over **1,024 characters**. Our worst is **995 — 29 characters of headroom**, and the failure mode is install-time validation rejection, not a lint note.

**2. A clock nothing was tracking.** BI-ACC7A2B5's `⟦runtime:⟧` marks facts that drift with the environment. Facts that drift with **model releases** had no marker — and the guidance shows the correct instruction *inverting between adjacent releases*.

## Changes

### 1. Hard 1,024-character description gate

- **`check-instruction-plane-size.mjs`** — `descriptionChars` per item, counted by **code point** (an astral glyph is one character to the API's validator, two to `.length`). Hard-errors over `maxDescriptionChars`, regardless of `structuralStrict` / `--strict`. A **90% shoulder warning** fires first, so approach is visible before the wall.
- **`instruction-plane-manifest.json`** — `maxDescriptionChars: 1024`, commented as *not ours to set*.

**This is deliberately a different measure from `maxExtractedItemChars` (700)**, which budgets the serialised `name`+`description` **bytes** the harness injects per session. Conflating them would be a real bug: a 1,100-byte block with a 400-char description is merely fat; a 1,030-char description fails validation and no byte budget catches it. `extractGroup`'s header documents both.

### 2. The `⟦model:⟧` clock

> `⟦model: <what this compensates for, and the assumption behind it>⟧`

*"Re-verify on model upgrade" is implied by the kind and is not restated* — dropping that redundancy cut the first draft by 35%.

The guidance shows the correct instruction reversing one release apart:

| Behaviour | Opus 4.8 | Opus 5 |
|---|---|---|
| Subagent delegation | under-reaches — *add* "delegate more" | over-reaches — *cap* delegation |
| Verification instructions | prompt for them | **delete them** — they cause over-verification |
| Self-check ("double-check your answer") | standard good practice | counterproductive; **inverts** the usual advice |

A rule tuned for one model becomes wrong prose one release later, with no edit and no failing test. The byte ratchet freezes a baseline; model behaviour doesn't hold still that long.

**Applied to 2 sites** — line 3 (`Read in full before any action` → the front-loading premise of the whole always-on plane) and §7 Subagent Dispatch (the injected "run the gate and fix errors" lines).

**Only two sites qualified, and that count is the finding.** `AGENTS.md`'s bulk is *enforced procedure*, not model-tuned prose — so **§12d's enforcement criterion, not model-behaviour deletion, is the lever that shrinks this plane.** The convention is mostly **prospective**: it exists so Phase 1 and the destination skills don't accumulate prose that silently inverts. Manufacturing more markers would mean marking rules that aren't model-dependent.

**A malformed marker hard-fails.** The convention's only value is that `grep "⟦model:"` returns the complete set, so a broken marker is a broken index, not a cosmetic slip.

## Test plan

- [x] **Source-only change** (guard script, tests, manifest/baseline, doctrine annotation, docs — no server route, MCP tool, runtime wiring, migration, or UX surface)
  - [x] Targeted unit tests — named below
  - [x] Guard self-run, doc index, doc links, doc-reference integrity, module size, context economy

### Verification evidence

```
$ node --test scripts/check-instruction-plane-size.test.mjs          # tests 31 / pass 31 / fail 0  (was 25)
$ node --test scripts/check-instruction-plane-rule-coverage.test.mjs # tests 13 / pass 13 / fail 0
$ node --test scripts/ci-policy-guards.test.mjs                      # tests  5 / pass  5 / fail 0

$ node scripts/check-instruction-plane-size.mjs
Instruction-plane OK — 108267 bytes across 3 always-on files
  + 16195 bytes harness-injected across 31 skill frontmatters
  (baseline 108267; ~27067 tokens advisory).
  Contingency markers: 10 ⟦runtime⟧ / 2 ⟦model⟧. 50 advisory structural note(s).

  [advisory] .../dpf-drive-portal-and-observe-build/SKILL.md description is 995 of 1024
             characters (97% of the hard API limit) — little headroom before the skill
             fails validation

$ node scripts/check-instruction-plane-rule-coverage.mjs → OK — 46 rule anchors reachable.
$ node scripts/gen-doc-index.mjs --check          → doc index fresh (583 pages).
$ node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs                → PASS — no error-level findings.
$ node scripts/check-doc-reference-integrity.mjs  → OK — no net-new broken references.
$ node scripts/check-module-size.mjs              → Module-size OK.
$ node scripts/check-context-economy.mjs          → Context-economy OK.
```

**Both gates proven negatively, not just green.** New tests assert: a 1,025-char description **errors with `structuralStrict:false`** (the sibling frontmatter signal is downgradeable; this one must not be); exactly 1,024 passes (inclusive); 995 warns but doesn't fail; an unterminated `⟦model:` is reported malformed and **not counted** as a real marker; and an unrecognised kind (`⟦todo:⟧`) inflates neither counter.

- [x] **Verification-harness limitation acknowledged** — no runtime-bound gate applies to this diff; nothing was skipped for harness reasons.

## Pre-PR readiness

Docs/source-only path; no shared-sandbox lease taken. Full CI is the backstop.

Local-CI-Override: source-only change (guard script + tests + manifest/baseline + two doctrine annotations + docs); no runtime code in the diff, all applicable gates runnable source-locally and captured above.

## Related issues / Epic

Refs **BI-0020D511** §12d/§12f (recorded as §12f-i sub-point *a-ii*) and extends **BI-ACC7A2B5**'s marking convention with a sibling clock.

## Overlap sweep

Touches `check-instruction-plane-size.{mjs,test.mjs}`, the manifest and its baseline, two single-line annotations in `AGENTS.md`, the ACC7A2B5 audit doc, and one paragraph of the BI-0020D511 spec. The baseline uses `merge=union` per `.gitattributes`. No overlap with BI-C5A31A24 (§8/§8a of `AGENTS.md`, untouched).

## Notes for the reviewer

- **Second consecutive growth on a shrink-only ratchet — naming the pattern rather than re-baselining quietly.** `AGENTS.md` 91,400 → 91,634 (**+234**), plane total 108,267. Markers were trimmed 35% before landing. But two growth PRs in a row is exactly how a ratchet stops meaning anything, and **Phase 1 now cuts from 108,267 rather than the 106,931 it was scoped against.** If you'd rather hold the line, the `⟦model:⟧` markers are the droppable half of this PR — the description gate costs nothing.
- **`maxDescriptionChars` is not a knob.** The manifest comment says so explicitly. If a skill hits it, the fix is moving how-to into the SKILL.md body, never raising the number — the API will reject it regardless of what we write here.
- **Why only two `⟦model:⟧` markers.** I went looking for the failure modes the guidance names (verification instructions, self-check nudges, forced progress narration, delegate-more guidance) and mostly did not find them in `AGENTS.md`. That is a real result, not a shallow search: it relocates the over-specification problem from "delete model-tuned prose" to "collapse enforced procedure to statement + pointer", which is §12d. I'd rather ship two defensible markers than pad the count.
- **Two documented skill limits we still don't measure**, both from the same guidance: SKILL.md body **under 500 lines**, and reference files **one level deep** from SKILL.md. Those are §12e's progressive-disclosure gap (31 single-file monoliths, 250,245 bytes, zero sub-files) and are Phase 1 work, not this PR's.

author: iddogino
body:
## What changed

- Fix the halftone IntersectionObserver/RAF initialization race so observed canvases do not start animating before their first positive intersection callback.
- Gate reduced-motion drawing on visibility as well.
- Add a `LazyHalftone` wrapper that mounts canvases only near the viewport and unmounts them after they leave.
- Use lazy-mounted halftones for home agent cards.
- Add regression coverage for RAF scheduling, intersection transitions, reduced motion, and lazy mounting.

## Why

Offscreen agent cards created canvases and briefly entered the animation loop before IntersectionObserver had reported their visibility. With dozens or hundreds of agents, that produced enough main-thread work to starve Playwright timers and make the E2E suite appear hung. It was also a real board performance and memory risk, not only a test issue.

## Validation

- Focused Vitest suite: 45/45 passed.
- TypeScript typecheck passed.
- Targeted ESLint passed.
- 204-agent browser profile:
  - only 6 canvases mounted near the top and 5 near the bottom

  - ScriptDuration reduced from 83.9s to 1.50s
  - TaskDuration reduced from 105s to 2.65s
- Full 6-worker web E2E run completed in 9 minutes without the former timeout cascade: 283 passed, 22 skipped, 2 isolated failures, and 2 retry-pass flakes.
- Both isolated failures passed together in a clean targeted rerun: 7/7 in 37.3 seconds.
- The halftone visual test passed in the full run.

author: angeles725
body:
Doc-only. Six corrections, one per **category** of documentation defect — the categories are the point, not the line count.

| Category | Treatment | Applied to |
|---|---|---|
| Volatile telemetry | **Delete**; consult the instrument | suite + case counts |
| Volatile telemetry, 2nd form | Replace coordinates with a searchable anchor | `verify-registry.sh:244` |
| Unmet invariant | Keep the contract, **declare the deviation** | §8 `DO` → `MUST` + #140 |
| False claim | Replace with the measurement that refutes it | §3 in-place mutation |
| New doctrine | Add | enumerator coverage |
| Rule with zero incidence | **Record, do not schedule** | authority-capture |

## Why the counts are deleted rather than refreshed

The snapshot read 79 suites against 81 on disk. But the decisive finding is sharper: **two careful measurements of the same commit differ.** Plain run is deterministic — 1694 both times. `--prove-teeth` gave 1868 and 1871.

That gap is not measurement noise. It means **some mutation controls skip conditionally**, so the teeth count is a property of the *run*, not of the *commit*. Recording it in doctrine as if it were the second was itself a false claim — and it leaves a cheap diagnostic for the teeth audit: run `--prove-teeth` twice, diff per-suite counts, and the suites that differ are the ones whose controls come and go.

## Why §8 says MUST and not DO

Measured on temp copies, for both operational cases named in that sentence:

| Script | `TARGETS.md` absent | broken `lib/` helper |
|---|---|---|
| `verify-registry.sh` | **0** | **0** |
| `sweep-retros.sh` | 1 | 1 |
| `sweep-audits.sh` | 1 | 1 |

Rewording the sentence to describe what the code does would promote a defect to official contract. Deleting it would lose the obligation. So the contract stays as **MUST**, with a Known-deviation note pointing at #140 that disappears when the script is fixed.

## Why the §3 premise had to go

It claimed `--prove-teeth` mutates implementation files in place, and therefore PRs must serialise. **False** — 25 samples over 500 s, dirty-file count never moved; every `sed -i` targets a mutant copy. It cost a session's throughput, and it was merged *by this session* in the doctrine PR that added the anti-silent-zero rules.

The paragraph's **conclusion** survives its false premise: a gate is still invalidated by writers editing during the run. So the rule stays and the reason is corrected. Two additions from the same session's damage: two actors in one checkout share the branch and index (a `git checkout` discarded uncommitted work twice), and hand-made worktrees do **not** isolate a subagent here because the harness resets cwd between commands.

## The new doctrine, and the case that earned it

> An audit instrument must prove the coverage of its own enumerator.

`e727cde` audited the pipefail race fleet-wide by enumerating `producer | grep -q`. `decompile-native.sh:27` reproducibly returns **141** for `/bin/bash` — same early-terminating-consumer family, outside that enumerator (#139). Rigorous about what it looked at; silent about what it could not see.

## Two overclaims caught in the paragraph that forbids them

One found by review (*"failing on every substantial binary"* — measured on two binaries, and "substantial" undefined), one by re-reading my own diff for `every|always|never|all`. Both narrowed to what was measured.

That the defect appears **while writing the rule against it**, with full attention on the subject, is the argument for having the rule and an external reviewer rather than trusting care.

## Gate

`shellcheck rc=0` · `run-all.sh --prove-teeth` 81/81 suites, 0 failed, 0 skipped.

Run as a **single pass** — the duplicate baseline this file used to mandate is measured redundant (0 of 81 suites report fewer cases under teeth; CI has always run only `--prove-teeth`). Its removal from §5 is queued separately so this PR stays doc-truth only.

author: ronlimon
body:
Enabling debug logging on this library writes the live bearer token into the consumer's log on every signed request. Three places:

- `calculate_sig` logs the signature base string, and since `authorization` is in `ALLOWED_HEADERS` that string literally contains `authorization:<token>`
- `sign_request` and `generateHMAC` each log the whole signed header dict — the token, `X-SIGNATURE`, and the `X-HMAC-ACCESS-KEY` / `X-HMAC-SIGNATURE` / `X-HMAC-DIGEST` triple
- `network` logs request and response bodies in full, which covers the login response and its `accessToken`

And `_safe_json`'s decode-failure path logged up to 500 characters of the body at ERROR, so that one needs no debug logging at all to fire.

The token isn't read-only — the same session does remote unlock, climate and charge control. Home Assistant consumers ship `home-assistant.log` in full backups and in Download Diagnostics.

## Fix

A small `redact` module, used at every logging site. Values are masked rather than dropped, so header names, JSON shape and status codes stay readable.

Bodies that aren't JSON keep a bounded excerpt with name/value pairs scrubbed. I didn't want to just drop them — that excerpt is what makes a 502 diagnosable. A JWT is masked wherever it appears, since a token can arrive with no key to match on.

The helpers are in their own module because `network` imports the signing modules, so they can't be shared from there.

Debug blocks are now behind `isEnabledFor(DEBUG)`. Arguments get evaluated regardless of level, and redacting costs meaningfully more than the `str()` it replaces.

## Tests

Five of them drive the real request functions with logging at DEBUG and assert the secrets are absent. I checked they fail against each of the three sites above, so they pin the behaviour rather than the implementation.

## Left alone on purpose

Both noted in the module rather than left silent:

- The TSP code — `data.code` in the response, `identifier` in the request. `identifier` is masked; `code` isn't, because that substring would also hide `countryCode`, `errorCode` and every `code: 200`.
- Credentials that `client` interpolates into exception messages, which reach the log at ERROR through `_refresh_token`. Separate change — happy to do that one too if you want it.

Nothing on the request path changes, and `_safe_json` still returns the parsed body untouched to callers.

author: jgocunha
body:
Closes #122.

**File → Quit** and **Ctrl+Q** called `std::exit(0)` from inside the ImGui render callback. That ends the process without unwinding the stack, so `Application::close()` never runs and no destructor fires — and it cannot be tested, because the test binary would simply vanish.

Both triggers now call `Application::requestQuit()`. `hasGUIBeenClosed()` reports the request, so the ordinary main loop exits and `close()` plus every destructor runs on its normal path.

The request lives on `Application` rather than on the menu bar so that **existing main loops keep working unchanged** — `while (!app.hasGUIBeenClosed())` now ends on Quit with no edit. No example or downstream loop needed touching.

The save/close/clean asymmetry between the two triggers (the menu item saves, Ctrl+Q does not) predates this fix and is preserved.

Tests: a pure `decideQuitAction()` covers the trigger→action mapping headlessly; `MainMenuBarQuitTest` covers the simulation side effects and asserts an unmodified main loop terminates after `requestQuit()`. Suite 1105/1107 locally — the 2 failures are the known pre-existing `LoggerTest` order dependence fixed on #140.

Docs: `wiki/Application and UI.md` gains a Quitting section; CHANGELOG updated.

author: gabrielsanbrito
body:
In https://github.com/tobie/pr-preview/pull/172, spec-generator migrated from using the api.csswg.org/bikeshed service to the w3.org/publications/spec-generator for generating Bikeshed documents. The HTTP APIs very similar but not the same. The Web Audio CI relies on setting the `force` param to 1, which is not part of the API surface of the new service. 

The same functionality can be achieved in the new service by setting the `die-on` parameter to `"nothing"`. More info [here](https://github.com/w3c/spec-generator/wiki/Migrating-Bikeshed-HTTP-API-usage-to-spec%E2%80%90generator).

Manually validated by:
1. pr-preview fails in https://github.com/WebAudio/web-audio-api/pull/2675
2. The generated URL is https://www.w3.org/publications/spec-generator/?type=bikeshed-spec&output=html&url=https%3A%2F%2Fraw.githubusercontent.com%2Fgabrielsanbrito%2Fweb-audio-api%2F857f48a208522456fd05522a02424b73ce858e7b%2Findex.bs&force=1&md-warning=not%20ready
3. If we switch "force=1" for "die-on=nothing" it works: https://www.w3.org/publications/spec-generator/?type=bikeshed-spec&output=html&url=https%3A%2F%2Fraw.githubusercontent.com%2Fgabrielsanbrito%2Fweb-audio-api%2F857f48a208522456fd05522a02424b73ce858e7b%2Findex.bs&die-on=nothing&md-warning=not%20ready

**Note:** This PR was auto-generated by the Roxie AI agent and is experimental.

## Summary

Fixes missing visual separators in the Intelligent Assistant notebook file attachments sidebar ([RHDHBUGS-3511](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHDHBUGS-3511)).

## Problem

In the notebook view, the file attachments sidebar lacked clear visual separation between:

1. The notebook title header and the documents list section
2. The main chat area and the resizable sidebar panel (drawer splitter)

Both dividers rely on PatternFly v6 design tokens (for example, `--pf-t--global--border--color--default`). When those CSS custom properties are not defined in the host application's theme context, borders render as transparent, so the sidebar sections visually blend together and the resize handle is hard to discover.

## Solution

- **`DocumentSidebar`**: Add an explicit horizontal `sectionDivider` between the notebook title row and the documents section, styled with the PatternFly border token and a `#c7c7c7` fallback color so the line stays visible even without theme variables.
- **`NotebookView`**: Add a `borderRight` on the PatternFly drawer splitter so the drag handle is visible when resizing the sidebar.
- **Tests**: Regression coverage ensures the separator renders with the expected ARIA role and CSS fallback.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a notebook with file attachments and confirm a horizontal line appears between the notebook title and the documents count
- [ ] Confirm a vertical line is visible on the drawer splitter when resizing the sidebar
- [ ] Run `DocumentSidebar` unit tests

embedded at `/studio` rather than deployed separately.** The schema is not configuration in this
system: its validation rules encode the scheduling constraints the public timetable reads, so
schema and frontend change together. Splitting them would put a review boundary through the middle
of single changes.

Sanity's own guided setup recommends the opposite, and the ADR records that rather than ignoring
it — including what the vendor's default optimises for (a Studio with its own lifecycle, its own
release cadence, or several consumers) and why none of those conditions hold here. If they later
do, the ADR names them as the trigger to revisit.

**The project holds itself to the Free plan's limits** despite starting on a 30-day Growth trial.
A capability that exists only during the trial would fail a month later, in a context far removed
from the decision that introduced it.

## The one thing that did not work

`/studio` returned 500 on first compile:

```
Export default doesn't exist in target module
  import useSWR from "swr";
```

Importing `sanity.config.ts` from a Server Component pulls the whole `sanity` package into the RSC
graph, where the `react-server` export condition resolves `swr` to a build with no default export.
Fixed with an explicit client boundary, which puts the Studio's module graph in the layer it
already belonged to. Recorded in `docs/architecture.md` with the error text, because recognising
it is most of the fix.

React also moves 19.2.4 → 19.2.8: `@portabletext/editor` requires ≥ 19.2.7 and `create-next-app`
had pinned lower.

## Verified

- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` — clean, both run.
- `/` and `/studio` — 200.
- The Studio boots in a browser, authenticates against the project, and reports an empty schema.
- The dataset reads over HTTP without credentials — checked, not assumed. This is what lets a
  reader clone the repository and run it without an account.

Runbook sections 1–3 are marked verified because they were executed. Everything not executed is
still marked unverified.

## Review notes

Rebase-merge rather than squash. The commit boundaries are deliberate and the roadmap refers to
them.

author: thewoolleyman
body:
Row 10 of the `qndn` triage — `inspect_worktree_pack`. Offenders **37 → 36**,
universe **161 → 164** (three new leaf modules), re-derived at both ends with
`_find_offenders` over `resolve_check_universe()` and the new modules STAGED.
Two Red→Green pairs, both carrying both trailer sets.

## The conversion was the cheap half. Three fail-opens were not.

The supervisor lead asked whether malformed and unreadable are distinguishable
in this unit, and said that if they are not, **the unit is the split, not the
signature**. They are not — and the split runs the OPPOSITE way from PR #988's,
which is why it was silent rather than loud.

**1. 🔴 The MANDATORY hook arm passed a hook whose bytes differ.** The parent's
docstring states the contract as *"STRICT BYTE-IDENTITY (zs22.7.9.5)"* and
*"Any deviation — a hook that is … whose bytes differ from the canonical body —
is a FAIL"*. `inspect_hook` compared **decoded text**, and `Path.read_text`
performs universal-newline translation, so a CRLF-converted `pre-push` decoded
back to the canonical string and the check returned **exit 0**. The Red leg
states it in one line: `expected the fail exit; got 0`.

**2. 🔴 The pack arm reported a repo it could not read as a repo it does not
govern.** `_read_pack_policy` collapsed three conditions into
`_PACK_POLICY_UNGOVERNED` — config absent (definitive), present-and-unparseable
(definitive), and *the read never happening* (definitive about nothing). An
ungoverned tree needs no pack, so the arm returned no violations and the check
exited 0. A governed repo whose config could not be read was told its pack
requirement did not apply — the exact fail-open zs22 A2 exists to close,
re-entered through the config read.

**3. The pack byte-identity arm had defect 1 too**, plus two crashes: an
undecodable pack file and an undecodable justfile each raised
`UnicodeDecodeError` out of the check where a definitive finding was available.

Fixed by **not decoding**: compare `read_bytes()` against the canonical body
encoded UTF-8, and search the justfile's bytes for the ASCII `import?` lines.

## The converse is what kept the failure track honest

Asked per condition — *which of these is this code entitled to be definitive
about?*

| condition | definitive? | track |
|---|---|---|
| hook absent / non-executable | YES | success (violation) |
| hook bytes differ, incl. CRLF or not UTF-8 | YES | success (violation) |
| config absent | YES | success (`ungoverned`) |
| config present and unparseable | YES | success (`ungoverned`) |
| `worktree_discipline` garbled | YES | success (violation) |
| pack bytes differ / justfile lacks `import?` | YES | success (violation) |
| **any of those reads not happening** | **NO** | **FAILURE** |

Only the last leaves the success track, and it is the sole inhabitant of
`CheckInputUnreadable`. Spelling this *"catch `OSError`"* would have swept
`FileNotFoundError` — an absent hook, which **is** the violation this check
exists to report, and an absent config, which is what makes a directory
ungoverned — into a silent non-answer. Every read sits past an `is_file()`
probe, and that is what keeps absence off the failure track.

**Three of the four conditions that *look* unreadable turn out to be
definitively answerable, and making them so is what shrank the failure track to
one honest inhabitant.** The fix was to stop decoding, not to widen a `try`.

## Instance seven of the suite pinning the defect

Two tests named `*_unreadable_*`, and neither fixture ever made a file
unreadable — both wrote invalid JSON. Name, fixture and docstring disagreed,
exactly as in #988's five. Both renamed to `*_unparseable_*`, and genuine
unreadability now has its own coverage. **Read the fixture, never the test
name.**

## Two dead ends recorded, because both would have reported work not done

- **Public names in the extracted siblings measured 38 offenders, not 36** —
  five unconverted functions enrolled in the railway universe *by a move*. The
  names stay `_`-prefixed and are re-exported through `__all__`, which pyright
  honours for `reportUnusedFunction` (probed both ways: a listed private
  function is clean, an unlisted one errors). Only the count said so.
- **A bare sibling import of the shared failure type creates a second class
  object**, so a failure raised in an arm did not compare equal to one the
  parent matched. Measured — the unit tests' equality assertions failed on
  exactly that. `CheckInputUnreadable` is imported ABSOLUTELY where the other
  sibling imports are bare.

`_inspect_hook` and `_find_vendored_hook_copies` are therefore **not convicted**
by the check, and are converted anyway: the fail-open is real whether or not the
count can see it.

## LLOC, as the chain predicted

The parent was at **247/250 hard** before this change and hit **285**. Three
splits — `_primary_checkout_unreadable` (the shared failure type),
`_primary_checkout_hook_files` (the two arms), `_primary_checkout_narration`
(every finding the check can emit, in one place). Every module is now under even
the **200** soft ceiling.

## Verification

- `just check` green at both commits and on the pushed branch (465s).
- Full suite **2385 passed**; `check-per-file-coverage` 100%.
- Both commits carry `TDD-Red-*` + `TDD-Green-*`.
- Every new fixture was negative-controlled: the two parent read-failure arms
  fail without their perturbation, and no fixture uses `chmod 000` — this suite
  runs as root, where a mode-based fixture cannot fail.

Refs: `livespec-dev-tooling-8o8e`
